items.text: The system asks how reason can retain objective authority, practical orientation, and systematic unity after unrestricted speculative metaphysics, methodological transfer, and aggregate organization have failed.

Its central claim is that rational authority survives only through a differentiated constitution assigning theoretical cognition to possible experience, practical legislation to moral law, and systemic organization to architectonic criticism.
At this scale the argument becomes a transcendental-juridical architectonic that constructs reason’s unity by allocating powers, exposing usurpations, and regulating their permissible interaction.

Possible experience and moral law operate as distinct centers of validity, while criticism coordinates them without converting either theoretical limitation or practical necessity into supersensible cognition.

The movement is recursive and spiral: rational aspiration exceeds its jurisdiction, conflict reveals the excess, critique restricts it, and the restricted demand returns as empirical inquiry, practical belief, or reconstructed system.
Negation becomes generative because every exclusion of illegitimate cognition produces a positive differentiation of method, assent, practical employment, or institutional form.

The rational subject becomes simultaneously legislator, accused, and finite believer, while rational time divides into retrospective diagnosis, recursive self-correction, and prospective moral-systematic completion.

Closure is conditional rather than final: theoretical cognition is bounded, practical commitment remains non-cognitive, empirical and critical inquiry stay open, and collective architectonic completion is deferred.
[Persistent] Possible experience is the exclusive field of theoretical objectivity and the primary tribunal for claims concerning objects, causes, and explanations.
[Persistent] Objective cognition requires an authorized mode of presentation and a prior deduction of the validity and synthesis of its concepts.
[Mutating] Rational entitlement is function-specific: construction, deduction, empirical explanation, regulation, practical legislation, and critical adjudication cannot substitute for one another.
[Attractor] Reason is autonomous only when it legislates its own powers while submitting every exercise of those powers to criticism.
[Emergent] Systematic unity is necessary but never self-validating; architectonic organization requires critical authorization because error can itself assume systematic form.
[Mutating] Supersensible ideas lose constitutive theoretical status but persist as regulative orientations, practical concerns, postulates, beliefs, or retractable defensive suppositions.
[Terminal] Moral law is autonomous from happiness and theology and supplies the only proper canon of pure practical reason.

[Emergent] The highest good generates practically necessary belief by requiring a unity of virtue and happiness that natural causality cannot guarantee, while objective theoretical sufficiency remains absent.
[Emergent] Theoretical objectivity and practical necessity are irreducible but coordinated modalities of reason rather than competing claims to one undifferentiated validity.
[Mutating] Limitation reverses from deprivation into productive protection by securing cognition, belief, inquiry, and systematic order against illegitimate extension.

[Attractor] Architectonic unity orders objects, methods, disciplines, practical interests, and historical positions under a single human destination without supplying speculative possession of that destination.
[Mutating] The rational subject becomes a self-legislating and self-accusing office that must act and believe without becoming the sovereign producer of its objects.
[Emergent] Rational development has a recursively divided temporality in which failure discloses prior conditions, criticism reorganizes the present, and moral-systematic completion remains future.
[Terminal] The system terminates in bounded theoretical authority, practically governed commitment, open inquiry, and prospective rather than completed architectonic closure.
Possible experience retains its identity as the condition of objective cognition while expanding into the theoretical pole of a larger constitutional architecture.
Proof mutates from inferential support among propositions into a jurisdictional demonstration that concepts possess objective reference and lawful scope.
Limitation reverses valence twice: it first protects theoretical cognition and then enables practical belief without licensing theoretical recovery of the supersensible.
The supersensible undergoes terminal status transformation from attempted object-cognition through regulative orientation to practically necessary but non-cognitive belief.
Discipline escalates from local restriction of method into criticism’s general tribunal over theoretical, practical, historical, and architectonic entitlement.
Systematicity retains its scientific necessity but loses sufficiency once opposed dogmatic and sceptical procedures prove equally capable of systematic organization.
Opposition migrates from external doctrinal combat into reason’s internal adversarial procedure and then into historical diagnosis of recurrent rational positions.
Universality divides into objectively communicable cognition, universally binding moral law, and publicly reproducible criticism.
Teleology escalates from regulation of inquiry and moral interpretation of nature into the architectonic destination governing the entire economy of reason.
Scepticism disappears as an independent destination after its interruptive function is absorbed into criticism, while dogmatism survives only as a recurrent object of that criticism.

Mathematical construction, individual proof restrictions, and detailed hypothesis tests remain lower-layer machinery; their current-level result is the non-transferability of cognitive functions across jurisdictions.
Exact distribution within the highest good and classifications of historical schools remain local specifications until absorbed into the wider coordination of moral ends and epistemic positions.

Possible experience, transcendental deduction, and the non-cognitive status of practical postulates scale upward because they jointly determine the boundary between cognition and legitimate orientation.
Discipline, canon, teleology, and criticism bridge the units by connecting jurisdictional restriction, practical legislation, and architectonic reconstruction.
Methodological temptation, natural insufficiency, and object-source-method misalignment catalyze transitions because each exposes a demand operating without its enabling conditions.
Object-level victory, merely problematical assent, technical unity, and naturalism are superseded by jurisdictional critique, practical necessity, and rationally warranted system.
No successful method, formal derivation, or a priori status authorizes transfer into a domain lacking the relevant mode of presentation.
Neither affirmation nor denial of supersensible conditions can become theoretical cognition merely through conceptual consistency, practical need, or rational demand.
Regulative utility, practical necessity, and moral desirability cannot be converted into evidence for the objective reality of their supersensible correlates.
Theology cannot legislate morality from outside because divine command would destroy the autonomy that alone generates legitimate practical orientation.
Neither aggregation nor systematic form alone constitutes science, truth, or rational legitimacy.
Dogmatism, scepticism, and explanatory closure are rejected as terminal positions because each suppresses the critical examination of reason’s authority.
Private assurance and coercively imposed belief cannot substitute for objective warrant, autonomous moral law, or publicly sustainable criticism.
The architecture requires that intellectual intuition be unavailable to finite reason, since its availability would collapse the distinction between thought, presentation, belief, and cognition.
It rejects the rival model in which cognition exhausts rational legitimacy, because practical action must remain possible without a speculative science of the supersensible.
It excludes any natural harmonism capable of guaranteeing the coincidence of virtue, happiness, and moral completion within empirical history.

It disqualifies the assumption that accumulation or historical succession can generate their own rational plan, while also refusing to admit that architectonic unity is merely retrospectively imposed.
No standpoint external to reason can validate reason’s powers, practical commitments, or system without sacrificing autonomy or reproducing the unexamined conditions of illusion.
Ultimate ends cannot remain coordinate, yet the final unity of nature and freedom cannot become a theoretically possessed object.
The unavailable presentation of supersensible objects is the central absence around which theoretical limitation, practical postulation, and differentiated assent are organized.
The absent empirical moral world structures hope and futurity because reason requires a completed moral order that can never be present as theoretical knowledge.
The system lacks both an external standpoint and an actual philosopher-legislator, leaving critique to exercise authority that no embodied subject can finally possess.
The missing positive procedure of criticism and the missing guarantee of the true architectonic idea remain concealed conditions of the system’s claim to final jurisdiction.
The unity of nature and freedom functions as an unavailable horizon that organizes the whole while postponing final satisfaction beyond present critical achievement.

Once experiential validity is combined with architectonic allocation, epistemic legitimacy becomes relational: a claim is entitled only when object, source, presentation, method, scope, and systemic position align.
Speculative restriction preserves supersensible demand by routing it through autonomous moral law and then classifying its objects as practical belief rather than recovered knowledge.

The distinction between discipline and canon yields a constitutional model of reason in which negative regulation is general, while positive legislation belongs only to a demonstrably proper employment.
Internalized opposition becomes historically and institutionally productive when autonomous self-criticism is reproduced as a collective method rather than confined to private rational mastery.
The moral future and the architectonic future converge as distinct expressions of completion demanded in the present but unavailable as present possession.
Moral belief can be universally accessible without becoming objectively communicable knowledge, while public criticism prevents this accessibility from licensing coercion or philosophical monopoly.
Metaphysics survives its speculative defeat by becoming the regulated office that organizes unavoidable questions, prevents error, and coordinates rational functions.
The same boundary that blocks transcendent explanation protects empirical inquiry from closure and practical agency from suspension pending impossible certainty.
Reality becomes a jurisdictionally stratified coordination system in which appearances, practical ends, supersensible ideas, and historical positions possess different modes of admissibility.
Rational validity becomes topological rather than scalar because claims occupy distinct coordinates of objectivity, subjective commitment, practical necessity, and systemic placement.
The subject is reconstructed as legislator, accused, investigator, and believer whose autonomy consists in disciplined self-government rather than metaphysical sovereignty.
Time becomes ethically and architectonically asymmetric: present disunity is interpreted through prior rational conditions and directed toward an unpossessed future completion.
The architecture has a political-institutional consequence: belief loses coercive authority, specialist reason loses sovereignty, and criticism must become publicly reproducible.
Rational agency is action under disciplined undecidability: finite reason must act from law while refusing both dogmatic possession and sceptical suspension.
Metaphysics changes its criterion of success from transcendent acquisition to productive differentiation, error-prevention, and durable coordination of rational powers.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Cognitive success or metaphysical interest generates expansion, expansion generates conflict, conflict generates criticism, and criticism returns the original demand in a restricted function.

Possible experience and moral law form paired attractors: one repeatedly draws theoretical claims back to objective presentation, while the other draws practical orientation back to autonomous obligation.
The highest good is an escalation machine carrying unconditional law through worthiness and natural insufficiency toward postulation and disciplined belief.
The single human destination and the absent complete philosophy function as architectonic attractors that organize present cognition without becoming presently possessed objects.
Opposition becomes a machine when reason produces its own objections, submits them to public stabilization, and uses the resulting method to regenerate autonomous criticism.
Practical postulation contains itself recursively: speculative limitation generates belief, and belief reactivates the same limitation to prevent theological inflation.
Systematicity undergoes phase change when accumulated organization discloses its governing idea but simultaneously reveals that formal unity requires critical adjudication.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Cognitive ambition, moral demand, and accumulated metaphysical construction generate a field requiring rational reconstruction.
Every claim is tested for object, source, mode of presentation, method, scope, and objective validity.
Valid functions are allocated to construction, deduction, empirical explanation, regulation, practical legislation, and architectonic adjudication.
Adversarial testing and transcendental classification exclude every operation that exceeds its enabling conditions or substitutes contingent organization for rational necessity.
Excluded speculative demand is preserved as empirical openness, regulative orientation, autonomous obligation, or practical postulation.
The assent matrix assigns each surviving demand a status determined by subjective sufficiency, objective sufficiency, and practical necessity.
Architectonic integration orders the resulting jurisdictions under a human end, then reopens the machine because collective criticism and the unity of nature and freedom remain incomplete.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Cognitive success and aggregate organization → unauthorized expansion → metaphysical conflict → demand for transcendental jurisdiction.
Jurisdictional assay → possible experience → differentiated cognitive functions → bounded theoretical authority → open empirical inquiry.
Speculative subtraction → autonomous moral law → highest good → natural insufficiency → practical postulates → moral belief → renewed speculative containment.
Critical differentiation → architectonic placement → historical self-diagnosis → public reproduction of criticism → prospective moral-systematic closure.
The a priori becomes a differentiated constitutional field rather than a homogeneous method transferable across mathematics, experience, morality, and metaphysics.
Proof and refutation are relocated from proposition-level combat to examination of the conditions authorizing objective reference.
Boundaries become enabling instruments that preserve cognition, practical agency, empirical openness, and systematic unity.
Belief becomes a positive rational modality coordinated with but irreducible to knowledge, opinion, persuasion, and theological doctrine.
Metaphysics is reclassified from transcendent doctrine into the critically regulated organization of unavoidable rational questions.
History becomes an internal audit of reason’s architecture rather than a chronological record external to philosophical validity.
Universality divides into cognitive communicability, moral accessibility, and public methodological reproducibility, dissolving the equation of universality with one evidential form.
At the surface level, proofs, hypotheses, supersensible ideas, moral postulates, forms of assent, sciences, and philosophical schools are classified and tested.
At the structural level, jurisdictional alignment among objects, sources, presentations, methods, laws, and ends determines every claim’s admissibility.
At the metastrategic level, struggle shifts from possessing supersensible objects to assigning claim-status, policing conversion between functions, and reconstructing inherited positions.
At the ontological and temporal level, experiential reality remains theoretically ordered while moral-systematic completion recedes into a future horizon disclosed through recursive failure.
At the methodological and performative level, the system enacts its thesis by generating claims, exposing their inflation, reclassifying their functions, and reopening criticism.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Universal criticizability conflicts with critique’s need to function as the final tribunal rather than one more revisable position.

Possible experience validates transcendental principles while those principles constitute possible experience, leaving the theoretical criterion reflexively dependent on the deduction it is meant to authorize.
The passage from speculative failure to practical authority is indispensable but does not by itself demonstrate that reason’s supersensible demand has acquired legitimate positive objects.
The postulation of God and future life depends on an underdemonstrated claim that no alternative conditions could realize the required moral unity.
Moral law is independently binding, yet the represented efficacy and completion of its maxims depend on postulated conditions that remain objectively insufficient.
Practical freedom is retained as necessary for agency while transcendental freedom remains theoretically suspended, leaving their relation structurally unresolved.
The architectonic idea claims a priori authority although it becomes visible through historical accumulation and classificatory compression.
Proof changes function when inferential support is subordinated to deduction of objective validity and jurisdiction.
Limitation changes from prohibition into the productive condition of cognition, practical belief, and continuing inquiry.
Supersensible objects change into regulative ideas and then into objects of practical belief without acquiring theoretical objecthood.
Criticism changes from an internal restrictive organ into the tribunal governing the history, architecture, and future reproduction of reason.
Systematicity changes from the defining contrast with aggregation into a merely necessary form requiring independent critical authorization.
Teleology changes from local regulation of inquiry into the singular moral destination ordering the complete economy of cognition.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is imaged as a stratified court-organism whose regions possess different laws and whose unity depends on adjudicated coordination rather than homogeneous substance.
The subject is a finite provisional legislator who judges cognition, submits its own powers to trial, and commits practically without possessing the supersensible.
Time is a recursive vector in which prior rational conditions are disclosed through conflict and projected toward an unexperienced future completion.
Struggle consists in navigating jurisdictional boundaries between dogmatic possession and sceptical suspension while sustaining empirical inquiry, autonomous action, and public criticism.

The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the current-level engine if experiential objectivity, practical legislation, differentiated assent, architectonic placement, and recursive criticism remain jointly operative.

The architecture remains underdetermined concerning the transcendental deductions validating possible experience, the exclusivity of the moral postulates, and the criterion identifying the true architectonic idea.
The system is coherent at this scale only if theoretical cognition, practical necessity, and architectonic regulation remain distinct without becoming disconnected.
The architecture is strongest where repeated negation produces positive differentiation among cognitive functions, modes of assent, jurisdictions, and systemic positions.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only when temptation, conflict, speculative subtraction, practical return, and historical reorganization remain recursive rather than successive discarded errors.

The indispensable remainder resistant to axiomatic reduction is the transition from critical restriction to moral-teleological orientation, because that transition bears terminal weight beyond its supplied demonstrations.

items.text: Finite reason must authorize necessary objective cognition while preserving its demands for totality and orientation without converting those demands into knowledge of supersensible objects.
Rational authority is reconstructed as a differentiated constitution in which possible experience grounds theoretical objectivity and distinct jurisdictions govern reason’s remaining functions.
Objective experience arises through the synthesis of sensible multiplicity under concepts whose authority extends only to the conditions under which objects can be presented.
The successful legislation of lawful nature produces conditioned cognition, which necessarily generates a further demand for unconditioned completion.
Critique becomes a reflexive tribunal that secures cognition by diagnosing contradiction and proof failure as effects of unauthorized object-construction.
Negation becomes generative when the exclusion of transcendent knowledge redistributes reason’s demands into empirical, regulative, practical, and architectonic functions.
The movement is spiral: each recovered condition enables cognition, generates a new demand or excess, and returns that excess through another jurisdictional mediation.
Closure is asymmetrical: phenomenal lawfulness and formal jurisdiction close, while empirical inquiry, practical realization, criticism, and systematic construction remain open.
[Persistent] Finite cognition requires irreducibly differentiated sensible presentation and conceptual synthesis under the common restriction of possible experience.
[Attractor] Mediation is the operative center through which cognitive functions acquire authority only by being coordinated within their proper jurisdictions.
[Attractor] Possible experience is simultaneously the constituted field of objective cognition and the tribunal testing every theoretical claim to object-reference.
[Mutating] Objectivity changes from presumed correspondence with independent being into universally necessary, temporally enacted, and jurisdictionally restricted synthesis.
[Mutating] The subject is generated as an apperceptive integrating function and subsequently divided into projector, legislator, accused party, critic, and finite believer.
[Attractor] The field of conditioned experience necessarily activates reason’s demand for complete determination, systematic unity, and an unconditioned ground.
[Emergent] Transcendental illusion is generated when valid conceptual or inferential functions are detached from sensible authorization and transferred to unpresentable total objects.
[Emergent] Contradiction and proof collapse acquire critical force by exposing an invalid completed object-model shared by opposed metaphysical claims.
[Emergent] Critique is a positive governance mechanism that produces valid cognition by allocating, restricting, and coordinating heterogeneous rational functions.
[Persistent] Rational validity is topological because differentiated faculties and functions support irreducibly distinct modes of authorization rather than one homogeneous scale.
[Mutating] Limitation changes from apparent deprivation into the condition protecting objective validity, empirical openness, practical commitment, and systematic orientation.
[Terminal] Supersensible objects remain theoretically indeterminate, and their regulative or practical recovery cannot restore theoretical objecthood.
[Terminal] Formal legislation and jurisdiction can close while particular empirical determinations and the realization of rational ends remain unfinished.
[Attractor] Rational autonomy consists in recursively legislating and criticizing authority through the same finite powers whose legitimacy remains under examination.
[Stable identity with expansion] Experience remains cognition’s field but expands from constituted outcome into the central jurisdictional pole governing theoretical reference.
[Serial mutation] Synthesis escalates from the prior operation of object-constitution into lawful natural legislation and becomes dialectical totalization when extended beyond presentation.
[Functional recurrence] Faculty differentiation migrates from an account of cognitive production into a constitutional prohibition against jurisdictional substitution.
[Subject mutation] Subjectivity reverses from suspected distortion into a universal formal condition, then becomes a divided architect implicated in its own projections.
[Domain expansion] Time develops from sensible form and schematic medium into the recursive asymmetry of incomplete self-presence, regress, criticism, and prospective completion.
[Valence reversal] Critique and negation change from restraint into the constructive, institutional, and procedural governance of positive rational production.
[Reversal] Contradiction changes from an apparent collision within reality into a diagnostic instrument for exposing valid forms operating through an invalid object-model.

[Absorption] Noumenal objecthood and the unconditioned are absorbed into a differentiated boundary architecture of negative limit, regulative horizon, practical concern, and architectonic destination.
[Terminal transformation] Completion ceases to mean possession of total content and becomes formal completeness in the allocation of permanently open inquiry.
Detailed logical inventories, temporal schemata, reflection-concepts, proofs, examples, and hypothesis tests remain local instruments rather than the whole-book architecture.
Faculty differentiation scales upward because it governs both the production of objects and the constitutional separation of rational jurisdictions.
Synthesis, apperception, judgment, and schematism bridge object-constitution to the universal criterion separating objective cognition from nonobjective orientation.
The completion of phenomenal constitution catalyzes the transition to dialectic because every constituted object remains conditioned and therefore reactivates the demand for completion.
The underived inventory of cognitive forms and the underdetermined force of regulative and practical principles scale upward as limits of transcendental self-explanation.
Ready-made correspondence, substantial soul, completed world-totality, and supreme object lose terminal authority and survive only as critically recoded positions or functions.
Empirical recurrence and association cannot generate the necessity required for universally valid objective cognition.
Concepts and categories cannot determine objects without sensible givenness and the conditions of possible experience.
Sensible multiplicity cannot constitute an object before synthesis because an unsynthesized manifold lacks objective conjunction and unity.
Logical consistency, formal validity, and conceptual completeness cannot establish material truth, objective possibility, or existence.
Neither the world-whole nor intrinsic reality can be surveyed from an external or unconditioned standpoint.
Theoretical reason can neither affirm nor deny supersensible objects when categorial application lacks sensible authorization.
Regulative utility and practical necessity cannot become evidence for theoretical objecthood or existence.
Neither an exhaustive application algorithm nor a single successful critique can abolish judgment, recurrent illusion, or the need for renewed criticism.
The architecture requires the falsity of any model in which independently constituted objects arrive already unified and can be inspected from outside finite cognition.
Receptivity and spontaneity cannot be dissolved into a homogeneous faculty or validity continuum without eliminating the mediations that generate cognition.
Finite reason cannot possess intellectual intuition because immediate presentation of complete conditions would dissolve both synthesis and critical jurisdiction.
No transparent or substantial subject can convert its integrating activity into cognition of itself as an independently subsisting entity.
Universal formal order cannot determine particular existence or guarantee the empirical coincidence of nature, freedom, virtue, and happiness.
No external authority can validate critique, yet self-validation cannot confer unconditioned sovereignty on the finite powers being examined.
The deepest absent capacity is an intellectual intuition that would disclose the common ground of receptivity and spontaneity while presenting complete conditions immediately.
The system circles an unavailable all-sufficient ground that would terminate conditioning without becoming another conditioned object.
The unavailable identity of thinkability, knowability, and complete possession of reality prevents the complete world and all its conditions from becoming one object.
The absent empirical unity of nature, freedom, virtue, and happiness gives practical hope its orientation while withholding theoretical completion.
Final completion and an external guarantor must remain absent because criticism, inquiry, and practical approximation derive their force from nonpossession.
The conditions constituting objective experience also generate its boundary, so authorization and restriction are two operations of one critical structure.
The same categories that generate lawful nature produce dialectical illusion when their constitutive use is extended into complete totalization.
Successful phenomenal constitution internally generates an unknown remainder whose withdrawal from objecthood permits regulative and practical use without restoring theoretical cognition.
Temporal schematization and recursive noncompletion jointly make finitude appear as both incomplete self-presence and the impossibility of possessing total conditions at once.
Positive object-constitution and negative criticism form a feedback system in which valid production depends on recurrent exclusion of unauthorized transitions.
Because nature is formally legislated but materially open, regulative totality can guide empirical inquiry only as a procedure that prevents arbitrary arrest.
Domain-indexed theoretical authority and practical necessity form distinct attractors, preventing practical authorization from becoming supersensible evidence.
Since reason judges itself through the powers under judgment, criticism must remain recurrent and publicly reproducible rather than privately or finally completed.
Epistemic authority becomes a conditioned and procedural achievement established through provenance, application, scope, and jurisdiction rather than direct possession of being.
Subject and object become differentiated effects of distributed synthesis, while the subject’s later rational roles remain irreducible to a knowable substance.
Reality-for-cognition becomes a formally legislated field of conditioned appearances whose material laws remain empirical and whose totality remains an unpossessed task.
Time becomes a layered recursive operator joining succession, schematic application, regress, retrospective diagnosis, and prospective completion.
Error is an internally recurrent jurisdictional effect because valid rational forms generate illusion when detached from their authorized conditions.
Metaphysics becomes a constitutional topology of grounding, application, recurrent error, differentiated validity, and regulated function.
Critical authority acquires a public and institutional dimension because recurrent illusion cannot be governed by specialist sovereignty or private correction alone.
Rational agency becomes disciplined action under noncompletion rather than sovereign command over objects, history, or the totality of conditions.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Experience provokes a demand for necessity, necessity triggers a regress to conditions, those conditions constitute experience, and every determination returns for renewed jurisdictional testing.
Faculty separation enables cooperation, cooperation produces cognition, and reason then resubmits both its operations and restrictions to criticism.
Conditioned cognition generates demand, demand becomes projection, and projection passes through reification into paralogism, antinomy, or theological proof.
Valid forms generate illusion, but contradiction or proof collapse converts that illusion into a diagnostic phase change from object-dispute to object-critique.
Phenomenal constitution intensifies the unknown, while the resulting boundary returns excluded totalizing demand as empirical, regulative, practical, or architectonic work.
Rules reproduce the application regress, and criticism reproduces the authorization regress, so judgment and public review interrupt but never abolish recursive mediation.
Practical belief is recursively contained because speculative limitation enables it, while belief reactivates that same limitation against theological inflation.
Possible experience, synthesis, moral law, and unavailable completion form coupled attractors that repeatedly redistribute reason’s operations without terminal convergence.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessary cognition plus metaphysical contradiction → demand for synthetic a priori authorization → critique of finite rational competence.
Receptive presentation plus irreducibly distinct conceptual activity → prior synthesis → objectively unified sensible multiplicity.
Synthesis plus apperception plus judgment → category → temporal schema → authorized objective application.
Schematized categories → principles of experience → universal lawful nature → materially open and conditioned cognition.
Conditioned cognition plus recursive inquiry → demand for total conditions → illusory objectification of subject, world, and supreme ground.
Antinomial contradiction plus proof dependency → exposure of reification → invalidation of procedural unity converted into existence.
Withdrawal of the invalid object-model → speculative suspension → redistribution into constitutive cognition, regulation, practical legislation, and architectonic placement.
Public criticism plus architectonic integration → formally bounded authority → reopening of empirical, practical, and systematic tasks.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Scientific necessity and metaphysical conflict → synthetic a priori demand → transcendental regress from objects to enabling conditions.
A priori sensible field → manifold requiring synthesis → original apperception → co-generation of self-ascription and object-relation.
Judgmental function → category → temporal schema → principles of experience → lawful but empirically open nature.
Conditioned experience → unavoidable demand for completion → projected subject, world, and supreme ground → transcendental illusion.
Paralogism, antinomy, and proof collapse → diagnosis of shared reification → withdrawal of constitutive totality.
Speculative restriction → empirical continuation → regulative systematization → practical commitment → architectonic allocation → recurrent public criticism.
Objectivity is reclassified from correspondence with ready-made objects into necessary synthesis compatible with empirical realism and the deobjectification of totality.
The subject–object opposition becomes an internal differentiation of one synthetic architecture whose subject occupies multiple irreducible roles without becoming a substance.
A priori origin is separated from unrestricted range, making boundaries enabling instruments rather than external restraints on an otherwise unlimited reason.
Truth and validity become stratified and topological, requiring each claim to be located by presentation, function, scope, object, and mode of assent.
Contradiction becomes a metacritical method for testing the validity of the alleged object and question before evaluating competing answers.
Nature divides into invariant formal lawfulness and empirical material determination, while world-totality is withdrawn as an object.
Metaphysics and history become recursive audits of reason’s claims, errors, jurisdictions, and future-oriented construction rather than inventories of transcendent being.
At the surface level, mathematics, natural science, selfhood, world-totality, freedom, theology, morality, and system are coordinated around the validity and limits of rational claims.
At the structural level, receptivity, synthesis, imagination, apperception, understanding, judgment, and reason form a distributed circuit that constitutes objects and projects totalities.
At the metastrategic level, inquiry shifts from doctrinal assertion to provenance-testing, object-model criticism, jurisdictional allocation, and governance of claim-production.

At the ontological and temporal level, reality-for-cognition is a lawfully synthesized field of conditioned appearances, while time mediates constitution, regress, correction, and unavailable completion.

At the methodological and performative level, the system constructs rational mechanisms, generates their excesses, reclassifies their functions, and derives limitations from their enabling conditions.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reason must validate criticism through the powers under examination even though universal criticizability denies the tribunal an unrevisable foundation.
Cognition presupposes affection by independently constituted objects whose passage into formal representation remains underexplained.
Claims of categorial and architectonic completeness depend on inventories whose completeness is asserted while substantive inquiry remains permanently unfinished.
Possible experience is constituted by transcendental principles while simultaneously serving as their validating field, producing reflexive dependence rather than external proof.
Judgment must remain irreducible to rules, while regulative principles exercise axiom-like force whose precise authority over inquiry remains underdetermined.
Speculative limitation enables practical authority but does not itself establish the efficacy, necessity, or exclusivity of particular practical postulates.
Practical freedom and intelligible grounding must remain compatible with empirical lawfulness despite the absence of any guaranteed harmony or resolved relation between them.
The a priori mutates from independence from experience into the structural condition, juridical boundary, and differentiated authorization of possible experience.
Synthesis mutates from a logical relation into the operation generating objecthood and then into dialectical totalization when absolutized.
Objectivity mutates from apparent correspondence into invariant synthesis, valid application, and temporally procedural constitution.
The subject mutates from presumed bearer into an integrating function and then into a finite architect, accused party, legislator, critic, and believer.
Time mutates from intuitive form into schematic transformation medium and then into a vector of recursive diagnosis and future completion.
Critique and negation mutate from limitation into the positive governance that generates, secures, and differentiates cognition, belief, and system.
Closure mutates from possession of substantive totality into formal self-limitation, open inquiry, and prospective practical-architectonic completion.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality-for-cognition is a gated recursive court-engine that receives multiplicity, synthesizes objects, generates totalizing claims, and adjudicates them across stratified jurisdictions.
The subject is a finite switching-center, regressor, legislator, defendant, and critic situated inside the system it attempts to judge.
Time is the transformation medium and recursive vector through which succession becomes objectivity, renewed conditioning, retrospective correction, and never-present completion.
Struggle consists in routing claims through presentation and jurisdiction while navigating between dogmatic possession and sceptical suspension.
The resulting world is a lawful but empirically open interior whose unity depends on adjudicated coordination and whose boundary generates an unknowable remainder.

The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the movement from synthetic a priori authorization through phenomenal constitution to dialectical projection, critical restriction, and functional redistribution.
The system is coherent only if receptivity, synthesis, apperception, theoretical cognition, regulation, practical necessity, and architectonic legitimacy remain distinct but recursively coordinated.
The architecture is strongest where phenomenal object-generation and dialectical diagnosis converge on one boundary logic that simultaneously authorizes and restricts reason.
The affection–form relation, exact mediation mechanism, categorial completeness, regulative force, practical postulation, and intelligible grounding remain underdetermined.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only by retaining recursive sequencing, projection, conflict, restriction, functional return, and renewed criticism.
Finite reason’s capacity to discipline itself without an external standpoint remains the indispensable element resistant to complete axiomatic reduction.
