identity.original_context: Introduction · Sect. I. Of The Origin Of Our Ideas · Sect. II. Division Of The Subject

items.text: The central problem is to explain how impression-derived ideas can preserve experience, depart from it, form regular complexes, and generate spatial and temporal order without acquiring independent content.
The governing thesis is that ideational differences arise primarily from force, arrangement, recurrence, and relational operation rather than from heterogeneous elemental origins.
The argument becomes an empirical genealogy of mental organization: impressions supply materials, while faculties and relations determine how those materials recur, combine, and appear.
Memory conserves force and experienced order; imagination releases copied elements from that order; association then supplies noncompulsory pathways through the liberated field.
Spatiality and temporality complete the architecture by showing that order itself is not an additional impression but the disposition or succession of content.
Mental freedom is therefore bounded twice: it cannot originate unprecedented simple contents, and its ordinary transitions remain weighted by natural associative tendencies.
The movement is recursive rather than linear: copied order is preserved, dissolved, probabilistically regenerated, and finally exposed as constitutive of the ideas of space and time.
Closure occurs through paired limits: conception terminates in content-filled minima, while explanation terminates at experimentally established principles whose ultimate causes remain unknown.
[Persistent] Every legitimate idea must derive its elemental content from antecedent impression-material.
[Emergent] Elemental provenance and relational organization are distinct explanatory levels: identical copied materials can support preservation, recombination, association, or ordered appearance.
[Attractor] Order is the common object of the cluster: memory conserves it, imagination alters it, association regenerates it, and space and time consist in its coexistent or successive forms.
[Mutating] Difference licenses distinguishability and separability, but separation remains possible only where a positive component can be conceived apart.
[Persistent] Memory is recurrence under retained vivacity and fidelity to the experienced form, order, and position of its objects.
[Persistent] Imagination is dependent at the level of simple contents but free to separate, transpose, and recombine those contents at the level of arrangement.
[Emergent] Associative tendency mediates between compulsory connexion and random succession, producing regularity without abolishing imaginative liberty.
[Persistent] Resemblance, spatiotemporal contiguity, and cause and effect are the primary operators by which one idea introduces another.
[Mutating] Relational efficacy is graded: it propagates through intermediaries, weakens with distance, and expands causally from production to capacity and social influence.
[Emergent] Space and time are ordered manners of appearance rather than independent impressions: extension is coexistent disposition, and duration is noncoexistent succession.
[Mutating] Abstraction produces general representation by selectively regarding a determinate particular, not by generating a contentless universal.

[Attractor] An idea’s genealogy limits its legitimate application: recombination may alter conjunctions, but predication cannot properly exceed the kind of content or order supplied by the originating impression.
[Terminal] Empirical explanation may stop at a recurrent principle established through its effects even when the ultimate cause of that principle remains inaccessible.
[Terminal] Conceptual decomposition cannot terminate in nonentity: spatial minima must retain sensible quality, and temporal minima must be filled by successive existence.
The copy principle retains stable identity across the cluster, functioning first as a faculty constraint and later as a test of spatial, temporal, and predicative legitimacy.
Order mutates from a criterion of mnemonic fidelity into an object of imaginative alteration, an associative product, and finally the constitutive form of extension and duration.
Separability expands from the ground of imaginative liberty to a universal compositional premise, then reverses into a limiting test when no distinct spatial or temporal content can be isolated.
Imagination changes function from a faculty of transposition into a regulated field whose transitions are weighted by resemblance, contiguity, and causation.
Contiguity migrates from the experienced order preserved by memory into a customary associative pathway grounded in spatial and temporal arrangements.
Complex ideas divide into three generative regimes: freely rearranged fictions, associatively stabilized objects of thought, and compounds whose order constitutes extension or duration.
Causation migrates from an associative relation between ideas into a model of production, counterfactual capacity, authority, and social subordination.
Vivacity remains indispensable for establishing the memory–imagination distinction but disappears from the later explanations of associative order and spatiotemporal composition.
Connexion changes valence: memory approximates inseparable conservation, association supplies nonnecessary cohesion, and space and time remain nonseparable from some positive content.
Fiction reverses from a successful exercise of combinatorial liberty into a mark of illegitimate application when duration or spatiality is detached from every possible originating content.
[Local] The precise degree of vivacity distinguishing memory from imagination remains a faculty-specific criterion and does not govern association or spatiotemporal conception.
[Local] The claim that sight and touch alone provide extension’s source is required for spatial genealogy but does not scale into a general theory of all ideational recurrence.
[Local] The asserted exhaustiveness of resemblance, contiguity, and causation remains local to the associative taxonomy; the current level requires only nonnecessary relational regulation.
[Scaled] The copy principle scales upward because it constrains faculty content, abstract representation, spatial and temporal conception, and semantic application.
[Scaled] The distinction between content and arrangement becomes the cluster’s primary architecture, subsuming memory, imagination, association, space, and time.

[Bridge] Separability connects imaginative composition to conceptual analysis, but its cross-unit use requires distinguishing separation from an original complex from separation from every content-bearing instance.
[Catalyst] Imaginative freedom generates the problem solved by association: once ideas can combine arbitrarily, recurrent regularity demands a non-random but noncompulsory principle.
[Superseded] The binary opposition between necessary determination and pure chance is replaced by graded tendency, custom, and attenuating relational force.
[Recoded] Fiction is divided into lawful relational recombination and genealogically unsupported predication; novelty alone no longer determines illegitimacy.
[Transition] The expansion of causal association into social power demonstrates domain migration, but it does not itself govern the spatial and temporal ontology of the cluster.
No faculty, abstraction, or relational operation can originate an unprecedented simple idea independently of prior impression-material.
Copy-dependence does not entail preservation of original conjunctions, positions, or sequences.
Mental regularity is neither necessary determination nor random succession.
Order, extension, and duration are not additional simple impressions superadded to the contents they organize.
Generality cannot consist in an indeterminate or contentless universal representation.
Neither empty spatiality nor bare duration can remain positively conceivable after all sensible or successive existence is removed.
Memory cannot properly vary experienced order as freely as imagination, while imagination cannot escape impression-derived elements.
Empirical adequacy does not require speculative access to the ultimate mechanism producing associative attraction.
The system requires the falsity of any model in which the origin of an idea determines all of its possible arrangements; otherwise imagination and association collapse into mere replay.
It excludes both the passive-copy model of mind and the sovereign-creation model: the mind transforms relations without supplying its own simple materials.
It disqualifies any account that treats relations as independently given substances rather than operations, dispositions, successions, or tendencies among contents.
It rejects an ontology of empty frameworks in which space and time exist for thought independently of sensible points or successive existences.
It excludes semantic autonomy from genealogy: common language, objective occurrence, or habitual predication cannot by themselves legitimate an idea’s application.
It requires that stable mental order be explainable without necessary connexion, because necessity would destroy imaginative freedom while pure chance would destroy recurrence.
It rejects the demand that every empirically usable principle possess an independently known metaphysical substrate or ultimate cause.
The deepest unavailable object is pure order without ordered content: empty space, bare time, relation without relata, and memory without a prior arrangement are structurally inadmissible.
Sovereign mental spontaneity is absent; all available freedom is post-impressional freedom exercised through separation, recombination, and selective regard.
Necessary mental connexion is the missing force around which association is organized: gentle attraction occupies its functional place without acquiring its compulsion.
Ultimate explanatory grounding remains absent; “original qualities of human nature” marks the point where operational regularity survives without disclosed origin.
No independent tribunal verifies original order, absolute succession, or pure spatiality apart from the perceptual materials whose fidelity or arrangement is being judged.
Mental novelty consists primarily in relational transformation: copied elements remain constrained while their conjunction, sequence, emphasis, and representative function vary.
Association supplies default trajectories to a freely recombinable imagination, explaining stable complex thought without converting tendency into necessity.
Memory and associated imagination partially overlap because customary contiguity can lead imagination to reproduce the experienced sequences that memory preserves by fidelity.
Because space and time are arrangements of content, mnemonic fidelity conserves constitutive coexistence and succession rather than merely locating objects inside independent containers.
Customary association by contiguity depends on perceived spatial and temporal order: sensory succession supplies the sequence that custom converts into an imaginative transition.

Separability is conditional rather than absolute: components may be detached from original complexes, but extension cannot be detached from all sensible quality and time cannot be detached from every succession.
Fiction bifurcates into legitimate composition and illegitimate predication: an unexperienced complex can be formed lawfully, whereas duration without change exceeds its genetic basis.
Abstract space and time demonstrate how generality can arise without spontaneous simple content: imagination varies instances while retaining a recurrent disposition or succession.
The expansion of causal association into power and government shows that ideational relations can organize social complexes by converting possible action into associative proximity.
Impression-audit and effect-oriented inquiry combine into a restricted science of mind that maps sources, operations, and consequences without postulating inaccessible substrates.
The cluster produces a relational ontology in which many apparent mental objects are reclassified as organized configurations of more elementary content.
The subject becomes a differential operator rather than an origin: it retains, weakens, separates, recombines, follows tendencies, and selectively generalizes impression-derived materials.
Temporality is generated through perceptible succession, conserved through memory, routed through customary association, and rearranged through imagination without becoming an empty medium.
Novelty becomes finite and grammatical: new complexes arise through transformations of relation and order rather than through creation of new simple elements.
Epistemic legitimacy is jointly genetic and operational: an idea must possess an impression-source and must not be applied beyond the structure that source can represent.
Causal explanation acquires political reach when powers of possible production are treated as sufficient to associate authority, duty, government, and obedience.
Methodologically, the system substitutes source-tracing, compositional analysis, and observable effects for unrestricted speculation about hidden essences.
Reality is thinkable only as content-bearing order: relations may vary, weaken, or generalize, but no positive spatial, temporal, or ideational structure survives complete removal of its terms.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Impression → idea → genealogical audit → permissible operation → renewed audit forms the basic recursive loop governing both composition and application.
Impression → memory recurrence → imaginative release → associative rerouting → stable complex converts experienced order into a reproducible but nonnecessary pattern.
Difference → distinction → separation → recombination → recurrent complex → demand for association transforms a logical test into a generative mental machine.
Sensory succession → custom → associative expectation → repeated transition recursively reinforces temporal contiguity as an imaginative pathway.
Order is the principal attractor: it returns as original position, changed conjunction, associative sequence, spatial disposition, temporal succession, and abstract invariant.
Causation follows an escalation path from ideational transition to actual production, possible exertion, interpersonal influence, and institutional hierarchy.
Particular configuration → selective regard → general term → heterogeneous applications → renewed particular representation forms the abstraction loop.
Absence of a distinct impression → non-distinguishability → non-separability → reclassification as manner of appearance is the cluster’s principal eliminative loop.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Impression-field supplies simple sensible and reflective materials; no subsequent operation adds unprecedented elemental content.
Impression-material recurs as ideas differentiated by retained force and fidelity: strong ordered recurrence produces memory, diminished recurrence opens imagination.
Distinguishable components become separable; separable components become recombinable; recombination produces unexperienced complexes.
Recurrent regularity among free combinations generates the requirement for a bond weaker than necessity and stronger than chance.
Resemblance, contiguity, and causation route ideational transitions through direct and progressively attenuated relational chains.
Associative routing stabilizes simple ideas into complex objects of thought while preserving the possibility of divergent recombination.
Analysis of order reveals spatial coexistence and temporal succession as arrangements of content rather than independent receptacles.
Selective recurrence of disposition or succession permits abstract representation without generating a contentless universal.
Genealogical testing excludes empty space, bare duration, changeless time, and other applications that outrun possible originating impressions.
The machine terminates in content-filled minima and experimentally established original tendencies rather than metaphysically disclosed ultimate causes.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Impression-given content → copied elemental ideas.
Copied recurrence → differentiation by vivacity and fidelity → memory/imagination bifurcation.
Imaginative release → separation and recombination → novel but derivative complexes.
Free combination → recurrent uniformity → rejection of chance → gentle associative regulation.
Associative regulation → relational chains → causal expansion → stabilized complex thought and social power.
Analysis of relation and order → coexistence/succession distinction → reconstruction of space and time as content-arrangements.
Impression genealogy → separability test → exclusion of empty forms and unsupported predications → content-filled conceptual closure.
Ideas cease to form a homogeneous class of copies and become differentiated by force, fidelity, compositional role, associative position, and representative function.
Provenance and operation become separable dimensions: common impression-derived materials can be archived, recombined, associated, or abstractly deployed.
Order becomes a productive object rather than a passive background, spanning mnemonic conservation, imaginative transposition, associative transition, and spatiotemporal constitution.
The opposition between freedom and determination collapses into bounded liberty governed by recurrent but defeasible tendencies.
Space and time are removed from the category of independent containers and relocated within the ordered appearance of positive contents.
Fiction is reclassified by operation: recombined complexes remain conceivable, while contentless forms and genealogically unsupported applications do not.
Causation becomes a cross-domain operator connecting natural production, possible action, mental transition, and institutional authority.
Philosophical method is redrawn around impression-audit, operational decomposition, and experimentally observable effects rather than unrestricted metaphysical postulation.
[Surface] The explicit objects are memory, imagination, ideational association, extension, duration, abstraction, and the formation of complex ideas.
[Structural] The active mechanisms are copying, recurrence, vivacity loss, order preservation, separation, recombination, associative routing, abstraction, and decomposition.
[Metastrategic] Conceptual disputes are reframed as questions of source, operation, relational distance, and permissible application rather than contests among untested metaphysical entities.

[Ontological / Temporal] Reality available to thought consists of content-bearing configurations, while time emerges from perceptible noncoexistence and is preserved or rearranged through mental recurrence.

[Methodological / Performative] The system repeatedly performs its own claim by decomposing apparent unities, tracing their sources, removing unsupported additions, and reconstructing them as relational operations.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The exact-copy principle strains against abstraction, which suppresses determinate sensible peculiarities while requiring a particular sensible representative.
Universal separability of simple ideas conflicts with the insistence that spatiality cannot be separated from all sensible quality and temporality cannot be separated from every succession.
Memory’s fidelity criterion presupposes access to an original arrangement whose independent recovery the system does not explain.
Vivacity and relational fidelity can classify the same recurrence differently, yet mixed cases are not formally resolved.
Imagination is described as freely combinatorial and universally guided by association, but the strength and defeasibility of that guidance remain unquantified.
Association is treated as an original quality, while contiguity is explained through acquired custom; the relation between innate principle and acquired pathway remains unresolved.
Causation receives maximal associative force before its nature is analyzed, and its extension into duty and authority compresses normative relations into productive power.
The inference from an idea’s perceptual genealogy to the impossibility or illegitimacy of independent existence exceeds what a theory of conception alone securely establishes.
Experienced duration varies with perceptual rate, but the relation between variable experienced time and objective succession remains underdetermined.
Order mutates from a standard against which recurrence is judged into a generative operator and then into the constitutive structure of spatial and temporal ideas.
Separability mutates from a positive authorization of imaginative freedom into a negative criterion for denying independent space and time.
Relation mutates from preserved or altered conjunction into a graded force capable of producing recall, complex thought, and social hierarchy.
Fiction mutates from lawful recombination into genealogical excess when an idea is predicated where no corresponding perceptual order can occur.
Causation mutates from one associative transition among ideas into a generalized schema of actual production, latent capacity, and institutional command.
Abstraction mutates copying from literal reproduction into selective representation while retaining dependence on determinate particular content.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality appears as a field of content-filled points and events whose coexistences, successions, similarities, and productive relations generate the structures ordinarily mistaken for independent forms.
The mind is an archive-workshop-network: memory preserves routes, imagination cuts and recombines components, and association weights the available transitions.
The subject is not a sovereign producer but a switching point through which impression-derived materials acquire differential force, order, and relational direction.
Time is a pulse of distinguishable succession rather than an empty stream; memory binds its experienced sequence, while imagination and association reroute its components.
The remaining freedom is navigational: the system permits movement among copied contents and weighted relations but no escape into contentless form or absolute spontaneity.
The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if the distinction between elemental provenance and relational organization remains primary.
Reconstruction is strongest where copy-dependence, separability, nonnecessary association, and content-bearing order jointly explain bounded mental productivity.

The system remains underdetermined at its thresholds and taxonomic closures: mnemonic vivacity, the exhaustiveness of associative relations, and the limits of separation are asserted rather than fully derived.
Coherence depends on recursive sequencing: imaginative freedom must precede associative regulation, and relational analysis must precede the rejection of independent space and time.
The architecture depends on productive omission at two terminal points: the unknown origin of associative attraction and the unverified phenomenology of sensible or successive minima.

No indispensable propositional element resists reduction, but the system’s actual movement is preserved only if order is allowed to mutate from remembered relation into associative machine and spatiotemporal form.

items.text: The governing problem is how factual assent and practical reality can exceed bare conception when existence contributes no additional idea and positive conception remains bounded by perceptions.
The core thesis is that actuality is not represented by added content; belief differentiates an otherwise invariant object-idea through its forceful, steady, impression-related manner of conception.
A present impression and customary relation generate this manner by transferring vivacity to an absent, future, or otherwise merely conceived object.
The argument begins as an eliminative genealogy of existential content and becomes a reconstructive naturalistic psychology of assent, motivation, and affect.
Its movement is cumulative and recursive: ontological de-addition produces a modal theory of belief, which expands into a distributed economy of mental force.
Poetry, eloquence, passion, and madness then reverse the evidential direction by showing that apparent vivacity can imitate belief without supplying its settled authority.
Closure is operational rather than metaphysical: the system explains how ideas acquire reality-effects while withholding positive comprehension of mind-independent actuality.
The terminal correction appeals to causal provenance, steadiness, reflection, and general rules, but leaves their authority and relation to external reality incompletely grounded.
[Persistent] Positive conceptual content is restricted to impressions, ideas, and their copied or recombined perceptual materials.
[Persistent] Existence is not an additional quality, predicate, or idea but is identical with the object as conceived.
[Emergent] Bare conception, existential conception, and factual belief can preserve identical representational content while producing radically different cognitive and practical effects.
[Mutating] Belief begins as a difference in manner, becomes an intensification of force and vivacity, and terminates as a comparatively steady, impression-related, causally regulated mode.
[Persistent] Since contrary matters of fact remain conceivable, factual selection cannot arise from demonstrative necessity and must be determined by custom or association.
[Emergent] A present impression functions both as the experiential anchor of inference and as the reservoir from which vivacity is transmitted to a related idea.
[Emergent] Selective vivification gives absent and future objects present motivational efficacy without granting equivalent efficacy to every passing fiction.
[Mutating] Force and vivacity expand from a distinction between impressions and ideas into a transmissible causal currency linking belief, passion, imagination, and action.
[Emergent] Judgment, imagination, passion, and volition form a reciprocally permeable system rather than independent faculties.
[Attractor] Factuality converges on stable practical presence: an idea counts as real for the mind by persistently affecting inference, passion, and conduct without acquiring new content.
[Terminal] First-order vividness cannot authenticate itself; settled conviction requires discrimination by source, steadiness, reality-connection, reflection, and general rules.
[Attractor] Reality is retained as a regulative relation organizing assent and correction while its intrinsic extra-perceptual nature remains positively unrepresented.
Stable identity: the non-addition of existence persists unchanged from the analysis of being into the analysis of belief.

Absorption: the original question concerning the idea of existence disappears as an independent inquiry after becoming the premise that forces belief into a modal rather than representational explanation.
Functional mutation: present perception changes from the maximal positively available instance of being into the anchor and force-source of factual inference.
Escalation: force and vivacity move from taxonomic differences between perceptions to the defining mode of belief and then to a trans-domain mechanism of psychological causation.
Domain migration: custom moves from selecting one conceivable factual alternative to transmitting vivacity and thereby generating motivation, passion, and action.
Displacement: externality shifts from an intrinsically unfilled relative correlate to the “connection with reality” invoked when reflection regulates assent.
Reversal: vivacity initially explains why belief exceeds fiction, but counterfeit vivacity later demonstrates that intensity alone cannot establish genuine conviction.
Terminal transformation: the fact–fiction distinction moves from presumed content difference to scalar force difference and finally to causal pedigree, steadiness, and second-order correction.
Disappearance through absorption: conception, judgment, and reasoning cease to function as irreducible faculties once they have been recoded as modes and transitions within one conception-system.
The intrinsic nature of external objects remains a local ontological boundary; at cluster level, its scalable function is to deny any content-internal marker of actuality.
Poetry and madness remain local cases in subject matter but scale upward as indispensable stress tests of the proposed identity between belief and vivacity.
The proposition that existence adds no idea scales directly because it organizes both the boundary of ontology and the reconstruction of factual assent.
The present-impression requirement bridges conceptual genealogy and causal psychology by converting perceptual presence into a mechanism for generating belief.
The motivational dilemma catalyzes the major transition from defining belief phenomenologically to demonstrating its systemic necessity for conduct.
The simple equation of belief with occurrent intensity is superseded by a distinction between accidental vehemence and settled, source-regulated conviction.
The impression–idea taxonomy survives, but its original binary form is recoded into a graded and dynamically transmissible economy of perceptual force.
Neither existence nor belief is an additional predicate, quality, or representational component attached to an object-idea.
No intrinsic semantic mark distinguishes an actual object from the same object merely conceived.
No positive representational passage gives direct comprehension of a specifically extra-perceptual kind of being.
Matter-of-fact assent is not demonstrative necessity, and disbelief is not failure to understand the rejected proposition.
Judgment, reasoning, passion, and imagination are not causally sealed faculties governed by irreducibly different operations.
First-order intensity, imaginative completeness, and rhetorical vehemence do not independently authenticate factual belief.
Fiction and fact cannot be separated by an impermeable boundary at the level of represented content or raw vivacity.
Viable motivation can arise neither from present impressions alone nor from the indiscriminate efficacy of every passing idea.
The system excludes any ontology in which actual existence alters the intrinsic representational constitution of an object.
It excludes direct representational realism: positive knowledge cannot cross from perceptual content to the intrinsic nature of a heterogeneous external realm.
It excludes a rationalist construction of the factual world in which necessary conceptual connection determines existential truth.
It excludes faculty psychology as a final explanation: judgment cannot be an independent act that stamps truth onto completed ideas.
It excludes a sovereign rational subject insulated from custom, bodily condition, affective feedback, repetition, and rhetoric.
It excludes introspective foundationalism because the immediate felt strength of a perception cannot guarantee its own epistemic legitimacy.
The governing absence is the positively knowable essence of mind-independent actuality: it must remain thinkable as a correlate while unavailable as represented content.
The unavailable possibility is an intrinsic sign by which an idea could announce that its object exists independently.
No exact threshold separates vivid imagination, counterfeit belief, probable assent, and settled conviction.
The terminal ungrounded condition is the authority of general rules that distinguish legitimate causal vivification from accidental or pathological force.
Since existence adds no idea but belief exceeds bare conception, the surplus of factual assent must be modal and intensive rather than representational.
Perceptual closure combined with present-impression anchoring makes factual commitment a relation generated within experience rather than direct cognition of an external object’s intrinsic being.
If identical content produces different degrees of assent and action, force and steadiness must function as causal variables independent of representational composition.
The same intensification that constitutes factual assent also gives an absent object practical efficacy; epistemic commitment and motivation therefore share one mechanism.
The appeal to “connection with reality” regulates belief by reference to a term whose extra-perceptual nature the system denies it can positively comprehend.
Poetry, eloquence, and madness force belief to mutate from raw intensity into intensity qualified by causal provenance, steadiness, and resistance to reflective correction.
Customary transfer from impression to idea and passionate transfer back to the object-idea form a self-amplifying loop capable of strengthening assent beyond its initial basis.
Because fictional and factual ideas can share content, a familiar or believed component can lend force to an entire fictional network without converting the network into settled belief.

The reduction of judgment and reasoning to modes of conception, combined with the permeability of passion and imagination, yields a unified dynamics of mental force rather than a hierarchy of faculties.

Custom is accepted as the causal generator of factual assent while education is rejected as a valid ground of assent; the system therefore distinguishes psychological genesis from epistemic warrant without fully formalizing that distinction.
The system separates ontological content from actuality-effects: nothing representational is added, yet intensified conception transforms inference, passion, persistence, and conduct.
Factual warrant becomes second-order and genealogical: assent must be evaluated by how vivacity was produced and regulated, not merely by how forcefully it is felt.
Temporality becomes a force-transfer structure in which a present perception confers present efficacy upon absent and future objects.
The subject becomes a relay within circulating intensities rather than an autonomous judge: impressions, habits, passions, bodily states, and rhetoric jointly modulate assent.
Pathological and aesthetic cases are theoretically privileged because they separate apparent intensity from legitimate belief and thereby expose hidden conditions of the ordinary mechanism.
The mechanism enabling action toward absent realities simultaneously exposes judgment to capture by repetition, eloquence, temperament, and affective feedback.
The cluster produces practical realism without positive metaphysical realism: ideas can govern life as realities even though independent actuality supplies no distinct conceptual content.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Negative recursion: existence adds no content → belief cannot add content → factual difference relocates to manner → manner requires an intensive mechanism.
Generative loop: present impression → customary transition → transferred vivacity → intensified related idea → belief → action and passion.
Affective feedback loop: belief excites passion → passion vivifies its object → the vivified object increases assent → strengthened assent reinforces passion.
Fictional diffusion loop: familiar anchor → relational spread of vivacity → easier imaginative reception → affective engagement without complete judgmental assent.
Counterfeit escalation: temperament, eloquence, or bodily ferment raises ideas toward impression-like force, culminating in the possible collapse of operative truth–falsehood discrimination.
Corrective loop: excessive vividness generates error → reflection identifies accidental provenance → general rules discount local force → graded conviction is restored.

Aporetic return: correction invokes reality-connection, but positive comprehension of external reality remains unavailable, returning epistemic regulation to the boundary established by perceptual closure.

The conceptual attractor is regulated vivacity: sufficient force to make ideas cognitively and practically present, sufficient steadiness to resist fluctuation, and sufficient pedigree to distinguish them from counterfeits.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Perceptual admissibility: every positive idea must derive from perceptual materials; no extra-perceptual existential content is available.
Representational invariance: content of object O = content of O-as-existent = content of believed O; therefore factual difference cannot be compositional.
Modal generation: present impression I + customary relation R(I,O) → transfer of vivacity → steady intensified conception of O → belief.
Operational expansion: belief in O → increased presence and persistence of O → influence on passion, imagination, and action.
Recursive amplification: passion or related vivid ideas → renewed vivacity in O → strengthened assent and affective efficacy.
Counterfeit production: non-customary vivification by rhetoric, temperament, or bodily ferment → belief-like force without secure factual pedigree.
Regulatory closure: source-reflection + general rules + reality-connection → correction of apparent intensity, while external actuality remains an intrinsically unfilled correlate.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Existential-origin test → elimination of added being-content → perceptual closure → belief-surplus problem → content invariance → relocation to manner → force-and-vivacity definition → customary transfer from present impression → practical and affective expansion → counterfeit vivification → correction by provenance and general rules → unresolved appeal to reality beyond positive representation.
Being is reclassified from a detachable predicate into the nondiscriminating status of conceived presentation.
The actual–possible distinction is relocated from represented content to the force, steadiness, provenance, and practical effects of conception.
The internal–external distinction is redrawn as a problem of mediation, relational attribution, and causal anchoring rather than qualitative content.
Understanding is reclassified from a hierarchy of faculties into a single conception-system differentiated by necessity, association, intensity, and transition.
Absent and future objects are reclassified as potentially present causes of conduct when belief supplies sufficient force.
Fact, fiction, persuasion, and madness become neighboring configurations within one economy rather than categorically separate mental domains.
Epistemic reading must become genealogical and second-order, tracking the source and regulation of vivacity rather than trusting represented content or felt intensity alone.
Surface level: the system addresses existence, external objects, belief, factual assent, motivation, passion, fiction, eloquence, and madness.
Structural level: impression-copy constraints, present-perception anchoring, customary association, force transmission, affective feedback, and corrective rules compose one distributed mechanism.
Metastrategic level: metaphysical and epistemic distinctions are converted into tests of perceptual origin, modal difference, causal provenance, and susceptibility to correction.
Ontological/Temporal level: being adds no essence, while absent and future objects acquire present causal efficacy through impression-related modes of conception.

Methodological/Performative level: the system first compresses distinctions into a scalar mechanism and then uses poetry and madness to force its own refinement from simple intensity to regulated intensity.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The system oscillates between existence as the universal status of every presented perception and existence as the actuality affirmed only in belief; the same term covers conceptual presence and factual commitment.
Perceptual closure denies positive access to extra-perceptual being, yet external objects are said to occasion perceptions and “reality-connection” regulates assent.
The scalar reduction of belief is strained by vivid fiction and poetry, which may exhibit greater apparent vehemence while remaining experientially and epistemically weaker.
General rules repair the insufficiency of first-order force but lack a specified origin, authority, and mechanism capable of avoiding circular dependence on already accepted beliefs.
Habit is necessary to generate factual assent, while education demonstrates that repeated habit can produce epistemically invalid assent; causal production and warrant remain incompletely separated.
Existence mutates from the explicit object of conceptual genealogy into a zero-addition constraint governing every subsequent account of belief.
Force and vivacity mutate from marks distinguishing impressions and ideas into transferable quantities linking cognition, affect, imagination, and action.
Belief mutates from intensified conception into regulated intensification once counterfeit cases show that occurrent vividness is insufficient.
Truth and reality mutate from presumed properties of represented objects into causal and regulatory terms governing easy reception, assent, and reflective correction.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly modeled as a perceptually closed transmission machine in which impressions and ideas circulate, receive, lose, and redistribute force.
The subject is a relay and regulatory threshold within this machine, not its sovereign origin: habit, affect, bodily ferment, and reflection compete to set the force of ideas.
Time is organized around present anchors that draw absent and future objects into current causal efficacy through associative transmission.

The remaining struggle is navigational: distinguish customary and regulated reality-effects from rhetorical, passionate, poetic, or pathological counterfeits without access to an intrinsic sign of actuality.

The current-level axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the principal engine: existential non-addition → modal belief → customary vivification → practical expansion → counterfeit stress → regulatory correction.
What remains underdetermined is the exact dimensional structure of force and vivacity, the mechanism of their transfer, and the threshold separating belief from vivid imagination.
The architecture is coherent at the functional level but not metaphysically closed: it explains reality-effects more successfully than independent actuality or the warrant of correction.
Its strongest construction is the transition from representational invariance to a unified mechanism explaining assent, motivation, passion, imagination, and action.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if poetry, eloquence, and madness remain recursive tests that transform the initial scalar account rather than detachable illustrations.

The elements resistant to axiomatic reduction are the felt quality of belief, the positive nature of external actuality, and the authority of the general rules that arbitrate genuine and counterfeit force.

items.text: The central problem is how the same natural operations can generate causal belief, prejudice, fictive ontology, and the procedures by which philosophy regulates them.
Repeated conjunction, relation, and facilitated transition form a common engine whose outputs differ less by origin than by the degree to which comparison and experiment control them.

At this scale the argument becomes a genealogical-methodological reconstruction: intrinsic substance and power are displaced by collections of qualities, observable relations, customary transitions, and regulated causal projections.
Reflection does not transcend natural belief; it exposes discrepancies within it and forces a bifurcation between fictive metaphysical repair and more extensive general rules.
Resemblance and ease of transition are epistemically neutral: uncontrolled, they produce prejudice and fictive unity; experimentally opposed by difference, they isolate causal circumstances.

Philosophical correction therefore consists in recursive circumstance-analysis, widened experience, and semantic restraint rather than access to necessary connection or an independent rational faculty.
The movement is spiral and mutation-driven: custom generates an inference, discrepancy reopens it, a higher-order rule reorganizes it, and the corrective result becomes subject to renewed testing.

Closure is operational but nonterminal: metaphysical inquiry into hidden substance or power ceases, while empirical causal judgment remains corrigible because neither custom nor circumstance-analysis admits final completion.
[Persistent] Repeated conjunction and close relation acquire cognitive efficacy by facilitating transitions among perceptions rather than by revealing intrinsic bonds among objects.
[Persistent] Neither substance nor causal power is available through mere inspection; actual causal judgment begins only from experienced relational structure.
[Mutating] Ease of mental transition produces belief when it transfers vivacity, but produces fictive identity and simplicity when its own fluency is attributed to objects.
[Persistent] Natural customary transition precedes reflection and remains active after reflective correction; philosophy can redirect but cannot abolish it.
[Mutating] Resemblance extends inference beyond identical cases, becoming prejudice when material differences are neglected and an experimental operator when resemblance is controlled by contrast.
[Emergent] Reflection works through comparison, counterinstance, and circumstance-variation; it corrects fluent apprehension by making suppressed differences operationally salient.
[Emergent] Philosophical normativity is immanent to custom: more extensive and constant regularities regulate narrower associations without invoking an extra-customary tribunal.
[Emergent] Actual causation is operationally constituted by contiguous, temporally ordered, uniform conjunction among experimentally discriminated circumstances.
[Persistent] Phenomena are compound, so causal identity must migrate from whole objects to qualities, differences, and auxiliary circumstances isolated through comparative tests.
[Mutating] Contradiction and disappointed expectation do not determine their own resolution: they can provoke fictive substrates, prejudicial persistence, or renewed experimental decomposition.

[Persistent] Evidential warrant and experienced conviction are separable because conviction varies with vivacity, transition, temporal distance, and presentation, while warrant depends on comparative regularity.
[Terminal] Corrective inquiry has no self-applying or final form: every metarule competes with prior habit, and every experiment becomes subject to renewed circumstance-analysis.
[Attractor] Legitimate explanation converges on two constraints: terms must possess assignable ideational content, and causal distinctions must survive discriminating variation.
[Attractor] Moderate scepticism suspends claims to hidden substance and power while preserving disciplined empirical inquiry into observable regularities.
[Stable Identity] Constant conjunction retains its function as the empirical condition of causal inference while remaining explicitly distinct from perceived necessary connection.

[Functional Recurrence] Facilitated transition recurs as belief-production, inferential compression, imputed identity, and imputed simplicity; its function changes with the object onto which fluency is projected.
[Mutation] Custom moves from a first-order producer of expectation and prejudice to the material from which second-order philosophical rules are constructed.
[Reversal] Resemblance changes from a source of illicit transfer into a controlled comparative instrument once difference is deliberately introduced.
[Migration] Reflective comparison migrates from exposing variation and composition in bodies to isolating causal circumstances within compound phenomena.
[Escalation] The general rule expands from a correction of prejudicial inference into a recursive methodology for causal projection, decomposition, and experimental enlargement.
[Displacement] Qualities cease to require a substantial bearer and become separable elements whose causal relevance must be experimentally determined.
[Terminal Transformation] Contradiction ceases to be evidence for an unknown substrate and becomes a demand to identify an omitted difference, scope condition, or auxiliary cause.
[Absorption] The local theory of vivacity is absorbed into the current-level distinction between psychological uptake and methodological warrant.
[Disappearance] Substance, substantial form, accident, faculty, and occult quality disappear after supplying negative cases of how unexplained transition is converted into simulated ontology.
[Lower-Layer Local] Temporal fading, historical transmission, sign generality, and passion-amplification remain local specifications of how belief-force varies.
[Lower-Layer Local] The individual comparative, proportional, and incomplete-cause rules remain local instruments; their recursive subjection to renewed variation scales upward.
[Lower-Layer Local] The specific genealogy of matter, substantial forms, accidents, and occult qualities remains a local historical diagnosis.
[Scaled] The denial of intrinsic causal legibility scales upward into a general restriction against both a priori causal ontology and metaphysical explanation by hidden powers.
[Bridge] The conflict between first-order and second-order general rules bridges the psychology of prejudice and the methodology of experimental causal judgment.
[Bridge] Smooth mental transition connects belief-formation to fictive object-construction, revealing a shared mechanism beneath epistemic and ontological error.
[Catalyst] Reflectively disclosed contradiction catalyzes the transition from passive customary association to either metaphysical repair or active experimental differentiation.
[Recoded] “Same cause” is recoded from identity of whole objects to identity of experimentally isolated operative circumstances.
[Superseded] Objective substances, intrinsic faculties, and occult agencies are superseded by relational descriptions that remain answerable to assignable ideas and observable variation.
[Current-Level Emergent] Genuine philosophy becomes the conjunction of psychological self-diagnosis, comparative experiment, and refusal of semantically empty closure.
Causal roles cannot be assigned by conceptual inspection or an a priori taxonomy of objects.
Identity, simplicity, cohesion, and causal agency cannot be grounded in an intelligible invariant substance.
No proposition possesses a belief-force invariant under temporal distance, mediation, presentation, and disposition.
Philosophical correction cannot appeal to a rational faculty independent of custom, imagination, comparison, and experience.
Ease, repetition, resemblance, and customary inseparability do not by themselves establish object identity, metaphysical dependence, or causal efficacy.
Technical vocabulary cannot acquire explanatory force through repetition, professional authority, or verbal resemblance alone.
Neither formal rules nor a decisive experiment can eliminate the need for renewed judgment and circumstance-analysis.
Reflection does not permanently suppress the customary propensity whose outputs it corrects.
Human affects, intentions, and inward agency cannot be projected into nature as explanations of external phenomena.
The system requires rationalist transparency to be false: causes, substances, and powers must not be intrinsically legible to conception.
It also excludes absolute irregularity and total kind-instability; without provisionally stable resemblances, causal uniformity and comparative projection would collapse.

Normative correction must not depend on an external tribunal, yet it must not reduce to whichever custom is psychologically strongest; the system survives only through comparative extension and constancy.
Object identity and causal identity cannot be primitively given; both must remain decomposable into qualities, relations, and operative circumstances.
Explanatory usefulness cannot legitimate an otherwise inconceivable posit; fictive reconciliation and verbal closure must remain distinguishable from explanation.
A temporally invariant, affectively insulated, and uniformly rational subject cannot be admitted because belief is produced as a variable event of force-transmission and habit.
Experimental competence cannot be exhausted by possession of explicit rules; decisive variation must remain dependent on judgment that the rules cannot independently generate.
The system is organized around the absent metaphysical interior of causation: repeated conjunction is available, but the power supposedly connecting cause and effect is not.
The unavailable possibility of a transcendent criterion gives correction its recursive form: philosophy can judge custom only through a more extensive organization of custom.
No final reconciliation between natural propensity and reflective discipline is available; their conflict is constitutive rather than temporary.
No terminal causal decomposition is admissible because every isolated circumstance can become part of a newly compounded phenomenon requiring further control.
The invariant bearer is absent on both sides of cognition: objects dissolve into related qualities, while subjects dissolve into temporally variable operations of habit, comparison, and force.
The system circles but cannot fully formalize the exact boundary between warranted generalization and prejudice; that boundary remains dependent on scope, constancy, and discriminating judgment.

Because prejudice, fictive ontology, and causal judgment arise from related customary mechanisms, causal method must be understood as a disciplined mutation of association rather than the intervention of a foreign faculty.
Resemblance has no stable epistemic valence: left unopposed, it exports vivacity and object-unity; paired with controlled difference, it isolates operative causal circumstances.
Contradiction is a methodological fork: imagination may conceal it through a substrate, preserve it through prejudice, or convert it into a test for omitted differences and auxiliary causes.
Causal uniformity functions as a regulative rule for organizing experience, not as evidence that necessary connection or productive power has become perceptible.

A methodologically warranted inference may remain psychologically faint, while an experimentally defective association may remain vivid; epistemic rank and subjective force therefore require separate assessment.
Correction is necessarily provisional because reflective metarules never erase first-order habit and experimental controls never escape renewed circumstance-analysis.

Once bodies are treated as collections of separable qualities, causal inquiry can no longer take whole substances as primitive causes; it must identify operative qualities within relational compounds.
Legitimate theoretical distinctions are constrained simultaneously by semantics and experiment: they must correspond to assignable ideas and support discriminating variations.

Moral inquiry is especially unstable because obscure variables interact with vivid signs, passions, and anthropomorphic projection, increasing both causal opacity and susceptibility to prejudicial inference.
Moderate scepticism does not terminate causal practice; it terminates the conversion of empirically useful rules into claims about hidden ontological powers.
Normativity is naturalized without being reduced to immediate habit: warranted judgment is the recursive stabilization of custom through broader comparison, counterinstance, and experimental control.
The resulting ontology is thin and relational: separable qualities enter recurring spatiotemporal conjunctions, but neither substantial bearers nor intrinsic productive powers are required.
The epistemic subject becomes a temporally variable relay among impressions, habits, comparisons, passions, and reflective rules rather than a stable faculty of rational assent.
Anomaly becomes productive only when it is prevented from hardening into fiction: disappointed expectation must trigger decomposition rather than occult supplementation.
Time is constitutive at two levels: causal order requires priority and succession, while belief-strength varies with recency, mediation, and the temporal mode of survey.
Evidence becomes two-dimensional: comparative regularity determines warrant, whereas vivacity and transitional facility determine experienced conviction and affective efficacy.
Method cannot be fully formalized because its rules generate tasks of discrimination whose decisive execution depends on non-algorithmic judgment and expanded experience.
Natural and moral phenomena occupy one causal field, but moral inquiry demands stronger safeguards because its operative circumstances are obscured by affective and imaginative participation.
Philosophical success consists not in recovering objective necessity but in keeping inference revisable, terms meaningful, and metaphysical demands from dictating fictive closure.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Repetition → custom → facilitated transition → vivified expectation → reinforced readiness for the same transition forms the basal belief loop.
Related qualities → fluent survey → imputed identity or simplicity → reflective contradiction → substance fiction → further metaphysical categories forms the ontological escalation loop.
Resemblance → first-order generalization → counterinstance → more general rule → continued competition with the first propensity forms the prejudice-correction loop.
Compound phenomenon → controlled variation → provisional circumstance-isolation → new compound description → renewed variation forms the experimental recursion.
Contradiction is the principal bifurcation point: one path proliferates fictive entities, while the other intensifies comparison and experimental differentiation.
“General rule” becomes a machine when it ceases merely to state regularity and begins selecting, condemning, and reorganizing lower-order transitions.
“Circumstance” becomes a machine when causal identity shifts from whole objects to variables that can be compared, removed, decomposed, or supplied as co-causes.
Moderate scepticism functions as an attractor that halts metaphysical proliferation without halting empirical recursion.

Apparent repetition marks phase change when customary recurrence is re-entered as an object of reflection: the same mechanism then becomes belief, error, diagnosis, or correction according to its recursive position.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Distinct qualities + repeated conjunction + close relation → facilitated transition among perceptions.
Facilitated transition + present force or fluent survey → causal expectation / imputed identity / imputed simplicity.
Temporal distance, contrary instance, analytic comparison, or changed circumstance → interrupted fluency → weakened conviction or disclosed contradiction.
Uncontrolled contradiction + retained demand for unity or agency → substance / occult quality / prejudicial persistence → simulated closure.
Controlled contradiction + counterinstance + broader comparison → second-order general rule → accidental–efficacious distinction.
Compound phenomenon + controlled resemblance and difference → operative circumstance / common quality / missing co-cause → provisional causal attribution.
Provisional attribution + renewed circumstance-analysis + enlarged experimental sphere → recursively corrected causal map.
Absence of intrinsic power + absence of final control → moderate sceptical restriction + continued empirical inquiry.
Variable vivacity and presentation → unequal psychological uptake of equally regulated conclusions → persistent gap between method and assent.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Repeated conjunction and related qualities → fluent customary transition.
Fluent transition → causal belief, resemblance-extension, and imputed object-unity.
Temporal, comparative, or experimental disruption → diminished conviction, disclosed composition, or failed expectation.
Disruption → bifurcation between fictive metaphysical repair and reflective reclassification.
Reflective reclassification → more general rules + controlled resemblance and difference → causal circumstance-isolation.
Circumstance-isolation → provisional projection → renewed experimental control → widened evidential field.
Recursive correction → rejection of hidden power and empty terminology → moderate sceptical, nonterminal closure.
Reason and error cease to belong to independent faculties; both become differently organized outputs of relation, custom, comparison, and rule-governed correction.
Ontology is divided into two registers: fictive intrinsic structure is genealogically dissolved, while observable relational structure remains available for causal practice.
Resemblance becomes a truth-neutral operator whose epistemic status depends on whether difference and counterinstance control its extension.
Contradiction is reclassified from a demand for an unseen bearer into a diagnostic opportunity for causal decomposition.
Causation becomes thinkable without intrinsic power: its legitimate content lies in regular succession, controlled comparison, and projection within tested kinds.
Evidence divides into logical-methodological warrant and psychological-affective force, dissolving the assumption that valid arguments must command proportionate conviction.
Philosophical vocabulary is judged by ideational content and experimental work rather than by systematic position or technical appearance.
Natural and moral phenomena enter a unified causal terrain, differentiated by variable opacity rather than by distinct causal architectures.
The hidden presuppositions of empirical inquiry become visible: stable kinds, discriminable circumstances, and nonbrute irregularity are required even after necessary connection is denied.
Surface level: the system addresses variations in belief, rules for judging causes, and the ancient categories of substance, form, accident, faculty, and occult quality.
Structural level: relation and repetition facilitate transitions; comparison and variation interrupt them; higher-order rules reorganize the resulting expectations and contradictions.
Metastrategic level: philosophy intervenes by redirecting custom, expanding the experimental field, and refusing fictive or verbal closure when objective connection is unavailable.

Ontological / Temporal level: reality is composed of separable qualities in temporally ordered conjunctions, while identity, conviction, and causal attribution vary with survey, succession, and experimental scope.
Methodological / Performative level: the architecture performs its thesis by repeatedly turning its own rules, categories, and conclusions into objects of further comparison and correction.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Custom supplies prejudice, causal belief, corrective metarules, and the criterion of greater regularity; the distinction between bad and good custom therefore remains immanent and incompletely secured.
The claim that causation depends wholly on constant conjunction remains strained by the additional requirements of contiguity and temporal priority.
Strict causal uniformity conflicts with contrary experience and graded probability unless every apparent exception is reassigned to an undiscovered difference or missing co-cause.
A priori causal openness coexists with dependence on stable kinds, clear experiments, and discriminable circumstances whose criteria are not fully specified.
Denial of observable necessary connection coexists with strong projection from a clear experiment, leaving the practical authority of uniformity stronger than its ontological basis.
A genealogy of substance explains why it is believed but does not alone establish its falsity; the refutation additionally depends on the absence of an assignable idea and the separability principle.
Experimentally isolated qualities risk becoming replacements for occult qualities unless their identity remains tied to reproducible comparison rather than verbal designation.
The architecture distinguishes warrant from conviction but supplies no quantitative rule connecting impression-strength, transitional facility, and resulting assent.
Resemblance mutates from spontaneous evidence into a controlled experimental variable when paired with discriminating difference.
The general rule mutates from a habitual extension that produces prejudice into a reflective metarule that regulates lower-order inference.
Contradiction mutates from a stimulus for ontological repair into an experimental demand for further differentiation.
Cause mutates from an apparently whole object into a common quality, differentiating circumstance, compound contribution, or auxiliary condition.
Sceptical cessation mutates from termination of the search for intrinsic power into the enabling boundary of continued empirical causal inquiry.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a field of separable qualities entering recurrent, contiguous, temporally ordered configurations without an observable inner power binding them.
The subject is a relay-system in which impressions, custom, imagination, comparison, passion, and reflective rules transfer, amplify, interrupt, and reorganize force.
Time is not a neutral container: causal priority, recency, gradual survey, distant comparison, and inferential mediation actively constitute both objects and beliefs.

The remaining struggle is between fluent closure and recursive differentiation; escape is not departure from custom but the controlled reopening of its products through variation, comparison, and sceptical restraint.
The global axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if facilitated transition, reflective disruption, and the bifurcation between fictive repair and experimental correction are preserved.
The architecture remains underdetermined at the points where it invokes more general rules, same kinds, clear experiments, adequate repetition, and essential circumstances.
The system is coherent at this scale as an immanent account of naturalized correction: the mechanisms generating error also supply the materials for disciplined judgment.
Its strongest architecture is the conversion of relation and custom into a branching machine capable of producing belief, prejudice, fictive ontology, and recursive causal method.
Reconstruction depends on recursive sequencing: natural transition must precede disruption, and disruption must precede either metaphysical proliferation or methodological control.
The architecture is weakest where anti-scholastic valuation, causal uniformity, and the superiority of sceptical cessation are asserted more strongly than their internal criteria determine.
Experimental sagacity and the variable force of conviction remain resistant to complete axiomatic reduction because neither decisive variation nor psychological intensity is rendered calculable.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if correction is not represented as abolishing imagination and scepticism is not represented as abolishing empirical inquiry.
