items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo necessitas Naturae, constitutio Mentis ut idea Corporis et historia affectionum corporalium generationem finium imaginatorum ac iudiciorum aestimativorum explicent.
Thesis globalis est Naturam necessario et sine fine producere, dum Mens finita res per affectiones Corporis percipit atque dispositionem propriam in rerum structuram transfert.
Argumentatio metaphysico-deductiva, physico-genetica et diagnostica progreditur a necessitate divina ad individuationem corporalem, inde ad imaginationem, memoriam et genealogiam teleologiae.
Clausura causalis attributorum et identitas ordinis idearum cum ordine rerum simul dualismum Mentis et Corporis atque causalitatem finalem excludunt.
Motus verus est recursivus: metaphysica Mentem ex Natura deducit, physica cognitionem ex Corpore constituit, deinde haec cognitio anthropocentricam metaphysicam ut projectionem corporis detegit.
Imaginatio mutatur ex nomine generali praeiudicii in mechanismum vestigiorum corporalium, quo absentia praesentantur, memoriae conectuntur et valores rebus attribuuntur.
Error non remanet mera carentia cognitionis, sed fit effectus positive generatus ex affectione, utilitate, memoria et defectu contextus causarum efficientium.
Clausura est diagnostica et praeparatoria, non beatifica: apparatus erroris restituitur, sed plena deductio cognitionis adaequatae et beatitudinis in posterum differtur.
[Persistent] Omnia ex actuosa necessitate naturae divinae consequuntur; nullus finis externus productionem Naturae antecedit.
[Persistent] Causa efficiens effectu prior est, et omnis mutatio finita per alias causas determinatur potius quam per effectum futurum.
[Persistent] Cogitatio et Extensio unam eandemque substantiam exprimunt, sed modi cuiusque attributi intra propriam seriem causaliter producuntur.
[Persistent] Mens humana non est substantia separata, sed idea Corporis actu existentis, cum quo unum idemque individuum constituit.
[Mutating] Corpus a modo Extensionis determinato in individuum dynamicum mutatur, cuius identitas in ratione motus et quietis, non in partibus permanentibus, consistit.
[Emergent] Quaelibet affectio naturam corporis affecti et afficientis involvit, sed perceptio externi constitutionem Corporis percipientis potissimum indicat.
[Mutating] Imaginatio est effectus mentalis affectionum et vestigiorum corporalium, non facultas a corpore separata nec mera imago rei externae.
[Persistent] Cognitio finita per ideas affectionum procedit atque, si earum contextum causaliter integratum non comprehendit, necessario partialis et inadaequata manet.
[Mutating] Perfectio non conformitas ad exemplar externum est, sed gradus naturae, potentiae et autonomiae causalis rei singularis.
[Emergent] Error teleologicus et aestimativus oritur cum ignorantia causarum, utilitas corporis et ordo consuetudinarius imaginationis in iudicium universale de Natura coalescunt.
[Attractor] Adaequatio requirit ideam per contextum causarum intelligi; neque convenientia externa neque praesentia imaginata sufficit.
[Emergent] Metaphysica immanens psychologiam corporis generat, quae vicissim teleologiam transcendentem ut effectum localem huius corporis explicat.
[Terminal] Nullus locus extra Naturam neque ulla perspectiva finita extra historiam proprii Corporis admittitur.
Necessitas identitatem functionalem servat, sed ab exclusione finis ad productionem attributorum, corporum, affectionum et idearum extenditur.
Deus ab obiecto polemicae contra artificem indigentem in causam immanentem et actuosam omnium serierum causalium mutatur.
Causa efficiens a criterio refutandae teleologiae migrat ad regulam causalitatis attributivae et determinationis corporum ab aliis corporibus.
Ordo bifariam codificatur: ut attributum obiectivum rebus ad commodum imaginationis dispositis negatur, sed ut connexio causalis rerum et idearum retinetur.
Imaginatio a fonte generali finium et valorum ad mechanismum corporeum praesentiae absentis, memoriae et consuetudinis specificatur.
Perfectio ab immunitate divina ab indigentia transit ad potentiam singularis rei et deinde ad capacitatem Corporis pluribus modis agendi ac patiendi.
Unio Mentis et Corporis ab identitate abstracta sub duobus attributis ad historiam concretam affectionum eiusdem individui amplificatur.
Individuum humanum, prius substantia negatum, positive restituitur ut ratio dynamica per substitutionem et variationem partium perseverans.
Ignorantia ab asylo rhetorico voluntatis divinae in statum formalem ideae affectionis sine sufficienti contextu causarum transfertur.
Beatitudo attractor directionis manet, sed postquam munus ordinandi transitum ad theoriam Mentis perfecit, ab hac clausura locali abscedit.
Gradatio perfectionis inter effectus immediate et mediate productos manet machina localis refutationis teleologiae neque structuram psychophysicam totius gregis per se ordinat.
Definitio essentiae per reciprocitatem strictam localiter tuetur distinctionem inter dependentiam a Deo et constitutionem rei, sed non fit principium dominante huius synthesis.
Vestigia in partibus fluidis mechanismum localem imaginationis praebent; gradus praesens retinet functionem geneticam, non exclusivitatem huius causae physicae.
Necessitas divina, causalitas attributiva et determinatio corporum sursum amplificantur in unam doctrinam causalitatis immanentis sine contingentia principiali.
Reductio iudiciorum ad imaginationem et doctrina affectionis coniunguntur in propositionem superiorem secundum quam perceptio externi constitutionem corporis percipientis exprimit.
Transitus a corpore ut obiecto Mentis ad individuum relationale efficit ut cognitio, memoria et identitas personalis ex eadem structura dynamica deriventur.
Negatio ordinis imaginarii non superat ordinem causalium connexionum; homonymia inferior duabus functionibus distinctis hoc gradu reordinatur.
Promissio beatitudinis transitionem ad doctrinam Mentis movet, sed eius demonstratio extra clausuram praesentis gregis manet.
Natura non agit propter fines futuros neque media ad exemplar extrinsecum disponit.
Potentia Dei non est voluntas regia quae res contingenter eligit, conservat aut destruit.
Mens et Corpus non sunt substantiae realiter separatae quarum commercium causalitatem transversam requirat.
Idea non causatur ab ideato ut modo alterius attributi; utraque expressio propriam seriem causalem servat.
Mens Corpus, externa et se ipsam non cognitione immediata ac sui causa sufficienti apprehendit.
Identitas individui non in permanentia partium, figurae, magnitudinis vel situs consistit.
Imaginatio non est per se falsitas; error ex absentia ideae quae praesentiam imaginatam corrigat constituitur.
Bonum, malum, ordo et pulchritudo non sunt naturae intrinsecae rerum quae independentem normam ontologicam exhibeant.
Falsum esse debet mundum propter hominem factum esse, quia haec positio affectionem localem in rationem universalis productionis convertit.
Falsum esse debet effectum futurum causam efficientem antecedentem regere posse, quia talis ordo causalitatem invertit.
Falsum esse debet Mentem esse spectatorem sui et mundi a Corpore independentem atque sibi immediate transparentem.
Falsum esse debet perceptionem externi consistere in similitudine figurativa rei immediate recepta.
Falsum esse debet individuum per materiam permanentem definiri, quia identitas eius variationem partium tolerat.
Falsum esse debet nomen valoris vel ordinis proprietatem realem eo ipso significare.
Falsum esse debet veritatem ideae sola comparatione externa cum obiecto constitui; aliter causalitas interna Cogitationis corrueret.
Extra Naturam nullum tribunal ontologicum manet ex quo Deus, res, perfectiones et defectus communi norma iudicentur.
Perspectiva finita sine corpore, historia affectionum et ordine causarum ontologice indisponibilis est.
Praesentia pura rei externae Mentis humanae non datur; externum tantum per affectionem Corporis apparet.
Norma finalis quae omnem varietatem rerum ad unum exemplar perfectionis redigat inadmissibilis est.
Ruptura contingens seriei causarum, sive in voluntate divina sive in motu corporis, systematis causalitatem dissolveret.
Cognitio adaequata totius contextus manet possibilitas nondum exhibita circa quam diagnosis cognitionis confusae ordinatur.
Teleologia non tantum falsa doctrina, sed effectus naturaliter generatus Mentis corporeae fit: affectio perspectivam localem praebet, imaginatio autem eam in causam rerum transformat.
Anthropocentrismus est dilatatio illegitima indicii corporalis, qua id quod constitutionem corporis humani ostendit pro natura universali obiecti accipitur.
Ignorantia causalitatis non vacuum iners est: vestigia et consuetudines affectionum seriem imaginativam efficiunt quae finem fictum loco causae absentis collocat.
Correctio cognitionis non fit per fugam e Corpore, sed per integrationem ideae affectionis in ampliorem ordinem causarum et idearum.
Affectio corporalis et idea eius non sunt eventus causaliter coniungendi, sed idem eventus sub Extensione et Cogitatione expressus.
Negatio ordinis imaginarii causalitatem obiectivam non destruit; e contrario, distinctionem inter ordinem facilitatis memorialis et ordinem necessariae connexionis instituit.
Identitas dynamica Corporis memoriam personalem sine permanentia materiae possibilitatem reddit, quia ratio individui et vestigia affectionum per substitutiones partium perseverare possunt.
Maior apertura Corporis ad affectiones bifurcationem producit: potentiam perceptivam auget, sed sine cognitione causarum materiam confusionis simul multiplicat.
Auctoritas interpretis transcendentis ex eodem apparatu nascitur quo Mens absentia imaginatur: obscuritas causalis stabilitur per concatenationes affectionum donec cognitio causarum eas dissolvat.
Realitas fit rete immanens expressionum causalium cui nullum exterior est: eadem natura sub attributis diversis exprimitur atque per modos finitos determinatur.
Subiectum humanum fit individuum distributum et historicum, cuius reflexio ex ideis affectionum Corporis relationaliter perseverantis oritur.
Error fit intelligibilis eventus naturae: imaginatio positive producitur, dum falsitas ex carentia ideae corrigentis et contextus causalis nascitur.
Temporalitas duplicatur inter necessitatem aeternam productionis et historiam finitam vestigiorum, qua praeteritum velut praesens redit et futurum velut finis causaliter retroicitur.
Quod velut finis futurus causam regere videtur reclassificatur ut effectus praesens imaginationis intra seriem causarum efficientium.
Adaequatio fit amplificatio contextus causalis, non abolitio corporis: idea localis corrigitur cum locus eius in connexione ampliori intelligitur.
Potestas interpretativa quae causas occultas voluntati divinae attribuit pendet a reproductione sociali et memoriali ignorantiae corporalis.
Methodus investigationis a quaestione finis et similitudinis ad generationem, determinationem, dispositionem corporis et ordinem causarum transfertur.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Ignorantia causae efficientis quaestionem finis generat; finis imaginatus ignorantiam nomine voluntatis tegit; haec clausura investigationem causarum impedit atque ignorantiam reprodu­cit.
Affectio externi vestigium relinquit, vestigium absentiam praesentat, memoria praesentias consuetudine conectit, utilitas autem hanc seriem in iudicia valoris stabilit.
Complexitas Corporis plures affectiones et ideas producit; inde simul crescunt potentia percipiendi et periculum confusionis, donec cognitio causarum bifurcationem dirimat.
Cognitio causarum circuitum teleologicum dissolvit, quia praesentiam imaginatam in ordinem determinationum reinserit et medium auctoritatis ex obscuritate ortae evacuat.
Immanentia est attractor principalis: Deus, attributa, corpora, ideae et iudicia ad diversas expressiones unius Naturae causaliter clausae reducuntur.
Corpus relationale est attractor medians, quia identitatem, capacitatem perceptivam, memoriam, cognitionem sui et variationem mentium eadem ratione ordinat.
Circuitus totius gregis est metaphysica necessitatis → constitutio Mentis corporeae → genesis imaginationis → diagnosis metaphysicae teleologicae → restitutio necessitatis.
Finis subit transformationem terminalem: desinit esse causa Naturae et fit indicium mechanismi imaginativi qui causam cum effectu invertit.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessitas actuosa divina → productio sine fine → exclusio artificis indigentis et contingentiae principialis.
Attributa distincta + causalitas intra attributum + idem ordo → una res sub Cogitatione et Extensione dupliciter expressa.
Ratio motus et quietis → individuum compositum → identitas per mutationem partium → Corpus humanum ut obiectum Mentis.
Occursus corporum → affectio naturam utriusque implicans → idea affectionis → externum per dispositionem proprii Corporis praesentatum.
Affectio perseverans → vestigium → praesentia rei absentis → concatenatio consuetudinaria → imaginatio et memoria.
Cognitio mediata + contextus causarum incompletus + utilitas → confusio → fines, valores et ordines imaginarii.
Iudicium corporis localis universalizatum → Natura ad commodum humanum mensurata → teleologia et imperfectio fictae.
Reintegratio in ordinem causalium connexionum → finis reclassificatus ut effectus → valor restitutus ad relationem → perfectio mensurata ex potentia rei.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessitas divina → causalitas attributiva → unitas Mentis et Corporis → individuum dynamicum → affectio → imaginatio et memoria → cognitio localis et confusa.
Ignorantia causarum → quaestio finis → praesentia imaginata → utilitas corporis → iudicium aestimativum → proiectio anthropocentrica → Natura falso ordinata.
Diagnosis projectionis → distinctio ordinis imaginarii ab ordine causali → ampliatio contextus idearum → perfectio ex natura et potentia → restitutio immanentiae.
Deus reclassificatur ab artifice voluntario in causam immanentem cuius potentia cum essentia actuosa coincidit.
Natura reclassificatur ab opere ad finem disposito in productionem necessariam sine exteriori et sine norma extrinseca.
Homo reclassificatur a substantia vel anima separata in modum finitum cuius Mens idea Corporis est.
Corpus reclassificatur ab aggregato materiali in relationem motus et quietis quae per mutationes componentium perseverat.
Perceptio reclassificatur a receptione immediata obiecti in ideam affectionis quae externum per constitutionem percipientis exhibet.
Imaginatio et memoria reclassificantur a thesauro imaginum falsarum in effectus neutros vestigiorum et consuetudinum corporis.
Ordo et valor dividuntur inter structuram causalem realem et modos imaginandi ex facilitate, utilitate atque affectione ortos.
Veritas perceptionis non amplius ex similitudine apparente, sed ex proprietatibus ideae et integratione eius in contextum causarum aestimatur.
Gradus superficiei fines Naturae, unionem Mentis et Corporis, perceptionem externorum, imaginationem, memoriam et iudicia boni vel mali tractat.
Gradus structuralis necessitatem divinam, clausuram causalem attributorum, rationem motus individui, affectiones et vestigia tamquam unum apparatum distribuit.
Gradus metastrategicus quaestionem a fine et qualitate apparente ad causas efficientes, condiciones corporales iudicii et ordinem generationis transfert.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem ut productionem immanentem, individuum ut relationem perseverantem et memoriam ut praeteritum corporaliter reactum constituit.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus primum fines ac valores extrinsecos destruit, deinde machinam corporalem quae eos producit restituit, ita critique genealogiam causaliter perficiens.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Negatio ordinis ut attributi Naturae et affirmatio identitatis ordinis idearum ac rerum cohaerent tantum si ordo imaginativus ab ordine causali stricte distinguitur.
Identitas Mentis et Corporis ut unius individui cum clausura causarum intra attributa componenda est sine commercio causali neque mera duplicatione.
Maior capacitas Corporis plura percipiendi cognitionem auget quantitative, sed adaequationem non praestat; transitus a pluralitate ad intellectum manet incompletus.
Idea affectionis naturam externi corporis involvit, sed constitutionem proprii Corporis potissimum indicat; mensura cognitionis externi inter praesentiam et inadaequationem instabilis manet.
Omnes ideae ex necessitate Naturae producuntur, sed distinctio inter adaequationem et errorem vim normativam retinere debet sine norma extrinseca.
Beatitudo motum argumenti dirigit, quamquam apparatus hic extractus tantum condiciones ontologicas et epistemicas eius ponit.
Causa finalis mutatur in effectum imaginationis et indicium ignorantiae causarum efficientium.
Corpus mutatur ab obiecto actu existente Mentis in individuum relationale cuius compositio gradus cognitionis determinat.
Idea mutatur a modo formaliter intra Cogitationem causato in registrum localem affectionum et historiae corporis.
Imaginatio mutatur a cognitione simpliciter falsa in mechanismum neutralem, cui falsitas tantum per privationem correctionis accedit.
Perfectio mutatur a conformitate ad commodum vel exemplar in potentiam rei et capacitatem eius ex propria constitutione agendi.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est machina infinita sui expressionis, cuius modi per necessarias series causarum producuntur neque ab exteriori artifice ordinantur.
Individuum est vortex relationalis motus et quietis qui materiam permutat, figuram variat et tamen rationem constitutivam conservat.
Mens est tabula activa occursuum Corporis, in qua externa simul apparent et secundum dispositionem recipientis refringuntur.
Tempus systematis aeternam necessitatem cum duratione finita coniungit: vestigia praeteritum in praesentiam revocant, dum finis imaginatus futurum in causam retrovertit.
Captatio fit per utilitatem, memoriam et ignorantiam; fuga possibilis non est exitus e Natura vel e Corpore, sed navigatio ampliorem contextum causarum restituens.
Axiomata necessitatis, identitatis Mentis et Corporis, individuationis relationalis, affectionis et imaginationis sufficiunt ad machinam principalem huius gregis restituendam.
Structura firmissima est nexus inter causalitatem immanentem, Corpus compositum et ideam affectionis, ex quo perceptio localis atque teleologia proiectiva simul derivantur.
Nondum satis determinatur quomodo cognitio affectionum in cognitionem adaequatam et beatitudinem transeat.
Explicatio imaginationis per vestigia causam sufficientem, non demonstratam causam exclusivam, praebet.
Extensio doctrinae individui ad Naturam totam indicatur, sed demonstratio huius amplificationis suspenditur.
Commissura maxime fragilis est distinctio inter ordinem imaginarium et ordinem causalem, una cum transitu a relationibus affectivis ad structuram obiectivam singularium rerum.
Restitutio verum motum servat tantum si synthesis non ut series linearis, sed ut circuitus a necessitate ad Mentem corpoream et ab ea ad criticam teleologiae legitur.
The system asks how the necessity of Nature, the constitution of Mind as the idea of Body, and the history of bodily affections explain the generation of imagined ends and evaluative judgments.

The global thesis is that Nature necessarily and without end produces, while the finite Mind perceives things through affections of the Body and transfers its own disposition into the structure of things.
The metaphysical-deductive, physical-genetic, and diagnostic argument proceeds from divine necessity to bodily individuation, thence to imagination, memory, and the genealogy of teleology.
The causal closure of attributes and the identity of the order of ideas with the order of things simultaneously exclude the dualism of Mind and Body and final causality.
The true movement is recursive: metaphysics deduces Mind from Nature, physics constitutes cognition from Body, and then this cognition exposes anthropocentric metaphysics as a projection of the body.
Imagination is transformed from a general name for prejudice into a mechanism of bodily traces by which absences are presented, memories connected, and values attributed to things.
Error does not remain a mere lack of cognition, but becomes an effect positively generated from affection, utility, memory, and the lack of a context of efficient causes.
The closure is diagnostic and preparatory, not beatific: the apparatus of error is reconstructed, but the full deduction of adequate cognition and blessedness is deferred to the future.
[Persistent] All things follow from the active necessity of the divine nature; no external end precedes the production of Nature.
[Persistent] The efficient cause is prior to the effect, and every finite change is determined by other causes rather than by a future effect.
[Persistent] Thought and Extension express one and the same substance, but the modes of each attribute are causally produced within their own series.
[Persistent] The human Mind is not a separate substance, but the idea of a Body actually existing, with which it constitutes one and the same individual.
[Mutating] The Body is transformed from a determinate mode of Extension into a dynamic individual whose identity consists in a ratio of motion and rest, not in permanent parts.
[Emergent] Every affection involves the nature of the affected and affecting body, but perception of the external chiefly indicates the constitution of the perceiving Body.
[Mutating] Imagination is the mental effect of bodily affections and traces, not a faculty separate from the body nor a mere image of the external thing.
[Persistent] Finite cognition proceeds through ideas of affections and, if it does not comprehend their causally integrated context, necessarily remains partial and inadequate.
[Mutating] Perfection is not conformity to an external model, but the degree of the nature, power, and causal autonomy of a singular thing.
[Emergent] Teleological and evaluative error arises when ignorance of causes, the utility of the body, and the customary order of imagination coalesce into a universal judgment concerning Nature.
[Attractor] Adequacy requires that an idea be understood through a context of causes; neither external correspondence nor imagined presence suffices.
[Emergent] Immanent metaphysics generates a psychology of the body, which in turn explains transcendent teleology as a local effect of this body.
[Terminal] No place outside Nature, nor any finite perspective outside the history of its own Body, is admitted.
Necessity preserves functional identity, but is extended from the exclusion of end to the production of attributes, bodies, affections, and ideas.
God is transformed from the object of polemic against a needy artificer into the immanent and active cause of all causal series.
The efficient cause migrates from a criterion for refuting teleology to a rule of attributive causality and the determination of bodies by other bodies.
Order is codified in two ways: it is denied as an objective attribute of things arranged for the convenience of imagination, but retained as the causal connection of things and ideas.
Imagination is specified from a general source of ends and values into a bodily mechanism of absent presence, memory, and custom.
Perfection passes from divine immunity from need to the power of the singular thing and then to the capacity of the Body to act and be acted upon in many ways.
The union of Mind and Body is amplified from abstract identity under two attributes to the concrete history of affections of the same individual.
The human individual, previously denied as substance, is positively reconstructed as a dynamic ratio persisting through the substitution and variation of parts.
Ignorance is transferred from a rhetorical asylum of divine will into the formal state of an idea of affection without a sufficient context of causes.
Blessedness remains an attractor of direction, but after fulfilling the function of ordering the transition to the theory of Mind, it departs from this local closure.

The gradation of perfection among immediately and mediately produced effects remains a local engine for refuting teleology and does not by itself order the psychophysical structure of the whole group.

The definition of essence through strict reciprocity locally preserves the distinction between dependence on God and the constitution of a thing, but does not become the dominant principle of this synthesis.
Traces in fluid parts provide a local mechanism of imagination; the present level retains the genetic function, not the exclusivity of this physical cause.
Divine necessity, attributive causality, and the determination of bodies are amplified upward into a single doctrine of immanent causality without principial contingency.

The reduction of judgments to imagination and the doctrine of affection are joined in the higher proposition according to which perception of the external expresses the constitution of the perceiving body.
The transition from body as object of Mind to relational individual makes cognition, memory, and personal identity derivable from the same dynamic structure.
The negation of imaginary order does not supersede the order of causal connections; lower homonymy is reordered at this level into two distinct functions.
The promise of blessedness moves the transition to the doctrine of Mind, but its demonstration remains outside the closure of the present group.
Nature does not act for future ends, nor does it arrange means toward an extrinsic model.
God's power is not a royal will that contingently chooses, preserves, or destroys things.
Mind and Body are not really separate substances whose commerce would require transverse causality.
An idea is not caused by the ideate as a mode of another attribute; each expression preserves its own causal series.
The Mind does not apprehend Body, external things, and itself by immediate cognition and through a cause sufficient in itself.
The identity of the individual does not consist in the permanence of parts, figure, magnitude, or position.
Imagination is not in itself falsity; error is constituted by the absence of an idea that corrects imagined presence.
Good, evil, order, and beauty are not intrinsic natures of things that display an independent ontological norm.
It must be false that the world was made for man, because this position converts a local affection into the rationale of universal production.
It must be false that a future effect can govern a preceding efficient cause, because such an order inverts causality.
It must be false that Mind is a spectator of itself and of the world, independent of Body and immediately transparent to itself.
It must be false that perception of the external consists in the figurative likeness of a thing immediately received.
It must be false that the individual is defined by permanent matter, because its identity tolerates variation of parts.
It must be false that a name of value or order thereby signifies a real property.
It must be false that the truth of an idea is constituted by external comparison alone with the object; otherwise the internal causality of Thought would collapse.
Outside Nature no ontological tribunal remains from which God, things, perfections, and defects may be judged by a common norm.
A finite perspective without body, history of affections, and order of causes is ontologically unavailable.
Pure presence of an external thing is not given to the human Mind; the external appears only through an affection of the Body.
A final norm that reduces all the variety of things to one model of perfection is inadmissible.
A contingent rupture in the series of causes, whether in divine will or in bodily motion, would dissolve the system's causality.
Adequate cognition of the whole context remains an as-yet unexhibited possibility around which the diagnosis of confused cognition is ordered.
Teleology becomes not merely a false doctrine, but a naturally generated effect of the embodied Mind: affection provides a local perspective, while imagination transforms it into a cause of things.
Anthropocentrism is the illegitimate expansion of a bodily indication, whereby that which shows the constitution of the human body is taken for the universal nature of the object.
Ignorance of causality is not an inert void: traces and habits of affections produce an imaginative series that places a fictitious end in the place of the absent cause.
The correction of cognition does not occur through flight from Body, but through integration of the idea of affection into a broader order of causes and ideas.
A bodily affection and its idea are not events to be causally connected, but the same event expressed under Extension and Thought.
The negation of imaginary order does not destroy objective causality; on the contrary, it establishes the distinction between the order of mnemonic facility and the order of necessary connection.
The dynamic identity of Body makes personal memory possible without permanence of matter, because the ratio of the individual and the traces of affections can persist through substitutions of parts.
The greater openness of Body to affections produces a bifurcation: it increases perceptive power, but without cognition of causes simultaneously multiplies the material of confusion.

The authority of the transcendent interpreter arises from the same apparatus by which Mind imagines absences: causal obscurity is stabilized through concatenations of affections until cognition of causes dissolves them.
Reality becomes an immanent network of causal expressions with no exterior: the same nature is expressed under diverse attributes and determined through finite modes.
The human subject becomes a distributed and historical individual, whose reflection arises from ideas of affections of the relationally persisting Body.
Error becomes an intelligible event of nature: imagination is positively produced, while falsity arises from the lack of a correcting idea and causal context.
Temporality is doubled between the eternal necessity of production and the finite history of traces, whereby the past returns as if present and the future is causally projected backward as if an end.
That which seems as if a future end to govern a cause is reclassified as a present effect of imagination within the series of efficient causes.
Adequacy becomes an amplification of causal context, not an abolition of body: a local idea is corrected when its place in a broader connection is understood.
Interpretative power that attributes hidden causes to divine will depends on the social and memorial reproduction of bodily ignorance.
The method of inquiry is transferred from the question of end and likeness to generation, determination, the disposition of the body, and the order of causes.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Ignorance of the efficient cause generates the question of end; the imagined end covers ignorance under the name of will; this closure impedes inquiry into causes and reproduces ignorance.
An affection of the external leaves a trace, the trace presents absence, memory connects presences by custom, and utility stabilizes this series into value judgments.
The complexity of Body produces more affections and ideas; thus the power of perceiving and the danger of confusion grow together, until cognition of causes resolves the bifurcation.
Cognition of causes dissolves the teleological circuit, because it reinserts imagined presence into an order of determinations and empties the medium of authority arising from obscurity.
Immanence is the principal attractor: God, attributes, bodies, ideas, and judgments are reduced to diverse expressions of one causally closed Nature.
The relational Body is an intermediate attractor, because it orders identity, perceptive capacity, memory, self-cognition, and the variation of minds according to the same ratio.
The circuit of the whole group is metaphysics of necessity → constitution of embodied Mind → genesis of imagination → diagnosis of teleological metaphysics → restoration of necessity.
End undergoes a terminal transformation: it ceases to be a cause of Nature and becomes an indication of an imaginative mechanism that inverts cause and effect.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Active divine necessity → production without end → exclusion of the needy artificer and principial contingency.
Distinct attributes + causality within the attribute + the same order → one thing expressed in two ways under Thought and Extension.
Ratio of motion and rest → composite individual → identity through change of parts → human Body as object of Mind.
Encounter of bodies → affection implicating the nature of both → idea of affection → external presented through the disposition of one's own Body.
Persisting affection → trace → presence of an absent thing → customary concatenation → imagination and memory.
Mediated cognition + incomplete context of causes + utility → confusion → imagined ends, values, and orders.
Universalized judgment of the local body → Nature measured for human convenience → fictitious teleology and imperfection.
Reintegration into the order of causal connections → end reclassified as effect → value restored to relation → perfection measured from the power of the thing.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Divine necessity → attributive causality → unity of Mind and Body → dynamic individual → affection → imagination and memory → local and confused cognition.
Ignorance of causes → question of end → imagined presence → utility of body → evaluative judgment → anthropocentric projection → falsely ordered Nature.
Diagnosis of projection → distinction of imaginary order from causal order → expansion of the context of ideas → perfection from nature and power → restoration of immanence.
God is reclassified from a voluntary artificer into an immanent cause whose power coincides with active essence.
Nature is reclassified from a work arranged toward an end into necessary production without exterior and without extrinsic norm.
Man is reclassified from a separate substance or soul into a finite mode whose Mind is the idea of Body.
Body is reclassified from a material aggregate into a relation of motion and rest that persists through changes of components.
Perception is reclassified from immediate reception of the object into an idea of affection that presents the external through the constitution of the perceiver.
Imagination and memory are reclassified from a storehouse of false images into neutral effects of bodily traces and habits.
Order and value are divided between real causal structure and modes of imagining arising from facility, utility, and affection.
The truth of perception is no longer assessed from apparent likeness, but from the properties of the idea and its integration into a context of causes.
The surface level treats the ends of Nature, the union of Mind and Body, perception of external things, imagination, memory, and judgments of good or evil.
The structural level distributes divine necessity, the causal closure of attributes, the ratio of motion of the individual, affections, and traces as one apparatus.
The metastrategic level transfers the question from end and apparent quality to efficient causes, the bodily conditions of judgment, and the order of generation.
The ontological and temporal level constitutes reality as immanent production, the individual as a persisting relation, and memory as a bodily reactivated past.
The methodological and performative level first destroys extrinsic ends and values, then reconstructs the bodily machine that produces them, thereby causally completing the critique's genealogy.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The negation of order as an attribute of Nature and the affirmation of the identity of the order of ideas and things cohere only if imaginary order is strictly distinguished from causal order.
The identity of Mind and Body as one individual must be reconciled with the closure of causes within attributes without causal commerce or mere duplication.
The greater capacity of Body to perceive more increases cognition quantitatively, but does not guarantee adequacy; the transition from plurality to understanding remains incomplete.

The idea of affection involves the nature of the external body, but chiefly indicates the constitution of one's own Body; the measure of cognition of the external remains unstable between presence and inadequacy.
All ideas are produced from the necessity of Nature, but the distinction between adequacy and error must retain normative force without an extrinsic norm.
Blessedness directs the movement of the argument, although the apparatus extracted here only lays down its ontological and epistemic conditions.
Final cause is transformed into an effect of imagination and an indication of ignorance of efficient causes.
Body is transformed from the actually existing object of Mind into a relational individual whose composition determines degrees of cognition.
Idea is transformed from a mode formally caused within Thought into a local record of the affections and history of the body.
Imagination is transformed from cognition simply false into a neutral mechanism to which falsity accrues only through the privation of correction.
Perfection is transformed from conformity to convenience or a model into the power of the thing and its capacity to act from its own constitution.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly an infinite machine of self-expression, whose modes are produced through necessary series of causes and are not ordered by an external artificer.
The individual is a relational vortex of motion and rest that exchanges matter, varies figure, and yet preserves its constitutive ratio.
Mind is an active tablet of encounters of Body, in which external things simultaneously appear and are refracted according to the disposition of the recipient.
The time of the system joins eternal necessity with finite duration: traces recall the past into presence, while the imagined end turns the future backward into a cause.
Captivity occurs through utility, memory, and ignorance; possible escape is not an exit from Nature or Body, but navigation that restores a broader context of causes.
The axioms of necessity, the identity of Mind and Body, relational individuation, affection, and imagination suffice to reconstruct the principal machine of this group.
The firmest structure is the nexus between immanent causality, composite Body, and the idea of affection, from which local perception and projective teleology are simultaneously derived.
It is not yet sufficiently determined how cognition of affections passes into adequate cognition and blessedness.
The explanation of imagination through traces provides a sufficient cause, not a demonstrated exclusive cause.
The extension of the doctrine of the individual to the whole of Nature is indicated, but the demonstration of this amplification is suspended.
The most fragile juncture is the distinction between imaginary order and causal order, together with the transition from affective relations to the objective structure of singular things.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement only if the synthesis is read not as a linear series, but as a circuit from necessity to embodied Mind and from it to the critique of teleology.

items.text: Systema quaerit quibus condicionibus Mens finita, quae extra Naturam poni non potest, cognitionem, actionem et affectus suos intra eundem ordinem necessarium intelligere possit.
Thesis globalis adæquationem facit principium commune veritatis et actionis: ideæ adæquatæ veram cognitionem atque causalitatem activam, inadæquatæ autem mutilationem et passionem constituunt.
Argumentatio diagnostica, reconstructiva et geometrica errorem, voluntatem liberam atque vitiorum moralizationem resolvit, deinde eorum loco structuram causalitatis graduatæ constituit.
Motus procedit ab affectione corporis ad communitatem rationalem, cognitionem Dei, dissolutionem facultatis liberæ, conatum actualem atque formationem affectuum.
Motus non vere linearis sed recursivus est, quia eadem realitas ideationalis successive ut perceptio, affirmatio, causalitas et variatio potentiæ redit.
Mutatio principalis cognitionis vocabula in dynamicam agentiæ transfert: adæquatio et inadæquatio desinunt solum statum epistemicum designare et gradus agendi vel patiendi fiunt.
Clausura positiva libertatem non restituit ut exemptionem a necessitate, sed ut actionem ex intellecta necessitate et causalitate magis adæquata ortam.

Clausura tamen provisionaliter aperta manet, quia principium conversionis cognitionis in potestatem datur, sed criterium practicum augmenti adæquationis et plena affectuum taxonomia nondum constituuntur.
[Persistent] Natura uno ordine necessario et eisdem legibus agit; homo, cognitio et affectus nullam regionem exceptionalem intra eam constituunt.
[Persistent] Mens finita per affectiones Corporis cognoscit, dum Mens et Corpus eandem rem sub diversis attributis exprimunt.
[Mutating] Adæquatio ex principio veritatis in principium causalitatis activæ mutatur: quod ex ideis adæquatis sequitur simul cognitio et actio est.
[Persistent] Inadæquatio ordinem positivum falsitatis non constituit, sed privationem cognitionis, partialitatem causæ et passionem exprimit.
[Persistent] Quod commune et invariabile est adæquate concipitur, atque idea rei singularis per attributum divinum essentiam Dei implicat.
[Terminal] Facultates universales voluntatis et intellectus causalitatem propriam amittunt, quia omnis idea affirmationem vel negationem intrinsecam involvit.
[Emergent] Conatus est essentia actualis rei, cui nullus terminus temporalis internus assignatur.
[Mutating] Voluntas ex facultate libera in affirmationem singularem mutatur, deinde ut conatus Mentis, Appetitus et Cupiditas dynamice redistribuitur.
[Emergent] Affectus est variatio potentiæ Corporis una cum idea eiusdem variationis, unde potentia agendi et cogitandi simul ordinantur.
[Attractor] Libertas est maior adæquatio causalis intra necessitatem, non indifferentia eligendi aut imperium voluntatis.
[Persistent] Conscientia actionis vel appetitus scientiam causarum non includit; reflexivitas sine causalitate cognita libertatem originariam non probat.
[Mutating] Tempus dividitur inter contingentiam imaginativam, durationem conatus indefinitam et necessitatem quam ratio sub specie æternitatis percipit.
Idea affectionis Corporis redit ut affectus: mediatio epistemica idem fundamentum retinet, sed nunc variationem potentiæ et statum agentiæ exprimit.
Inadæquatio ab origine falsitatis ad principium passionis migrat; privatio cognitionis fit etiam defectus causalitatis plenæ.
Adæquatio functionem mutat ab autocertitudine ideæ ad productionem actionum quarum Mens causa sufficiens est.
Affirmatio intrinseca ideæ amplificatur in affirmationem existentiæ Corporis et tandem in conatum perseverandi.
Negatio voluntatis liberæ redit cum mutatione functionis: primo errorem de iudicio dissolvit, deinde causalitatem appetitus et affectuum aperit.
Corpus ex medio cognitionis in substratum dynamicum potentiæ mutatur; quod perceptionem mediat idem variationes agendi et cogitandi sustinet.
Imaginatio non simpliciter eliminatur: ex fonte contingentiae et confusionis in operationem conatus, quæ imagines potentiæ faventes seligit, transfertur.
Cognitio Dei, initio terminus ascensus epistemici, in fundamentum tacitum naturalizationis affectuum absorbetur.
Facultates universales evanescunt postquam actus singulares explicaverunt, sed doctrina de Deo et ideis adæquatis persistit ut infrastructura sectionis affectivæ.

Doctrinæ locales de terminis transcendentalibus et tribus cognitionis generibus non integræ amplificantur; earum functio præsens est discrimen inter imaginationem confusam et adæquationem constituere.
Nexus ideæ singularis cum Deo supra gradum localem ascendit, quia immanentiam qua cognitionem et affectus legibus communibus subiici possunt constituit.
Identitas voluntatis et intellectus fit commissura inter epistemologiam et affectuum doctrinam, cum affirmatio ideæ in Appetitum et Cupiditatem extenditur.
Taxonomia Cupiditatis, Lætitiæ et Tristitiæ manet mechanismus localis; structura huius gradus est conditio causalitatis qua talis taxonomia generatur.
Distinctio causæ adæquatæ et partialis unitates coniungit, quia distinctionem veri et falsi in discrimen agendi et patiendi convertit.
Exitus ethico-politicus directionem globalem indicat, sed efficacia practica qua cognitio necessitatis affectus et civium actiones mutet nondum demonstratur.
Promissa taxonomia reliquorum affectuum ultra hunc gradum manet; hic restituitur tantum machina quæ affectus primarios producere potest.
Mens cognitionem sui, Corporis et rerum externarum immediate atque sine affectionibus datam non habet.
Falsitas non est forma positiva cogitationis, sed defectus relationis cognitivæ sufficientis.
Voluntas nec causa libera nec potentia infinita supra ideas singulares est.
Mens et Corpus causalitatem transversam inter attributa non exercent.
Homo non est imperium intra imperium, et affectus non sunt vitia contra Naturæ ordinem insurgentia.
Nulla res principium internum propriæ destructionis continet.
Bonum appetitum non antecedit ut causa externa; iudicium boni ex appetitu iam operante sequitur.
Falsum esse debet exemplar subiecti sui iuris quod ante ideas, Corpus et causas suas constitutum sit.
Falsum esse debet exemplar duorum ordinum, quorum alter veritatis et libertatis, alter erroris et necessitatis sit.
Falsum esse debet exemplar rationis vel affectus a corporeis relationibus separabilis.
Falsum esse debet exemplar normæ externæ quæ veritatem ideæ aut bonitatem appetitus ab extra constituat.
Falsum esse debet exemplar cognitionis causaliter inertis, quia differentia inter ideas adæquatas et inadæquatas differentiam inter actionem et passionem producit.
Falsum esse debet exemplar temporis imaginati ut ultimi horizontis rerum, cum necessitas æterna et duratio conatus indefinita ad diversa tempora pertineant.
Nulla regio exterior Naturæ admittitur ex qua Deus, veritas, libertas aut affectus absolute iudicentur.
Nulla origo absoluta cogitationis vel actionis, a serie causarum immunis, ontologice disponibilis est.
Libertas ut pura indifferentia impossibilis est; sola libertas admissibilis per necessitatem intellectam et causalitatem auctam transit.
Principium intrinsecum non-essendi excluditur, unde negatio, destructio et imminutio per relationes externas vel partialitatem explicandæ sunt.
Eadem differentia quæ ideam veram ab inadæquata separat actionem a passione distinguit; adæquatio epistemica fit potentia causalis.
Mediatio corporalis non tantum cognitionem finitam limitat, sed etiam campum realem potentiæ constituit in quo cognitio et affectus variantur.
Cum omnis idea affirmationem involvat et essentia actualis conatus sit, volitio fit expressio conscia perseverantiæ potius quam actus facultatis liberæ.
Quia idea singularis essentiam Dei implicat et Natura ubique iisdem legibus agit, affectus ex ipsa immanentia divina demonstrabiles fiunt.
Credulitas libertatis ex conscientia sine scientia causarum oritur; eius substitutum non est fatalis inertia, sed maior causalitas adæquata.
Imaginatio functionem duplicem et instabilem habet: contingentiam atque errorem generat, sed simul imagines potentiæ faventes conative ordinat.
Persistentia rei finitæ neque contingentia pura neque æternitas est: conatus durationem indefinitam habet, dum ratio eius necessitatem sub specie æternitatis intelligit.
Cum iudicium boni Cupiditatem sequatur sed libertas ex necessitate intellecta oriatur, normativitas fit ordinatio immanens conatus, non imperium externum appetitui oppositum.
Veritas, agentia et potentia non sunt regiones separatæ, sed tres mensuræ unius gradus expressionis causalis.
Subiectum humanum non est substantia clausum principiumque actuum, sed ratio mobilis inter causas externas, corporis affectiones et ideas plus minusve adæquatas.
Libertas augetur non minuendo necessitatem, sed augendo proportionem effectuum qui per ipsius individui naturam adæquate intelliguntur.
Systema tres temporalitates componit: successionem imaginativam contingentem, perseverantiam indefinitam singularis et necessitatem æternam ordinis divini.
Deus non est obiectum remotum contemplationis, sed conditio immanens qua singularia, cognitiones et affectus sub uno ordine intelligibiles sunt.
Interventio ethica vel politica causas, ideas et compositiones potentiæ mutare debet potius quam voluntati imperare; modus practicus huius mutationis adhuc incompletus est.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Affectio Corporis ideam generat; qualitas ideæ actionem vel passionem determinat; inde potentia Corporis et Mentis variatur atque novis affectionibus exponitur.
Fortuitus rerum occursus ideas inadæquatas producit, quæ partialem causalitatem et ulteriorem dependentiam ab ordine externo conservant.
Communitates Corporis cum aliis corporibus ideas adæquatas multiplicare possunt; ideæ adæquatæ actiones augent, unde via amplificationis rationalis aperitur.
Conatus imagines potentiæ augentis retinet et contrarias excludere conatur, ita ut imaginatio circuitum conservativum ipsius perseverantiæ efficiat.
Conscientia actionum sine cognitione causarum opinionem libertatis parit; hæc opinio causalitatem occultans eandem ignorantiam interpretativam reproducit.
Idea singularis ad Dei essentiam ascendit, necessitas divina singularitatem reordinat, et ratio eandem rem sub specie æternitatis recipit.
Attractor totius structuræ est causalitas adæquata: cognitio, actio, libertas et moderatio affectuum circa eius augmentum convergunt.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Natura una et necessaria → nullum privilegium humanum → cognitio et affectus eisdem legibus explicandi.
Corpus affectum → idea affectionis → cognitio et affectus tamquam duplex expressio unius processus.
Occursus externus fortuitus → idea inadæquata; proprietas communis invariabilis → idea adæquata.
Idea → affirmatio intrinseca → dissolutio facultatis voluntatis separatæ.
Idea adæquata → causa adæquata → actio; idea inadæquata → causa partialis → passio.
Essentia actualis → conatus → Appetitus conscius → Cupiditas → transitus potentiæ → Lætitia vel Tristitia.
Necessitas intellecta + incrementum adæquationis → maior actio → libertas immanens sine imperio voluntatis.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Ordo naturalis necessarius → affectio Corporis et idea → bifurcatio inter imaginationem inadæquatam et communitatem adæquatam → veritas vel privatio → affirmatio sine facultate libera → actio vel passio → conatus → Cupiditas et variatio potentiæ → libertas ut causalitas adæquata.
Ager cognitionis et ager agentiæ in unam tabulam graduum adæquationis causaliter connectuntur.
Subiectum reclassificatur ex centro mentali clauso in modum naturalem cuius autonomia variabilis est secundum rationem causalitatis plenæ et partialis.
Oppositio Mentis imperantis et Corporis oboedientis corruit; loco eius ponitur parallelismus expressionum eiusdem rei.
Deus reclassificatur ex obiecto externo vel imaginabili in immanentem condicionem intelligibilitatis omnium singularium.
Imaginatio dividitur inter functionem epistemice confusivam et functionem affective conservativam; ideo nec ratio est nec merus defectus iners.
Ordo valoris invertitur: bonum appetitum non causat, sed conatus res appetitas ut bonas constituit.
Oppositio simplicis temporis et æternitatis solvitur in distinctionem inter contingentiam imaginatam, durationem indefinitam et necessitatem rationalem.
Gradus superficiei ideas veras et falsas, cognitionem Dei, voluntatem, Cupiditatem, Lætitiam atque Tristitiam explicat.
Gradus structuralis affectiones Corporis, adæquationem causalitatis, parallelismum attributorum, conatum et vestigia imaginativa in unam machinam componit.
Gradus metastrategicus vocabula experientiæ communis causaliter redéfinit et moralizationem affectuum intellectione geometrica substituit.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem ut ordinem necessarium concipit, cuius singularia conatu perseverant dum imaginatio contingentiam producit.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus ipsam thesim necessitatatis efficit, quia terminos psychologicos in definitiones et consequentias causales resolvit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Cognitio Dei omnibus ideis singularibus communis dicitur, sed gradus claritatis, adæquationis et passionis inter homines inæquales manent.

Causalitas directa inter Mentem et Corpus negatur, quamvis variatio potentiæ corporalis variationem potentiæ cogitandi simul inducere dicatur; parallelismus relationem servat, mechanismum autem non ulterius explicat.
Necessitas universalis cum exhortatione ethica et directione politica coniungitur, sed transitus a cognitione necessitatis ad efficaciam practicam nondum plenus est.
Ratio rem sub specie æternitatis percipit, dum essentia actualis singularis durationem indefinitam affirmat; relatio inter hos duos modos temporalitatis non omnino explicatur.
Imaginatio simul unica falsitatis causa primi generis et instrumentum conservativum conatus est; eius status nec pure privativus nec simpliciter activus manet.
Idea affectionis in affectum mutatur ubi mediatio cognitiva variationem potentiæ Corporis simul exprimere incipit.
Inadæquatio mutatur ex privatione epistemica in causalitatem partialem et passionem.
Affirmatio intrinseca ideæ mutatur in affirmationem existentiæ, conatum, Appetitum et Cupiditatem.
Corpus mutatur ex medio cognitionis externæ in variabilem potentiam cuius transitus affectus constituunt.
Libertas mutatur ex facultate non determinata in gradum causalitatis adæquatæ intra necessitatem.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est una machina causalis quæ se sub Cogitatione et Extensione dupliciter exprimit, non duo regna inter se imperantia.
Subiectum est nodus corporeus et mentalis conatu perseverans, cuius potentia secundum affectiones et gradum adæquationis variatur.
Tempus huius machinæ triplex est: successio contingens imaginationis, duratio indefinita perseverantiæ et æternitas ordinis intellecti.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga ex necessitate, sed transitus ab occursibus externis et causalitate partiali ad ideas, relationes et actiones magis adæquatas.
Axiomata de immanentia Naturæ, mediatione corporis, adæquatione, affirmatione ideæ, conatu et affectu sufficiunt ad nucleum huius gradus restituendum.
Structura firmissima est continuatio inter distinctionem veritatis et privationis atque seriem destructionis externæ, conatus, essentiæ actualis et durationis indefinitæ.
Minus determinatum manet quomodo cognitio necessitatis adæquationem augeat, affectus moderetur et directionem socialem efficacem producat.
Restitutio doctrinis prioribus de Deo et attributis pendet, dum nexus terminalis inter rem singularem et essentiam Dei demonstratione locali incompletus manet.
Motus verus servatur si epistemologia, dissolutio voluntatis, conatus et affectus ut una machina continua leguntur, quamvis plena taxonomia affectuum reductioni adhuc resistat.
The system asks under what conditions the finite Mind, which cannot be placed outside Nature, can understand its cognition, action, and affects within the same necessary order.
The global thesis makes adequacy the common principle of truth and action: adequate ideas constitute true cognition and active causality, whereas inadequate ideas constitute mutilation and passion.
Diagnostic, reconstructive, and geometrical argumentation dissolves error, free will, and the moralization of vices, then establishes in their place a structure of graded causality.
The movement proceeds from the affection of the Body to rational commonality, knowledge of God, the dissolution of the free faculty, actual conatus, and the formation of affects.
The movement is not truly linear but recursive, because the same ideational reality returns successively as perception, affirmation, causality, and variation of power.
The principal change transfers the terms of cognition into a dynamics of agency: adequacy and inadequacy cease merely to designate an epistemic state and become degrees of acting or undergoing.
The positive closure restores freedom not as exemption from necessity, but as action arising from understood necessity and more adequate causality.

The closure nevertheless remains provisionally open, because the principle of converting cognition into power is given, but the practical criterion of increased adequacy and a full taxonomy of affects are not yet established.
[Persistent] Nature acts in one necessary order and by the same laws; the human being, cognition, and affects constitute no exceptional region within it.
[Persistent] The finite Mind knows through affections of the Body, while Mind and Body express the same thing under different attributes.
[Mutating] Adequacy changes from a principle of truth into a principle of active causality: what follows from adequate ideas is at once cognition and action.
[Persistent] Inadequacy does not constitute a positive order of falsity, but expresses a privation of cognition, partiality of cause, and passion.
[Persistent] What is common and invariable is adequately conceived, and the idea of a singular thing through a divine attribute involves the essence of God.
[Terminal] The universal faculties of will and intellect lose their proper causality, because every idea involves an intrinsic affirmation or negation.
[Emergent] Conatus is the actual essence of a thing, to which no internal temporal limit is assigned.
[Mutating] Will changes from a free faculty into singular affirmation, then is dynamically redistributed as the conatus of the Mind, Appetite, and Desire.
[Emergent] An affect is a variation of the power of the Body together with the idea of that same variation, whence the power of acting and thinking are ordered together.
[Attractor] Freedom is greater causal adequacy within necessity, not indifference of choosing or dominion of the will.
[Persistent] Consciousness of action or appetite does not include knowledge of causes; reflexivity without known causality does not prove original freedom.
[Mutating] Time is divided among imaginative contingency, the indefinite duration of conatus, and necessity which reason perceives sub specie æternitatis.
The idea of an affection of the Body returns as affect: epistemic mediation retains the same foundation, but now expresses a variation of power and a state of agency.
Inadequacy migrates from the origin of falsity to the principle of passion; privation of cognition also becomes a defect of complete causality.
Adequacy changes function from the self-certainty of the idea to the production of actions of which the Mind is the sufficient cause.
The intrinsic affirmation of the idea is amplified into affirmation of the existence of the Body and finally into the conatus of persevering.
The negation of free will returns with a change of function: first it dissolves error concerning judgment, then it opens the causality of appetite and affects.
The Body changes from a medium of cognition into the dynamic substrate of power; what mediates perception also sustains variations of acting and thinking.
Imagination is not simply eliminated: it is transferred from a source of contingency and confusion into an operation of conatus that selects images favorable to power.
Knowledge of God, initially the terminus of epistemic ascent, is absorbed into the tacit foundation of the naturalization of affects.
Universal faculties vanish after they have explained singular acts, but the doctrine of God and adequate ideas persists as the infrastructure of the affective section.

Local doctrines concerning transcendental terms and the three kinds of cognition are not expanded integrally; their present function is to establish the distinction between confused imagination and adequacy.
The nexus of the singular idea with God rises above the local level, because it establishes the immanence by which cognition and affects can be subjected to common laws.
The identity of will and intellect becomes the joint between epistemology and the doctrine of affects, when the affirmation of the idea is extended into Appetite and Desire.
The taxonomy of Desire, Joy, and Sadness remains a local mechanism; the structure of this level is the condition of causality by which such a taxonomy is generated.
The distinction between adequate and partial cause joins the units, because it converts the distinction between true and false into the difference between acting and undergoing.
The ethical-political outcome indicates the global direction, but the practical efficacy by which cognition of necessity may change affects and the actions of citizens is not yet demonstrated.
The promised taxonomy of the remaining affects remains beyond this level; here only the machine capable of producing primary affects is reconstructed.
The Mind does not possess cognition of itself, of the Body, and of external things given immediately and without affections.
Falsity is not a positive form of thought, but a defect of sufficient cognitive relation.
Will is neither a free cause nor an infinite power above singular ideas.
Mind and Body do not exercise transverse causality between attributes.
The human being is not an empire within an empire, and affects are not vices rising up against the order of Nature.
No thing contains an internal principle of its own destruction.
The good does not precede appetite as an external cause; the judgment of good follows from appetite already operating.
The model of a self-governing subject constituted prior to its ideas, Body, and causes must be false.
The model of two orders, one of truth and freedom, the other of error and necessity, must be false.
The model of reason or affect separable from bodily relations must be false.
The model of an external norm that establishes from without the truth of an idea or the goodness of appetite must be false.
The model of causally inert cognition must be false, because the difference between adequate and inadequate ideas produces the difference between action and passion.
The model of imagined time as the ultimate horizon of things must be false, since eternal necessity and the indefinite duration of conatus belong to different times.
No region external to Nature is admitted from which God, truth, freedom, or affects may be judged absolutely.
No absolute origin of thought or action, immune from the series of causes, is ontologically available.
Freedom as pure indifference is impossible; the only admissible freedom passes through understood necessity and increased causality.
An intrinsic principle of non-being is excluded, whence negation, destruction, and diminution must be explained through external relations or partiality.
The same difference that separates a true idea from an inadequate one distinguishes action from passion; epistemic adequacy becomes causal power.
Bodily mediation not only limits finite cognition, but also constitutes the real field of power in which cognition and affects vary.
Since every idea involves affirmation and actual essence is conatus, volition becomes the conscious expression of perseverance rather than an act of a free faculty.
Because the singular idea involves the essence of God and Nature acts everywhere by the same laws, affects become demonstrable from divine immanence itself.
The belief in freedom arises from consciousness without knowledge of causes; its substitute is not fatal inertia, but greater adequate causality.
Imagination has a double and unstable function: it generates contingency and error, but at the same time conatively orders images favorable to power.
The persistence of a finite thing is neither pure contingency nor eternity: conatus has indefinite duration, while reason understands its necessity sub specie æternitatis.
Since the judgment of good follows Desire but freedom arises from understood necessity, normativity becomes the immanent ordering of conatus, not an external command opposed to appetite.
Truth, agency, and power are not separate regions, but three measures of one degree of causal expression.
The human subject is not a closed substance and principle of acts, but a mobile relation among external causes, bodily affections, and more or less adequate ideas.
Freedom increases not by diminishing necessity, but by increasing the proportion of effects that are adequately understood through the nature of the individual itself.
The system composes three temporalities: contingent imaginative succession, the indefinite perseverance of the singular, and the eternal necessity of the divine order.
God is not a remote object of contemplation, but the immanent condition by which singular things, cognitions, and affects are intelligible under one order.
Ethical or political intervention must change causes, ideas, and compositions of power rather than command the will; the practical mode of this change remains incomplete.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: An affection of the Body generates an idea; the quality of the idea determines action or passion; thence the power of Body and Mind is varied and exposed to new affections.
The fortuitous encounter of things produces inadequate ideas, which preserve partial causality and further dependence on the external order.
Communities of the Body with other bodies can multiply adequate ideas; adequate ideas increase actions, whence a path of rational amplification opens.
Conatus retains images of increasing power and attempts to exclude contrary ones, so that imagination produces a conservative circuit of perseverance itself.
Consciousness of actions without knowledge of causes gives rise to the opinion of freedom; this opinion, concealing causality, reproduces the same interpretive ignorance.
The singular idea ascends to the essence of God, divine necessity reorders singularity, and reason receives the same thing sub specie æternitatis.
The attractor of the whole structure is adequate causality: cognition, action, freedom, and the moderation of affects converge around its increase.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: One necessary Nature → no human privilege → cognition and affects to be explained by the same laws.
Affected Body → idea of affection → cognition and affects as a double expression of one process.
Fortuitous external encounter → inadequate idea; invariable common property → adequate idea.
Idea → intrinsic affirmation → dissolution of the faculty of separate will.
Adequate idea → adequate cause → action; inadequate idea → partial cause → passion.
Actual essence → conatus → conscious Appetite → Desire → transition of power → Joy or Sadness.
Understood necessity + increase of adequacy → greater action → immanent freedom without dominion of the will.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessary natural order → affection of the Body and idea → bifurcation between inadequate imagination and adequate commonality → truth or privation → affirmation without free faculty → action or passion → conatus → Desire and variation of power → freedom as adequate causality.
The field of cognition and the field of agency are causally connected in one map of degrees of adequacy.
The subject is reclassified from a closed mental center into a natural mode whose autonomy is variable according to the relation of complete and partial causality.
The opposition of commanding Mind and obedient Body collapses; in its place is posited the parallelism of expressions of the same thing.
God is reclassified from an external or imaginable object into the immanent condition of the intelligibility of all singular things.
Imagination is divided between an epistemically confusing function and an affectively conservative function; therefore it is neither reason nor a mere inert defect.
The order of value is inverted: the good does not cause appetite, but conatus constitutes desired things as good.
The opposition of simple time and eternity is dissolved into the distinction among imagined contingency, indefinite duration, and rational necessity.
The surface level explains true and false ideas, knowledge of God, will, Desire, Joy, and Sadness.
The structural level composes affections of the Body, adequacy of causality, parallelism of attributes, conatus, and imaginative traces into one machine.
The metastrategic level causally redefines the terms of common experience and replaces the moralization of affects with geometrical understanding.
The ontological and temporal level conceives reality as a necessary order, whose singular things persevere by conatus while imagination produces contingency.
The methodological and performative level effectuates the thesis of necessity itself, because it resolves psychological terms into causal definitions and consequences.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Knowledge of God is said to be common to all singular ideas, but degrees of clarity, adequacy, and passion remain unequal among human beings.

Direct causality between Mind and Body is denied, although variation of bodily power is said simultaneously to induce variation of the power of thinking; parallelism preserves the relation but does not further explain the mechanism.
Universal necessity is joined with ethical exhortation and political direction, but the transition from cognition of necessity to practical efficacy is not yet complete.
Reason perceives a thing sub specie æternitatis, while the actual essence of the singular affirms indefinite duration; the relation between these two modes of temporality is not wholly explained.
Imagination is at once the sole cause of falsity of the first kind and the conservative instrument of conatus; its status remains neither purely privative nor simply active.
The idea of affection changes into affect where cognitive mediation simultaneously begins to express variation of the power of the Body.
Inadequacy changes from epistemic privation into partial causality and passion.
The intrinsic affirmation of the idea changes into affirmation of existence, conatus, Appetite, and Desire.
The Body changes from the medium of external cognition into variable power, whose transitions constitute affects.
Freedom changes from an undetermined faculty into a degree of adequate causality within necessity.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly one causal machine that expresses itself doubly under Thought and Extension, not two realms commanding one another.
The subject is a bodily and mental node persevering by conatus, whose power varies according to affections and the degree of adequacy.
The time of this machine is triple: the contingent succession of imagination, the indefinite duration of perseverance, and the eternity of the understood order.
Possible navigation is not flight from necessity, but passage from external encounters and partial causality to more adequate ideas, relations, and actions.
The axioms concerning the immanence of Nature, bodily mediation, adequacy, affirmation of the idea, conatus, and affect suffice to reconstruct the nucleus of this level.
The firmest structure is the continuity between the distinction of truth and privation and the series of external destruction, conatus, actual essence, and indefinite duration.
Less determined remains how cognition of necessity increases adequacy, moderates affects, and produces effective social direction.
Reconstruction depends on prior doctrines concerning God and attributes, while the terminal nexus between the singular thing and the essence of God remains incomplete in local demonstration.
The true movement is preserved if epistemology, the dissolution of will, conatus, and affects are read as one continuous machine, although the full taxonomy of affects still resists reduction.
