items.text: Hoc gradu quaeritur qua grammatica causalis conatus, affectiones Corporis et imagines rerum affectus privatos, relationes sociales atque actionem producant.
Cupiditas essentiam individui operantem exprimit, Laetitia et Tristitia mutationes potentiae metiuntur, atque valor obiecti ex relatione affectiva potius quam ex proprietate intrinseca nascitur.
Argumentatio genetica et diagnostica affectus compositos ex paucis legibus deducit, dum vocabula psychologica et moralia vulgaria in mechanismos causales resolvit.
Motus procedit ab associatione imaginativa et causalitate per accidens ad imitationem, reciprocitatem, rivalitatem, collectivizationem et comparationem reflexivam.
Affectus socialis fit circuitus recursivus: affectus alterius imaginatus potentiam propriam mutat, responsionem generat et condicionem affectivam alterius vicissim reordinat.
Diversitas constitutionum Corporum et mutatio corporis per fruitionem prohibent ne idem obiectum valorem vel effectum affectivum stabilem retineat.
Punctum terminale mutat criterium affectus: inadequatio imaginationis passionem constituit, idea adaequata actionem, Laetitiam activam, Animositatem et Generositatem producit.
Motus totus est cumulativus, recursivus et mutatione actus; clausura non est catalogus ultimus affectuum, sed grammatica causalis quae transitum a passionibus ad actionem tractabilem reddit.
[Persistent] Cupiditas est conatus sive essentia individui, quatenus affectione determinata ad agendum dirigitur, sive huius determinationis conscia sit sive non.
[Persistent] Laetitia et Tristitia non sunt status fixi, sed transitus ad maiorem vel minorem potentiam agendi.
[Persistent] Imago est affectio Corporis quae rem absentem, praeteritam vel futuram affective praesentem reddere potest, quamdiu existentiam eius affirmat.
[Persistent] Coaffectio, memoria, similitudo et associatio transferunt affectum inter obiecta, ita ut res causaliter neutra causa affectiva per accidens fieri possit.
[Persistent] Laetitia vel Tristitia cum idea causae externae Amorem vel Odium constituit, unde conatus conservandi, promovendi, removendi aut destruendi sequitur.
[Mutating] Idem obiectum affectus contrarios aut diversos producit secundum compositionem Corporis, tempus, memoriam et constitutionem ex fruitione mutatam.
[Mutating] Similitudo affectum alienum in observantem transfert, sed Odium, differentia essentiarum et mutatio relationis signum vel intensionem translationis invertere possunt.
[Emergent] Affectus interpersonales sunt circuitus reciproci in quibus Amor, Odium, Gloria, Vindicta et aestimatio sui per affectus imaginatos aliorum reproducuntur.
[Emergent] Attributio causae est operator directionis affectivae: causa individuata affectum intendit, distributa diluit, universalizata collectivizat.
[Emergent] Bonum et malum affectum et Cupiditatem non antecedunt, sed nomina sunt quibus res secundum desiderium, aversionem et mutationem potentiae aestimantur.
[Emergent] Trias Cupiditatis, Laetitiae et Tristitiae innumerabiles affectuum species generat, quamquam nulla taxonomia lexicalis ultimam earum clausuram praebet.
[Terminal] Passio et actio non exteriori forma sed modo cognitionis distinguuntur: idea inadequata passionem, idea adaequata actionem Mentis constituit.
[Terminal] Affectus activi ad Laetitiam et Cupiditatem pertinent; Tristitia activa excluditur, et actio rationalis in Animositatem atque Generositatem determinatur.
[Attractor] Conservatio et augmentum potentiae agendi sunt attractor communis ad quem imaginatio, desiderium, cognitio et actio diversis viis diriguntur.
Conatus identitatem stabilem retinet: initio praesentias potentiam iuvantes quaerit, deinde ut essentia Mentis et Cupiditatis explicatur.
Laetitia et Tristitia redeunt functione mutata: primo mutationes potentiae mensurant, postea discrimen terminale constituunt quo sola Laetitia ad actionem referri potest.
Imaginatio migrat a praesentificatione temporali ad propagationem interpersonalem et denique ad reflexivam aestimationem sui per imagines affectuum aliorum.
Associatio per accidens amplificatur: ex causa locali Amoris vel Odii fit principium ominis, credulitatis asymmetricae et Superstitionis.
Similitudo mutatur ab imitatione affectus in conatum reciprocitatis et comparationis, sed differentia essentiarum eius universalitatem terminat.
Amor et Odium a relationibus dyadicis in structuram triadicam rivalitatis atque circuitus reciprocos migrant, deinde in generaliorem operationem attributionis causae absorbentur.
Approbatio imaginata primo actionem ad placendum et Gloriam producit; in clausura criterium sui a favore alieno ad contemplationem adaequatam propriae potentiae dislocatur.
Conflictus amplificatur a consensu affectivo impedito ad exclusivitatem, Zelotypiam et comparationem cum aequalibus potentioribus.
Identitas affectiva obiecti opere structurali peracto evanescit: corpus variabile et reconfigurabile efficit ut valor sit eventus relationis, non possessio rei.
Spes, Metus, Zelotypia, Admiratio et similes figurae manent compositiones locales; hoc gradu valent ut probationes grammaticae generativae, non ut principia globalia separata.
Vindicta, Gratitudo et asymmetria earum sunt exitus locales reciprocitatis; sursum amplificatur forma circuitus qua responsio affectiva causam ulterioris responsionis fit.
Omen et Superstitio manent ramus particularis associationis inter Spem et Metum; structura praesentis gradus servat mechanismum causalizationis accidentalis, non omnes formas sociales superstitionis.
Memoria, imitatio et comparatio sursum amplificantur, quia affectum ex obiecto singulari in reticulum causale, interpersonalem et reflexivum distribuunt.
Antagonismus non fit axioma universale: conflictus indiget affectibus oppositis, approbatione frustrata, comparatione coercitiva aut obiecto exclusive possidendo.
Transitus ab imaginatione inadequata ad ideam adaequatam est mutatio propria huius magnitudinis: taxonomias passionum concludit easque sub distinctione actionis et passionis reordinat.
Systema negat affectum ex proprietate intrinseca obiecti aut ex sola causa efficiente eius determinari.
Systema negat praesentiam actualem rei esse condicionem necessariam efficaciae affectivae, quia memoria et imaginatio absentiam praesentificant.
Systema negat subiectum affective sui iuris, immediate sibi transparens et a causis corporalibus vel socialibus immune.
Systema negat bonum, malum et iudicium morale tribunal obiectivum a desiderio et constitutione individui independens constituere.
Systema negat consensum affectivum pacem spontaneam vel propagationem socialem responsionem uniformem necessario producere.
Systema nec affectum purum, nec stabilitatem finalem, nec clausuram lexicalem specierum affectivarum admittit.
Falsum esse oportet iudicium boni aut mali Cupiditatem causaliter antecedere; aliter tota reductio valoris ad affectum corrueret.
Falsum esse oportet causam affective efficacem semper cum causa efficiente vere cognita coincidere; imago causae potest actionem dirigere quamvis eius veritas nondum constet.
Falsum esse oportet relationem ad se ipsam immediatam esse, quia subiectum se per affectiones Corporis et affectus aliorum imaginatos cognoscit.
Falsum esse oportet relationes sociales simpliciter dyadicas aut consensum ex se pacificum esse; tertii, rivales, collecta et obiecta exclusiva structuram medientur.
Falsum esse oportet universalitatem legum affectuum uniformitatem responsionum implicare, cum una grammatica per essentias et corpora diversa exitus diversos generet.
Falsum esse oportet Tristitiam principium actionis Mentis fieri posse, quia imminutio potentiae causaliter adversatur modo activo.
Systema circa absentiam cuiuslibet loci extra causalitatem affectivam ordinatur: nullum subiectum purum affectus suos ab origine interna absoluta producit.
Indisponibile est tribunal transcendentale quod valorem rerum et rectitudinem affectuum ante motus potentiae definiat.
Impossibilis est identitas affectiva terminalis, quia corpora reconfigurantur, affectus transeunt et species eorum nullam enumerationem ultimam admittunt.
Libertas ut causa incausata ontologice inadmissibilis manet; actio possibilis est tantum ut augmentum intelligibilitatis causalis per ideam adaequatam.
Cum conjunctio imaginativa rem neutram causam per accidens faciat et imitatio affectum alienum in proprium traducat, causalitas socialis oriri potest sine causa efficienti obiecti cognita.
Attributio causae et imaginatio affectuum aliorum eandem operationem complent: affectus socialis dirigitur ad causam imaginatam, deinde ad aestimationem sui revertitur.
Affectus ad classem vel nationem universalizari potest, sed diversitas Corporum efficit ut collectivizatio sit distributio inaequalis, non identitas responsionum.
Possessio exclusiva, amor impeditus et comparatio cum aequali unam machinam rivalitatis efficiunt, in qua obiectum, rivalis et imago propriae potentiae mutuo se determinant.
Imaginatio temporalis eandem rem praesentificare potest, sed mutatio constitutionis Corporis prohibet ne praesentificatio eundem affectum restituat.
Quia affectus affirmationem et negationem selectivas regit, Cupiditas valorem constituit et vocabula vulgaria mechanismum occultant, iudicium morale fit effectus epistemico-affectivus.
Imaginata approbatio potentiam sui per Gloriam auget, sed idea adaequata criterium actionis a favore alieno ad causalitatem propriam transfert.
Amor passionem Odii dissolvere potest, sed Generositas non est simplex inversio Odii: ex alio modo causali, scilicet cognitione adaequata, procedit.
Subiectum est processus nodalis qui se per affectiones Corporis, imagines causarum et responsiones aliorum constituit, non centrum sibi immediate datum.
Obiectum affectivum est eventus relationis inter corpus, memoriam, causam imaginatam et statum potentiae; mutata relatione, eius valor mutatur vel invertitur.
Causalitas imaginata, quamvis a causalitate vera distinguenda sit, realem efficaciam habet quia intensionem, directionem et extensionem actionis affectivae ordinat.
Ordo socialis emergit ex propagatione et differentiatione affectuum: circuitus reciproci collecta constituunt, sed varietas Corporum eorum unitatem perpetuo frangit.
Tempus affectivum non est successio nuda: memoria praeteritum praesentificat, dubitatio futurum modulatur, et reconfiguratio corporis efficit ut repetitio temporalis mutationem status contineat.
Interventio efficax non imperio voluntatis nudae, sed mutatione attributionis causae, condicionum imaginatarum et constitutionis corporalis operari debet.
Ethica fit transitus immanens a captura per causas inadequatas ad actionem ex cognitione adaequata, cuius forma socialis terminalis est Generositas potius quam oboedientia passioni contrariae.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Imago potentiam iuvans → Laetitia → Cupiditas conservandi imaginem vel obiectum → ulterior praesentificatio eiusdem auxilii.
Coaffectio → memoria conjunctiva → causalitas per accidens → Amor vel Odium → nova coaffectio obiecti cum affectu iam constituto.
Amor rei similis → conatus amoris reciproci → Amor imaginatus → Gloria → intensificatio conatus placendi et recipiendi.
Odium imaginatum → Odium reciprocum → malum illatum → Vindicta → confirmatio imaginis inimici et ulterior augmentatio Odii.
Approbatio imaginata → actio ad placendum → Gloria vel Acquiescentia → Ambitio conformandi alios → nova dependentia ab approbatione.
Obiectum exclusivum → impedimentum appetitus → Zelotypia → Odium rivalis → conatus removendi impedimentum; hic conflictus attractorem triadicum format.
Imago universalis collecti affectum extendit, sed diversitas Corporum responsiones dividit; divergentia inde orta novas attributiones causae et novas collectivizationes excitat.
Idea adaequata → contemplatio propriae potentiae → Laetitia et Cupiditas activae → Fortitudo → Animositas aut Generositas; cognitio causalis fit attractor clausurae activae.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Essentia individualis sive conatus + affectio determinans → Cupiditas ad agendum.
Affectio Corporis + augmentum aut imminutio potentiae → Laetitia aut Tristitia.
Coaffectio + memoria + similitudo + praesentificatio temporalis → translatio affectus et causa per accidens.
Laetitia aut Tristitia + idea causae externae → Amor aut Odium → conservatio, promotio, remotio aut destructio.
Imago affectus rei similis → imitatio → reciprocitas → circuitus Amoris, Odii, Gloriae, Vindictae et aestimationis sui.
Exclusivitas + rivalis + comparatio + imago universalis → Zelotypia, Invidia, conflictus et collectivizatio affectuum.
Diversitas et reconfiguratio Corporis → mutatio affectus erga idem obiectum → dissolutio valoris affectivi fixi.
Idea inadequata → passio et captura causali-imaginativa; idea adaequata → actio → Laetitia et Cupiditas activae → Fortitudo.
Iteratio huius schemae per obiecta et essentias diversas → species affectuum indefinitae; reductio ad primitivas causas → intelligibilitas sine catalogo clauso.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Coaffectio corporalis → causalitas imaginativa → Amor et Odium → imitatio et reciprocitas → rivalitas et collectivizatio → variatio corporalis → dissolutio valorum fixorum → distinctio passionis et actionis → Fortitudo.
Effectus sociales → imago sui per alios → nova Laetitia vel Tristitia → nova Cupiditas → actio in alios → reconfiguratio Corporis et relationis; motus igitur spiraliter redit ad principium mutatum.
Obiecta reclassificantur a portatoribus valoris intrinseci in nodos reticuli inter potentiam, memoriam, imaginationem et attributionem causae.
Tempus reclassificatur a distantia chronologica in modum praesentificationis, dubitationis et reconfigurationis corporalis.
Socialitas reclassificatur ab aggregatione individuorum in circulationem imaginum affectivarum, cuius propagatio simul connexionem et differentiam producit.
Bonum, malum et iudicium morale transferuntur ex ordine proprietatum rerum in cartographiam desiderii et mutationum potentiae.
Subiectum reclassificatur a causa libera et interiori in conatum corporaliter ac socialiter mediatum, qui tamen per ideam adaequatam activus fieri potest.
Methodus psychologica transit a catalogo nominum ad grammaticam causalium primitivorum, quae varietatem infinitam sine clausura lexicali tractat.
In gradu superficiei definiuntur affectus singulares, relationes reciprocae, iudicia valoris, comparationes sociales atque figurae actionis rationalis.
In gradu structurali conatus, transitus potentiae, affectiones Corporis, memoria, imitatio et causalitas imaginata unam machinam recurrentem componunt.
In gradu metastrategico certamen mutatur in pugnam pro attributione causarum, approbatione, directione imaginum et condicionibus quibus Cupiditas iuvatur aut coercetur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali individuum est potentia perseverans sed reconfigurabilis, res absentes affective adsunt, et tempus per transitiones potius quam per successionem nudam operatur.
In gradu methodologico et performativo textus ipsa vocabula vulgaria dissolvendo et affectus recursive deducendo formam causalitatis quam asserit exercet.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Efficacia causae imaginatae clare demonstratur, sed criterium internum quo causa affective attributa a causa vere cognita discernatur incompletum manet.
Extensio affectus ad classes vel nationes generalizationem requirit, dum diversitas Corporum uniformitatem illius generalizationis dissolvit.
Imago causae liberae affectum intendit, quamvis tota machina affectuum ex causis necessariis deducatur; vis imaginationis libertatis explicatur, non libertas metaphysica.
Trias primitiva tractabilitatem promittit, sed varietas infinita obiectorum et essentiarum relinquit indeterminatum quantum definitiones generales de differentiis singularibus explicent.
Transitus terminalis ad actionem ab principiis cognitionis adaequatae antecedentibus pendet, quae intra hunc gregem adhibentur sed non integre refondantur.
Res causaliter neutra, associatione affectiva adiuncta, in causam per accidens Amoris, Odii aut Cupiditatis mutatur.
Similitudo quae affectum eodem signo propagat per Odium inverti potest, unde identitas relationis in contrarietatem mutatur.
Amor exclusivus, impedimento rivalis affectus, in Zelotypiam atque Odium maius quam affectus sine amore antecedente converti potest.
Fruitio quae Cupiditatem implet Corpus ita reconfigurare potest ut obiectum antea appetitum in Fastidium vel Taedium vertatur.
Mutatio ab idea inadequata ad ideam adaequatam statum affectus mutat: quod passio erat actio fit, non quia obiectum mutatur, sed quia modus causal-cognitivus mutatur.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est reticulum corporum afficientium, imaginum praesentificantium et attributionum causalium, per quod potentia augetur, minuitur et redistribuitur.
Subiectum intra hanc machinam est conatus nodalis qui se per alios et per affectiones Corporis cognoscit, sed cognitione adaequata modum activum acquirere potest.
Tempus est campus praesentificationum et mutationum irreversibilium: praeteritum affective redit, sed corpus mutatum prohibet ne idem reditus eundem statum restituat.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga a causalitate, sed transitus a captura imaginum causalium ad earum cognitionem adaequatam, cuius forma socialis est Generositas.
Axiomata de conatu, transitu potentiae, imaginatione, associatione, imitatione, causalitate affectiva et cognitione adaequata sufficiunt ad machinam principalem huius gradus restituendam.
Restitutio tamen pendet a principiis antecedentibus de imaginatione, parallelismo Mentis et Corporis, conatu et ideis adaequatis, quae hic assumuntur potius quam demonstrantur.
Structura firmissima est ubi eadem regula mutationis potentiae et ideae causae affectus privatos, circuitus sociales et distinctionem actionis a passione ordinat.
Minus determinata manent compositio affectuum contrariorum in actionem finalem, stabilitas socialis Superstitionis et mensura singularium differentiarum ex varietate infinita.
Restitutio verum motum servat, quia a causalitate imaginativa et affectibus socialibus ad variationem corporalem, criticam valoris et mutationem terminalem a passionibus ad actionem progreditur.
At this level it is asked by what causal grammar conatus, affections of the Body, and images of things produce private affects, social relations, and action.

Cupiditas expresses the operative essence of the individual, Laetitia and Tristitia measure changes of power, and the value of an object arises from affective relation rather than from intrinsic property.
Genetic and diagnostic argumentation deduces composite affects from a few laws, while resolving common psychological and moral terms into causal mechanisms.
The movement proceeds from imaginative association and causality per accidens to imitation, reciprocity, rivalry, collectivization, and reflexive comparison.
Social affect becomes a recursive circuit: the imagined affect of another modifies one's own power, generates a response, and in turn reorders the affective condition of the other.
The diversity of the constitutions of Bodies and the alteration of the body through enjoyment prevent the same object from retaining stable value or affective effect.
The terminal point changes the criterion of affect: the inadequacy of imagination constitutes passion, an adequate idea produces action, active Laetitia, Animositas, and Generositas.

The whole movement is cumulative, recursive, and transformative of action; the closure is not a final catalogue of affects, but a causal grammar that renders the transition from passions to action tractable.
[Persistent] Cupiditas is conatus, or the essence of the individual, insofar as it is directed to acting by a determinate affection, whether it is conscious of this determination or not.
[Persistent] Laetitia and Tristitia are not fixed states, but transitions to greater or lesser power of acting.
[Persistent] An image is an affection of the Body that can render an absent, past, or future thing affectively present, so long as it affirms its existence.
[Persistent] Co-affection, memory, similarity, and association transfer affect among objects, such that a causally neutral thing can become an affective cause per accidens.
[Persistent] Laetitia or Tristitia together with the idea of an external cause constitutes Amor or Odium, from which follows the conatus to preserve, promote, remove, or destroy.
[Mutating] The same object produces contrary or diverse affects according to the composition of the Body, time, memory, and constitution altered through enjoyment.
[Mutating] Similarity transfers another's affect to the observer, but Odium, difference of essences, and alteration of relation can reverse the sign or intensity of the transfer.
[Emergent] Interpersonal affects are reciprocal circuits in which Amor, Odium, Gloria, Vindicta, and self-estimation are reproduced through the imagined affects of others.
[Emergent] Attribution of cause is an operator of affective direction: an individuated cause intensifies affect, a distributed one dilutes it, a universalized one collectivizes it.
[Emergent] Good and evil do not precede affect and Cupiditas, but are names by which things are assessed according to desire, aversion, and change of power.
[Emergent] The triad of Cupiditas, Laetitia, and Tristitia generates innumerable species of affects, although no lexical taxonomy provides their final closure.
[Terminal] Passion and action are distinguished not by external form but by mode of cognition: an inadequate idea constitutes passion, an adequate idea action of the Mind.
[Terminal] Active affects pertain to Laetitia and Cupiditas; active Tristitia is excluded, and rational action is determined in Animositas and Generositas.
[Attractor] Preservation and increase of the power of acting are the common attractor toward which imagination, desire, cognition, and action are directed by diverse paths.
Conatus retains a stable identity: at first it seeks presences aiding power, then it is explained as the essence of the Mind and of Cupiditas.
Laetitia and Tristitia return with an altered function: first they measure changes of power, later they constitute the terminal distinction by which Laetitia alone can be referred to action.
Imagination migrates from temporal presentification to interpersonal propagation and finally to reflexive self-estimation through images of the affects of others.
Association per accidens is amplified: from a local cause of Amor or Odium it becomes the principle of omen, asymmetric credulity, and Superstitio.
Similarity changes from imitation of affect into a conatus of reciprocity and comparison, but the difference of essences limits its universality.
Amor and Odium migrate from dyadic relations into the triadic structure of rivalry and reciprocal circuits, then are absorbed into the more general operation of attribution of cause.
Imagined approval first produces action aimed at pleasing and Gloria; in the closure, the criterion of self is displaced from others' favor to adequate contemplation of one's own power.
Conflict is amplified from obstructed affective agreement to exclusivity, Zelotypia, and comparison with more powerful equals.
The affective identity of the object vanishes once its structural work is completed: the variable and reconfigurable body makes value an event of relation, not a possession of the thing.
Spes, Metus, Zelotypia, Admiratio, and similar figures remain local compositions; at this level they serve as tests of the generative grammar, not as separate global principles.
Vindicta, Gratitudo, and their asymmetry are local outcomes of reciprocity; upward, the form of circuit is amplified, whereby an affective response becomes the cause of a further response.

Omen and Superstitio remain a particular branch of association between Spes and Metus; the structure of the present level retains the mechanism of accidental causalization, not all social forms of superstition.
Memory, imitation, and comparison are amplified upward because they distribute affect from a singular object into a causal, interpersonal, and reflexive network.
Antagonism does not become a universal axiom: conflict requires opposed affects, frustrated approval, coercive comparison, or an exclusively possessed object.
The transition from inadequate imagination to an adequate idea is a change proper to this magnitude: it concludes taxonomies of passions and reorders them under the distinction of action and passion.
The system denies that affect is determined by an intrinsic property of the object or by its efficient cause alone.
The system denies that the actual presence of a thing is a necessary condition of affective efficacy, because memory and imagination presentify absence.
The system denies an affectively self-governing subject, immediately transparent to itself and immune from bodily or social causes.
The system denies that good, evil, and moral judgment constitute an objective tribunal independent of the desire and constitution of the individual.
The system denies that affective agreement necessarily produces spontaneous peace or that social propagation produces a uniform response.
The system admits neither pure affect, nor final stability, nor lexical closure of affective species.
It must be false that a judgment of good or evil causally precedes Cupiditas; otherwise the entire reduction of value to affect would collapse.
It must be false that an affectively efficacious cause always coincides with a truly known efficient cause; the image of a cause can direct action although its truth has not yet been established.
It must be false that the relation to oneself is immediate, because the subject knows itself through affections of the Body and imagined affects of others.
It must be false that social relations are simply dyadic or that agreement is peaceful in itself; third parties, rivals, collectives, and exclusive objects mediate the structure.
It must be false that the universality of the laws of affects implies uniformity of responses, since one grammar generates diverse outcomes through diverse essences and bodies.
It must be false that Tristitia can become a principle of action of the Mind, because diminution of power causally opposes the active mode.
The system is ordered around the absence of any place outside affective causality: no pure subject produces its affects from an absolute internal origin.
There is no available transcendental tribunal that defines the value of things and the rectitude of affects before movements of power.
A terminal affective identity is impossible, because bodies are reconfigured, affects pass, and their species admit no final enumeration.
Freedom as an uncaused cause remains ontologically inadmissible; action is possible only as an increase in causal intelligibility through an adequate idea.

Since imaginative conjunction makes a neutral thing a cause per accidens and imitation translates another's affect into one's own, social causality can arise without the object's efficient cause being known.
Attribution of cause and imagination of the affects of others complete the same operation: social affect is directed toward an imagined cause, then returns to self-estimation.
Affect can be universalized to a class or nation, but the diversity of Bodies makes collectivization an unequal distribution, not an identity of responses.
Exclusive possession, obstructed love, and comparison with an equal produce a single machine of rivalry, in which object, rival, and image of one's own power mutually determine one another.
Temporal imagination can presentify the same thing, but alteration of the constitution of the Body prevents the presentification from restoring the same affect.
Because affect governs selective affirmation and negation, Cupiditas constitutes value and common terms conceal the mechanism, moral judgment becomes an epistemic-affective effect.
Imagined approval increases self-power through Gloria, but an adequate idea transfers the criterion of action from others' favor to one's own causality.
Amor can dissolve the passion of Odium, but Generositas is not a simple inversion of Odium: it proceeds from another causal mode, namely adequate cognition.
The subject is a nodal process that constitutes itself through affections of the Body, images of causes, and responses of others, not a center immediately given to itself.
The affective object is an event of relation among body, memory, imagined cause, and state of power; when the relation changes, its value changes or is inverted.
Imagined causality, although it must be distinguished from true causality, has real efficacy because it orders the intensity, direction, and extension of affective action.
Social order emerges from the propagation and differentiation of affects: reciprocal circuits constitute collectives, but the variety of Bodies perpetually breaks their unity.
Affective time is not bare succession: memory presentifies the past, doubt modulates the future, and bodily reconfiguration makes temporal repetition contain a change of state.
Effective intervention must operate not by the command of bare will, but by changing attribution of cause, imagined conditions, and bodily constitution.
Ethics becomes the immanent transition from capture by inadequate causes to action from adequate cognition, whose terminal social form is Generositas rather than obedience to a contrary passion.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Image aiding power → Laetitia → Cupiditas to preserve the image or object → further presentification of the same aid.
Co-affection → conjunctive memory → causality per accidens → Amor or Odium → new co-affection of the object with an already constituted affect.
Amor of a similar thing → conatus for reciprocal love → imagined Amor → Gloria → intensification of the conatus to please and to be received.
Imagined Odium → reciprocal Odium → harm inflicted → Vindicta → confirmation of the image of the enemy and further increase of Odium.
Imagined approval → action aimed at pleasing → Gloria or Acquiescentia → Ambitio to conform others → new dependence on approval.
Exclusive object → obstruction of appetite → Zelotypia → Odium of the rival → conatus to remove the obstacle; this conflict forms a triadic attractor.
A universal image of the collective extends affect, but the diversity of Bodies divides responses; the divergence arising therefrom prompts new attributions of cause and new collectivizations.
Adequate idea → contemplation of one's own power → active Laetitia and Cupiditas → Fortitudo → Animositas or Generositas; causal cognition becomes the attractor of active closure.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Individual essence or conatus + determining affection → Cupiditas to act.
Affection of the Body + increase or diminution of power → Laetitia or Tristitia.
Co-affection + memory + similarity + temporal presentification → transfer of affect and cause per accidens.
Laetitia or Tristitia + idea of an external cause → Amor or Odium → preservation, promotion, removal, or destruction.
Image of the affect of a similar thing → imitation → reciprocity → circuits of Amor, Odium, Gloria, Vindicta, and self-estimation.
Exclusivity + rival + comparison + universal image → Zelotypia, Invidia, conflict, and collectivization of affects.
Diversity and reconfiguration of the Body → alteration of affect toward the same object → dissolution of fixed affective value.
Inadequate idea → passion and causal-imaginative capture; adequate idea → action → active Laetitia and Cupiditas → Fortitudo.
Iteration of this schema through diverse objects and essences → indefinite species of affects; reduction to primitive causes → intelligibility without a closed catalogue.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Bodily co-affection → imaginative causality → Amor and Odium → imitation and reciprocity → rivalry and collectivization → bodily variation → dissolution of fixed values → distinction of passion and action → Fortitudo.

Social effects → image of self through others → new Laetitia or Tristitia → new Cupiditas → action upon others → reconfiguration of Body and relation; the movement therefore returns spirally to a changed beginning.
Objects are reclassified from bearers of intrinsic value into nodes of a network among power, memory, imagination, and attribution of cause.
Time is reclassified from chronological distance into a mode of presentification, doubt, and bodily reconfiguration.
Sociality is reclassified from an aggregation of individuals into a circulation of affective images, whose propagation produces connection and difference simultaneously.
Good, evil, and moral judgment are transferred from the order of properties of things into a cartography of desire and changes of power.
The subject is reclassified from a free and interior cause into a bodily and socially mediated conatus, which nevertheless can become active through an adequate idea.
Psychological method passes from a catalogue of names to a grammar of causal primitives, which treats infinite variety without lexical closure.
At the level of the surface, singular affects, reciprocal relations, judgments of value, social comparisons, and figures of rational action are defined.
At the structural level, conatus, transitions of power, affections of the Body, memory, imitation, and imagined causality compose one recurrent machine.
At the metastrategic level, contest is transformed into a struggle over attribution of causes, approval, direction of images, and the conditions by which Cupiditas is aided or constrained.

At the ontological and temporal level, the individual is a persevering but reconfigurable power, absent things are affectively present, and time operates through transitions rather than bare succession.
At the methodological and performative level, the text itself exercises the form of causality it asserts by dissolving common terms and recursively deducing affects.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The efficacy of an imagined cause is clearly demonstrated, but the internal criterion by which an affectively attributed cause is distinguished from a truly known cause remains incomplete.
The extension of affect to classes or nations requires generalization, while the diversity of Bodies dissolves the uniformity of that generalization.
The image of a free cause intensifies affect, although the whole machine of affects is deduced from necessary causes; the force of the imagination of freedom is explained, not metaphysical freedom.
The primitive triad promises tractability, but the infinite variety of objects and essences leaves indeterminate how much general definitions explain singular differences.
The terminal transition to action depends on prior principles of adequate cognition, which are employed within this cluster but are not fully re-grounded.
A causally neutral thing, conjoined by affective association, is transformed into a cause per accidens of Amor, Odium, or Cupiditas.
Similarity that propagates affect with the same sign can be inverted through Odium, whence identity of relation is transformed into contrariety.
Exclusive Amor, affected by the obstacle of a rival, can be transformed into Zelotypia and into Odium greater than affect without preceding love.
Enjoyment that fulfills Cupiditas can so reconfigure the Body that an object previously desired turns into Fastidium or Taedium.
The change from an inadequate idea to an adequate idea changes the state of affect: what was passion becomes action, not because the object changes, but because the causal-cognitive mode changes.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a network of affecting bodies, presentifying images, and causal attributions, through which power is increased, diminished, and redistributed.
Within this machine the subject is a nodal conatus that knows itself through others and through affections of the Body, but can acquire an active mode through adequate cognition.
Time is a field of presentifications and irreversible changes: the past returns affectively, but the altered body prevents the same return from restoring the same state.
Navigation is possible not as an escape from causality, but as a transition from capture by causal images to their adequate cognition, whose social form is Generositas.
Axioms concerning conatus, transition of power, imagination, association, imitation, affective causality, and adequate cognition suffice to reconstruct the principal machine of this level.
The reconstruction nevertheless depends on prior principles concerning imagination, the parallelism of Mind and Body, conatus, and adequate ideas, which are assumed here rather than demonstrated.
The firmest structure is where the same rule of change of power and idea of cause orders private affects, social circuits, and the distinction of action from passion.
Less determined remain the composition of contrary affects into final action, the social stability of Superstitio, and the measure of singular differences arising from infinite variety.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement, because it proceeds from imaginative causality and social affects to bodily variation, critique of value, and the terminal transition from passions to action.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo pluralitas affectuum ex paucis motibus generetur et cur cognitio melioris hominem finitum a passionibus non necessario liberet.
Thesis globalis vitam affectivam constituit variationem potentiae corporis, cuius servitus ex asymmetria causarum oritur et cuius restitutio ethica per conatum immanentem incipit.
Argumentatio fit diagnostica et reconstructiva: species apparentes, fines transcendentes et imperium veritatis removet, deinde campum ut certamen potentiarum restituit.
Motus procedit a reductione nominum affectivorum ad causalitatem passionum, inde ad servitutem finiti, postremo ad compositionem rationalem potentiarum.
Progressio est cumulativa, recursiva et mutatione acta, quia affectus semel definiti redeunt ut vires certantes, normae practicae et gradus intellectionis.
Clausura non liberationem absolutam sed directionem conditionalem producit: finita potentia per rationem, commune utile et Dei cognitionem ordinatur, manente causalitate externa.
[Persistent] Lætitia et Tristitia sunt directiones fundamentales mutationis potentiae, quae postea conatum augent vel minuunt atque ordinem boni et mali affectivum sustinent.
[Persistent] Passio oritur ubi mens ideis inadæquatis determinatur et homo effectus sui causa tantum partialis est.
[Mutating] Cupiditas ex determinatione affectiva in essentiam actualem hominis et deinde in potentiam activam ex intellectione procedentem mutatur.
[Mutating] Imaginatio temporalis affectum rei absentis praesentem efficere potest, sed praesentia, propinquitas et contingentia gradum eius virium ordinant.
[Emergent] Servitus est asymmetria necessaria inter potentiam hominis finiti et causas externas, quae cupiditates passivas ultra mensuram potentiae propriae augere possunt.
[Persistent] Veritas sola affectionem positivam corporis non delet; cognitio efficax esse nequit nisi ordinem affectuum ingrediatur.
[Attractor] Affectus coercetur tantum per affectum contrarium et fortiorem, unde omnis moderatio realis fit redistributio potentiarum, non refutatio logica.
[Mutating] Bonum et malum ab institutione affectiva et praedicatis absolutis transferuntur ad duplicem ordinem: variationem potentiae et relationem certam ad intellectionem.
[Terminal] Virtus est potentia propria quatenus conatus sese conservandi ex ductu Rationis agere potest.
[Emergent] Individuum indiget rebus externis, sed convenientia positiva naturarum potest dependentiam in compositionem maioris potentiae convertere.
[Mutating] Relatio socialis affectus imitativos et conflictus generat quatenus imaginatione regitur, sed concordiam necessariam producit quatenus actio ex Ratione procedit.
[Attractor] Intellegere est criterion utilitatis certae, cuius terminus supremus est Dei cognitio tamquam summum Mentis bonum.
[Persistent] Natura agit necessitate immanenti, non causa finali; Ratio igitur non contra Naturam imperat sed intra eius causalitatem potentiam ordinat.
Lætitia et Tristitia identitatem directionalem retinent, sed ex transitionibus affectivis in indices ethicos augmentationis et diminutionis conatus amplificantur.
Cupiditas functionem mutat: primo determinatio Mentis est, deinde essentia perseverandi, tandem vector activus vel passivus secundum causam determinantem.
Idea causae externae e principio denominationis affectuum migrat in principium mensurandae servitutis, cum potentia causae potentiae hominis comparatur.
Tempus affectivum mutatur sine inversione: res absens eundem affectum genere movere potest, quamvis praesentia maiorem gradum intensitatis tribuat.
Imaginatio alterius primo familias affectuum socialium producit, deinde dissensionem passionum explicat, postremo Rationi ut contrariae formae concordiae cedit.
Vocabula moralia ab effectibus institutionis ad praedicata non absoluta et tandem ad indices intellectionis transferuntur.
Veritas ab auctoritate explicativa contra sermonem vulgarem ad vim affective condicionatam transit: recta explicatio manet necessaria, sed sola non imperat.
Virtus, prius e classe passionum exclusa, redit ut potentia activa ipsius naturae humanae.
Negatio liberi decreti in theoriam servitutis absorbetur: quod initio falsa causa imaginata erat, postea conditio finiti intra causas externas fit.
Nomina singularium affectuum opere taxonomico peracto recedunt; structura superior retinet relationes causales, non inventarium omnium compositorum.
Definitiones Amoris, Odii, Impudentiae aliorumque affectuum nominatorum manent mechanismi locales, non axiomata huius gregis.
Exclusiones Admirationis et virtutum moderatricium e numero passionum limites taxonomicos inferiores constituunt, quorum effectus globalis est distinctio passionis a potentia activa.
Differentiae locales Spei, Metus, Securitatis et Desperationis sursum amplificantur in legem generalem qua imaginatio temporalis vires distribuit.
Definitio passionis ut idea confusa mutationis corporis sursum amplificatur in theoriam servitutis tamquam causalitatis partialis.
Trias affectuum et duplex ordo boni ac mali unitates coniungunt, quia mutationes potentiae fiunt materia iudicii ethici immanentis.
Transitus maior efficitur ubi cognitio desinit esse mera veritas et fit cupiditas affectiva quae cum passionibus confligit.
Affectus sociales inferiores in structuram praesentis gradus absorbentur ut bifurcatio inter conflictum imaginativum et compositionem rationalem.
Taxonomia psychologica fit secundario codificata, quia calculus potentiarum et certamen affectivum maiorem vim explicativam obtinent.
Systema liberum decretum negat et servitutem non ut culpam voluntariam sed ut condicionem causaliter necessariam constituit.
Natura nec fines externos intendit nec appetitum humanum in causam finalem rerum convertit.
Actus, bonum et malum proprietates absolutas non continent, sed significationem ex institutione, potentia et intellectione accipiunt.
Affectus a corpore separatus non admittitur, quia omnis passio constitutionem actualem corporis affirmat.
Contradictio logica vel cognitio vera affectum non annihilat nisi ipsa contrariam vim affectivam producat.
Individuum humanum per se sufficiens excluditur, quia finitum semper a potentiis exterioribus exceditur et rebus externis indiget.
Communis humanitas, defectus vel finitas concordiam positivam non constituunt; convenientia requirit potentiam communem sub Ratione.
Liberatio neque exemptio a causis externis neque actus voluntariae sui annihilationis esse potest.
Ut systema constet, falsum esse debet exemplar Naturae artificis vel legislatoris qui fines et valores ante causalitatem distribuit.
Falsum esse debet mentem veritate instructam posse corpus et imaginationem sine productione causae affectivae gubernare.
Falsum esse debet individuum esse substantiam clausam, cuius potentia nulla re singulari superari possit.
Falsum esse debet tempus esse mensuram affective neutralem, quia memoria, exspectatio, praesentia et contingentia ipsam vim passionum distribuunt.
Falsum esse debet virtutem in negatione naturae propriae, sacrificio sui vel obedientia mandato externo fundari.
Falsum esse debet communitatem ex infirmitate communi nasci; sola convenientia positiva potentiae concordiam generare potest.
Possibilitas entis affectivi extra nexum causarum est ontologice indisponibilis, quia etiam actio rationalis intra necessitatem Naturae manet.
Systema circum absentiam conversionis instantaneae veritatis in potentiam ordinatur; scientia sine transmutatione affectiva impotens manet.
Status terminalis in quo homo ab omni passione, mutatione externa et potentia superiore liber sit non admittitur.
Absentia principalis est mechanismus plene explicatus quo cognitio vera affectum fortiorem et societatem rationalem ex hominibus passionalibus producat.
Finis transcendentis forma excluditur, quamvis Dei cognitio attractorem supremum constituat; attractio terminalis igitur causa finalis Naturae fieri non potest.
Nomina affectuum non iam species psychologicae sunt, sed coordinatae quibus relationes causales in certamine potentiarum describuntur.
Cupiditas est commissura totius gregis, quia eadem forma transit a determinatione locali ad essentiam perseverandi et ad potentiam activam intellectionis.
Quia passio affirmatio positiva corporis est et causae externae potentiam hominis superare possunt, veritas moderatrix debet fieri affectus contrarius fortior.
Res praeterita vel futura potest affectum eiusdem generis ac praesens producere, sed non necessario eiusdem gradus; identitas qualitatis et asymmetria intensitatis simul valent.
Praedicata moralia oriuntur ex consuetudine affectiva, auctoritatem absolutam amittunt et legitime retinentur tantum ut indices utilitatis atque intellectionis.
Socialitas bifurcatur: imaginatio aliorum passionem et oppositionem amplificat, sed actio ex natura rationaliter communi potentias componit.
Libertas non est decretum indeterminatum neque exemptio a Natura, sed gradus quo homo ex propria potentia intelligibili agit.
Ethica fit ars componendi affectiones contrarias, utilitates individuales et potentias communes, non tribunal quod passiones verbis condemnat.
Dei cognitio ordinem intellectionis claudit sine restitutione finalitatis, quia Deus obiectum supremum Mentis est, non finis ab artifice Naturae praestitutus.
Ontologia huius gregis relationes potentiae primarias facit: res affectiva est status corporalis cuius vis tantum comparatione causalium potentiarum determinatur.
Subiectum non est auctor clausus sed locus causalitatis partialis, qui tamen conatu actuali propriam perseverantiam ordinare potest.
Cognitio statum causaliter performativum obtinet: vera esse non sufficit, nisi ipsa in distributione virium affectivarum operetur.
Tempus fit campus intensitatum affectivarum, in quo praesentia imaginata, memoria, exspectatio et contingentia efficaciam causaliter variant.
Ethica transit ab aestimatione actuum ad ordinationem potentiae, cuius criterium est quid conatum, intellectionem et compositionem naturarum augeat.
Politica implicita concordiam rationalem ut amplificationem potentiae singularis concipit, non ut suppressionem conatus individui.
Libertas fit variabilis gradus causalitatis adæquatae: homo liberior est quatenus ex eo quod intelligit agit.
Methodus vocabula recepta non simpliciter abolere sed ab ontologia vulgari ad functiones causales et practicas transferre debet.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Mutatio corporis ideam affectivam producit, affectus cupiditatem determinat, iudicium boni directionem cupiditatis format, actio autem novam corporis constitutionem efficit.
Causa externa passionem auget, passio potentiam propriam minuit, et potentia imminuta facilius ulterioribus causis externis superatur.
Institutio iudicium sociale affectibus coniungit, imaginatum iudicium Pudorem vel Gloriam producit, et affectus sic productus vim institutionis recreat.
Suavitas praesens affectum futuri coercet, inde ratio minus sequitur, et opinio vel libido praesentem vim denuo amplificat.
Circuitus moderationis incipit cum affectus contrarius producitur, maiorem vim acquirit et existentiam affectus prioris excludit.
Conatus est attractor immanens: perseverantia potentiam definit, Lætitia eam auget, et virtus formam rationalem eiusdem conatus exprimit.
Convenientia rationalis potentias componit, compositio commune utile auget, et utilitas communis ulteriorem concordiam rationis confirmat.
Intellegere est attractor ascensionalis qui utile certum ordinat et in Dei cognitione terminum supremum invenit.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessitas Naturae sine fine causas finales excludit atque perfectionem et valorem absolutum in relationes comparativas convertit.
Mutatio potentiae corporis per ideam affirmatur et, ubi idea confusa est, formam passionis accipit.
Lætitia, Tristitia et Cupiditas motus primarios praebent, dum nomina plurima ex relationibus additis generantur.
Causa imaginata, tempus et relatio socialis motum primarium determinant atque affectus denominatos producunt.
Finitas hominis et excessus causae externae passionem in servitutem structuralem amplificant.
Moderatio requirit ut cognitio fiat affectus contrarius maioris potentiae, non mera correctio propositionis falsae.
Conatus servitutem non delet sed principium restitutionis praebet, cum virtus et Ratio potentiam propriam ordinant.
Ratio convenientiam naturarum componit et motum ad commune utile atque Dei cognitionem dirigit.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Pluralitas affectuum nominalis → reductio ad variationes potentiae → modulatio per causam, tempus et societatem → dissolutio finalitatis et valorum absolutorum → finitas causalis et servitus → affectivizatio cognitionis → conatus ut virtus → compositio rationalis utilitatum → Dei cognitio ut attractor terminalis.
Psychologia affectuum reordinatur ex inventario specierum in tabulam motuum relationalium potentiae.
Moralia praedicata reclassificantur ut relationes practicae utilitatis, impedimenti, Lætitiae et Tristitiae.
Oppositio veri et falsi desinit sufficere ad vitam affectivam, quia efficacia cognitionis a vi causali distinguitur.
Tempora chronologica fiunt gradus praesentiae affectivae, quibus res absens vim praesentem vel imminutam accipit.
Agentia transfertur a subiecto libero ad conatum finitum, cuius virtus est potentia immanens agendi.
Ager socialis mutatur ex scena iudicii et aemulationis in problema compositionis, ubi alter homo rationalis fit res singularis utilissima.
Utilitas propria et commune utile desinunt esse opposita, quia concordia potest potentiam individui amplificare.
Lectio vocabularii affectivi debet functiones mutantes investigare, quia eadem verba ab usu vulgari ad calculum immanentem transferuntur.
In gradu superficiei agitur de nominibus affectuum, homine meliora cognoscente sed passionibus obnoxio, et dictaminibus Rationis de utilitate ac virtute.
In gradu structurali omnia ordinantur per mutationes corporis, causalitatem partialem, proportionem potentiarum et convenientiam vel contrarietatem naturarum.
In gradu metastrategico moderatio transit a vocabulario morali et cognitione recta ad productionem affectus contrarii atque compositionem utilitatum.
In gradu ontologico et temporali Natura necessario agit, subiectum est conatus corporalis finitus, et tempus efficaciam imaginativam variat.
In gradu methodologico et performativo textus ipse reductionem, exclusionem et mutationem terminorum peragit, atque diagnosis impotentiae in reconstructionem ethicam convertitur.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reductio ad tres affectus primitivos cum multitudine compositorum sine nomine cohaeret tantum si primitivum principium generativum, non genus taxonomicum exhaustivum, significat.
Negatio perfectionis obiectivae tensionem cum retentione exemplaris humanae naturae et normarum utilitatis relinquit.
Veritas imperium automaticum non habet, sed Ratio tamen directionem ethicam praebere debet; modus quo cognitio vim superiorem acquirit nondum perficitur.
Aequalitas affectus praesentis et absentis secundum genus cum inaequalitate secundum vehementiam componitur, sed distinctio inter qualitatem et gradum tacite sustinetur.
Ascensus ad summum bonum Dei cognitionis formam quasi teleologicam inducit, quamquam Natura nullum finem externum intendit.
Concordia sub Ratione necessaria dicitur, sed transitus hominum passionalium ad talem compositionem causaliter indeterminatus manet.
Nexus inter definitionem corpoream affectus et ordines sociales, rationales ac normativos praesupponitur firmius quam singulis gradibus demonstratur.
Cupiditas punctum mutationis principale est, cum ex affectu primitivo in essentiam actualem et potentiam agendi convertitur.
Bonum et malum mutantur ab associationibus institutionis ad relationes potentiae et tandem ad criterion intellectionis.
Socialitas sensum mutat ubi imaginatio alterius, quae affectus imitativos producit, cedit convenientiae hominum ex Ratione agentium.
Virtus e termino negativo, quo passiones moderatrices distinguuntur, in principium positivum potentiae et conservationis sui mutatur.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est rete virium finitarum, in quo nulla res singularis absolute dominatur et omnis status ex proportione potentiarum nascitur.
Subiectum est nodus corporalis causarum externarum et conatus proprii, non centrum liberum quod affectiones ex nihilo instituit.
Tempus est topologia praesentiae affectivae, in qua memoria et futurum possunt ad praesens accedere sed non eandem semper vehementiam retinent.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga e Natura, sed productio affectuum fortiorum, compositio potentiarum et directio conatus ad intellectionem.
Trias affectuum, idea confusa corporis, asymmetria causalium potentiarum, conatus et Ratio sufficiunt ad structuram minimam huius gregis restituendam.
Structura firmissima est connexio inter finitudinem, excessum causarum externarum, conatum, virtutem et actionem ex intellectu.
Nondum satis determinantur productio positiva affectus rationalis fortioris et mechanismus quo homines passionales ad compositionem communem transeant.
Cohaerentia nititur reditu terminorum cum mutatione functionis; derivationes locales singulorum affectuum et regula semantica vocabularii reductioni plenae resistunt.
Restitutio motum verum servat, quia a reductione affectuum ad diagnosin servitutis et inde ad reconstructionem rationalem procedit, manentibus mediationibus normativis incompletis.
The system asks how a plurality of affects is generated from a few motions and why knowledge of the better does not necessarily free the finite human being from passions.
The global thesis constitutes affective life as variation of the body's power, whose servitude arises from an asymmetry of causes and whose ethical restoration begins through immanent conatus.
The argument is diagnostic and reconstructive: it removes apparent species, transcendent ends, and the sovereignty of truth, then restores the field as a contest of powers.
The movement proceeds from the reduction of affective names to the causality of passions, thence to the servitude of the finite, and finally to the rational composition of powers.
The progression is cumulative, recursive, and driven by mutation, because affects once defined return as competing forces, practical norms, and degrees of understanding.
The closure produces not absolute liberation but conditional direction: finite power is ordered through reason, common utility, and knowledge of God, while external causality remains.
[Persistent] Joy and Sadness are fundamental directions of change in power, which subsequently increase or diminish conatus and sustain the affective order of good and evil.
[Persistent] Passion arises where the mind is determined by inadequate ideas and the human being is only a partial cause of its effect.
[Mutating] Desire changes from affective determination into the actual essence of the human being and then into active power proceeding from understanding.
[Mutating] Temporal imagination can render the affect of an absent thing present, but presence, proximity, and contingency order the degree of its force.
[Emergent] Servitude is the necessary asymmetry between the power of the finite human being and external causes, which can increase passive desires beyond the measure of one's own power.
[Persistent] Truth alone does not destroy a positive affection of the body; knowledge cannot be effective unless it enters the order of affects.
[Attractor] An affect is restrained only by a contrary and stronger affect; hence all real moderation is a redistribution of powers, not logical refutation.
[Mutating] Good and evil are transferred from affective institution and absolute predicates to a double order: variation of power and a determinate relation to understanding.
[Terminal] Virtue is one's own power insofar as the striving to preserve oneself can act under the guidance of Reason.
[Emergent] The individual needs external things, but a positive compatibility of natures can transform dependence into a composition of greater power.
[Mutating] Social relation generates imitative affects and conflicts insofar as it is governed by imagination, but produces necessary concord insofar as action proceeds from Reason.
[Attractor] To understand is the criterion of certain utility, whose supreme terminus is knowledge of God as the highest good of the Mind.
[Persistent] Nature acts by immanent necessity, not by final cause; Reason therefore does not command against Nature but orders power within its causality.
Joy and Sadness retain directional identity, but are amplified from affective transitions into ethical indices of the increase and diminution of conatus.
Desire changes function: first it is a determination of the Mind, then the essence of persevering, finally an active or passive vector according to the determining cause.
The idea of an external cause migrates from the principle of denominating affects into the principle of measuring servitude, as the power of the cause is compared with human power.
Affective time changes without inversion: an absent thing can move the same affect in kind, although presence confers a greater degree of intensity.
Imagination of another first produces families of social affects, then explains the dissension of passions, and finally yields to Reason as the contrary form of concord.
Moral terms are transferred from the effects of institution to non-absolute predicates and finally to indices of understanding.
Truth passes from explanatory authority against common speech to affectively conditioned force: correct explanation remains necessary, but does not rule by itself.
Virtue, previously excluded from the class of passions, returns as the active power of human nature itself.
The negation of free decree is absorbed into the theory of servitude: what was initially an imagined false cause later becomes the condition of the finite within external causes.
The names of particular affects recede once the taxonomic work is completed; the higher structure retains causal relations, not an inventory of all compounds.
Definitions of Love, Hate, Shamelessness, and other named affects remain local mechanisms, not axioms of this group.
The exclusions of Wonder and moderating virtues from the number of passions constitute lower taxonomic limits, whose global effect is to distinguish passion from active power.
Local differences of Hope, Fear, Security, and Despair are amplified upward into the general law by which temporal imagination distributes forces.
The definition of passion as a confused idea of bodily change is amplified upward into a theory of servitude as partial causality.
The triad of affects and the double order of good and evil join the units, because changes of power become the matter of immanent ethical judgment.
A major transition occurs where knowledge ceases to be mere truth and becomes affective desire that conflicts with passions.
Lower social affects are absorbed into the structure of the present level as a bifurcation between imaginative conflict and rational composition.
Psychological taxonomy becomes secondarily codified, because the calculus of powers and affective contest acquire greater explanatory force.
The system denies free decree and constitutes servitude not as voluntary fault but as a causally necessary condition.
Nature neither intends external ends nor converts human appetite into the final cause of things.
Actions, good, and evil contain no absolute properties, but receive their meaning from institution, power, and understanding.
An affect separated from the body is not admitted, because every passion affirms the actual constitution of the body.
Logical contradiction or true knowledge does not annihilate an affect unless it itself produces a contrary affective force.
The self-sufficient human individual is excluded, because the finite is always exceeded by external powers and needs external things.
Common humanity, defect, or finitude do not constitute positive concord; compatibility requires common power under Reason.
Liberation can be neither exemption from external causes nor an act of voluntary self-annihilation.
For the system to hold, the model of Nature as artificer or legislator who distributes ends and values prior to causality must be false.
It must be false that a mind furnished with truth can govern body and imagination without producing an affective cause.
It must be false that the individual is a closed substance whose power can be surpassed by no singular thing.
It must be false that time is an affectively neutral measure, because memory, expectation, presence, and contingency distribute the very force of passions.
It must be false that virtue is grounded in the negation of one's own nature, self-sacrifice, or obedience to an external command.
It must be false that community arises from common weakness; only positive compatibility of power can generate concord.
The possibility of an affective being outside the nexus of causes is ontologically unavailable, because even rational action remains within the necessity of Nature.
The system is ordered around the absence of an instantaneous conversion of truth into power; knowledge without affective transmutation remains powerless.
A terminal state in which the human being is free from every passion, external change, and superior power is not admitted.
The principal absence is a fully explained mechanism by which true knowledge produces a stronger affect and rational society from passionate human beings.
The form of a transcendent end is excluded, although knowledge of God constitutes the supreme attractor; terminal attraction therefore cannot become Nature's final cause.
Names of affects are no longer psychological species, but coordinates by which causal relations are described in the contest of powers.
Desire is the joint of the whole group, because the same form passes from local determination to the essence of persevering and to the active power of understanding.
Because passion is a positive affirmation of the body and external causes can surpass human power, moderating truth must become a stronger contrary affect.
A past or future thing can produce an affect of the same kind as a present one, but not necessarily of the same degree; identity of quality and asymmetry of intensity hold together.
Moral predicates arise from affective custom, lose absolute authority, and are legitimately retained only as indices of utility and understanding.
Sociality bifurcates: imagination of others amplifies passion and opposition, but action from rationally common nature composes powers.
Freedom is neither indeterminate decree nor exemption from Nature, but the degree to which the human being acts from its own intelligible power.
Ethics becomes the art of composing contrary affections, individual utilities, and common powers, not a tribunal that condemns passions with words.
Knowledge of God closes the order of understanding without restoring finality, because God is the supreme object of the Mind, not an end pre-established by an artificer Nature.
The ontology of this group makes relations of power primary: an affective thing is a bodily state whose force is determined only by comparison of causal powers.
The subject is not a closed author but a site of partial causality, which can nevertheless order its own perseverance through actual conatus.
Knowledge obtains a causally performative status: being true is insufficient unless it itself operates in the distribution of affective forces.
Time becomes a field of affective intensities, in which imagined presence, memory, expectation, and contingency causally vary efficacy.
Ethics passes from the evaluation of actions to the ordering of power, whose criterion is what increases conatus, understanding, and the composition of natures.
Implicit politics conceives rational concord as an amplification of singular power, not as suppression of individual conatus.
Freedom becomes a variable degree of adequate causality: the human being is freer insofar as it acts from what it understands.
Method must not simply abolish received terms but transfer them from common ontology to causal and practical functions.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: A bodily change produces an affective idea, affect determines desire, judgment of the good shapes the direction of desire, and action in turn produces a new bodily constitution.
An external cause increases passion, passion diminishes one's own power, and diminished power is more easily surpassed by further external causes.
Institution joins social judgment to affects, imagined judgment produces Shame or Glory, and the affect thus produced recreates the force of institution.
Present sweetness restrains the affect of the future, hence reason is followed less, and opinion or lust again amplifies present force.
The circuit of moderation begins when a contrary affect is produced, acquires greater force, and excludes the existence of the prior affect.
Conatus is an immanent attractor: perseverance defines power, Joy increases it, and virtue expresses the rational form of that same conatus.
Rational compatibility composes powers, composition increases common utility, and common utility confirms further concord of reason.
To understand is an ascending attractor that orders certain utility and finds its supreme terminus in knowledge of God.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: The necessity of Nature without end excludes final causes and converts perfection and absolute value into comparative relations.
A change in bodily power is affirmed through an idea and, where the idea is confused, takes the form of passion.
Joy, Sadness, and Desire provide primary motions, while the many names are generated from added relations.
Imagined cause, time, and social relation determine primary motion and produce denominated affects.
Human finitude and the excess of external cause amplify passion into structural servitude.
Moderation requires that knowledge become a contrary affect of greater power, not the mere correction of a false proposition.
Conatus does not destroy servitude but provides the principle of restoration, when virtue and Reason order one's own power.
Reason composes the compatibility of natures and directs movement toward common utility and knowledge of God.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Nominal plurality of affects → reduction to variations of power → modulation through cause, time, and society → dissolution of finality and absolute values → causal finitude and servitude → affectivization of knowledge → conatus as virtue → rational composition of utilities → knowledge of God as terminal attractor.
The psychology of affects is reordered from an inventory of species into a map of relational motions of power.
Moral predicates are reclassified as practical relations of utility, impediment, Joy, and Sadness.
The opposition of true and false ceases to suffice for affective life, because the efficacy of knowledge is distinguished from causal force.
Chronological times become degrees of affective presence, by which an absent thing receives present or diminished force.
Agency is transferred from the free subject to finite conatus, whose virtue is the immanent power of acting.
The social field changes from a scene of judgment and emulation into a problem of composition, where another rational human being becomes the most useful singular thing.
Self-interest and common utility cease to be opposed, because concord can amplify the power of the individual.
The reading of affective vocabulary must investigate changing functions, because the same words are transferred from common usage to immanent calculation.
At the surface level, the concern is with names of affects, with the human being knowing what is better yet subject to passions, and with the dictates of Reason concerning utility and virtue.
At the structural level, everything is ordered through bodily changes, partial causality, the proportion of powers, and the compatibility or contrariety of natures.
At the metastrategic level, moderation passes from moral vocabulary and correct knowledge to the production of a contrary affect and the composition of utilities.
At the ontological and temporal level, Nature acts necessarily, the subject is finite bodily conatus, and time varies imaginative efficacy.
At the methodological and performative level, the text itself performs reduction, exclusion, and mutation of terms, and diagnosis of impotence is converted into ethical reconstruction.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reduction to three primitive affects coheres with a multitude of unnamed compounds only if primitive signifies a generative principle, not an exhaustive taxonomic genus.
The negation of objective perfection leaves a tension with the retention of the model of human nature and norms of utility.
Truth has no automatic sovereignty, yet Reason must provide ethical direction; the manner in which knowledge acquires superior force is not yet completed.
The equality in kind of present and absent affect is combined with inequality in vehemence, but the distinction between quality and degree is tacitly maintained.
The ascent to the highest good of knowledge of God introduces an almost teleological form, although Nature intends no external end.
Concord under Reason is said to be necessary, but the transition of passionate human beings to such composition remains causally indeterminate.
The connection between the bodily definition of affect and social, rational, and normative orders is presupposed more firmly than it is demonstrated at individual stages.
Desire is the principal point of mutation, as it is converted from a primitive affect into actual essence and the power of acting.
Good and evil change from associations of institution to relations of power and finally to the criterion of understanding.
Sociality changes meaning where imagination of another, which produces imitative affects, yields to the compatibility of human beings acting from Reason.
Virtue changes from a negative term, by which moderating passions are distinguished, into a positive principle of power and self-preservation.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a network of finite forces, in which no singular thing absolutely dominates and every state arises from a proportion of powers.
The subject is a bodily node of external causes and its own conatus, not a free center that establishes affections from nothing.
Time is a topology of affective presence, in which memory and the future can approach the present but do not always retain the same vehemence.
Possible navigation is not flight from Nature, but the production of stronger affects, the composition of powers, and the direction of conatus toward understanding.
The triad of affects, the confused idea of the body, the asymmetry of causal powers, conatus, and Reason suffice to reconstruct the minimal structure of this group.
The strongest structure is the connection among finitude, the excess of external causes, conatus, virtue, and action from understanding.
The positive production of a stronger rational affect and the mechanism by which passionate human beings pass to common composition are not yet sufficiently determined.
Coherence depends on the return of terms with change of function; local derivations of individual affects and the semantic rule of vocabulary resist complete reduction.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement, because it proceeds from the reduction of affects to the diagnosis of servitude and thence to rational reconstruction, while incomplete normative mediations remain.
