items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo conatus propriae utilitatis sub necessitate Naturae et imperio affectuum in libertatem communem converti possit sine libero arbitrio aut altruismo sui negante.
Libertas constituitur non ut proprietas absoluta individui, sed ut gradus quo homo ex causis adequate intellectis agit intra corpus, societatem et Naturam.
Fundamentum conversionis est convenientia rationalis qua conservatio sui utilitatem aliorum postulat et bonum communicabile efficit.
Probatio negativa ostendit hanc convenientiam non sponte dominari, quia potentia causarum externarum homines in passiones, partialitatem et conflictum distribuit.
Civitas propterea ab apparatu coactionis ad medium libertatis mutatur: primo conflictum continet, deinde condiciones cooperationis rationalis sustentat.
Motus argumenti est recursivus et amplificativus: actus a causa sua reclassificatur, causa ad totum corporis refertur, totum ad societatem, societas ad ordinem Naturae.
Clausura practica acquiescentiam producit, qua potentia finita suum officium agit et eventus inevitabiles ex necessitate Naturae intellegit.
Clausura absoluta differtur: homo perfecte liber manet terminus hypotheticus, dum libertas actualis per gradus corporales, affectivos, civiles et cognitivos efficitur.
[Persistent] Conatus fit virtus quatenus conservatio sui ex natura proprie intellecta procedit et in actionem adequate causatam transit.
[Persistent] Utilitas rationalis singularis structuram non-rivalem habet, quia potentiam propriam per utilitatem mutuam et bonum communicabile auget.
[Mutating] Ratio ab intellectu normae in cupiditatem activam, amorem, generositatem et institutionem transit; tantum sic vim affectivam acquirit.
[Persistent] Servitus oritur ubi determinatio externa, cognitio inadaequata aut affectus partialis potentiam agendi definit.
[Persistent] Valor affectus aut rei ex effectu in potentiam integratam corporis, multiplicitatem perceptionis et conservationem totius hominis iudicatur.
[Mutating] Civitas incipit ut securitas minis firmata, sed per iura communia, fidem et cooperationem in infrastructuram libertatis rationalis convertitur.
[Mutating] Bonum et malum ab effectibus potentiae ad relationes comparativas vitae finitae transferuntur, dum iustum et iniustum institutionem civilem requirunt.
[Emergent] Libertas est relatio immanens inter causalitatem propriam, corpus aptum, affectus ordinatos, societatem fidelem et necessitatem intellectam.
[Emergent] Nutritio, res externae, labor, commutatio et cura publica non sunt adiuncta ethicae, sed condiciones materiales cognitionis et libertatis.
[Attractor] Cognitio Dei et intellecta necessitas Naturae convergunt in acquiescentiam qua conatus finitus ordinem totius affirmative participat.
[Terminal] In termino hominis perfecte liberi bonum et malum functionem amittunt, quamvis ad navigationem vitae finitae necessaria maneant.
Conatus identitatem structuralem servat, sed ab auto-conservatione singulari ad cooperationem, fidem et conservationem communem amplificatur.
Ratio functionaliter redit: primo convenientiam demonstrat, deinde causam actionis qualificat, postremo affectus, institutiones et condiciones materiales ordinat.
Civitas mutatur ab exteriori coactione affectuum in medium internum libertatis, neque tamen originem coercitivam omnino deponit.
Bonum et malum a nominibus effectuum ad comparationes rationales migrant atque in libertate perfecta terminaliter evanescunt.
Corpus ab identitate per rationem motus et quietis definita ad infrastructuram nutritionis, cognitionis, laboris et societatis extenditur.
Metus ab instrumento initiali securitatis ad formam concordiae infidae deicitur; amor, generositas et fides eius functionem stabilientem absorbent.
Affectus particulares post reclassificationem evanescunt ut indices morales autonomi et redeunt ut modi causales augmenti, diminutionis vel transitionis potentiae.
Discrimen inter homines et bruta localiter terminum reciprocitatis designat, sed structuram libertatis praesentis gradus non generat nisi ut exemplum utilitatis secundum naturae convenientiam.
Criterium mortis per mutationem formae corporis manet locale; sursum persistit tantum principium quod integritas relationalis, non species exterior, potentiam constituit.
Casus risus, commiserationis, fugae, beneficii, gratiae et pecuniae non amplificantur singillatim; coniunguntur sub regula qua actus ex causa, toto et effectu aestimatur.
Doctrina affectus affectu fortiore coercendi transitum efficit inter diagnosin servitutis et constructionem cupiditatum activarum atque institutionum efficacium.
Institutio civilis unitates coniungit, quia eadem potestas quae conflictum coërcet iura, cooperationem materialem et libertatem gradualem sustinere potest.
Moralitas per tristitiam, culpam et opinionem obsolescit ut codex virtutis, sed conditionaliter servatur ut disciplina transitoria multitudinis nondum rationalis.
Utilitas propria rationalis non est possessio competitiva, quia potentiam singularis per bonum communicabile et mutuum auxilium constituit.
Virtus non oritur ex tristitia, metu, paenitentia, abiectione aut odio, quamvis haec affectus ad disciplinam transitoriam adhiberi possint.
Libertas non est arbitrium indeterminatum, solitudo aut exemptio a Naturae necessitate, sed actio relativa ex causis propriis intellectis.
Civitas rationalis non reducitur ad metum nec libertati opponitur, quia concordia fidelis iura communia et cooperationem requirit.
Bonum, malum, iustum et iniustum non sunt genera absoluta rerum, sed relationes potentiae, cognitionis aut institutionis.
Falsum esse oportet intellectum abstractum sine affectu activo aut mediatione institutionali posse passionum potentiam superare.
Falsum esse oportet individuum corpore, rebus externis et aliis hominibus carere posse quin facultas cognoscendi simul minuatur.
Falsum esse oportet speciem externam actus eius valorem determinare, quia servitus et libertas in modo causationis eiusdem actus distinguuntur.
Falsum esse oportet ordinem moralem transcendentem inter potentiam naturalem et institutionem civilem intervenire, quia normae ex relationibus immanentibus generantur.
Systema circa absentiam subiecti extra Naturam ordinatur: nulla potentia humana causationem totius transcendere aut sibi originem absolutam tribuere potest.
Possibilitas inadmissibilis est libertas perpetua sine passione, corpore, societate aut exterioribus causis; homo perfecte liber tantum attractor hypotheticus manet.
Communitas immediata hominum iam rationalium excluditur; omnis communitas actualis mediationes affectivas, iuridicas et materiales requirit.
Conservatio sui sub necessitate Naturae fit principium cooperationis, quia singulare potentiam suam non auget nisi bonum communicabile et auxilia communia producat.
Quoniam intellectus nudus affectum non coërcet, actio rationalis efficax debet formam cupiditatis activae, amoris, generositatis aut institutionis induere.
Civitas est convertor causalis: vim externam ad securitatem adhibet, securitatem in cooperationem transfert, cooperationem autem in maiorem causalitatem propriam civium.
Libertas requirit ecologiam potentiae in qua integritas corporis, res externae, nutritio, labor, commutatio et iura communia mutuo se sustentant.
Bonum et malum sunt instrumenta navigationis potentiae finitae: eo magis necessaria sunt quo minus homo liber est, atque attractore libertatis approximato recedunt.
Iustitia civiliter instituta potest rationem habere sine lege transcendente, si fides, aequitas et communis utilitas ipsas condiciones cooperationis conservant.
Cognitio Dei et cognitio necessitatis Naturae eundem attractorem practicalem efficiunt: cupiditatem communicandi bonum et acquiescentiam intra limites potentiae finitae.
Subiectum liberum non est substantia sui iuris, sed nexus relationum qui eo magis agit quo plures determinationes corporales, affectivas et sociales adequate ordinat.
Politica fit ars condiciones causalitatis propriae distribuendi, non simplex ars vetandi aut pacem metu imponendi.
Tempus ethicum duplicatur: imaginatio praesentia partialiter ponderat, dum Ratio utilitatem totius trans tempora ordinat quamvis durationem exacte cognoscere nequeat.
Ethica fit diagnostica causalis: non quaerit quid actus externe significet, sed quae determinatio potentiam totius augeat et quae dependentiam externam reproducat.
Clausura systematis est resilientia rationalis potius quam dominium: libertas augetur per cooperationem et intellectum necessitatis, non per abolitionem exteriorum causarum.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Conatus rationalis → utilitas mutua → societas → maior potentia singularis → amplificatio conatus rationalis.
Conflictus affectivus → metus et coactio → securitas civilis → cooperatio fidelis → imminutio necessitatis metus.
Aptitudo corporis → necessitas rerum externarum → labor et commutatio → interdependentia socialis → maior aptitudo corporis et Mentis.
Idea adequata → laetitia activa → cupiditas rationalis → actio augens potentiam → maior facultas idearum adequatarum.
Comparatio boni et mali → electio utilitatis integrae → libertas maior → minor dependentia a comparatione → attractio ad terminum ultra bonum et malum.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessitas Naturae generat conatum finitum; conatus ex cognitione adequata fit actio, ex cognitione inadaequata passio.
Actio rationalis propriam conservationem quaerit; convenientia humana hanc conservationem in bonum commune non-rivale amplificat.
Superioritas causarum externarum perturbat convenientiam; affectus contrarii et Civitas intervallum inter normam rationalem et multitudinem actualem mediantur.
Civitas securitatem in iura communia, fidem et cooperationem convertit; hae structurae causalitatem propriam civium augent.
Corpus multiplex res externas et mutuas operas postulat; oeconomia moderata libertatem cognitionis materialiter sustinet.
Potentia sic aucta necessitatem suam intelligit et ad acquiescentiam tendit, dum libertas perfecta terminus regulativus potius quam status empiricus manet.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Conatus necessarius → utilitas propria → convenientia rationalis → bonum communicabile.
Imperium affectuum → conflictus et partialitas → affectus contrarii → securitas civilis.
Securitas civilis → iura communia → fides et cooperatio → libertas socialiter amplificata.
Integritas corporis → res externae et oeconomia → potentia cognitiva → moderatio affectuum.
Moderatio affectuum → causalitas propria → intellectus necessitatis → acquiescentia → approximatio libertatis sine exemptione naturali.
Oppositio inter utilitatem propriam et commune bonum corruit; discrimen verum ponitur inter conatum adequate ordinatum et conatum ab externis causis captum.
Oppositio inter Civitatem et libertatem corruit; discrimen transfertur ad Civitatem quae metum tantum administrat et Civitatem quae potentiam communem auget.
Moralitas actuum exteriorum reordinatur in analysin causarum, adequationis, totius corporis et effectuum socialium.
Corpus et oeconomia ex adiunctis inferioribus in condiciones constitutivas intellectus, cooperationis et libertatis transferuntur.
Necessitas reclassificatur ab externo limite libertatis in campum immanentem intra quem causalitas propria, prudentia et acquiescentia augeri possunt.
Gradus superficiei affectus, actiones, beneficia, pericula, leges, alimenta et pecuniam examinat ut casus vitae sub servitute et libertate.
Gradus structuralis omnes casus secundum causalitatem actionis, potentiam corporis, adequationem cognitionis et mediationem socialem distribuit.
Gradus metastrategicus certamen morale in artem producendi affectus activos, fidem, cooperationem et condiciones libertatis convertit.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis hominem ut partem Naturae necessario determinatam constituit, cuius Ratio utilitatem trans tempora ordinat.
Gradus methodologicus reclassificationes suas performat: eundem actum inter passionem et actionem transfert atque Civitatem ex limite in medium libertatis mutat.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Ratio dicitur affectus sola coërcere non posse, sed omnes actiones passionum producere posse; medium quo idea adequata vim affectivam fortiorem acquirit imperfecte explicatur.
Civitas simul minis fundatur et libertatem perficit; transitus a coactione externa ad cooperationem rationalem non ex sola securitate deducitur.
Ratio bona futura ponderat, quamvis cognitio humana durationis necessario inadaequata sit; prudentia temporalis igitur certitudine quam non possidet operari debet.
Actiones Ratione definitae semper bonae dicuntur, sed homo perfecte liber boni et mali conceptus non format; distinctio perspectivarum manet implicita.
Utilitas mutatur a conservatione singularis in structuram communem quae corpus, cognitionem, cooperationem et iura simul conservat.
Libertas mutatur ab actione ex propria natura in gradum socialiter et materialiter sustentatum causalitatis adequatae.
Necessitas mutatur ab indice potentiae externae in obiectum intellectus quod acquiescentiam et libertatem relativam efficit.
Bonum et malum mutantur a criteriis potentiae in instrumenta comparativa et tandem in categorias terminaliter superfluas.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est reticulum virium in quo corpora, affectus, institutiones et res externae potentiam augent, minuunt aut ad novos circuitus transferunt.
Subiectum est nodus permeabilis qui libertatem non possidet, sed eam per ideas adequatas, affectus activos et relationes fideles componit.
Tempus systematis duplex est: imaginatio praesentia partialiter amplificat, Ratio autem seriem utilitatum sub specie necessitatis ordinat.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga extra Naturam, sed transitus inter determinationes quo homo conflictum in cooperationem et necessitatem in acquiescentiam convertit.
Axiomata de conatu, adequatione, potentia affectuum, corpore, Civitate et necessitate Naturae sufficiunt ad machinam huius gradus restituendam.
Structura firmissima est circuitus quo utilitas rationalis cooperationem generat, cooperatio potentiam singularis auget, et potentia aucta maiorem actionem rationalem permittit.
Minus determinata manent productio affectus rationalis efficacis et conversio Civitatis coercitivae in ordinem libertatem re vera sustinentem.
Restitutio verum motum servat si libertatem non ut statum terminalem, sed ut amplificationem recursivam potentiae corporalis, socialis et cognitivae sub necessitate exhibet.

The system asks how the striving for one's own advantage, under the necessity of Nature and the dominion of the affects, can be converted into common freedom without free will or self-denying altruism.
Freedom is constituted not as an absolute property of the individual, but as the degree to which a human being acts from adequately understood causes within body, society, and Nature.
The foundation of the conversion is rational agreement, by which self-preservation requires the advantage of others and produces a communicable good.
The negative proof shows that this agreement does not spontaneously prevail, because the power of external causes distributes human beings into passions, partiality, and conflict.
The State is therefore transformed from an apparatus of coercion into a means of freedom: first it contains conflict, then it sustains the conditions of rational cooperation.

The movement of the argument is recursive and amplificatory: an act is reclassified from its cause, the cause is referred to the whole of the body, the whole to society, society to the order of Nature.
The practical closure produces acquiescence, by which finite power performs its office and understands inevitable events from the necessity of Nature.
Absolute closure is deferred: the perfectly free human being remains a hypothetical limit, while actual freedom is effected through bodily, affective, civil, and cognitive degrees.
[Persistent] Conatus becomes virtue insofar as self-preservation proceeds from properly understood nature and passes into adequately caused action.
[Persistent] Rational individual advantage has a non-rival structure, because it increases its own power through mutual advantage and a communicable good.
[Mutating] Reason passes from the understanding of a norm into active desire, love, generosity, and institution; only thus does it acquire affective force.
[Persistent] Bondage arises where external determination, inadequate knowledge, or a partial affect defines the power of acting.
[Persistent] The value of an affect or thing is judged from its effect upon the integrated power of the body, the multiplicity of perception, and the preservation of the whole human being.
[Mutating] The State begins as security secured by threats, but through common rights, trust, and cooperation is converted into an infrastructure of rational freedom.
[Mutating] Good and evil are transferred from effects of power to comparative relations of finite life, while just and unjust require civil institution.
[Emergent] Freedom is an immanent relation among proper causality, an apt body, ordered affects, trustworthy society, and understood necessity.
[Emergent] Nourishment, external things, labor, exchange, and public care are not adjuncts to ethics, but material conditions of knowledge and freedom.
[Attractor] Knowledge of God and the understood necessity of Nature converge in the acquiescence by which finite conatus affirmatively participates in the order of the whole.
[Terminal] At the limit of the perfectly free human being, good and evil lose their function, although they remain necessary for navigating finite life.
Conatus preserves its structural identity, but is amplified from individual self-preservation into cooperation, trust, and common preservation.
Reason returns functionally: first it demonstrates agreement, then qualifies the cause of action, and finally orders affects, institutions, and material conditions.
The State is transformed from external coercion of the affects into an internal means of freedom, yet does not entirely lay aside its coercive origin.
Good and evil migrate from names of effects to rational comparisons and finally disappear in perfect freedom.
The body is extended from an identity defined through a ratio of motion and rest into an infrastructure of nourishment, knowledge, labor, and society.
Fear is cast down from an initial instrument of security to a form of untrustworthy concord; love, generosity, and trust absorb its stabilizing function.
Particular affects disappear after reclassification as autonomous moral indicators and return as causal modes of increase, decrease, or transition of power.

The distinction between humans and brute animals locally marks the limit of reciprocity, but does not generate the structure of present freedom except as an example of advantage according to agreement of nature.
The criterion of death through a change in the form of the body remains local; upward there persists only the principle that relational integrity, not external appearance, constitutes power.
The cases of laughter, compassion, flight, benefit, gratitude, and money are not individually amplified; they are joined under the rule by which an act is assessed from its cause, whole, and effect.
The doctrine of restraining an affect by a stronger affect effects the transition between the diagnosis of bondage and the construction of active desires and efficacious institutions.
Civil institution joins the units, because the same power that restrains conflict can sustain rights, material cooperation, and gradual freedom.
Morality through sadness, guilt, and opinion becomes obsolete as a code of virtue, but is conditionally preserved as a transitory discipline of the multitude not yet rational.
Rational self-advantage is not competitive possession, because it constitutes the power of the individual through a communicable good and mutual aid.
Virtue does not arise from sadness, fear, repentance, self-abjection, or hatred, although these affects may be employed for transitory discipline.
Freedom is not indeterminate choice, solitude, or exemption from the necessity of Nature, but relative action from understood proper causes.
The rational State is not reduced to fear nor opposed to freedom, because trustworthy concord requires common rights and cooperation.
Good, evil, just, and unjust are not absolute kinds of things, but relations of power, knowledge, or institution.
It must be false that abstract understanding without active affect or institutional mediation can overcome the power of the passions.
It must be false that an individual can lack body, external things, and other human beings without the faculty of knowing being diminished at the same time.
It must be false that the external appearance of an act determines its value, because bondage and freedom are distinguished in the mode of causation of the same act.
It must be false that a transcendent moral order intervenes between natural power and civil institution, because norms are generated from immanent relations.
The system is ordered around the absence of a subject outside Nature: no human power can transcend the causation of the whole or attribute an absolute origin to itself.
The inadmissible possibility is perpetual freedom without passion, body, society, or external causes; the perfectly free human being remains only a hypothetical attractor.
An immediate community of already rational human beings is excluded; every actual community requires affective, juridical, and material mediations.
Self-preservation under the necessity of Nature becomes a principle of cooperation, because the individual does not increase its power unless it produces a communicable good and common aids.
Since bare understanding does not restrain affect, efficacious rational action must assume the form of active desire, love, generosity, or institution.
The State is a causal converter: it employs external force for security, transfers security into cooperation, and cooperation into greater proper causality of citizens.
Freedom requires an ecology of power in which bodily integrity, external things, nourishment, labor, exchange, and common rights mutually sustain one another.
Good and evil are instruments for navigating finite power: they are more necessary the less free the human being is, and recede as the attractor of freedom is approached.
Civilly instituted justice can have reason without transcendent law, if trust, equity, and common advantage preserve the very conditions of cooperation.
Knowledge of God and knowledge of the necessity of Nature effect the same practical attractor: the desire to communicate good and acquiescence within the limits of finite power.
The free subject is not a substance in its own right, but a nexus of relations that acts all the more insofar as it adequately orders more bodily, affective, and social determinations.
Politics becomes the art of distributing the conditions of proper causality, not the simple art of forbidding or imposing peace through fear.
Ethical time is doubled: imagination weighs presents partially, while Reason orders the advantage of the whole across time, although it cannot know duration exactly.
Ethics becomes causal diagnostics: it does not ask what an act externally signifies, but which determination increases the power of the whole and which reproduces external dependence.
The closure of the system is rational resilience rather than mastery: freedom is increased through cooperation and understanding necessity, not through the abolition of external causes.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Rational conatus → mutual advantage → society → greater individual power → amplification of rational conatus.
Affective conflict → fear and coercion → civil security → trustworthy cooperation → diminution of the necessity of fear.
Aptitude of the body → necessity of external things → labor and exchange → social interdependence → greater aptitude of body and Mind.
Adequate idea → active joy → rational desire → power-increasing action → greater capacity for adequate ideas.
Comparison of good and evil → choice of integral advantage → greater freedom → lesser dependence on comparison → attraction toward a limit beyond good and evil.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: The necessity of Nature generates finite conatus; conatus becomes action from adequate knowledge, passion from inadequate knowledge.
Rational action seeks its own preservation; human agreement amplifies this preservation into a non-rival common good.
The superiority of external causes disturbs agreement; contrary affects and the State mediate the interval between the rational norm and the actual multitude.
The State converts security into common rights, trust, and cooperation; these structures increase the proper causality of citizens.
The multiple body requires external things and mutual services; a regulated economy materially sustains the freedom of knowledge.
Power thus increased understands its necessity and tends toward acquiescence, while perfect freedom remains a regulative limit rather than an empirical state.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Necessary conatus → self-advantage → rational agreement → communicable good.
Dominion of the affects → conflict and partiality → contrary affects → civil security.
Civil security → common rights → trust and cooperation → socially amplified freedom.
Bodily integrity → external things and economy → cognitive power → moderation of the affects.
Moderation of the affects → proper causality → understanding of necessity → acquiescence → approximation of freedom without natural exemption.
The opposition between self-advantage and the common good collapses; the true distinction is placed between adequately ordered conatus and conatus captured by external causes.
The opposition between the State and freedom collapses; the distinction is transferred to the State that merely administers fear and the State that increases common power.
The morality of external acts is reordered into an analysis of causes, adequacy, the whole body, and social effects.
Body and economy are transferred from inferior adjuncts into constitutive conditions of understanding, cooperation, and freedom.
Necessity is reclassified from an external limit of freedom into an immanent field within which proper causality, prudence, and acquiescence can be increased.
The surface level examines affects, actions, benefits, dangers, laws, food, and money as cases of life under bondage and freedom.
The structural level distributes all cases according to the causality of action, the power of the body, the adequacy of knowledge, and social mediation.
The metastrategic level converts moral contest into the art of producing active affects, trust, cooperation, and the conditions of freedom.
The ontological and temporal level constitutes the human being as a necessarily determined part of Nature, whose Reason orders advantage across time.
The methodological level performs its reclassifications: it transfers the same act between passion and action and transforms the State from a limit into a means of freedom.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reason is said not to be able by itself to restrain affects, yet to be able to produce all actions of the passions; the means by which an adequate idea acquires stronger affective force is imperfectly explained.
The State is at once founded on threats and perfects freedom; the transition from external coercion to rational cooperation is not deduced from security alone.
Reason weighs future goods, although human knowledge of duration is necessarily inadequate; temporal prudence must therefore operate with a certainty that it does not possess.
Actions defined by Reason are always called good, but the perfectly free human being does not form the concepts of good and evil; the distinction of perspectives remains implicit.
Advantage is transformed from the preservation of the individual into a common structure that simultaneously preserves body, knowledge, cooperation, and rights.
Freedom is transformed from action from one's own nature into a socially and materially sustained degree of adequate causality.
Necessity is transformed from an index of external power into an object of understanding that effects acquiescence and relative freedom.
Good and evil are transformed from criteria of power into comparative instruments and finally into terminally superfluous categories.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a network of forces in which bodies, affects, institutions, and external things increase, diminish, or transfer power into new circuits.
The subject is a permeable node that does not possess freedom, but composes it through adequate ideas, active affects, and trustworthy relations.
The time of the system is double: imagination partially amplifies presents, but Reason orders the series of advantages under the aspect of necessity.
Possible navigation is not flight outside Nature, but passage among determinations by which the human being converts conflict into cooperation and necessity into acquiescence.
The axioms concerning conatus, adequacy, the power of the affects, body, State, and the necessity of Nature suffice to reconstruct the machinery of this level.
The firmest structure is the circuit by which rational advantage generates cooperation, cooperation increases individual power, and increased power permits greater rational action.
The production of efficacious rational affect and the conversion of the coercive State into an order truly sustaining freedom remain less determined.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement if it presents freedom not as a terminal state, but as the recursive amplification of bodily, social, and cognitive power under necessity.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo Mens necessaria, corpori coniuncta et causis externis obnoxia libertatem acquirat sine imperio voluntatis, sine exemptione a causalitate et sine oeconomia praemii post mortem.
Thesis globalis potentiam Mentis in intelligentia collocat, quae affectus ordinando ad cognitionem intuitivam, Amorem Dei intellectualem et beatitudinem tamquam virtutem immanentem progreditur.
Argumentatio demonstrativa simul reconstructiva est: categorias voluntatis, passionis, amoris, aeternitatis et beatitudinis non tantum negat, sed secundum causalitatem idearum denuo constituit.
Motus a confusa attributione affectus causae externae transit ad ordinationem intellectualem, deinde ad tertium cognitionis genus et tandem ad actionem aeternam quae suam laetitiam secum fert.
Progressus verus spiralis est, quia cognitio passivitatem minuit, laetitia cognitionem auget, et beatitudo maiorem potentiam cognoscendi atque ordinandi affectus iterum producit.
Corpus ab sede durationis, imaginationis et passionum in condicionem strategicam mutatur, cuius aptitudo plures actiones, ampliorem cognitionem et maiorem partem Mentis aeternam sustinet.
Clausura figuram sapientis producit, cuius libertas non indeterminatio sed stabilitas sub necessitate intellecta est, contra ignorantem qui causis externis et libidinibus fluctuans determinatur.
Terminus argumenti in causam convertitur: beatitudo, quae primo ut finis liberationis apparet, tandem ipsa virtus et principium potentiae in affectus fit.
[Persistent] Potentia Mentis non voluntate separata, sed gradu intelligentiae et formationis idearum adaequatarum definitur.
[Persistent] Passio est affectus quatenus ex idea confusa oritur; claritas eius non obiectum delet, sed statum Mentis a pati ad agere transfert.
[Mutating] Libertas ab imminutione graduata passivitatis ad stabilem praevalentiam actionis intellectualis et tandem ad beatitudinem activam extenditur.
[Persistent] Necessitas causarum non est oppositum libertatis, sed ordo cuius intellectus affectum mitigat et actionem sapientis constituit.
[Persistent] Ordo idearum, affectionum Corporis, imaginum et memoriae unam machinam constituunt, per quam cognitio dispositio affectiva et corporalis fit.
[Mutating] Corpus simul est condicio imaginationis temporalis et instrumentum aptitudinis, quo Mens ad plures actiones et ampliorem aeternitatis participationem disponitur.
[Emergent] Genera cognitionis asymmetricam seriem formant: confusio primi generis tertium non parit, Ratio transitum aperit, intuitio autem essentias singulares ex Deo cognoscit.
[Mutating] Amor Dei a relatione passiva et reciproca ad Amorem intellectualem mutatur, quo amor Mentis pars est activae et infinitae sui cognitionis divinae.
[Emergent] Aeternitas Mentis neque duratio indefinita neque conservatio memoriae personalis est, sed conceptio essentiae Corporis et Mentis sub necessitate divina.
[Attractor] Cognitio tertii generis, summa laetitia, Amor Dei intellectualis et beatitudo in unum attractorem convergunt qui affectus non reprimit sed activitate superat.
[Emergent] Virtus proprium utile ratione quaerens a spe et metu separatur, atque beatitudo non merces virtutis sed eius exercitium constitutivum fit.
[Terminal] Discrimen inter sapientem et ignorantem est diversitas modorum existendi: sapientis stabilitas ex necessitate intellecta, ignorantia autem ex determinatione externa et fluctuatione oritur.
Intelligentia identitatem functionis servat: ab initio ad finem unica mensura potentiae Mentis manet, quamvis ab affectuum remedio ad aeternam actionem extendatur.
Affectus primum ut idea confusa, deinde ut proportio inter causas externas et cognitionem, postremo ut materia actionis beatificae reclassificatur.
Amor Dei inversionem patitur: amor passivus, reciprocus et anthropomorphicus excluditur, dum Amor intellectualis redit ut actus quo Deus per Mentem se ipsum amat.
Imaginatio et memoria primo instrumenta praeparationis rationalis sunt, sed in transitu ad aeternitatem structuram suam exhauriunt et cum duratione Corporis evanescunt.
Corpus a termino polemico dualismi ad condicionem temporalem passionis, deinde ad instrumentum positivum ampliandae potentiae Mentis migrat.
Necessitas ab argumento mitigandi dolorem in formam ontologicam libertatis sapientis amplificatur; eadem causalitas quae arbitrium excludit actionem intelligibilem constituit.
Libertas a moderamine partiali affectuum ad mutationem proportionis inter actionem et passionem, atque inde ad beatitudinem aeternam, transfertur.
Virtus primo ex origine adaequata Cupiditatis distinguitur, sed terminaliter cum Amore intellectuali et beatitudine ipsa identificatur.
Mortis metus ex centro morali removetur et in effectum cognitionis inadaequatae absorbetur; aucta parte intelligente, momentum partis pereuntis minuitur.
Mechanica concursus causarum, distributionis obiectivae et frequentiae imaginum localiter explicat regimen affectuum, sed hoc gradu sub ampliori transformatione actionis et passionis ordinatur.
Refutatio Stoicae et Cartesianae voluntatis munus fundamenti negativi retinet, sed non constituit clausuram, quae ex Amore intellectuali et beatitudine producitur.
Impossibilitas odii erga Deum, initio terminus demonstratione suspensus, sursum fit condicio transformationis amoris passivi in actionem intellectualem.
Relatio omnium affectionum ad ideam Dei a remedio locali affectuum in fundamentum cognitionis tertii generis et amoris aeterni amplificatur.
Distinctio actualitatis temporalis et aeternae unitates inferiores coniungit, quia eadem essentia Corporis imaginationem durantem ab intellectu aeterno separat.
Sterilitas primi generis respectu cognitionis intuitivae localem doctrinam cognitionis in legem transitionis vertit: sola cognitio adaequata cognitionem altiorem generat.
Fundamentum virtutis in utili rationali ab immortalitate independens manet, sed hoc gradu cum cognitione aeternitatis coniungitur sine reductione unius ad alterum.
Aptitudo Corporis excedit statum propositionis localis et fit commissura inter praxim temporalem, ordinationem affectuum et proportionem Mentis aeternam.
Libertas non est imperium absolutum voluntatis neque actus nudae coercitionis, sed effectus intelligentiae quae statum causalem affectuum mutat.
Libertas non requirit punctum extra seriem causarum, quia exemptio a determinatione naturalis ordinis ipsum fundamentum cognitionis destrueret.
Affectus non est vis cognitioni penitus extrinseca aut residuum opacum, quoniam mutatio cognitionis eius formam passivam dissolvere potest.
Deus non est particeps commercii affectivi reciproci, nec Amor Dei postulare potest ut natura divina ad cupiditatem finitam mutetur.
Aeternitas non est continuatio durationis, memoriae, imaginationis aut narrationis empiricae personae.
Virtus neque spe praemii neque metu supplicii fundatur; oeconomia moralis compensationis ad servitutem affectivam pertinet.
Beatitudo non est praemium posterius victoriae in libidines, sed vis praesens ex qua potentia ordinandi affectus sequitur.
Corpus non est adversarius aeternitatis, quia eius aptitudo temporalis dispositionem ad actionem intellectualem efficere potest.
Falsum esse debet Mentem extra Naturam consistere et voluntate nuda ordinem Corporis infringere; aliter correspondentia idearum et affectionum vacillaret.
Falsum esse debet vocem amoris eandem passionem in homine et Deo significare; impassibilitas divina et amor divinus cohaerent tantum per mutationem ab affectu passivo ad actionem intellectualem.
Falsum esse debet identitatem aeternam Mentis coincidere cum historia imaginativa singularis personae, quia memoria et imaginatio ad durationem Corporis restringuntur.
Falsum esse debet summum bonum structuram rivalem vel scarce distributam habere; eius communicatio Amorem auget potius quam partem cuiusquam minuit.
Falsum esse debet cognitionem esse repraesentationem inertem, quoniam cognitio adaequata laetitiam, ordinationem corporalem et maiorem agendi potentiam efficit.
Falsum esse debet mortalitatem Corporis omnem rationem virtutis abolere; recte vivere fundamentum immanens habet et mors solam structuram temporalem Mentis delet.
Ontologice inadmissibile est subiectum finitum extra Deum subsistens, quod ex exteriori loco causam totius contempletur aut amet.
Indisponibilis est Deus personalis qui precibus, offensa, amore reciproco aut mutatione voluntatis respondeat; relatio divina intra actionem intelligendi reponitur.
Inadmissibilis est mensura temporalis qua aeternitas quantificetur vel futura continuatio vitae personalis probetur.
Systema circum absentiam iudicis remunerantis ordinatur: sine praemio, poena et compensatione ultramortali virtus tamen causam sufficientem habere debet.
Impossibilis habetur destructio veritatis intellectualis per affectum contrarium, quia talis destructio falsitatem eius quod necessario intelligitur postularet.
Libertas duplicem sed continuam structuram accipit: in duratione est ordinatio imaginum et imminutio passionis; sub aeternitate est actio intuitiva cui beatitudo et Amor intellectualis insunt.
Cognitio et libertas circuitum positivum efficiunt: cognitio passionem minuit, cognitio adaequata cupiditatem cognitionis altioris parit, et beatitudo facultatem intelligendi iterum auget.
Negatio amoris divini et affirmatio amoris quo Deus homines amat cohaerere possunt tantum si nomen amoris a passione reciproca ad aeternam actionem sui cognitionis mutatur.
Corpus est simul terminus partis Mentis pereuntis et condicio augendae partis activae; eius temporalitas igitur aeternitati non simpliciter opponitur, sed ad eam disponit.
Intellectus necessitatis et praeparatio imaginativa coniuncti efficiunt ut actio non sit interruptio causalitatis, sed ordinata participatio nexus causarum.
Communitas summi boni et independentia virtutis a praemio constituunt ethicam non-rivalem, in qua aliena beatitudo potentiam propriam augere potest.
Imaginatio est structura transitoria: intra durationem rationem corporaliter praeparat, sed ad statum aeternum perveniens propriam operationem et memoriam amittit.
Valor Cupiditatis non ex obiecto sed ex origine ideationali pendet; eadem genealogia explicat cur cognitio confusa tertium genus parere nequeat et cur Ratio transitum ad intuitionem aperiat.
Affectuum libertas non exstinctionem absolutam, sed mutationem proportionis inter pati et agere requirit; incrementum intellectus efficacius est quam directum bellum contra passiones.
Subiectum liberum non est substantia voluntaria indivisa, sed proportio mutabilis idearum adaequatarum et inadaequatarum, actionum et passionum, cuius identitas secundum potentiam ordinatur.
Agendi potentia crescit non causalitate remota, sed causalitate intellecta; autonomia reclassificatur ut capacitas causas per ideas adaequatas interne explicandi.
Epistemologia fit technica affectiva, quia veritas non tantum cognitionem obiecti praestat sed ordinem Corporis, frequentiam imaginum et facultatem agendi immutat.
Aeternitas Mentis salutem personalem non promittit, sed identitatem empiricam dividit inter structuram memorativam pereuntem et intelligibilitatem essentiae quae tempori non subiacet.
Disciplina Corporis effectum ontologicum acquirit: multiplicata aptitudine ad agendum, Mens plura ordinate intelligit et minor pars eius a duratione imaginativa definitur.
Communicatio cognitionis et amoris non solum compatibilis cum libertate est, sed eam amplificat, quia summum bonum intellectum participatione aliena non consumitur.
Theologia in reflexivam ontologiam convertitur: Deus non alter affectivus est, sed causa immanens cuius infinita sui cognitio per Amorem intellectualem Mentis finite explicatur.

items.text: Ignorantia causarum rem ut liberam et externam figit, haec fixatio affectum auget, affectus autem Mentem impedit atque ignorantiam causalem reproducingit.
Claritas affectum a causa externa confuse imaginata separat, separatio ordinationem permittit, ordinatio actionem auget, et actio ulteriorem claritatem sustinet.
Praeceptum memoriae mandatum imagines futuras ordinat; occursus ita praeparatus affectum rationalem excitat, qui eandem dispositionem memorativam confirmat.
Cognitio secundi generis cupiditatem intuitionis parit; intuitio laetitiam et Amorem intellectualem producit, quibus aptitudo ad ulteriorem intuitionem amplificatur.
Aptitudo Corporis plures actiones aperit, plures actiones ampliorem cognitionem sustentant, cognitio passiones minuit, et imminutio passionum Corpus ad ordinem intellectus expeditius disponit.
Amor boni communis participatione aliorum augetur; incrementum gaudii communis Amorem iterum nutrit, unde socialitas rationalis circuitum amplificationis format.
Beatitudo est attractor terminalis qui terminum in machinam vertit: quo magis adest, eo plus Mens intelligit, minus patitur et potentius eandem beatitudinem conservat.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Variatio corporis intra nexum necessarium causarum → diversus gradus aptitudinis et diversae condiciones initiales passionis atque cognitionis.
Idea inadaequata + attributio causae externae → affectus passivus + fixatio imaginativa + dependentia a viribus externis.
Conceptus clarus affectus + intellectus necessitatis → separatio a causa confuse imaginata → imminutio passivitatis.
Ordo idearum → ordo affectionum Corporis → concatenatio imaginum → memoria praeceptorum → responsio rationalis anticipata.
Ratio adaequata → cupiditas cognitionis tertii generis → intuitio essentiae singularis ex dependentia divina.
Actualitas temporalis Corporis / essentia Corporis in Deo → imaginatio et memoria pereuntes / pars Mentis aeterna.
Cognitio intuitiva → summa laetitia cum idea Dei → Amor Dei intellectualis aeternus.
Amor intellectualis ut explicatio amoris divini → beatitudo ut virtus → augmentum intellectus → imminutio passionum → libertas stabilis sub necessitate.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Imperium voluntatis negatum → affectus ut idea confusa reconstitutus → necessitas intellecta → ordinatio imaginum et Corporis → cognitio tertii generis → Amor intellectualis → beatitudo activa → libertas sapientis.
Deus ut causa externa affective imaginata → impossibilitas odii et amoris reciproci → idea Dei adaequata → Amor intellectualis → amor Mentis ut explicatio amoris quo Deus se ipsum amat.
Corpus durans → imaginatio, memoria et praeparatio affectiva → Corpus ad plura aptum → amplius intelligere → maior proportio Mentis aeterna → imminutio mortis metus.
Libertas a dominio voluntatis et exemptione causali ad transformationem graduatam proportionis inter actionem et passionem reordinatur.
Affectus ab impetu psychologico externo ad structuram ideationalem, corporalem et causaliter ordinabilem reclassificatur.
Corpus a mero correlato mortalitatis ad instrumentum dispositionis rationalis et ampliandae potentiae Mentis transfertur.
Deus ab obiecto passionis reciprocae ad causam immanentem et structuram reflexivam Amoris intellectualis reclassificatur.
Aeternitas a continuatione temporali personae ad modum concipiendi essentiam sub necessitate divina transfertur.
Virtus a disciplina sustentata praemio et poena ad bonum immanens, non-rivale et causaliter beatificum convertitur.
Cognitio ab inspectione rerum ad operationem transformantem transit, quae affectus, Corpus, temporalitatem et statum subiecti simul ordinat.
In gradu superficiei agitur de moderandis affectibus, intelligenda aeternitate Mentis, minuendo mortis metu et constituenda beatitudine.
In gradu structurali ordines idearum, affectionum Corporis, imaginationis, generum cognitionis et actionis unam distributionem causalem efficiunt.
In gradu metastrategico certamen a repressione affectuum ad productionem activitatis, laetitiae et cognitionis aptae transfertur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali realitas est nexus necessarius et immanens, sub quo duratio imaginativa ab aeternitate intelligibili distinguitur sine oppositione substantialis Mentis et Corporis.
In gradu methodologico et performativo demonstratio ipsam transformationem quam docet exercet: terminos passionis ordinatim negat, reclassificat et in circuitum activum beatitudinis componit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Assertio quod omnis affectio conceptum clarum involvat non plene determinat quantum claritatis sufficiat ut affectus ipse desinat esse passio.
Pluralitas causarum affectum simul roborare et eius noxam minuere potest; systema distinctionem inter concursum, distributionem et frequentiam requirit, sed non universaliter formalizat.
Impassibilitas Dei et identitas Amoris Mentis cum amore divino tensionem semanticam pariunt, quae sola mutatione notionis amoris administratur.
Amor intellectualis aeternus sine principio dicitur, sed accessus Mentis ad cognitionem tertii generis ut progressio gradatim acquisita narratur.
Nexus inter aptitudinem Corporis et maiorem partem Mentis aeternam affirmatur potentius quam mechanismus proportionis demonstratur.
Virtus ab cognitione aeternitatis independens est, quamvis summa figura sapientis per intellectum aeternum et Amorem intellectualem definiatur.
Affectus mutatur ab idea confusa singularis passionis in indicem proportionis causalis inter determinationem externam et activitatem Mentis.
Amor Dei sensum mutat ubi reciproca passio excluditur et idem nomen actioni intellectus atque divinae sui cognitioni assignatur.
Corpus functionem mutat ubi ex sede durationis et imaginationis fit dispositio positiva ad plures actiones et ampliorem cognitionem.
Beatitudo statum mutat ubi ex fine disciplinae in ipsam virtutem et causam coercendi libidines invertitur.
Libertas mutatur ubi moderatio affectuum intra durationem in aeternam participationem actionis intellectualis et stabilitatem sub necessitate absorbetur.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est reticulum immanens causarum et idearum, in quo nulla voluntas extrinseca imperat, sed partes secundum gradum quo causas interne explicant agunt vel patiuntur.
Subiectum est nodus proportionaliter mutabilis huius reticuli, non centrum suum; fit liber quatenus nexus qui ipsum determinant clarius per ipsum exprimuntur.
Tempus bifariam ordinatur: duratio imagines, memoriam et passionem sustinet, aeternitas autem essentiam sine principio, successione aut recordatione exhibet.
Certamen non est expulsio affectuum, sed conversio canalium causalium, qua fixatio externa in ordinem idearum, laetitiam activam et Amorem intellectualem traducitur.
Navigatio possibilis est spiralis: Corpus aptius, Mens clarior, affectus minus passivus et beatitudo potentior invicem se amplificant, donec mors centrum ordinis ethici amittat.

Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad nucleum restituendum: intelligentia mutat passiones in actiones, necessitas intellecta libertatem constituit, et Amor intellectualis beatitudinem immanentem producit.
Structura firmissima est circuitus inter ideam adaequatam, intellectum necessitatis, imminutam passivitatem, laetitiam et auctam potentiam intelligendi.

Minus determinata manent quantitas cognitionis requisita ad passionem mutandam, mechanismus quo aptitudo Corporis maiorem partem Mentis aeternam efficit, et relatio experientiae aeternitatis ad absentiam memoriae.
Cohaerentia huius gradus non ex ordine lineari solo, sed ex reditu mutato eorundem terminorum constat: affectus, Corpus, amor, libertas et beatitudo singulis reditibus novam functionem accipiunt.
Restitutio verum motum servat si remedia temporalia affectuum non a doctrina aeternitatis separantur, sed ut dispositio ad cognitionem intuitivam et beatitudinem leguntur.

Reductioni axiomaticae adhuc resistit transitus ab demonstratione aeternitatis ad affirmationem experientialem eius atque imago terminalis sapientis, cuius vis affectiva plus operatur quam catena demonstrativa sola explicat.

The system asks how the necessary Mind, conjoined to the Body and subject to external causes, acquires freedom without dominion of the will, without exemption from causality, and without an economy of reward after death.

The global thesis locates the power of the Mind in understanding, which, by ordering the affects, advances toward intuitive knowledge, the intellectual Love of God, and blessedness as an immanent virtue.

The demonstrative argument is simultaneously reconstructive: it not only negates the categories of will, passion, love, eternity, and blessedness, but reconstitutes them according to the causality of ideas.

The movement passes from the confused attribution of an affect to an external cause to intellectual ordering, then to the third kind of knowledge, and finally to eternal action that bears its own joy with it.
True progress is spiral-shaped, because knowledge diminishes passivity, joy increases knowledge, and blessedness in turn produces a greater power of knowing and ordering the affects.

The Body is transformed from the seat of duration, imagination, and passions into a strategic condition, whose aptitude sustains more actions, broader knowledge, and a greater eternal part of the Mind.

The closure produces the figure of the wise person, whose freedom is not indeterminacy but stability under understood necessity, in contrast to the ignorant person, who is determined by external causes and fluctuating desires.
The terminus of the argument turns into a cause: blessedness, which first appears as the end of liberation, ultimately becomes virtue itself and the principle of power over the affects.
[Persistent] The power of the Mind is defined not by a separate will, but by the degree of understanding and the formation of adequate ideas.
[Persistent] A passion is an affect insofar as it arises from a confused idea; its clarification does not destroy the object, but transfers the state of the Mind from undergoing to acting.
[Mutating] Freedom extends from the gradual diminution of passivity to the stable predominance of intellectual action and finally to active blessedness.
[Persistent] The necessity of causes is not the opposite of freedom, but an order whose understanding mitigates affect and constitutes the action of the wise person.
[Persistent] The order of ideas, affections of the Body, images, and memory constitute one mechanism through which knowledge becomes affective and bodily disposition.
[Mutating] The Body is at once the condition of temporal imagination and the instrument of aptitude, by which the Mind is disposed toward more actions and a broader participation in eternity.

[Emergent] The kinds of knowledge form an asymmetric sequence: the confusion of the first kind does not produce the third; Reason opens the transition, whereas intuition knows singular essences from God.
[Mutating] Love of God is transformed from a passive and reciprocal relation into intellectual Love, by which the Mind's love is part of God's active and infinite knowledge of himself.
[Emergent] The eternity of the Mind is neither indefinite duration nor preservation of personal memory, but conception of the essence of the Body and Mind under divine necessity.
[Attractor] Knowledge of the third kind, supreme joy, intellectual Love of God, and blessedness converge in one attractor that does not repress affects but surpasses them through activity.
[Emergent] Virtue, seeking what is properly useful by reason, is separated from hope and fear, and blessedness becomes not the reward of virtue but its constitutive exercise.

[Terminal] The distinction between the wise and the ignorant is a diversity of modes of existing: the wise person's stability arises from understood necessity, whereas ignorance arises from external determination and fluctuation.
Understanding preserves its functional identity: from beginning to end it remains the single measure of the Mind's power, although it extends from the remedy of affects to eternal action.
The affect is reclassified first as a confused idea, then as a proportion between external causes and knowledge, and finally as the material of beatific action.
Love of God undergoes an inversion: passive, reciprocal, and anthropomorphic love is excluded, while intellectual Love returns as the act by which God loves himself through the Mind.
Imagination and memory are initially instruments of rational preparation, but in the transition to eternity they exhaust their structure and vanish with the duration of the Body.
The Body migrates from the polemical term of dualism to the temporal condition of passion, then to a positive instrument for expanding the Mind's power.
Necessity is enlarged from an argument for mitigating pain into the ontological form of the wise person's freedom; the same causality that excludes free choice constitutes intelligible action.
Freedom is transferred from partial governance of the affects to a change in the proportion between action and passion, and thence to eternal blessedness.
Virtue is first distinguished by the adequate origin of Desire, but terminally it is identified with intellectual Love and blessedness itself.
Fear of death is removed from the moral center and absorbed into an effect of inadequate knowledge; as the understanding part increases, the importance of the perishing part diminishes.

The mechanics of the concurrence of causes, objective distribution, and frequency of images locally explains the governance of affects, but at this level it is ordered under the broader transformation of action and passion.
The refutation of Stoic and Cartesian will retains the function of a negative foundation, but does not constitute the closure, which is produced by intellectual Love and blessedness.
The impossibility of hatred toward God, initially a terminus sustained by demonstration, becomes at a higher level the condition for transforming passive love into intellectual action.
The relation of all affections to the idea of God is enlarged from a local remedy for affects into the foundation of knowledge of the third kind and eternal love.
The distinction between temporal and eternal actuality joins lower unities, because the same essence of the Body separates enduring imagination from eternal intellect.
The sterility of the first kind with respect to intuitive knowledge turns a local doctrine of knowledge into a law of transition: only adequate knowledge generates higher knowledge.
The foundation of virtue in rational advantage remains independent of immortality, but at this level it is joined to knowledge of eternity without reduction of one to the other.
The aptitude of the Body exceeds the status of a local proposition and becomes the joint between temporal practice, the ordering of affects, and the eternal proportion of the Mind.
Freedom is neither absolute dominion of the will nor an act of naked coercion, but the effect of understanding that changes the causal state of affects.
Freedom does not require a point outside the series of causes, because exemption from the determination of the natural order would destroy the very foundation of knowledge.
An affect is not a force wholly extrinsic to knowledge or an opaque residue, since a change in knowledge can dissolve its passive form.
God is not a participant in reciprocal affective commerce, nor can Love of God require that the divine nature be transformed toward finite desire.
Eternity is not the continuation of duration, memory, imagination, or the empirical narrative of a person.
Virtue is founded neither on hope of reward nor fear of punishment; the moral economy of compensation belongs to affective servitude.
Blessedness is not a later reward for victory over desires, but a present force from which the power of ordering affects follows.
The Body is not the adversary of eternity, because its temporal aptitude can effect a disposition toward intellectual action.
It must be false that the Mind stands outside Nature and by naked will breaks the order of the Body; otherwise the correspondence of ideas and affections would waver.

It must be false that the word love signifies the same passion in human beings and in God; divine impassibility and divine love cohere only through the transformation from passive affect to intellectual action.
It must be false that the eternal identity of the Mind coincides with the imaginative history of a singular person, because memory and imagination are restricted to the duration of the Body.
It must be false that the highest good has a rivalrous or scarcely distributed structure; its communication increases Love rather than diminishing anyone's share.
It must be false that knowledge is inert representation, since adequate knowledge effects joy, bodily ordering, and a greater power of acting.
It must be false that the mortality of the Body abolishes every ground of virtue; living rightly has an immanent foundation, and death destroys only the temporal structure of the Mind.
A finite subject subsisting outside God, which contemplates or loves the cause of the whole from an external position, is ontologically inadmissible.
A personal God who responds to prayers, offense, reciprocal love, or a change of will is unavailable; the divine relation is relocated within the action of understanding.
A temporal measure by which eternity might be quantified or the future continuation of personal life proved is inadmissible.
The system is ordered around the absence of a remunerating judge: without reward, punishment, and post-mortem compensation, virtue must nevertheless have a sufficient cause.
The destruction of intellectual truth by a contrary affect is held impossible, because such destruction would require the falsity of what is necessarily understood.

Freedom receives a dual but continuous structure: in duration it is the ordering of images and diminution of passion; under eternity it is intuitive action containing blessedness and intellectual Love.

Knowledge and freedom produce a positive circuit: knowledge diminishes passion, adequate knowledge generates the desire for higher knowledge, and blessedness in turn increases the faculty of understanding.

The negation of divine love and the affirmation of the love by which God loves human beings can cohere only if the name of love is transformed from reciprocal passion into the eternal action of self-knowledge.

The Body is at once the terminus of the perishing part of the Mind and the condition for increasing the active part; its temporality therefore is not simply opposed to eternity, but disposes toward it.
Understanding necessity and imaginative preparation jointly bring it about that action is not an interruption of causality, but an ordered participation in the nexus of causes.
The community of the highest good and the independence of virtue from reward constitute a non-rivalrous ethics, in which another's blessedness can increase one's own power.
Imagination is a transitory structure: within duration it bodily prepares reason, but upon reaching the eternal state it loses its own operation and memory.

The value of Desire depends not on its object but on its ideational origin; the same genealogy explains why confused knowledge cannot produce the third kind and why Reason opens the transition to intuition.

Freedom from affects requires not their absolute extinction, but a change in the proportion between undergoing and acting; the increase of intellect is more effective than direct war against passions.
The free subject is not an undivided voluntary substance, but a mutable proportion of adequate and inadequate ideas, actions and passions, whose identity is ordered according to power.
The power of acting increases not through remote causality, but through understood causality; autonomy is reclassified as the capacity internally to explain causes through adequate ideas.
Epistemology becomes affective technique, because truth not only provides knowledge of an object but changes bodily order, the frequency of images, and the faculty of acting.
The eternity of the Mind does not promise personal salvation, but divides empirical identity between a perishing memorial structure and the intelligibility of essence that is not subject to time.
The discipline of the Body acquires an ontological effect: with multiplied aptitude for acting, the Mind understands more things in order and a lesser part of it is defined by imaginative duration.
The communication of knowledge and love is not only compatible with freedom, but amplifies it, because the highest good understood is not consumed by another's participation.
Theology is converted into reflexive ontology: God is not an affective other, but the immanent cause whose infinite self-knowledge is finitely explicated through the intellectual Love of the Mind.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Ignorance of causes fixes a thing as free and external, this fixation increases affect, and affect impedes the Mind and reproduces causal ignorance.
Clarity separates an affect from the confusedly imagined external cause, separation permits ordering, ordering increases action, and action sustains further clarity.
The precept of memory orders future images; an encounter thus prepared arouses rational affect, which confirms the same memorial disposition.
Knowledge of the second kind generates the desire for intuition; intuition produces joy and intellectual Love, through which the aptitude for further intuition is amplified.

The aptitude of the Body opens more actions, more actions sustain broader knowledge, knowledge diminishes passions, and the diminution of passions disposes the Body more readily toward the order of intellect.
Love of the common good is increased by the participation of others; the increase of common joy nourishes Love in turn, whence rational sociability forms a circuit of amplification.

Blessedness is a terminal attractor that turns the terminus into a mechanism: the more it is present, the more the Mind understands, the less it undergoes, and the more powerfully it preserves that blessedness.

items.text: Variation of the body within the necessary nexus of causes → a different degree of aptitude and different initial conditions of passion and knowledge.
Inadequate idea + attribution of an external cause → passive affect + imaginative fixation + dependence on external forces.
Clear conception of affect + understanding of necessity → separation from the confusedly imagined cause → diminution of passivity.
Order of ideas → order of affections of the Body → concatenation of images → memory of precepts → anticipated rational response.
Adequate Reason → desire for knowledge of the third kind → intuition of singular essence from divine dependence.
Temporal actuality of the Body / essence of the Body in God → perishing imagination and memory / eternal part of the Mind.
Intuitive knowledge → supreme joy with the idea of God → eternal intellectual Love of God.
Intellectual Love as explication of divine love → blessedness as virtue → increase of intellect → diminution of passions → stable freedom under necessity.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Dominion of the will negated → affect reconstituted as confused idea → understood necessity → ordering of images and Body → knowledge of the third kind → intellectual Love → active blessedness → freedom of the wise person.

God as affectively imagined external cause → impossibility of hatred and reciprocal love → adequate idea of God → intellectual Love → love of the Mind as explication of the love by which God loves himself.
Enduring Body → imagination, memory, and affective preparation → Body apt for more → understanding more → greater eternal proportion of the Mind → diminution of fear of death.
Freedom is reordered from dominion of the will and causal exemption to the gradual transformation of the proportion between action and passion.
Affect is reclassified from an external psychological impulse into an ideational, bodily, and causally orderable structure.
The Body is transferred from a mere correlate of mortality into an instrument of rational disposition and of expanding the Mind's power.
God is reclassified from the object of reciprocal passion into immanent cause and the reflexive structure of intellectual Love.
Eternity is transferred from the temporal continuation of the person to a mode of conceiving essence under divine necessity.
Virtue is converted from a discipline sustained by reward and punishment into an immanent, non-rivalrous, and causally beatifying good.
Knowledge passes from inspection of things to a transformative operation that simultaneously orders affects, the Body, temporality, and the state of the subject.
At the surface level, the concern is with governing affects, understanding the eternity of the Mind, diminishing fear of death, and constituting blessedness.
At the structural level, the orders of ideas, affections of the Body, imagination, kinds of knowledge, and action effect one causal distribution.
At the metastrategic level, the struggle is transferred from repression of affects to the production of activity, joy, and adequate knowledge.

At the ontological and temporal level, reality is a necessary and immanent nexus, under which imaginative duration is distinguished from intelligible eternity without substantial opposition of Mind and Body.

At the methodological and performative level, demonstration enacts the very transformation it teaches: it systematically negates, reclassifies, and composes the terms of passion into the active circuit of blessedness.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The assertion that every affection involves a clear conception does not fully determine how much clarity suffices for the affect itself to cease being a passion.

A plurality of causes can simultaneously strengthen an affect and lessen its harm; the system requires a distinction among concurrence, distribution, and frequency, but does not universally formalize it.
Divine impassibility and the identity of the Mind's Love with divine love produce a semantic tension, which is managed only by changing the notion of love.
Eternal intellectual Love is said to be without beginning, but the Mind's access to knowledge of the third kind is narrated as a gradually acquired progression.
The nexus between the aptitude of the Body and the greater eternal part of the Mind is affirmed more strongly than the mechanism of proportion is demonstrated.
Virtue is independent of knowledge of eternity, although the highest figure of the wise person is defined through eternal intellect and intellectual Love.
The affect changes from the confused idea of a singular passion into an index of the causal proportion between external determination and activity of the Mind.
Love of God changes its meaning where reciprocal passion is excluded and the same name is assigned to the action of intellect and divine self-knowledge.
The Body changes function where it becomes, from the seat of duration and imagination, a positive disposition toward more actions and broader knowledge.
Blessedness changes status where it is inverted from the end of discipline into virtue itself and the cause of restraining desires.
Freedom changes where the governance of affects within duration is absorbed into eternal participation in intellectual action and stability under necessity.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly an immanent network of causes and ideas, in which no extrinsic will rules, but parts act or undergo according to the degree to which they internally explain causes.
The subject is a proportionally mutable node of this network, not its center; it becomes free insofar as the nexuses that determine it are more clearly expressed through it.
Time is ordered in two ways: duration sustains images, memory, and passion, whereas eternity presents essence without beginning, succession, or recollection.
The struggle is not the expulsion of affects, but the conversion of causal channels, through which external fixation is transferred into the order of ideas, active joy, and intellectual Love.

Possible navigation is spiral-shaped: a more apt Body, a clearer Mind, a less passive affect, and more powerful blessedness mutually amplify one another, until death loses the center of ethical order.
The present axioms suffice to restore the core: understanding transforms passions into actions, understood necessity constitutes freedom, and intellectual Love produces immanent blessedness.
The firmest structure is the circuit among adequate idea, understanding of necessity, diminished passivity, joy, and increased power of understanding.

What remain less determined are the quantity of knowledge required to transform a passion, the mechanism by which the aptitude of the Body effects a greater eternal part of the Mind, and the relation of the experience of eternity to the absence of memory.
The coherence of this level consists not in linear order alone, but in the altered return of the same terms: affect, Body, love, freedom, and blessedness receive a new function with each return.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement if the temporal remedies for affects are not separated from the doctrine of eternity, but are read as a disposition toward intuitive knowledge and blessedness.

What still resists axiomatic reduction is the transition from the demonstration of eternity to its experiential affirmation, and the terminal image of the wise person, whose affective force accomplishes more than the demonstrative chain alone explains.
