items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo una Natura necessario immanens corpora, mentes, cognitiones, conatus et relationes affectivas generet, dum intra eandem necessitatem transitus a determinatione externa ad actionem propriam possibilis manet.

Thesis globalis affirmat omne ens esse expressionem unius Naturae, cuius causalitas per individua corporea, ideas, imaginationes et affectus distribuitur atque secundum gradum adaequationis in passionem vel actionem mutatur.

Argumentatio geometrica fit genealogia recursiva: exclusio exterioritatis causalitatem necessariam constituit, causalitas constitutionem corporis et Mentis explicat, atque haec constitutio errores, valores et circuitus sociales tamquam effectus naturales restituit.

Motus procedit a substantia sui causa ad productionem modalem, a modo finito ad individuum corporeum, ab affectione ad ideam et affectum, atque a circuitibus passionum ad actionem causaliter adaequatam.

Motus verus est cumulativus et spiralis, quia psychologia corporis explicat errores metaphysicos iam exclusos, affectuum doctrina cognitionis structuram in socialitatem transfert, et quilibet reditus subiectum iam mutatum recipit.

Necessitas mutatur ab clausura ontologica in regulam individuationis, cognitionis et agentiae; quod initio omnem exterioritatem tollit, terminaliter libertatem ut gradum causalitatis propriae definit.
Error, teleologia, voluntas libera et valor transcendens non extra Naturam cadunt, sed positive ex cognitione partiali, memoria, utilitate, attributione causae et circulatione affectuum producuntur.

Clausura est immanens sed provisionaliter aperta: fuga ex necessitate excluditur, actio et Generositas intra eam constituuntur, sed mechanismus plenus quo adaequatio passionum ordinem stabiliter transformat nondum absolvitur.
[Persistent] Una Natura necessario existens est causa immanens omnium rerum; nullum ens, tribunal aut principium causale extra eam datur.
[Persistent] Omne finitum est modus et nodus causaliter dependens; Mens humana et Corpus non substantiae separatae, sed eiusdem individui expressiones attributivae sunt.
[Mutating] Necessitas causalis a productione modorum ad ordinem cognitionis, actionis et propagationis socialis extenditur, sine ruptura inter ontologiam et psychologiam.
[Mutating] Individuum corporeum est relatio dynamica perseverans, cuius affectiones simul perceptionem Mentis et variationes potentiae agendi constituunt.
[Mutating] Imaginatio est mechanismus naturalis quo affectiones, vestigia, absentiae, similitudines et consuetudines praesentias affectivas atque nexus aestimativos producunt.
[Mutating] Adaequatio et inadaequatio non tantum qualitates cognitionis sunt: prior causalitatem activam, altera causalitatem partialem, passionem et capturam per causas externas constituit.
[Emergent] Conatus est essentia actualis individui, cuius operationes ad conservationem et augmentum potentiae agendi convergunt.
[Emergent] Bonum, malum et perfectio non proprietates extrinsece normatae, sed indices relationis inter constitutionem rei, appetitum et variationem potentiae sunt.
[Emergent] Subiectum est processus corporeus, historicus et socialiter distributus, qui se per affectiones, ideas et responsiones imaginatas aliorum constituit.
[Terminal] Libertas est augmentum causalitatis adaequatae intra necessitatem, non indifferentia, exemptio causalis aut initium absolutum actionis.
[Persistent] Cogitatio et Extensio eundem ordinem exprimunt sine causalitate transversa; congruentia Mentis et Corporis identitatem processus, non commercium substantiarum, significat.
[Emergent] Tempus systematis stratificatur in aeternam necessitatem Naturae, durationem indefinitam conatus et praesentificationes imaginativas praeteriti vel futuri.
[Attractor] Intelligibilitas causalis est attractor communis: ideas locales in contextum ampliorem inserit, passionem in actionem reordinat et fictas exterioritates dissolvit.
[Terminal] Ethica est reconfiguratio immanens cognitionis, corporis et relationum, cuius forma activa socialis in Animositate et Generositate culminat, non in imperio voluntatis.
Substantia identitatem ontologicam retinet, sed postquam clausuram immanentem constituit, e proscenio recedit et ut infrastructura tacita cognitionis atque affectuum operatur.
Immanentia ab relatione Dei et modorum ad constitutionem Mentis corporeae, demonstrabilitatem affectuum et circulationem socialem causalitatis amplificatur.
Necessitas functionem mutat: clausura modalitatis fit principium geneticum imaginationis, discrimen actionis et passionis atque condicio libertatis internae.
Corpus a modo determinato in individuum relationale, deinde in substratum variabile potentiae et tandem in condicionem mutabilitatis valorum convertitur.
Idea affectionis redit ut affectus: eadem mediatio quae externum per constitutionem Corporis exhibet nunc augmentum vel diminutionem potentiae exprimit.
Imaginatio mutatur a nomine generali erroris in mechanismum neutralem praesentificationis, deinde in operatorem conativum, interpersonalem et reflexivum.
Libertas inversionem stabilem patitur: indifferentia evanescit, necessitas propriae naturae manet, et gradus libertatis ex proportione causalitatis adaequatae mensuratur.
Perfectio et bonum ab exemplaribus externis ad potentiam rei migrant; terminaliter etiam identitas valoris obiecti dissolvitur in eventum relationis mutabilis.
Conatus ab essentia actuali singularis ad principium selectionis imaginum, productionis Cupiditatis et conservationis socialiter mediatae amplificatur.
Finis, postquam causalitas Naturae esse desinit, in indicem imaginationis transfertur et tandem in generaliorem operationem attributionis causae absorbetur.
Demonstrationes locales de unicitate substantiae hoc gradu in clausuram generaliorem absorbentur qua omnis exterioritas ontologica, epistemica et practica excluditur.
Modi infiniti, modi finiti et Natura Naturata architecturam mediationis praebent, sed praesentis gradus nexus est continuatio illius mediationis in corporibus, ideis et affectibus.
Vestigia corporalium partium manent hypothesis localis imaginationis; sursum persistit tantum functio qua historia affectionum absentias et consuetudines efficaciter praesentat.
Taxonomiae affectuum singularium ad gradum inferiorem pertinent; hoc gradu earum varietas in grammaticam conatus, potentiae, imaginationis et attributionis causae comprimitur.
Critica localis finalismi amplificatur in diagnosin generalem qua cognitiones partiales, valores et auctoritates transcendentes ex corporeis atque socialibus mechanismis producuntur.
Parallelismus attributorum coniungit ontologiam, psychologiam et doctrinam affectuum, sed causalitatem transversam non introducit neque mechanismum congruentiae ulterius explicat.
Distinctio causae adaequatae et partialis transitum maioris ordinis efficit, quia veritatem et errorem in actionem, passionem atque formas socialis potentiae convertit.
Beatitudo manet attractor non completus: directionem a necessitate ad libertatem ordinat, sed plena conversio cognitionis in stabilitatem affectivam extra determinationem praesentem manet.
Nullus locus extra Naturam admittitur ex quo causalitas, cognitio, valor aut actio originem vel normam accipiat.
Nec mundus alternativus nec actus a serie causarum immunis possibilitatem realem constituunt.
Finis futurus, arbitrium divinum et utilitas humana causalitatem Naturae regere non possunt.
Mens et Corpus neque substantiae separatae neque agentes causaliter transversi sunt.
Subiectum finitum nec sibi immediate transparens nec affective sui iuris est.
Bonum, malum, ordo et perfectio proprietates intrinsecas rerum aut tribunal morale independente desiderio non constituunt.
Identitas individui, valoris et affectus neque materia permanenti neque obiecto invariabili neque catalogo terminali stabilitur.
Separatio essentiae, existentiae, potentiae et actualitatis divinae falsa esse debet, quia hiatum ontologicum introduceret unde contingentia et exterioritas redirent.
Cognitio causaliter iners falsa esse debet, quia differentia adaequationis eadem differentia est quae actionem a passione separat.
Universalitas legum affectuum uniformitatem responsionum implicare non potest; aliter diversitas corporum et singularitas essentiarum evanescerent.
Norma veritatis vel bonitatis ab exteriori imposita falsa esse debet, quia tam ideae quam appetitus ex ordine causali intrinseco aestimantur.
Error tamquam mera irruptio irrationalis extra Naturam falsus esse debet; falsitas privativa est, sed condiciones eius corporales et sociales positive generantur.
Libertas quae necessitatem minuat aut causam incausatam postulet falsa esse debet; aliter actio ad exemptionem ontologicam, non ad adaequationem, reduceretur.
Absentia suprema est ipsum extra, cuius exclusio substantiam, cognitionem, affectum et ethicam in eadem immanentia claudit.
Origo absoluta cogitationis, appetitus aut actionis ontologice indisponibilis est; omnis initium apparens nexus causalis iam constituti est.
Tribunal transcendens quod ordinem actualem, valores et affectus ante eorum generationem iudicet impossibile est.
Praesentia rei externae vel subiecti sibi ipsi non mediata corpore, affectione et historia causali indisponibilis est.
Possibilitas nondum exhibita est conversio integra cognitionis adaequatae in stabilitatem affectivam et socialem; haec absentia directionem ethicam ordinat sine clausura demonstrata.
Quia immanentia ontologica Mentem ex Corpore constituit, error non exceptio a Natura sed circuitus endogenus est quo affectio localis in structuram universalem proiectatur.

Necessitas universalis cum causalitate partiali et imitatione affectuum coniuncta dominationem non ut violationem naturae, sed ut reproductionem naturalem dependentiae per circuitus sociales explicat.
Critica finalismi et genesis valoris ex appetitu efficiunt ut normativitas sit cartographia compositionum quae potentiam augent vel minuunt, non lex supra desiderium posita.
Individuum relationale, conatus indefinitus et reflexio per alios constituunt subiectum metastabile, cuius identitas perseverat tantum per continuam reconfigurationem corporalem atque socialem.
Cum contingentia ad ignorantiam transferatur et futurum imaginatum affectum praesenter ordinet, causalitas finalis fit retroiectio affectiva intra ordinem causarum efficientium.
Libertas adaequata potentiam relationalem habet: proprietates communes et Generositas actiones componere possunt, quamquam forma politica stabilis huius compositionis nondum deducitur.
Novitas status non requirit ordinem possibilem extra actualitatem: intra ordinem necessarium emergit ex mutatione compositionis corporis, relationum et directionis affectivae.
Imaginatio est commissura ambigua totius systematis: superstitionem et causalitatem fictam sustinet, sed etiam conatum conservat atque materiam praebet quam cognitio adaequata reordinat.
Ontologia, epistemologia et ethica fiunt tres altitudines unius integrationis causalis: realitas est expressio, veritas est adaequatio expressionis, et actio est eius causalitas sufficiens.
Agentia subiecti non est proprietas binaria sed proportio variabilis inter causas externas, constitutionem corporis, ideas affectionum et effectus ex propria natura intelligibiles.
Libertas crescit per cognitionem et recompositionem necessitatis, non per subtractionem causarum; determinatio externa minuitur quatenus nexus causales in operationem propriam integrantur.
Ordo socialis est circulatio inaequalis imaginum, attributionum et variationum potentiae, quae individua simul componit, distinguit et in circuitus reciprocos implicat.
Tempus non est continens uniforme, sed relatio inter necessitatem aeternam, durationem perseverantiae et reditus imaginativos qui corpus mutatum numquam ad statum omnino eundem reducunt.
Interventio efficax condiciones compositionis, attributiones causae et ordines imaginativos mutare debet; imperium voluntatis sine tali reconfiguratione eandem causalitatem partialem reproducit.
Methodus geometrica naturalizationem quam affirmat performat: vocabula transcendentalia et moralia in definitiones, nexus causales, mutationes potentiae et circuitus recursivos resolvit.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Partitio entis in substantiam et modos dependentiam constituit; dependentia immanentiam requirit; immanentia psychologiam naturalizat; psychologia vicissim fictionem exterioritatis explicat.
Affectio imaginem generat, imago valorem et Cupiditatem dirigit, Cupiditas actionem producit, actio corpus et relationes mutat, atque mutatum corpus novas affectiones recipit.
Ignorantia causarum opinionem libertatis et finium parit; hae imagines causas occultant, auctoritatem fictam confirmant et ignorantiam initialem reproducunt.
Proprietates communes ideas adaequatas multiplicant; adaequatio actionem auget; actio compositiones potentiores efficit, unde amplificatio rationalis et socialis possibilis fit.
Conatus imagines potentiae faventes retinet, Laetitiam et Cupiditatem auget, atque per hanc selectionem condiciones propriae perseverantiae recursive confirmat.
Affectus imaginatus alterius responsionem excitat; responsio novam causam affectivam praebet; reciprocitas inde in Amorem, Gloriam, Odium, Vindictam vel rivalitatem escalat.
Repetitio affectiva numquam mera identitas est, quia corpus per fruitionem et occursus mutatur; eadem imago rediens affectum diversum aut contrarium producere potest.
Attractor principalis est causalitas adaequata, circa quam intelligibilitas, libertas, conservatio potentiae et Generositas convergunt sine egressu ex necessitate.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Una Natura necessario existens → nulla exterioritas substantialis → omnia entia ut modi causaliter dependentes.
Expressio per attributa → idem individuum sub Cogitatione et Extensione → series causales distinctae sine dualismo substantiali.
Occursus corporum → affectio relationem afficientis et affecti involvens → idea affectionis → perceptio perspectivalis et variatio potentiae.
Contextus causarum incompletus → vestigium et praesentificatio → associatio imaginativa → contingentia, finis, valor et causa per accidens.
Essentia actualis → conatus → Cupiditas → augmentum aut imminutio potentiae → Laetitia aut Tristitia → actio vel passio secundum qualitatem causae.
Imago affectus alieni → imitatio et attributio causae → responsio reciproca → circuitus socialis → reconfiguratio identitatis et potentiae.
Integratio ideae in contextum causarum → causa magis adaequata → actio → Laetitia et Cupiditas activae → Fortitudo atque Generositas.
Metaphysica immanentiae → constitutio Mentis corporeae → genesis erroris et affectus → explicatio projectionis transcendentis → reditus ad immanentiam sub forma libertatis causalis.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Substantia sui causa → causalitas immanens → modi finiti → individuum corporeum → Mens ut idea Corporis → affectio → imaginatio → conatus → affectus → socialitas.
Ignorantia causarum → contingentia et finis imaginati → utilitas et valor proiecti → auctoritas transcendentis → ulterior occultatio causalitatis.
Affectio → praesentificatio → imitatio → reciprocitas → rivalitas vel compositio → mutatio Corporis → novus circuitus affectivus.
Cognitio causalis → adaequatio aucta → passio imminuta → actio ex propria natura → Fortitudo et Generositas → libertas intra necessitatem.
Oppositio Dei et mundi corruit; Deus non est artifex iuxta res, sed causalitas immanens cuius modi totum campum realitatis constituunt.
Oppositio Mentis et Corporis reordinatur in duplicem expressionem unius individui, unde subiectum mentale clausum locum processui corporeo-relationali cedit.
Ager cognitionis et ager agentiae in unam scalam causalitatis plenae vel partialis coalescunt.
Valor reclassificatur a proprietate obiecti in indicem desiderii, compositionis corporis et mutationis potentiae.
Socialitas reclassificatur ab aggregatione subiectorum praeconstitutorum in circulationem imaginum, attributionum causarum et affectuum reciprocorum.
Tempus reclassificatur a successione homogena in coordinationem aeternitatis, durationis, memoriae, expectationis et mutationis irreversibilis corporis.
Methodus interventionis transit ab imperio, iudicio et catalogo ad analysin geneticam compositionum, contextuum causalium et circuituum amplificationis.
In gradu superficiei agunt Deus, Natura, Mens, Corpus, cognitio, voluntas, Cupiditas, Laetitia, Tristitia et relationes sociales.
In gradu structurali omnia haec obiecta distribuuntur per causalitatem immanentem, individuationem relationalem, affectiones, conatum, adaequationem et circuitus affectivos.
In gradu metastrategico quaestio transfertur ab electione, fine et iudicio ad generationem, attributionem causae, compositionem potentiae et condiciones interventionis.
In gradu ontologico et temporali realitas est una productio necessaria, singularia sunt relationes perseverantes, et tempus est nexus aeternitatis cum duratione atque praesentificatione.
In gradu methodologico et performativo systema negationibus exterioritatis, deductionibus geneticis et redefinitionibus causalibus ipsam naturalizationem quam asserit efficit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Attributa per se concipiuntur, sed eorum distinctio cum unitate numerica substantiae positive coordinanda manet; exclusio pluralitatis nexum plene non substituit.
Causalitas divina omnes modos determinat, dum finita immediate per finita producuntur; mediatio inter productivitatem aeternam et series singulares manet compressa.
Parallelismus identitatem processus Mentis et Corporis servat sine commercio causali, sed modum positivum huius congruentiae ultra duplicem expressionem non explicat.

Falsitas privatio cognitionis dicitur, quamquam error mechanismis corporalibus et socialibus positive producitur; privatio normativam formam, genesis causalitatem rei explicat, sed nexus earum manet delicatus.
Necessitas omnium idearum cum discrimine normativo inter adaequationem et inadaequationem componenda est sine tribunali externo.
Directio ethica et politica cognitioni adaequatae innititur, sed transitus ab intellecta necessitate ad transformationem stabilem affectuum et collectivorum incompletus manet.
Infinitas mutatur ab exclusione termini in potentiam productivam cuius effectus necessario actuantur.
Corpus mutatur ab obiecto Mentis in individuum relationale, deinde in variabilem potentiam quae cognitionem, affectum et valorem ordinat.
Imaginatio mutatur a praeiudicio generali in mechanismum neutrum, deinde in operatorem conativum et socialem qui tam capturam quam conservationem sustinet.
Adaequatio mutatur a qualitate veritatis in causalitatem activam, dum inadaequatio a partialitate epistemica in passionem et dependentiam socialem transit.
Libertas mutatur ab facultate indeterminata in necessitatem propriae naturae et tandem in gradum variablem causalitatis adaequatae.
Perfectio et valor mutantur ab conformitate externa in potentiam singularis, deinde in relationem affectivam cuius obiectum ipsum stabilitatem axiologicam amittit.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas est machina immanens sui expressionis, reticulum causarum et corporum in quo effectus non exeunt ex Natura sed eius potentiam localiter redistribuunt.
Subiectum est vortex corporeus et mentalis conatu perseverans, permeabilis causis externis et imaginibus aliorum, cuius autonomia secundum adaequationem variatur.
Tempus est machina stratificata in qua necessitas aeterna singularia durare facit, memoria absentia reducit, et corporis mutatio identitatem reditus impedit.
Captura est circuitus quo ignorantia, utilitas, imago causae et affectus reciproci individuum ad causas externas alligant dum speciem libertatis producunt.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga e machina, sed transitus per eam ab affectionibus partialiter intellectis ad compositiones causales adaequatas, quarum forma socialis est Generositas.
Axiomata immanentiae, individuationis corporeae, imaginationis, adaequationis, conatus et recursionis affectivae sufficiunt ad machinam huius metagregis restituendam.
Structura firmissima est continuatio qua causalitas immanens affectionem producit, affectio cognitionem et potentiam variat, atque variatio in actiones et circuitus sociales distribuitur.
Minus determinata manet conversio cognitionis adaequatae in moderationem stabilem affectuum, compositionem socialem et beatitudinem.
Systema hac magnitudine cohaeret tantum si ordo non ut series doctrinarum, sed ut circuitus a metaphysica ad corpus, ab corpore ad imaginationem et ab imaginatione ad criticam metaphysicae legitur.
Restitutio motum generativum servat, sed pluralitas singularium affectuum, differentiae corporum et forma terminalis vitae activae compressioni axiomaticae adhuc resistunt.

The system asks how one necessarily immanent Nature generates bodies, minds, cognitions, conatus, and affective relations, while within that same necessity the passage from external determination to proper action remains possible.

The global thesis affirms that every being is an expression of one Nature, whose causality is distributed through corporeal individuals, ideas, imaginations, and affects, and is transformed into passion or action according to the degree of adequacy.

Geometrical argumentation becomes a recursive genealogy: the exclusion of exteriority establishes necessary causality, causality explains the constitution of Body and Mind, and this constitution restores errors, values, and social circuits as natural effects.

The movement proceeds from substance that is its own cause to modal production, from finite mode to corporeal individual, from affection to idea and affect, and from circuits of passions to causally adequate action.

The true movement is cumulative and spiral, because the psychology of the body explains metaphysical errors already excluded, the doctrine of affects transfers the structure of cognition into sociality, and each return receives a subject already transformed.
Necessity changes from ontological closure into a rule of individuation, cognition, and agency; what initially removes all exteriority ultimately defines freedom as a degree of proper causality.

Error, teleology, free will, and transcendent value do not fall outside Nature, but are positively produced from partial cognition, memory, utility, attribution of cause, and the circulation of affects.

Closure is immanent yet provisionally open: escape from necessity is excluded, action and Generosity are constituted within it, but the full mechanism by which adequacy stably transforms the order of passions is not yet completed.
[Persistent] One necessarily existing Nature is the immanent cause of all things; no being, tribunal, or causal principle outside it is given.
[Persistent] Everything finite is a mode and a causally dependent node; the human Mind and Body are not separate substances, but attributive expressions of the same individual.
[Mutating] Causal necessity extends from the production of modes to the order of cognition, action, and social propagation, without rupture between ontology and psychology.
[Mutating] The corporeal individual is a persisting dynamic relation, whose affections simultaneously constitute the perception of the Mind and variations of the power of acting.
[Mutating] Imagination is the natural mechanism by which affections, traces, absences, similarities, and habits produce affective presences and evaluative connections.
[Mutating] Adequacy and inadequacy are not merely qualities of cognition: the former constitutes active causality, the latter partial causality, passion, and capture by external causes.
[Emergent] Conatus is the actual essence of the individual, whose operations converge upon the preservation and increase of the power of acting.
[Emergent] Good, evil, and perfection are not extrinsically normed properties, but indices of the relation between a thing's constitution, appetite, and variation of power.
[Emergent] The subject is a corporeal, historical, and socially distributed process, which constitutes itself through affections, ideas, and imagined responses of others.
[Terminal] Freedom is an increase of adequate causality within necessity, not indifference, causal exemption, or the absolute beginning of action.
[Persistent] Thought and Extension express the same order without transverse causality; the congruence of Mind and Body signifies the identity of process, not an interaction of substances.
[Emergent] The system's time is stratified into the eternal necessity of Nature, the indefinite duration of conatus, and imaginative presentifications of past or future.
[Attractor] Causal intelligibility is a common attractor: it inserts local ideas into a broader context, reorders passion into action, and dissolves fictive exteriorities.
[Terminal] Ethics is the immanent reconfiguration of cognition, body, and relations, whose active social form culminates in Courage and Generosity, not in the command of the will.
Substance retains ontological identity, but after establishing immanent closure, it recedes from the foreground and operates as the tacit infrastructure of cognition and affects.
Immanence is expanded from the relation of God and modes to the constitution of the corporeal Mind, the demonstrability of affects, and the social circulation of causality.
Necessity changes function: the closure of modality becomes the genetic principle of imagination, the distinction between action and passion, and the condition of internal freedom.
The Body is transformed from a determined mode into a relational individual, then into a variable substratum of power, and finally into the condition of the mutability of values.
The idea of affection returns as affect: the same mediation that presents the external through the constitution of the Body now expresses increase or diminution of power.
Imagination changes from a general name for error into a neutral mechanism of presentification, then into a conative, interpersonal, and reflexive operator.
Freedom undergoes a stable inversion: indifference disappears, the necessity of one's own nature remains, and the degree of freedom is measured by the proportion of adequate causality.
Perfection and good migrate from external models to the power of the thing; ultimately, even the identity of the value-object dissolves into the event of a mutable relation.
Conatus is expanded from the actual essence of the singular into a principle for the selection of images, the production of Desire, and socially mediated preservation.
End, after ceasing to be the causality of Nature, is transferred into an index of imagination and finally absorbed into the more general operation of attribution of cause.
Local demonstrations of the uniqueness of substance are absorbed at this level into the more general closure by which all ontological, epistemic, and practical exteriority is excluded.
Infinite modes, finite modes, and Natura Naturata provide the architecture of mediation, but the connection at the present level is the continuation of that mediation in bodies, ideas, and affects.
Traces of corporeal parts remain a local hypothesis of imagination; at the higher level, only the function persists by which the history of affections effectively presents absences and habits.
Taxonomies of singular affects belong to the lower level; at this level their variety is compressed into a grammar of conatus, power, imagination, and attribution of cause.
The local critique of finalism is expanded into a general diagnosis by which partial cognitions, values, and transcendent authorities are produced from corporeal and social mechanisms.
The parallelism of attributes connects ontology, psychology, and the doctrine of affects, but introduces no transverse causality and does not further explain the mechanism of congruence.
The distinction between adequate and partial cause produces a transition of higher order, because it transforms truth and error into action, passion, and forms of social power.
Blessedness remains an incomplete attractor: it orders the direction from necessity to freedom, but the full conversion of cognition into affective stability remains beyond the present determination.
No place outside Nature is admitted from which causality, cognition, value, or action might receive origin or norm.
Neither an alternative world nor an act immune from the series of causes constitutes a real possibility.
A future end, divine choice, and human utility cannot govern the causality of Nature.
Mind and Body are neither separate substances nor causally transverse agents.
The finite subject is neither immediately transparent to itself nor affectively autonomous.
Good, evil, order, and perfection do not constitute intrinsic properties of things or a moral tribunal independent of desire.
The identity of the individual, value, and affect is stabilized neither by permanent matter, nor by an invariant object, nor by a terminal catalogue.
The separation of divine essence, existence, power, and actuality must be false, because it would introduce an ontological gap through which contingency and exteriority would return.
Causally inert cognition must be false, because the difference of adequacy is the same difference that separates action from passion.
The universality of the laws of affects cannot imply uniformity of responses; otherwise the diversity of bodies and the singularity of essences would vanish.
A norm of truth or goodness imposed from outside must be false, because both ideas and appetites are assessed from an intrinsic causal order.
Error as a mere irrational irruption outside Nature must be false; falsity is privative, but its corporeal and social conditions are positively generated.
Freedom that diminishes necessity or requires an uncaused cause must be false; otherwise action would be reduced to ontological exemption, not adequacy.
The supreme absence is the outside itself, whose exclusion encloses substance, cognition, affect, and ethics within the same immanence.
An absolute origin of thought, appetite, or action is ontologically unavailable; every apparent beginning is a connection of an already constituted causal nexus.
A transcendent tribunal judging the actual order, values, and affects before their generation is impossible.
The presence of an external thing or of a subject to itself, unmediated by body, affection, and causal history, is unavailable.
The possibility not yet exhibited is the integral conversion of adequate cognition into affective and social stability; this absence orders ethical direction without demonstrated closure.
Because ontological immanence constitutes Mind from Body, error is not an exception to Nature but an endogenous circuit by which a local affection is projected into a universal structure.
Universal necessity joined with partial causality and imitation of affects explains domination not as a violation of nature, but as the natural reproduction of dependence through social circuits.
The critique of finalism and the genesis of value from appetite entail that normativity is a cartography of compositions that increase or diminish power, not a law placed above desire.
The relational individual, indefinite conatus, and reflection through others constitute a metastable subject, whose identity persists only through continuous corporeal and social reconfiguration.
When contingency is transferred to ignorance and the imagined future orders affect in the present, final causality becomes affective retrojection within the order of efficient causes.
Adequate freedom has relational power: common properties and Generosity can compose actions, although the stable political form of this composition is not yet deduced.
Novelty of state does not require an order of possibility outside actuality: within the necessary order it emerges from a change in the composition of body, relations, and affective direction.
Imagination is the ambiguous seam of the whole system: it sustains superstition and fictive causality, but also preserves conatus and provides the material that adequate cognition reorders.
Ontology, epistemology, and ethics become three heights of one causal integration: reality is expression, truth is adequacy of expression, and action is its sufficient causality.
The agency of the subject is not a binary property but a variable proportion among external causes, the constitution of the body, ideas of affections, and effects intelligible from one's own nature.

Freedom grows through cognition and recomposition of necessity, not through subtraction of causes; external determination is diminished insofar as causal connections are integrated into proper operation.
Social order is an unequal circulation of images, attributions, and variations of power, which simultaneously composes and distinguishes individuals and entangles them in reciprocal circuits.

Time is not a uniform container, but a relation between eternal necessity, the duration of perseverance, and imaginative returns that never reduce the transformed body to an altogether identical state.
Effective intervention must change conditions of composition, attributions of cause, and imaginative orders; command of the will without such reconfiguration reproduces the same partial causality.
The geometrical method performs the naturalization that it affirms: it resolves transcendental and moral terms into definitions, causal connections, variations of power, and recursive circuits.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: The division of being into substance and modes establishes dependence; dependence requires immanence; immanence naturalizes psychology; psychology in turn explains the fiction of exteriority.
Affection generates image, image directs value and Desire, Desire produces action, action changes body and relations, and the changed body receives new affections.
Ignorance of causes produces the opinion of freedom and ends; these images conceal causes, confirm fictive authority, and reproduce the initial ignorance.
Common properties multiply adequate ideas; adequacy increases action; action produces more powerful compositions, whence rational and social amplification becomes possible.
Conatus retains images favorable to power, increases Joy and Desire, and through this selection recursively confirms the conditions of its own perseverance.
The imagined affect of another provokes a response; the response provides a new affective cause; reciprocity thereby escalates into Love, Glory, Hatred, Vengeance, or rivalry.
Affective repetition is never mere identity, because the body is changed through enjoyment and encounters; the same returning image can produce a different or contrary affect.
The principal attractor is adequate causality, around which intelligibility, freedom, preservation of power, and Generosity converge without exit from necessity.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: One necessarily existing Nature → no substantial exteriority → all beings as causally dependent modes.
Expression through attributes → the same individual under Thought and Extension → distinct causal series without substantial dualism.
Encounter of bodies → affection involving the relation of affecting and affected → idea of affection → perspectival perception and variation of power.
Incomplete context of causes → trace and presentification → imaginative association → contingency, end, value, and accidental cause.
Actual essence → conatus → Desire → increase or diminution of power → Joy or Sadness → action or passion according to the quality of the cause.
Image of another's affect → imitation and attribution of cause → reciprocal response → social circuit → reconfiguration of identity and power.
Integration of an idea into the context of causes → more adequate cause → action → active Joy and Desire → Courage and Generosity.
Metaphysics of immanence → constitution of the corporeal Mind → genesis of error and affect → explanation of transcendent projection → return to immanence in the form of causal freedom.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Substance its own cause → immanent causality → finite modes → corporeal individual → Mind as idea of the Body → affection → imagination → conatus → affects → sociality.
Ignorance of causes → imagined contingency and end → projected utility and value → authority of the transcendent → further concealment of causality.
Affection → presentification → imitation → reciprocity → rivalry or composition → change of Body → new affective circuit.
Causal cognition → increased adequacy → diminished passion → action from one's own nature → Courage and Generosity → freedom within necessity.
The opposition of God and world collapses; God is not an artisan alongside things, but immanent causality whose modes constitute the whole field of reality.
The opposition of Mind and Body is reordered into the double expression of one individual, whence the closed mental subject yields place to a corporeal-relational process.
The field of cognition and the field of agency coalesce into one scale of full or partial causality.
Value is reclassified from a property of the object into an index of desire, composition of the body, and change of power.
Sociality is reclassified from an aggregation of preconstituted subjects into a circulation of images, attributions of causes, and reciprocal affects.
Time is reclassified from homogeneous succession into the coordination of eternity, duration, memory, expectation, and irreversible change of the body.
The method of intervention passes from command, judgment, and catalogue to genetic analysis of compositions, causal contexts, and circuits of amplification.
At the level of surface, God, Nature, Mind, Body, cognition, will, Desire, Joy, Sadness, and social relations operate.
At the structural level, all these objects are distributed through immanent causality, relational individuation, affections, conatus, adequacy, and affective circuits.
At the metastrategic level, the question is transferred from choice, end, and judgment to generation, attribution of cause, composition of power, and conditions of intervention.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality is one necessary production, singular things are persisting relations, and time is the nexus of eternity with duration and presentification.
At the methodological and performative level, the system effectuates the very naturalization it asserts through negations of exteriority, genetic deductions, and causal redefinitions.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Attributes are conceived through themselves, but their distinction remains to be positively coordinated with the numerical unity of substance; the exclusion of plurality does not fully replace the connection.
Divine causality determines all modes, while finite things are immediately produced by finite things; the mediation between eternal productivity and singular series remains compressed.
Parallelism preserves the identity of the process of Mind and Body without causal interaction, but does not explain the positive mode of this congruence beyond double expression.

Falsity is called a privation of cognition, although error is positively produced by corporeal and social mechanisms; privation explains the normative form, genesis the causality of the thing, but their connection remains delicate.
The necessity of all ideas must be composed with the normative distinction between adequacy and inadequacy without an external tribunal.
Ethical and political direction rests on adequate cognition, but the transition from understood necessity to the stable transformation of affects and collectives remains incomplete.
Infinity changes from the exclusion of a limit into productive power whose effects are necessarily actualized.
The Body changes from the object of the Mind into a relational individual, then into variable power that orders cognition, affect, and value.
Imagination changes from general prejudice into a neutral mechanism, then into a conative and social operator that sustains both capture and preservation.
Adequacy changes from a quality of truth into active causality, while inadequacy passes from epistemic partiality into passion and social dependence.
Freedom changes from an indeterminate faculty into the necessity of one's own nature and finally into a variable degree of adequate causality.
Perfection and value change from external conformity into the power of the singular, then into an affective relation whose object itself loses axiological stability.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is an immanent machine of self-expression, a network of causes and bodies in which effects do not leave Nature but locally redistribute its power.
The subject is a corporeal and mental vortex persisting through conatus, permeable to external causes and images of others, whose autonomy varies according to adequacy.
Time is a stratified machine in which eternal necessity makes singular things endure, memory brings back absences, and change of the body prevents the identity of return.
Capture is the circuit by which ignorance, utility, the image of a cause, and reciprocal affects bind the individual to external causes while producing the appearance of freedom.
Possible navigation is not escape from the machine, but passage through it from partially understood affections to adequate causal compositions, whose social form is Generosity.
The axioms of immanence, corporeal individuation, imagination, adequacy, conatus, and affective recursion suffice to reconstruct the machine of this metagregis.
The firmest structure is the continuation by which immanent causality produces affection, affection varies cognition and power, and variation is distributed into actions and social circuits.
The conversion of adequate cognition into stable moderation of affects, social composition, and blessedness remains less determined.

The system coheres at this magnitude only if order is read not as a series of doctrines, but as a circuit from metaphysics to body, from body to imagination, and from imagination to the critique of metaphysics.
The reconstruction preserves the generative movement, but the plurality of singular affects, differences of bodies, and the terminal form of active life still resist axiomatic compression.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo homo finitus, ex affectibus et causis externis compositus, libertatem communem et intellectualem acquirere possit sine imperio voluntatis aut exemptione a Natura.

Thesis globalis libertatem constituit ut amplificationem graduatam causalitatis propriae, quae servitutem affectivam per compositionem corporalem, civilem et cognitivam in beatitudinem activam transformat.
Argumentatio est apophatica et reconstructiva: falsas autonomiae, moralitatis et salutis formas excludit, deinde terminos negatos intra causalitatem immanentem denuo constituit.
Motus procedit a reductione affectuum ad servitutem, a servitute ad compositionem socialem potentiarum, atque ab hac compositione ad cognitionem intuitivam et Amorem intellectualem.
Progressio est cumulativa, recursiva, amplificativa et spiralis, quia quisque gradus causam efficaciae gradus sequentis producit et terminus ad operationem priorum retrovertitur.

Clausura non liberationem absolutam sed duplicem stabilitatem praebet: acquiescentiam finitam intra eventus necessarios et beatitudinem quae, ex fine apparente, in causam permanentem activitatis convertitur.
[Persistent] Natura ex necessitate immanenti agit; libertas igitur non causalitatem tollit, sed modum quo necessitas per rem finitam explicatur mutat.
[Persistent] Passio est determinatio corporalis et ideationalis cuius causa a subiecto tantum partialiter explicatur; actio crescit prout idea causae adaequatur.
[Mutating] Conatus transit ab essentia perseverandi ad virtutem rationalem, compositionem communem et actionem intellectualem beatificam, identitate directionis servata.
[Mutating] Libertas est gradus causalitatis adaequatae qui primum affectus ordinat, deinde condiciones corporales et civiles componit, postremo in stabilitatem intellectualem extenditur.
[Persistent] Cognitio efficax repraesentatio iners esse nequit: veritas tantum potentiam auget ubi affectum, corpus, institutionem aut ordinem imaginum causaliter immutat.
[Emergent] Finitas, quae causis externis servitutem exponit, eadem dependentia est ex qua compositio corporum, mutuum auxilium et potentia communis generantur.
[Mutating] Corpus ex sede affectionum in infrastructuram materialem libertatis et tandem in dispositionem positivam ad ampliorem actionem Mentis mutatur.
[Mutating] Ratio vim obtinet tantum cum ex norma intelligibili in affectum contrarium, cupiditatem activam, institutionem stabilem et transitum ad intuitionem convertitur.
[Mutating] Socialitas ab imitatione conflictiva ad Civitatem coercitivam et inde ad infrastructuram cooperationis rationalis progreditur, origine passionali numquam omnino deleta.
[Emergent] Bonum, malum, iustum et iniustum sunt instrumenta comparativa potentiae finitae; in libertate perfecta functionem terminaliter amittunt.
[Mutating] Necessitas ex signo dominationis externae in obiectum intellectus et formam ontologicam libertatis sapientis invertitur.
[Attractor] Intellegere, cognitio Dei, acquiescentia, intuitio, Amor intellectualis et beatitudo constituunt unum attractorem ascensionalem potentiae non-rivalis.
[Emergent] Tempus affectivum bifurcatur inter durationem imaginativam, quae praesentiam et intensitatem distribuit, et aeternitatem intelligibilem, quae successionem et memoriam non continuat.
[Terminal] Sapientis beatitudo non est praemium virtutis sed exercitium eius, quo positio terminalis in causam conservandae libertatis convertitur.

Lætitia et Tristitia identitatem directionalem servant, sed ex indicibus mutationis affectivae in criterios ethicos et tandem in differentiam inter laetitiam activam et fluctuationem passivam amplificantur.
Cupiditas ex affectu primitivo in essentiam conatus, cupiditatem rationalem et genealogiam actionis transit; obiectum eius causalitati originis subordinatur.
Veritas functionem mutat: ex auctoritate polemica fit vis affective condicionata, deinde technica corporalis et intellectualis transformationis.
Corpus ex correlato passionis in infrastructuram nutritionis et laboris, deinde in instrumentum ampliandae potentiae Mentis migrat.
Socialitas redit functione mutata: imaginatio alterius conflictum parit, Civitas eum coercet, cooperatio rationalis dependentiam in amplificationem convertit.
Libertas ab exclusione decreti indeterminati ad ecologiam materialiter sustentatam et tandem ad mutationem proportionis inter actionem et passionem transit.
Necessitas, initio negatio liberi decreti, in condicionem acquiescentiae et postremo in formam libertatis intellectualis absorbetur.
Vocabula moralia ab institutione affectiva ad comparationem rationalem migrant et, libertate perfecta approximata, opere navigationis peracto recedunt.
Dei cognitio ab attractore intellectionis ad acquiescentiam et Amorem intellectualem progreditur, dum amor reciprocus et anthropomorphicus invertitur in actionem reflexivam.
Imaginatio res absentes affective praesentat et rationem praeparat, sed in aeternitate memorativa operatione sua exhausta terminaliter evanescit.
Taxonomiae affectuum et casus actuum manent machinae locales; hoc gradu servantur tantum ut probationes legis qua causa, intensitas et totum potentiae valorem constituunt.
Differentiae temporales et concursus imaginum sursum amplificantur in doctrinam generalem de distributione praesentiae affectivae, sed nondum ipsae aeternitatem intelligibilem constituunt.
Aestimatio actuum singulorum absorbetur in genealogiam causae: eadem species exterior potest passionem, actionem rationalem aut virtutem exprimere.
Trias affectuum, doctrina affectus fortioris et relatio affectionum ad Deum unitates inferiores coniungunt, quia mutationem potentiae in transitum cognitivum convertunt.
Transitus praesentis gradus fit ubi cognitio desinit esse mera veritas et fit affectus activus, dispositio corporalis atque causa laetitiae intellectualis.
Civitas transitum maiorem efficit cum potestas coercitiva in iura, cooperationem materialem et causalitatem propriam civium convertitur.
Distinctio durationis et aeternitatis unitates superiores coniungit, dum aptitudo Corporis fit commissura inter praxim temporalem et cognitionem non successivam.
Moralitas tristitiae, inventarium affectuum et refutatio voluntatis fiunt secundaria, quia eorum opera negativa in machinam positivam cooperationis et beatitudinis absorbetur.
Libertas neque decretum indeterminatum neque imperium voluntatis est; nulla actio humana nexum causarum naturalium interrumpit.
Natura nec fines externos nec ordinem moralem transcendentem nec Deum voluntate mutabilem admittit.
Cognitio vera, si affectum et ordinem Corporis non mutat, passionem sola contradictione logica superare nequit.
Individuum sibi sufficiens excluditur, quia corpus, res externae, alii homines et Deus intra ipsam constitutionem potentiae agunt.
Utilitas propria et commune bonum non sunt contraria, nisi conatus sub imaginatione competitiva et causalitate inadaequata consideretur.
Civitas et libertas non sunt oppositiones absolutae; discrimen verum est inter administrationem metus et productionem potentiae communis.
Corpus non est adversarius Mentis aut aeternitatis, sed condicio sine qua affectus ordinari et intellectus amplificari nequeunt.
Aeternitas non est continuatio memoriae personalis, neque virtus ex spe praemii, metu poenae aut iudicio post mortem pendet.
Falsum esse oportet Naturam a legislatore finali vel Deo personali ordinari, quia omnis norma valida ex relationibus immanentibus potentiae generatur.
Falsum esse oportet mentem abstractam sine affectu et corpore veritatem inertem in imperium practicum convertere posse.
Falsum esse oportet subiectum esse substantiam clausam aut extra Deum subsistere, quia libertas ex relationibus adaequate compositis nascitur.
Falsum esse oportet speciem externam actus valorem eius continere; passio et actio discernuntur ex modo causationis, non ex similitudine operis.
Falsum esse oportet coactionem securitatemque per se cooperationem rationalem producere; communitas actualis mediationes affectivas, iuridicas et materiales postulat.
Falsum esse oportet aeternam Mentis identitatem cum historia memorativa personae coincidere aut mensura temporali definiri posse.
Ontologice inadmissibilis est locus exterior Naturae ex quo subiectum finitum causas totius sine participatione contemplaretur.
Systema circum absentiam conversionis instantaneae veritatis in potentiam ordinatur; nulla claritas minima per se transmutationem passionis praestat.
Impossibilis est status hominis finiti omni passione, corpore, societate et causa externa absolute liberati.
Absentia iudicis remunerantis et Dei affective reciproci cogit virtutem causam immanentem atque sufficientem sui ipsius fieri.
Systema circum pontem incompletum inter passionem actualem et libertatem perfectam laborat: affectus rationalis, Civitas cooperativa et experientia aeternitatis causaliter nondum plene nectuntur.
Libertas est ecologia potentiae, quia asymmetria causarum externarum tantum per relationem corporalis aptitudinis, cooperationis socialis et intelligentiae adaequatae convertitur.
Veritas vim practicam obtinet cum fit affectus contrarius, cupiditas activa, dispositio institutionalis et laetitia ex cognitione adaequata.
Conatus propriae conservationis structuram non-rivalem acquirit, quia auxilium commune et aliena beatitudo potentiam singularis minuere non debent sed augere possunt.
Corpus est simul terminus partis memorativae pereuntis et medium materiale quo cognitio, libertas et maior participatio actionis intellectualis producuntur.
Necessitas vim inversivam exercet: eadem causalitas quae libertatem arbitrii negat campum immanentem constituit in quo causalitas propria et libertas sapientis crescunt.
Civitas est convertor inter servitutem et libertatem, non terminus liberationis: vim externam in cooperationem mutat, dum Ratio transitum ad actionem intellectualem aperit.
Categoriae boni et mali necessariae sunt dum potentia finita navigat, sed attractore beatitudinis approximato recedunt, quia beatitudo iam non merces sed virtus est.
Tempus ethicorum operum duplicem rationem habet: praesentia imaginativa intensitates distribuit, Ratio utilitates trans durationem ordinat, aeternitas autem successionem omnino suspendit.
Beatitudo totam seriem retroactive ordinat, quia finis apparens in machinam fit quae intellectum auget, passiones minuit et propriam praesentiam conservat.
Subiectum est proportio multiscalaris causalitatum partialium, relationum socialium et idearum adaequatarum, cuius identitas ex potentia agendi potius quam clausura substantialis constat.
Ontologia fit ecologia multiscalaris potentiae, in qua corpora, affectus, institutiones et ideae sunt modi distribuendi causalitatem immanentem.
Libertas neque proprietas individui neque status politicus solus est, sed relatio distributa qua corpus, societas et intellectus causam actionis sufficientius exprimunt.
Epistemologia obtinet statum technologiae causalis, quia cognitio vera affectus, ordinem Corporis et facultatem ulterius cognoscendi simul producit.
Politica fit distributio condicionum causalitatis propriae, cuius mensura est utrum communicatio boni potentiam singularem et communem simul amplificet.
Tempus non est unum medium continuum: affectus inhabitant topologiam praesentiae, deliberatio seriem utilitatum, intellectus autem essentiam non durationalem.
Theologia in ontologiam reflexivam convertitur, quia Deus obiectum supremum manet sine persona affective reciproca, iar Amor intellectualis fit explicatio immanentis sui cognitionis.
Ethica est navigatio finitudinis quae ordinat potentiam donec instrumenta comparativa boni et mali in virtute beatifica propriam necessitatem amittant.

items.text: Causa externa passionem auget, potentiam propriam minuit et ignorantiam causae stabilit; ignorantia autem rem externam iterum quasi dominam affectus figit.
Affectus contrarius ordinationem incipit, ordinatio actionem auget, actio claritatem causae firmat, et claritas ulteriorem passivitatem minuit.
Convenientia rationalis potentias componit, cooperatio potentiam singularis auget, et potentia aucta maiorem cooperationem rationalem efficit.
Conflictus ad coercitionem, coercitio ad securitatem, securitas ad cooperationem tendit; circuitus tamen regreditur si metus fundamentum solum institutionis manet.
Oeconomia Corporis libertatem cognitionis sustinet, cognitio aptitudinem actionis auget, et Corpus ad plures actiones aptum novam cognitionem recipit.
Cognitio et libertas circuitum positivum efficiunt: Ratio cupiditatem intuitionis parit, intuitio laetitiam auget, et laetitia ulteriorem intelligentiam sustentat.
Communicatio boni non-rivalis Amorem auget, auctus Amor participationem aliorum desiderat, et participatio potentiam communem iterum amplificat.
Beatitudo est attractor terminalis et circuitus sui conservativus: quo magis adest, eo plus Mens intelligit et minus ab affectibus externis regitur.
