Creation is no longer situated in prior time, but time itself is reduced within the created order.
The opposition of eternity and time is transferred from a difference of quantity to a difference between stable presence and mutable succession.
«Principium» is reclassified from a merely chronological term to the eternal Word, which is at once the cause of creation and the interior teacher.
Past, present, and future are converted from three regions of things into three modes of the soul's present.
Celestial motion is demoted from the essence of time to an object measured by time.
The measurement of time is transferred from apprehension of a passing thing to comparison of present affections in memory.
Human life is described as a recursively dispersed temporal structure, not as a simple series of exterior events.
Common language about the three times is retained pragmatically, but its literal ontology is revoked.
Altitude 1 — Surface — The immediate object is the understanding of the sentence «In principio fecit Deus caelum et terram» and the answer to the question of what God was doing before creation.
Altitude 2 — Structural — The causal structure distinguishes the Creator, the coeternal Word, the created order, and the operations of the soul by which succession is apprehended.

Altitude 3 — Metastrategic — The text does not overcome the controversy by an answer within the adversary's grammar, but destroys the temporal presupposition of the question and subjects common words to semantic limits.
Altitude 4 — Ontological/Temporal — Divine reality as immutable present, the creature as mutable dependence, and temporal life as distention among memory, attention, and expectation are established.
The proposed axioms suffice to reconstruct the concatenation from confession and exegesis to creation, time, measurement, and spiritual gathering.
It is not yet fully determined whether time is ontologically the affection of the mind itself or can only be measured through the affection of the mind.
The doctrine of the trace explains what is measured after passage, but does not perfectly explain whence common proportionality and certainty of measurement arise.
A tension remains between a present lacking all duration and present attention, which is said to endure and to bring about the transfer of the future into the past.
Eternal reason preserves the novelty of effects without change in God, but does not positively explain the production of succession from a cause wholly without succession.
The possibility of a creature «above times» is admitted, but the manner in which such a creature is neither temporal nor coeternal with God remains indeterminate.
The strongest part of the system is the dissolution of time before times and the distinction of time from bodily motion.

The passage from descriptive distention to normative gathering through the Mediator rests upon theological premises, prayer, and the authority of Scripture; it is not deduced from analysis of time alone.

The reconstruction preserves the text's true movement: false models are excluded, the aporia of time is transferred into the soul, and the phenomenological solution concludes in confession of limit and desire for eternity.
Textus quaerit qua ratione initium Geneseos creationem, informitatem, ordinem et absentiam temporis simul significare possit.
Caelum principaliter creaturam intellectualem Deo contemplando inhaerentem, terra autem materiam informem ex qua mundus corporeus formatur significat, sine exclusione aliorum sensuum verorum.
Argumentatio a reconstructione metaphysica creationis ad disciplinam hermeneuticam pluralitatis verae procedit.
Conceptus tenebrarum et informitatis per privationem purgatur, ut materia neque nihil neque corpus monstruose formatum intelligatur.
Ex relatione inter formam, mutationem et tempus deducuntur duae creaturae temporibus carentes: una perfecte formata per inhaesionem, altera penitus informis.
Disputatio de re creata in disputationem de sensu Scripturae transit per distinctionem inter veritatem rerum et intentionem historicam Moysi.
Incertitudo de singulari intentione humana resolvitur non exclusione sensuum verorum, sed veritate communi, caritate interpretum et amplitudine intentionis Spiritus.
Deus aeternus est, nec substantia, scientia aut voluntas eius temporalem vicissitudinem patiuntur.
Omnis natura vel substantia quae Deus non est a Deo facta est.
Omnis creatura ex nihilo, non ex substantia Dei neque ex materia coaeterna, facta est.
Omnis creatura, quia non est idipsum quod Deus, mutabilitatem habet.
Verbum sive Sapientia increata est Principium coaeternum in quo Deus omnia creat.
Materia informis est aliquid prope nihil, capax tamen formarum ex quibus mundus constituitur.
Informitas perfecta omni specie actuali, ordine et variatione formata caret.
Tempora ex ordinatis mutationibus motuum et formarum fiunt.
Ubi nulla est varietas motuum aut formarum, nulla est vicissitudo temporis.
Caelum caeli est creatura intellectualis formata, Deo non coaeterna et natura mutabilis.
Inhaesio continua creaturae intellectualis Deo impedit ne eius mutabilitas in mutationem actualem exeat.
Aliquid altero prius esse potest aeternitate, tempore, electione aut origine.
Scriptura divina vera est et falsum Spiritui vel ministro veraci attribui non potest.
Sermo Scripturae paucus et humilis diversis intellectus gradibus divinitus accommodatur.
Eadem verba Scripturae plures sensus vere significatos sustinere possunt.
Veritas rei et intentio historica scriptoris sunt diversa obiecta cognitionis.
Caritas est finis et norma legitimi usus Scripturae.
Spiritus sanctus novit et per verba revelat quidquid veri posteris aperiendum est, etiamsi minister humanus unum tantum sensum cogitaverit.
Tenebrae non sunt substantia positiva, sed absentia lucis.
Materia informis non est omnino nihil, quia iam formari potest.
Informitas non est congeries formarum foedarum, insolitarum aut perturbatarum.
Materia informis neque forma intelligibilis, sicut vita vel iustitia, neque res sensibilis actu est.
Creatio neque ex substantia divina neque ex subiecto increato et Deo coaeterno procedit.
Sapientia creata sive caelum intellectuale non est Sapientia increata per quam omnia facta sunt.
Carentia temporis in creatura non est coaeternitas cum Deo.
Prioritas materiae respectu formae non est necessario prioritas temporalis.
Silentium Geneseos de productione alicuius rei non probat eam a Deo non esse factam.
Deus non creat ad modum corporis vel hominis nova voluntate moti, neque eius dictum est sonus temporaliter transiens.
Pluralitas sensuum verorum non est admissio falsitatis, contradictionis arbitrariae aut indifferentiae interpretativae.
Incertitudo de cogitatione Moysi neque veritatem rerum infirmat neque contentionem de intentione eius iustificat.
Tenebrae super abyssum nihil materiae addunt, sed statum eius nondum illuminatum et formatum significant.
Materia informis concipienda est subtractione omnis formae actualis, non fictione formarum deformium.
Formatio capacitatem materiae in species ordinatas actualizat, quarum mutationes tempora mundi constituunt.
Duae creaturae extra vicissitudinem dierum intelliguntur: intellectualis quia non mutatur, informis quia nondum habet quo mutetur.
Creatura intellectualis aeternitatem participat per inhaesionem, sed coaeterna Deo non est, quia facta et mutabilis manet.
Materia ante dies et ante formas est origine, non intervallo temporis.
Locutio «In principio» potest simul ad Sapientiam increatam et ad ordinem originis creaturarum referri.
Nomina caeli et terrae possunt diversas totalitates creatas vel diversas conditiones earum designare, dummodo sensus prolatus verus sit.
Veritas de creatione, forma et tempore certius cognosci potest quam cogitatio singularis quam Moyses scribendo habuit.
Assertio exclusiva de intentione Moysi caret fundamento, ubi plures sensus veri adsunt et mens auctoris directe non videtur.
Interpretes sensuum diversorum concordare possunt, si veritatem communem potius quam proprietatem sententiae sequuntur.
Humilitas superficiei Scripturae fidem rudium sustinet, dum brevitas eius eruditis plures nexus veros aperit.
Plenitudo sensuum divinorum non pendet ab eo quod minister humanus omnes sensus conscie perspexerit.
Interpres unum sensum verum, certum et bonum eligere potest, salva intentione qua sensum ministri quaerit et alios sensus veros non excludit.
Tempus non est receptaculum primarium creationis, sed effectus mutationis actualis in creaturis formatis.
Ordo creatus duos limites temporibus carentes habet: plenitudinem formae Deo inhaerentem et defectum formae prope nihil.
Initium Geneseos structuram dependentiae ontologicae potius quam seriem momentorum ante mundum describit.
Omissio narrativa numquam convertit creaturam in principium ontologice independens, quia universitas creati ex nihilo a Deo pendet.
Auctoritas Scripturae agrum sensuum verorum multiplicat, sed eum veritate divina et exclusione falsi circumscribit.
Inaccessibilitas intentionis humanae interpretationem non dissolvit, sed ab exclusivismo ad pluralitatem veritate et caritate limitatam transfert.
Simplicitas pedagogica et profunditas speculativa sunt operationes eiusdem sermonis canonici, non gradus inter se repugnantes.
Exemplar temporis tamquam spatii per se existentis, in quo etiam informitas et Deus locentur, falsum esse debet.
Necessaria conversio omnis mutabilitatis possibilis in mutationem actualem excluditur, alioquin caelum intellectuale temporibus carere non posset.
Aequatio realitatis cum forma actuali falsa esse debet, alioquin materia informis aut nihil aut iam formata esset.
Informitas ut principium positivum mali vel chaos Deo adversum tacite excluditur.
Praesuppositio qua nihil a Deo factum est nisi cuius factio expresse narratur repudianda est.
Praesuppositio qua veritas unicum tantum sensum verbalem requirit falsa esse debet.
Intentio conscia ministri humani non potest totum ambitum significationis divinae exhaurire.
Veritas non potest privatim possideri vel ex origine interpretis auctoritatem accipere, quia supra omnes mentes communis manet.
Cogitatio informitatis omnino imaginibus formatis carens indisponibilis manet; materia tantum per abstractionem et negationem specierum attingitur.
Actus interior Moysi, qui interpretationem univocam definitive confirmaret, ab interpretibus non videtur et etiam testimonio eius apparenti crederetur potius quam immediate cognosceretur.
Nullum «ante tempus» temporaliter repraesentabile admittitur; origo prae-temporalis narrari potest tantum quasi prioritas esset successio.
Clausura exhaustiva Scripturae praecluditur, quia finita inquisitio neque omnes sensus veros neque totam profunditatem verborum comprehendere potest.
Deus incommutabilis in Verbo + nulla materia coaeterna → creatio ex nihilo → creatura a Deo dissimilis et mutabilis.
Capacitas formarum sine specie → absentia ordinis et variationis → absentia temporis → receptio formarum → mutationes ordinatae → dies et mundus temporalis.
Creatura intellectualis formata + mutabilitas naturalis + inhaesio continua Deo → nulla mutatio actualis → participatio aeternitatis sine coaeternitate.
Distinctio aeternitatis, temporis, electionis et originis → prioritas materiae origine → lectio non chronologica initii Geneseos.
Verba pauca et profunda → sensus candidati multiplices → examen veritatis → exclusio falsi → retentio plurium sensuum verorum.

Veritas rei cognoscibilis + intentio Moysi non directe cognoscibilis + plenitudo Spiritus → recusatio monopolii interpretativi → concordia caritatis → electio unius sensus veri sine clausura ceterorum.
Motus ontologicus procedit: obscuritas verborum → purgatio informitatis → creatio ex nihilo → duplex creatura temporibus carens → distinctio originis a tempore.
Motus disputativus procedit: obiectio interpretum → consensus de veris metaphysicis → multiplicatio lectionum → distinctio rei ab intentione → imminutio certitudinis de mente Moysi.
Motus hermeneuticus procedit: incertitudo intentionis humanae → amplitudo intentionis Spiritus → veritas communis → caritas → electio non exclusiva sensus veri.
«Caelum» et «terra» ex nominibus univoce physicis in signa plurium ordinum creati reclassificantur.
Informitas et tenebrae ex entitatibus imaginatis in limites privativos formae et illuminationis convertuntur.
Tempus ex medio universali in effectum mutationum ordinatarum rerum formatarum transfertur.
Carentia temporis bifariam describitur: supra vicissitudinem per inhaesionem formae, infra vicissitudinem per defectum formae.
Oppositio «prius–posterius» in quattuor rationes separatur, unde ordo originis sine successione temporali cogitari potest.
Interpretatio ex certamine pro unico sensu in agrum pluralitatis verae, falsitate exclusa et caritate ordinata, transfertur.
Intentio auctoris humani manet norma quaerenda, sed desinit esse obiectum eadem certitudine cognoscibile ac veritas rerum.
Humilitas sermonis canonici ex simplicitate conceptus in mechanismum accommodationis et fecunditatis semanticæ reclassificatur.
Gradus superficiei verba «caelum», «terra», «tenebrae» et «in principio» immediate interpretatur.
Gradus structuralis creationem ex nihilo, capacitatem materiae, receptionem formarum, mutationem et productionem temporis connectit.
Gradus metastrategicus contentionem de sensu in distinctionem inter veritatem, intentionem, auctoritatem et caritatem reconstituit.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis Deum incommutabilem, creaturam mutabilem, participationem aeternitatis et tempus emergens distinguit.
Axiomata ontologica et hermeneutica sufficiunt ad utrumque motum argumentationis restituendum: interpretationem creationis et disciplinam pluralitatis sensuum.
Cohaerentia interna maxime nititur distinctionibus inter mutabilitatem et mutationem, inter originem et tempus, atque inter veritatem rei et intentionem scriptoris.
Firmissima deductio est quod sine variatione formarum non sit tempus, unde duplex carentia temporis intelligitur.
Status materiae informis manet incomplete determinatus, quia aliquid esse et omni specie actuali carere affirmatur per notionem capacitatis quae ulterius non resolvitur.
Textus inter persuasionem Moysen omnia vera sensisse et concessionem eum fortasse unum sensum cogitavisse fluctuat; plenitudo Spiritus commissuram tuetur, non ambiguitatem tollit.
Plures attributiones eorundem nominum verae declarantur, sed norma qua sensus diversi simul compatibiles potius quam tantum separatim veri sint non plene formalizatur.
Accommodatio sermonis et amplitudo intentionis divinae auctoritate theologica et analogia potius quam demonstratione independenter conclusa sustentantur.
Restitutio servat motum verum textus ab ontologia formae et temporis ad epistemicam modestiam, pluralitatem veram et concordiam caritatis.
The text asks by what account the beginning of Genesis can signify simultaneously creation, formlessness, order, and the absence of time.

Heaven principally signifies the intellectual creature adhering to God by contemplating Him, while earth signifies formless matter from which the corporeal world is formed, without excluding other true senses.
The argument proceeds from a metaphysical reconstruction of creation to a hermeneutical discipline of true plurality.
The concepts of darkness and formlessness are purified through privation, so that matter may be understood as neither nothing nor a monstrously formed body.
From the relation among form, change, and time are deduced two creatures lacking times: one perfectly formed through adherence, the other utterly formless.
The discussion of the created thing passes into a discussion of the sense of Scripture through the distinction between the truth of things and Moses' historical intention.
Uncertainty concerning a singular human intention is resolved not by excluding true senses, but by common truth, the charity of interpreters, and the breadth of the Spirit's intention.
God is eternal, and neither His substance, knowledge, nor will undergo temporal change.
Every nature or substance that is not God has been made by God.
Every creature has been made from nothing, not from God's substance nor from matter coeternal with Him.
Every creature, because it is not the very same thing as God, possesses mutability.
The Word, or uncreated Wisdom, is the coeternal Beginning in which God creates all things.
Formless matter is something close to nothing, yet capable of the forms from which the world is constituted.
Perfect formlessness lacks every actual species, order, and formed variation.
Times arise from ordered changes of motions and forms.
Where there is no variety of motions or forms, there is no succession of time.
The heaven of heaven is an intellectual creature, formed, not coeternal with God, and mutable by nature.
The continuous adherence of the intellectual creature to God prevents its mutability from issuing into actual change.
One thing can be prior to another in eternity, time, choice, or origin.
Divine Scripture is true, and falsehood cannot be attributed to the Spirit or to a truthful minister.
The sparse and humble speech of Scripture is divinely accommodated to diverse levels of understanding.
The same words of Scripture can support several truly signified senses.
The truth of the thing and the historical intention of the writer are distinct objects of knowledge.
Charity is the end and norm of the legitimate use of Scripture.
The Holy Spirit knows and reveals through words whatever truth is to be disclosed to posterity, even if the human minister thought of only one sense.
Darkness is not a positive substance, but the absence of light.
Formless matter is not altogether nothing, because it can already be formed.
Formlessness is not a heap of ugly, unfamiliar, or disordered forms.
Formless matter is neither an intelligible form, such as life or justice, nor an actual sensible thing.
Creation proceeds neither from divine substance nor from an uncreated subject coeternal with God.
Created wisdom, or the intellectual heaven, is not the uncreated Wisdom through which all things were made.
The lack of time in a creature is not coeternity with God.
The priority of matter with respect to form is not necessarily temporal priority.
Genesis' silence concerning the production of some thing does not prove that it was not made by God.
God does not create in the manner of a body or a human being moved by a new will, nor is His utterance a sound passing temporally.
The plurality of true senses is not an admission of falsehood, arbitrary contradiction, or interpretive indifference.
Uncertainty concerning Moses' thought neither weakens the truth of things nor justifies contention about his intention.
Darkness over the abyss adds nothing to matter, but signifies its state as not yet illuminated and formed.
Formless matter must be conceived through the subtraction of every actual form, not through the fiction of deformed forms.
Formation actualizes matter's capacity into ordered species, whose changes constitute the times of the world.
Two creatures are understood outside the succession of days: the intellectual because it does not change, the formless because it does not yet possess that by which it might change.
The intellectual creature participates in eternity through adherence, but is not coeternal with God, because it remains made and mutable.
Matter is before days and before forms by origin, not by an interval of time.
The expression «In principio» can refer simultaneously to uncreated Wisdom and to the order of the origin of creatures.
The names heaven and earth can designate diverse created totalities or their diverse conditions, provided that the proposed sense is true.
Truth concerning creation, form, and time can be known more certainly than the particular thought Moses had while writing.
An exclusive assertion concerning Moses' intention lacks foundation where several true senses are present and the author's mind is not directly seen.
Interpreters of diverse senses can agree if they follow common truth rather than ownership of an opinion.
The humility of Scripture's surface sustains the faith of the unlearned, while its brevity opens several true connections to the learned.
The fullness of divine senses does not depend upon the human minister's having consciously discerned all senses.
An interpreter can choose one true, certain, and good sense, while preserving the intention by which he seeks the minister's sense and does not exclude other true senses.
Time is not the primary receptacle of creation, but an effect of actual change in formed creatures.
The created order has two limits lacking times: the fullness of form adhering to God and the defect of form close to nothing.
The beginning of Genesis describes a structure of ontological dependence rather than a series of moments before the world.
Narrative omission never turns a creature into an ontologically independent principle, because the whole of creation depends on God from nothing.
The authority of Scripture multiplies the field of true senses, but circumscribes it by divine truth and the exclusion of falsehood.
The inaccessibility of human intention does not dissolve interpretation, but transfers it from exclusivism to a plurality limited by truth and charity.
Pedagogical simplicity and speculative profundity are operations of the same canonical speech, not mutually conflicting levels.
The model of time as a space existing in itself, in which even formlessness and God are located, must be false.
The necessary conversion of every possible mutability into actual change is excluded; otherwise the intellectual heaven could not lack times.
The equation of reality with actual form must be false; otherwise formless matter would be either nothing or already formed.
Formlessness as a positive principle of evil or as chaos opposed to God is tacitly excluded.
The presupposition that nothing was made by God unless its making is expressly narrated must be rejected.
The presupposition that truth requires only one verbal sense must be false.
The conscious intention of the human minister cannot exhaust the whole scope of divine signification.
Truth cannot be privately possessed or receive authority from an interpreter's origin, because it remains common above all minds.
The thought of formlessness entirely devoid of formed images remains unavailable; matter is attained only through abstraction and the negation of species.

Moses' inner act, which would definitively confirm a univocal interpretation, is not seen by interpreters and would be believed even on the basis of his apparent testimony rather than immediately known.
No temporally representable «before time» is admitted; pre-temporal origin can be narrated only as though priority were succession.
The exhaustive closure of Scripture is precluded, because finite inquiry can comprehend neither all true senses nor the whole depth of the words.
Immutable God in the Word + no coeternal matter → creation from nothing → creature unlike God and mutable.
Capacity for forms without species → absence of order and variation → absence of time → reception of forms → ordered changes → days and temporal world.
Formed intellectual creature + natural mutability + continuous adherence to God → no actual change → participation in eternity without coeternity.
Distinction of eternity, time, choice, and origin → priority of matter by origin → non-chronological reading of the beginning of Genesis.
Few and profound words → multiple candidate senses → examination of truth → exclusion of falsehood → retention of several true senses.

Knowable truth of the thing + Moses' intention not directly knowable + fullness of the Spirit → rejection of interpretive monopoly → concord of charity → choice of one true sense without closure upon the others.
The ontological movement proceeds: obscurity of words → purification of formlessness → creation from nothing → two creatures lacking times → distinction of origin from time.

The disputative movement proceeds: objection of interpreters → consensus concerning true metaphysical matters → multiplication of readings → distinction of the thing from intention → diminution of certainty concerning Moses' mind.
The hermeneutical movement proceeds: uncertainty of human intention → breadth of the Spirit's intention → common truth → charity → non-exclusive choice of a true sense.
«Caelum» and «terra» are reclassified from univocally physical names into signs of multiple orders of creation.
Formlessness and darkness are converted from imagined entities into privative limits of form and illumination.
Time is transferred from a universal medium into an effect of the ordered changes of formed things.
The lack of time is described in two ways: above succession through adherence to form, below succession through defect of form.
The opposition «prius–posterius» is separated into four accounts, whence an order of origin without temporal succession can be conceived.
Interpretation is transferred from contest over a single sense into a field of true plurality, with falsehood excluded and ordered by charity.
The intention of the human author remains a norm to be sought, but ceases to be an object knowable with the same certainty as the truth of things.
The humility of canonical speech is reclassified from simplicity of conception into a mechanism of accommodation and semantic fecundity.
The surface level immediately interprets the words «caelum», «terra», «tenebrae», and «in principio».
The structural level connects creation from nothing, matter's capacity, reception of forms, change, and the production of time.
The metastrategic level reconstitutes the contention concerning sense into a distinction among truth, intention, authority, and charity.
The ontological and temporal level distinguishes immutable God, mutable creature, participation in eternity, and emergent time.
The ontological and hermeneutical axioms suffice to reconstruct both movements of the argument: the interpretation of creation and the discipline of the plurality of senses.
Internal coherence depends most greatly upon the distinctions between mutability and change, between origin and time, and between the truth of the thing and the writer's intention.
The strongest deduction is that without variation of forms there is no time, whence the twofold lack of time is understood.
The status of formless matter remains incompletely determined, because that it is something and lacks every actual species is affirmed through a notion of capacity that is not further resolved.

The text fluctuates between the persuasion that Moses perceived all true things and the concession that he may have thought of one sense; the fullness of the Spirit preserves the joint, but does not remove the ambiguity.
Several attributions of the same names are declared true, but the norm by which diverse senses are simultaneously compatible rather than merely separately true is not fully formalized.
The accommodation of speech and the breadth of divine intention are sustained by theological authority and analogy rather than established independently by demonstration.
The reconstruction preserves the text's true movement from the ontology of form and time to epistemic modesty, true plurality, and the concord of charity.
Textus quaerit quo nexu bonitas Dei non indigentis, formatio creaturae, insinuatio Trinitatis, sanctificatio Ecclesiae et requies aeterna ex Genesi intelligantur.
Omne esse, formari, illuminari, bene vivere et quiescere creaturae ex gratuita operatione Dei procedit, qui nullo creato bono eget.
Argumentatio metaphysicam creationis, exegesim trinitariam, allegoriam ecclesialem et refutationem dualismi in unum systema reconstructivum coniungit.
Motus initialis a gratia praeveniente ad distinctionem Dei sufficientis et creaturae dependentis, deinde ad formationem per Verbum et elevationem per Spiritum procedit.
Ordo Geneseos in ordinem ecclesialem convertitur: illuminatio, auctoritas Scripturae, discretio fidelium, opera misericordiae, ministeria spiritualia, sacramenta, continentia et renovatio mentis.
Motus finalis a bonitate singulorum ad bonitatem totius, ab operibus temporalibus ad sabbatum sine vespera, et a divina operatione in nobis ad divinam quietem in nobis transit.
Deus solus simpliciter atque incommutabiliter est, scit et vult, eiusque beatitudo et quies ab essentia eius non differunt.
Deus nullo bono creato eget neque creatione vel perfectione creaturarum perficitur.
Omne creatum esse ex bonitate gratuita Dei accipit, nullo merito creaturae antecedente.
Creatura de nihilo, non de substantia Dei neque de materia Deo extranea, producitur; materia informis ipsa quoque concreatur.
In creatura aliud est esse et aliud formatum esse; in spiritu creato aliud est vivere et aliud sapienter ac beate vivere.
Creatura informis per Verbum revocatur ad unitatem, conversione formatur et illuminatione fit conformis Deo sine aequalitate.
Spiritus sanctus, ut donum et caritas, amorem infundit quo creatura vel sursum ad Deum vel deorsum ad inferiora fertur.
Creatura rationalis nullo bono quod Deo minus est, ne ipsa quidem sibi, ad beatam requiem satiatur.
Quidquid aliquo modo est, in quantum est, bonum est; singula bona sunt, universitas ordinata bona valde est.
Res sunt quia Deus aeternaliter eas videt; creatura autem temporaliter eas videt quia sunt.
Scriptura verbis temporalibus aeternum Verbum ministrat atque intellectui humano auctoritatem superiorem praebet.
Pater, Filius et Spiritus sanctus in primis Geneseos verbis in aenigmate leguntur, sine divisione unius creatoris.
Recta cognitio donorum Dei fit per Spiritum Dei, ita ut Deus in creatura cognoscat, videat et loquatur.
Expositio ordinem creationis atque narrationis Geneseos tamquam figuram formationis et sanctificationis Ecclesiae legit.
Sanctificatio ecclesialis secundum capacitatem progreditur a conversione initiali per disciplinam, opera et imitationem ad renovatum iudicium mentis.
Spiritualis homo iudicat signa, interpretationes et mores corrigibiles sub auctoritate Scripturae, non ipsam Scripturam neque occulta iudicia Dei.
Una res intelligibilis multipliciter enuntiari et una enuntiatio multipliciter vere intelligi potest.
Renovatio temporalis manet sub fide et spe donec opera transeant et creatura in sabbato aeterno requiescat in Deo.
Cultus et ministerium creaturae neque lassitudinem Dei levant neque potestatem eius supplent.
Creatura neque de divina substantia neque de natura hostili, increata et Deo contraria, constituitur.
Creatura neque esse, neque illuminari, neque beatificari antecedenti merito promeretur.
Esse non est idem ac pulchrum esse, nec vivere idem ac sapienter vel beate vivere.
Malum non est natura positiva Deo coaeterna, sed aversio, privatio luminis et inordinatus motus boni creati.
Spiritum aquis superferri non significat motum localem neque eminentiam soli Spiritui secundum divinitatem propriam.
Nulla copia quae Deus non est creaturae rationali plenitudo est.
Esse, nosse et velle in mente humana non sunt ipsa Trinitas, sed exercitatio analogica quae distantiam potius quam comprehensionem ostendit.
Lectio allegorica naturas rerum proprie considerandas non abolet.
Successio verborum et dierum in Scriptura successionem cognitionis, voluntatis vel actionis in Deo non imponit.
Multiplicitas verarum intelligentiarum non est fallacia errorum neque licentia sensuum indiscriminatorum.
Formula qua spiritualis omnia iudicat non extenditur ad auctoritatem Scripturae, status hominum occultos aut destinum eorum qui foris sunt.
Requies Dei neque cessationem operationis neque mutationem temporalem in Deo significat.
Invocatio Dei iam responsio est bonitati quae desiderium inspiravit, vocantem praevenit et aversum convertit.
Prioritas informitatis ad formam ontologica vel expositionis est, non necessario intervallum temporale, quia materia et forma sine mora produci possunt.
Spiritus creatus aversione non desinit esse vel moveri, sed lumen amittit et motus eius fit mors, obscuritas atque dissimilitudo.
Verbum Fiat lux vitam illuminabilem praesupponit, sed tam vita quam illuminatio eadem gratia gratuita sustentantur.
Amor est pondus creaturae: cupiditas deicit ad inquietudinem, caritas autem per Spiritum elevat ad locum proprium, qui est requies in Deo.
Spiritus singulariter superferri dicitur non quia Pater et Filius eminentia careant, sed quia donum caritatis proprie exprimit requiem et elevationem creaturae.
In mente una esse, nosse et velle inseparabiliter distincta sunt; haec unitas distincta ad Trinitatem dirigit, sed immutabilitatem divinam non repraesentat aequaliter.
Conversio fidelium veram lucem iam efficit, sed residua obscuritatis manent donec fides transeat in speciem et corpus redimatur.
Firmamentum figurat auctoritatem Scripturae, quae per ministros mortales dispensatur sed eorum morte non perit atque inferioribus populis superponitur.
Mare figurat cupiditates et societatem infidelium divino limite coercitas; arida figurat animas a mari discretas, Deum sitientes et ad opera misericordiae fecundas.
Sacramenta, miracula et voces corporales necessitati infidelium respondent, dum fideles maturiores per exemplum vitae, continentiam et intelligentiam formantur.
Mens renovata transit ab imitatione hominis melioris secundum genus ad probationem voluntatis Dei ad imaginem Dei, manens tamen sub Scriptura.
In beneficio datum est res exterior, fructus autem recta voluntas datoris; minister spiritualis fructu pascitur quia bono operantis gaudet, non quia indigentia sua tantum solvitur.
Benedictio crescendi piscibus et hominibus attributa figurat multiplicationem signorum corporalium et fecunditatem intellectuum rationalium.
Creaturam bonam videre nondum idem est ac Deum in ea amare; plenus spiritualis visus fit cum bonitas rei ad auctorem refertur.
Opera temporalia bona sunt quia Deus ea in nobis operatur, sed consummatio eorum est requies in qua Deus in nobis quiescit sine propria mutatione.
Creatio, illuminatio, recta voluntas, cognitio, benefactio et requies constituunt diversos gradus unius gratiae praevenientis, non provincias causalitatis creaturae autonomae.
Dualismus ontologicus corruit quia etiam creatura informis bonum essendi a Deo habet, dum malum ex aversione boni creati et non ex substantia aemula oritur.
Ecclesiae sanctificatio est recapitulatio temporalis grammaticae creationis: informitas, vocatio, discretio, fecunditas, multiplicatio, regimen et requies fiunt gradus conversionis.
Oeconomia ecclesialis distribuit media secundum capacitatem: signa sensibilia initiant, exempla ordinant affectus, dona spiritualia illuminant, mens renovata discernit.
Unitas Scripturae multiplicitatem interpretationum generat sine dissolutione veritatis, quia fecunditas sensuum sub auctoritate textus et cognitione per Spiritum continetur.
Divina causalitas humanam operationem non simpliciter substituit, sed eam participative constituit: Deus in homine videt et operatur, homo tamen temporaliter videt, vult et agit.
Finis temporalis ordinis non est perpetuatio operum, sed transitus eorum in requiem; bonitas creationis consummatur non in autosufficientia mundi, sed in fruitione Dei.
Nulla creatura potest se ipsam efficere, formare, illuminare, satiare aut ad consummationem perducere.
Nullus amor est neutralis, quia omnis affectus creaturam aut ad fontem vitae convertit aut ad inferiora conformanda deflectit.
Nulla fruitio creaturae ut finis ultimi ordinem bonitatis servat, etiam si res fruenda secundum esse bona est.
Nulla visio humana praesentis status immediata, plena et divinae autocognitioni aequalis est; signa, tempora, fides et aenigma manent.
Nulla maturitas spiritualis fit independentia a Verbo vel Scriptura, etiamsi mens ab imitatione magistri humani ad proprium iudicium ascendat.
Nulla potestas iudicandi omnia permittit creaturae usurpare occultam divisionem quam Deus solus ante manifesta opera novit.
Nulla actio exterior ex sola materia dati fructuosa est, nisi recta voluntas eam in ordinem caritatis inserat.
Extra causalitatem creatoris nullum residuum ontologicum positivum relinquitur ex quo mundus, malum vel creatura spiritualis independenter proveniat.
Creaturae mutabili praecluditur prospectus ex quo Deum sicut Deus se ipsum cognoscit cognoscere possit.
Consummatio intra ordinem praesentis temporis indisponibilis est; dum fides, signa et opera manent, plena species et quies differuntur.
In Deo impossibilia sunt indigentia, augmentum, successio deliberationis et requies post lassitudinem.
Sabbato ultimo vespera excluditur, quia requies finalis non est pars alterius cycli mutabilitatis.
Machina ontologica procedit hoc ordine: Deus sibi sufficiens → creatio gratuita ex nihilo → informitas dependens → conversio per Verbum → forma et bonitas ordinata.
Machina affectiva procedit hoc ordine: Spiritus ut donum → infusio caritatis → amor ut pondus → elevatio ad Deum → quies in bono creaturae proprio.

Prima series ecclesialis est: tenebrae ignorantiae → vocatio ad paenitentiam → lux conversionis → firmamentum Scripturae → coercitio maris infidelitatis → apparentia aridae fidelium → fructus misericordiae.

Secunda series ecclesialis est: luminaria donorum et ministrorum → sacramenta, miracula et voces ad initiationem → anima viva per continentiam → mens renovata ad imaginem → iudicium spirituale limitatum → ministerium mutuum per datum et fructum.

Machina hermeneutica procedit hoc ordine: enuntiatio corporalis una → intellectus veri multiplices → res intelligibilis una → expressionum corporalium multiplicatio → fecunditas sub auctoritate Scripturae et Spiritu.

Machina consummationis procedit hoc ordine: opera Dei in nobis → bona temporalia et incompleta → perseverantia fidei et spei → transitus ordinis mutabilis → sabbatum sine vespera → Deus quiescens in nobis.
Gratia praeveniens → Deus non indigens → creatura sine merito → informitas → conversio per Verbum → elevatio per Spiritum → requies in Deo.
Lectio trinitaria Geneseos → translatio creationis in Ecclesiam → distinctio graduum capacitatis → institutio per Scripturam et signa → ordinatio affectuum → renovatio mentis → iudicium spirituale.
Multiplicitas signorum et sensuum → visus bonitatis per Spiritum → bonitas singulorum et totius → temporalitas operum → spes consummationis → sabbatum aeternum.
Creatio ex fabricatione indigentiae in donationem plenitudinis reclassificatur.
Lux, tenebrae et informitas ex solis qualitatibus cosmicis in modos conversionis, aversionis et dependentiae ontologicae mutantur.
Amor ex affectu inter alios in principium gravitatis spiritualis, motus et loci proprii creaturae convertitur.
Ordo dierum creationis fit tabula formationis Ecclesiae, distinctionis ministeriorum et maturationis fidelium.
Sacramenta, miracula, praedicatio, exemplum et contemplatio non ut media aemula, sed ut operationes diversis capacitatis gradibus congruentes ordinantur.
Potestas spiritualis ex dominio indefinito in iudicium corrigibile sub auctoritate Scripturae restringitur.
Multiplicitas interpretationum ex signo ambiguitatis in fecunditatem ordinatam unius veritatis reclassificatur.
Oppositio boni et mali ab conflictu substantiarum ad oppositionem conversionis et aversionis transfertur.
Tempus creationis ex mensura actionis divinae in modum receptionis creaturae et narrationis Scripturae mutatur, cui sabbatum sine vespera terminum imponit.
Surface — Littera Geneseos de creatione, Trinitate, bonitate operum et die septimo interpretatur.
Structural — Conversio, Scriptura, sacramenta, dona, opera misericordiae, continentia et iudicium constituunt machinam institutionis Ecclesiae.
Metastrategic — Textus dualismum refellit, iudicium spirituale limitat et multiplicem exegesim intra auctoritatem et Spiritum ordinat.
Ontological/Temporal — Deus immutabilis aeternaliter causat et videt; creatura mutabilis temporaliter recipit, convertitur, operatur et ad requiem sine tempore ordinatur.
Axiomata extracta sufficiunt ad restituendos nexus inter creationem gratuitam, formationem per Verbum, elevationem per Spiritum, Ecclesiam et sabbatum aeternum.
Firmissima compages est distinctio inter Deum sibi sufficientem et creaturam cui esse, forma, lumen, bonum opus atque requies donantur.
Systema interne cohaeret quatenus conversionem et aversionem ad eandem ontologiam boni creati refert atque principium mali substantiale excludit.
Criterium quo multiplices intelligentiae verae ab interpretationibus falsis discernantur auctoritate, Spiritu et caritate circumscribitur, sed non in regulam plenam formaliter explicatur.
Transitus ab aeterno actu Dei ad successionem temporalem creaturae affirmatur per distinctionem Verbi et locutionis temporalis, sed modus relationis causaliter non absolvitur.
Assertio praefatoria universa nullo alio fine condita esse quam formatione Ecclesiae latius patet quam probatio corporis, quae ordinem creationis Ecclesiam figurare demonstrat.
Formula spiritualem omnia iudicare per exclusiones restringitur, sed principium generale quo ambitus iudicabilium definitur ex exemplis potius quam ex regula deducitur.
Divina operatio in voluntate humana responsabilitatem non tollere praesupponitur, quamvis articulatio inter gratiam causantem et actum proprium incompleta maneat.
Aequalitas rationalis feminae et subordinatio corporalis eius per analogiam actionis rationi subiectae componuntur, sed nexus inter aequalitatem naturae et ordinem subiectionis non ulterius solvitur.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus ab invocatione et creatione ad allegoriam ecclesialem, hermeneuticam fecunditatis, bonitatem universi et requiem finalem.

The text asks by what connection the goodness of God, who is not in need, the formation of creation, the intimation of the Trinity, the sanctification of the Church, and eternal rest are to be understood from Genesis.
Every being, formation, illumination, good living, and resting of creation proceeds from the gratuitous operation of God, who needs no created good.
The argument joins the metaphysics of creation, Trinitarian exegesis, ecclesial allegory, and the refutation of dualism into one reconstructive system.
The initial movement proceeds from prevenient grace to the distinction between self-sufficient God and dependent creation, then to formation through the Word and elevation through the Spirit.

The order of Genesis is converted into ecclesial order: illumination, the authority of Scripture, discernment of the faithful, works of mercy, spiritual ministries, sacraments, continence, and renewal of the mind.

The final movement passes from the goodness of individual things to the goodness of the whole, from temporal works to the sabbath without evening, and from divine operation in us to divine rest in us.
God alone simply and unchangeably is, knows, and wills, and his blessedness and rest do not differ from his essence.
God needs no created good and is not perfected by the creation or perfection of creatures.
Every created being receives being from the gratuitous goodness of God, with no preceding merit of the creature.
The creature is produced from nothing, not from the substance of God nor from matter extraneous to God; formless matter itself is also created together with it.
In the creature, being is one thing and being formed another; in created spirit, living is one thing and living wisely and blessedly another.
Formless creation is recalled to unity through the Word, is formed by conversion, and by illumination becomes conformed to God without equality.
The Holy Spirit, as gift and charity, infuses the love by which creation is borne either upward toward God or downward toward lower things.
The rational creature is not satisfied for blessed rest by any good less than God, not even by itself.
Whatever in any way is, insofar as it is, is good; individual things are good, and the ordered universe is very good.
Things are because God eternally sees them; but the creature sees them temporally because they are.
Scripture ministers the eternal Word in temporal words and supplies human understanding with a higher authority.
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are read enigmatically in the first words of Genesis, without division of the one Creator.
Right knowledge of God's gifts occurs through the Spirit of God, so that God may know, see, and speak in the creature.
The exposition reads the order of creation and of the narrative of Genesis as a figure of the formation and sanctification of the Church.
Ecclesial sanctification progresses according to capacity from initial conversion through discipline, works, and imitation to the renewed judgment of the mind.
The spiritual person judges corrigible signs, interpretations, and morals under the authority of Scripture, not Scripture itself nor the hidden judgments of God.
One intelligible thing can be expressed in many ways, and one expression can be truly understood in many ways.
Temporal renewal remains under faith and hope until works pass away and creation rests in God on the eternal sabbath.
The worship and ministry of creation neither relieve God's weariness nor supplement his power.
The creature is constituted neither from divine substance nor from a hostile, uncreated nature contrary to God.
The creature does not merit being, illumination, or beatification by preceding merit.
To be is not the same as to be beautiful, nor is to live the same as to live wisely or blessedly.
Evil is not a positive nature coeternal with God, but aversion, privation of light, and the disordered movement of created good.
The Spirit's being borne over the waters does not signify local movement or an eminence belonging to the Spirit alone according to his proper divinity.
No abundance that is not God is fullness for the rational creature.
Being, knowing, and willing in the human mind are not the Trinity itself, but an analogical exercise that shows distance rather than comprehension.
Allegorical reading does not abolish the natures of things that must properly be considered.
The succession of words and days in Scripture does not impose a succession of knowledge, will, or action upon God.
The multiplicity of true understandings is not the deception of errors nor a license for indiscriminate meanings.
The formula that the spiritual person judges all things does not extend to the authority of Scripture, the hidden states of human beings, or the destiny of those who are outside.
God's rest signifies neither cessation of operation nor temporal change in God.
The invocation of God is already a response to the goodness that inspired desire, anticipated the one calling, and converted the one turned away.
The priority of formlessness to form is ontological or expository, not necessarily a temporal interval, because matter and form can be produced without delay.
By aversion, created spirit does not cease to be or to move, but loses light, and its movement becomes death, darkness, and dissimilarity.
The word Fiat lux presupposes illuminable life, but both life and illumination are sustained by the same gratuitous grace.
Love is the weight of the creature: cupidity casts it down into restlessness, but charity through the Spirit raises it to its proper place, which is rest in God.
The Spirit alone is said to be borne over, not because Father and Son lack eminence, but because the gift of charity properly expresses the creature's rest and elevation.
In one mind, being, knowing, and willing are inseparably distinct; this distinct unity directs toward the Trinity, but does not represent divine immutability equally.
The conversion of the faithful already produces true light, but remnants of darkness remain until faith passes into sight and the body is redeemed.
The firmament figures the authority of Scripture, which is dispensed through mortal ministers but does not perish with their death and is set above inferior peoples.
The sea figures desires and the society of unbelievers restrained by a divine boundary; dry land figures souls separated from the sea, thirsting for God and fruitful in works of mercy.
Sacraments, miracles, and bodily voices answer the need of unbelievers, while more mature faithful are formed through the example of life, continence, and understanding.
The renewed mind passes from imitation of a better human being according to kind to testing the will of God according to the image of God, while nevertheless remaining under Scripture.

In a benefit, the external thing is the gift, but the fruit is the right will of the giver; the spiritual minister is nourished by the fruit because he rejoices in the good of the doer, not because only his own need is relieved.
The blessing of increase attributed to fish and human beings figures the multiplication of bodily signs and the fecundity of rational understandings.
To see a good creature is not yet the same as to love God in it; full spiritual sight occurs when the goodness of the thing is referred to its author.
Temporal works are good because God works them in us, but their consummation is the rest in which God rests in us without his own change.
Creation, illumination, right will, knowledge, beneficence, and rest constitute diverse stages of one prevenient grace, not provinces of autonomous creaturely causality.
Ontological dualism collapses because even formless creation has from God the good of being, while evil arises from the aversion of created good and not from a rival substance.

The sanctification of the Church is a temporal recapitulation of the grammar of creation: formlessness, calling, discernment, fecundity, multiplication, governance, and rest become stages of conversion.
Ecclesial economy distributes means according to capacity: sensible signs initiate, examples order affections, spiritual gifts illuminate, and the renewed mind discerns.

The unity of Scripture generates a multiplicity of interpretations without dissolution of truth, because the fecundity of meanings is contained under the authority of the text and knowledge through the Spirit.

Divine causality does not simply replace human operation, but constitutively establishes it by participation: God sees and works in the human being, yet the human being sees, wills, and acts temporally.
The end of temporal order is not the perpetuation of works, but their passage into rest; the goodness of creation is consummated not in the self-sufficiency of the world, but in the enjoyment of God.
No creature can make, form, illuminate, satisfy, or bring itself to consummation.
No love is neutral, because every affection either converts the creature to the fountain of life or turns it aside to conform to lower things.
No enjoyment of a creature as ultimate end preserves the order of goodness, even if the thing enjoyed is good according to being.
No human vision of the present state is immediate, full, and equal to divine self-knowledge; signs, times, faith, and enigma remain.
No spiritual maturity becomes independence from the Word or Scripture, even if the mind rises from imitation of a human teacher to its own judgment.
No power of judging all things permits the creature to usurp the hidden division which God alone knows before manifest works.
No external action is fruitful from the matter of the gift alone, unless right will inserts it into the order of charity.
Outside the causality of the Creator, no positive ontological residue remains from which the world, evil, or spiritual creature might independently arise.
The mutable creature is barred from any perspective by which it could know God as God knows himself.
Consummation is unavailable within the order of present time; while faith, signs, and works remain, full sight and rest are deferred.
In God, need, increase, succession of deliberation, and rest after weariness are impossible.
Evening is excluded from the final sabbath, because final rest is not part of another cycle of mutability.
The ontological machine proceeds in this order: self-sufficient God → gratuitous creation from nothing → dependent formlessness → conversion through the Word → form and ordered goodness.
The affective machine proceeds in this order: Spirit as gift → infusion of charity → love as weight → elevation to God → rest in the creature's proper good.

The first ecclesial series is: darkness of ignorance → call to repentance → light of conversion → firmament of Scripture → restraint of the sea of unbelief → appearance of the dry land of the faithful → fruit of mercy.

The second ecclesial series is: luminaries of gifts and ministers → sacraments, miracles, and voices for initiation → living soul through continence → renewed mind according to the image → limited spiritual judgment → mutual ministry through gift and fruit.

The hermeneutical machine proceeds in this order: one bodily utterance → multiple true understandings → one intelligible thing → multiplication of bodily expressions → fecundity under the authority of Scripture and the Spirit.

The machine of consummation proceeds in this order: God's works in us → temporal and incomplete goods → perseverance of faith and hope → passage beyond mutable order → sabbath without evening → God resting in us.
Prevenient grace → God not in need → creature without merit → formlessness → conversion through the Word → elevation through the Spirit → rest in God.

Trinitarian reading of Genesis → translation of creation into the Church → distinction of degrees of capacity → instruction through Scripture and signs → ordering of affections → renewal of the mind → spiritual judgment.
Multiplicity of signs and meanings → sight of goodness through the Spirit → goodness of individual things and of the whole → temporality of works → hope of consummation → eternal sabbath.
Creation is reclassified from the fabrication of need into the donation of fullness.
Light, darkness, and formlessness are changed from merely cosmic qualities into modes of conversion, aversion, and ontological dependence.
Love is converted from one affection among others into the principle of the creature's spiritual gravity, movement, and proper place.
The order of the days of creation becomes a table of the formation of the Church, the distinction of ministries, and the maturation of the faithful.
Sacraments, miracles, preaching, example, and contemplation are ordered not as rival means, but as operations suited to different degrees of capacity.
Spiritual power is restricted from indefinite dominion to corrigible judgment under the authority of Scripture.
The multiplicity of interpretations is reclassified from a sign of ambiguity into the ordered fecundity of one truth.
The opposition of good and evil is transferred from a conflict of substances to the opposition of conversion and aversion.
The time of creation is changed from a measure of divine action into a mode of the creature's reception and of Scriptural narration, to which the sabbath without evening sets an end.
Surface — The letter of Genesis is interpreted concerning creation, the Trinity, the goodness of works, and the seventh day.
Structural — Conversion, Scripture, sacraments, gifts, works of mercy, continence, and judgment constitute the machine of the Church's formation.
Metastrategic — The text refutes dualism, limits spiritual judgment, and orders multiple exegesis within authority and the Spirit.
Ontological/Temporal — Immutable God eternally causes and sees; mutable creation receives, converts, works temporally, and is ordered toward rest without time.
The extracted axioms suffice to restore the connections between gratuitous creation, formation through the Word, elevation through the Spirit, the Church, and the eternal sabbath.
The firmest framework is the distinction between self-sufficient God and the creature to which being, form, light, good work, and rest are given.
The system coheres internally insofar as it refers conversion and aversion to the same ontology of created good and excludes a substantial principle of evil.
The criterion by which multiple true understandings are distinguished from false interpretations is circumscribed by authority, Spirit, and charity, but is not formally explained as a complete rule.

The passage from the eternal act of God to the temporal succession of creation is affirmed through the distinction between the Word and temporal speech, but the mode of relation is not causally resolved.

The prefatory assertion that all things were created for no other end than the formation of the Church extends more broadly than the proof of the body, which demonstrates that the order of creation figures the Church.

The formula that the spiritual person judges all things is restricted through exclusions, but the general principle by which the scope of what may be judged is defined is derived from examples rather than from a rule.
Divine operation in the human will is presumed not to remove responsibility, although the articulation between causing grace and proper act remains incomplete.

The rational equality of woman and her bodily subordination are reconciled through the analogy of action subject to reason, but the connection between equality of nature and the order of subjection is not further resolved.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text from invocation and creation to ecclesial allegory, the hermeneutics of fecundity, the goodness of the universe, and final rest.
Systema quaerit quomodo homo a principio suo alienatus causam peccati, erroris et inquietudinis agnoscat atque ad Deum, quem imperfecte cognoscit, convertatur.
Thesis globalis statuit omne bonum a Deo procedere, peccatum autem ex conversione voluntatis ad bonum creatum extra ordinem summi boni oriri.
Argumentatio confessionem autobiographicam, analysim affectuum, criticam institutionum et correctionem ontologicam in unam genealogiam aversionis componit.
Motus ab origine memoriae abscondita per infantiam, adolescentiam et errorem doctrinalem progreditur, sed ordinem chronologicum in recursionem eiusdem amoris inordinati transformat.
Inordinatio crescit ab appetitu nondum efficaciter moderato ad transgressionem propter ipsam transgressionem, deinde ad captationem intellectus per falsam speciem veritatis.
Confessio praeteritum non simpliciter refert, sed memoriam ita reordinat ut culpabilis dispersio intra antecedentem providentiam legatur.
Misericordia non tantum post lapsum remittit, sed per fidem, correptionem, testimonium, poenam et dilationem ipsam facultatem confessionis praeparat.
Clausura est attractiva potius quam consummata: requies in Deo terminum constituit, sed conversio adhuc per dilationem providentialem promittitur, non narratur ut completa.
[Persistent] Deus est principium omnis esse et boni, summum bonum stabile, veritas immutabilis atque rector universi.
[Attractor] Creatura humana ad Deum ordinatur et, sive hoc desiderium agnoscat sive ignoret, extra eum in inquietudine et fame persistit.
[Persistent] Bona creata, facultates et signa suam bonitatem retinent, sed neque summum bonum supplere neque rectum usum suum garantire possunt.
[Mutating] Peccatum est ordinatio amoris qua voluntas a Deo ad bona particularia convertitur, in multa diffluit et partem privatam pro bono universali usurpat.
[Mutating] Malum non est substantia positiva, sed deordinatio, defectus et privatio boni quae agentem atque ordinem socialem realiter deformant.
[Emergent] Vitium operatur parasitice, quia speciem boni divini imitatur et libertatem, potestatem, societatem vel veritatem in formam diminutam convertit.
[Persistent] Alienatio a Deo non est distantia localis nec independentia ontologica, sed relatio affectiva deformata intra permanentem dependentiam creaturae.
[Mutating] Species moralis actus ex fine affectus, intentione, usu et tempore iudicatur, dum effectus utiles possunt providentiae tribui sine absolutione agentis.
[Mutating] Familia, schola, consortium et communitas doctrinalis appetitus non solum continent, sed etiam praemia, pudorem et criteria veritatis distribuendo amplificant.
[Emergent] Cognitio moraliter ordinatur: eloquentia, rectitudo signorum, sensus et nomina sacra veritatem non praestant, si animus phantasmatibus et superbiae subicitur.
[Mutating] Memoria confessionalis identitatem ultra recordationem directam restituit et praeteritum ex delectatione vel neutralitate in iudicium atque conversionem transfert.
[Persistent] Misericordia divina confessionem antecedit et errores, correptiones, poenas atque moras ad utilitatem ordinat sine approbatione culpae.
[Emergent] Reditus requirit simul conversionem amoris et modi cognoscendi, fide, Christo, humilitate et mediationibus providentiae sustentatam.
[Terminal] Requies, veritas et delectatio secura tantum in Deo stabili inveniuntur; omnis substitutio creata ad egestatem redit.
Inquietudo initialiter conditio ontologica est, in adolescentia dispersio affectiva fit, deinde ut fames epistemica veritatem in sensibilibus quaerens redit.
Bonum creatum persistit, sed eius functio mutatur ab instrumento male adhibito ad speciem boni vitio imitatam atque tandem ad superficiem per quam error doctrinalis captat.
Inordinatio infantilis non identice repetitur: in adolescentia fit voluntaria transgressio, in errore doctrinali autem migrat in intellectum qui falsam veritatem amplectitur.
Mediatio socialis a disciplina familiae et scholae ad consortium delinquentium, inde ad auctoritatem rhetoricam et sectariam transfertur.
Memoria ab instrumento reconstructionis originum in operationem moralem mutatur, qua delectatio criminis vel neutralitas praeteriti excluditur.
Libertas, primo sub tensione inter curiositatem et coactionem posita, invertitur in licentiam transgressionis, deinde per humilitatem ut receptivitas veritatis denuo constituitur.
Dilatio baptismi localiter periculum licentiae auget, sed dilatio correctionis doctrinalis postea in instrumentum providentiae et maturitatis epistemicae mutatur.
Distinctio inter culpam et effectum utilem amplificatur in duplicem causalitatem historiae, ubi voluntas delinquit et misericordia eandem seriem ad confessionem ordinat.
Infantia, furtum piri, spectacula et controversiae Manichaeae manent casus locales; hoc gradu valent ut probationes distinctarum formarum unius aversionis.
Negatio innocentiae infantilis sursum amplificatur in thesim continuitatis affectivae, secundum quam instrumenta et ambitus mutantur, non radix appetitus dominandi.
Inutilitas materialis furti manet probatio singularis, sed efficit transitionem globalem ab explicatione obiecti desiderati ad explicationem status voluntatis.
Correctio Manichaeismi non manet polemica localis, sed explicitat structuram iam implicatam in praesentia Dei non spatiali et in malo non substantiali.
Dilatio baptismi et dilatio disputationis non aequantur: prior licentiam involuntarie parere potest, altera capacitatem futuram discendi providentialiter tuetur.
Critica scholae, consortii et sectae coniungitur in propositionem praesentis gradus quod formatio socialis ordinem amoris atque criteria veri simul distribuit.
Creatura neque sui esse neque suae salutis principium est; omnis autonomia absoluta ontologicam dependentiam negat.
Deus neque spatium occupat neque corpus aut phantasma est; propinquitas eius mensura locali definiri non potest.
Malum neque substantia creata neque principium autonomum Deo oppositum est.
Bona creata et instrumenta culturalia neque per se damnantur neque pro fine ultimo haberi possunt.
Rectitudo grammatica, intensitas affectus, species externa facti et copia nominum sacrorum rectitudinem moralem vel veritatem non probant.
Consuetudo, laus socialis et consortium auctoritatem ultimam non habent, quia finis et lex divina formam moralem societatis iudicant.
Transgressio libertatem non constituit, sed dependentiam a bono sub specie autonomiae celat.
Providentia effectum utilem ordinare potest, sed utilitas neque intentionem pravum bonam facit neque culpam agentis aufert.
Systema corrueret si subiectum sui ipsius auctor, possessor sufficiens aut reparator autonomus esset.
Desiderium, lingua, educatio et societas neutralia esse non possunt, quia unumquodque ordinem amoris vel veritatis efficit.
Peccatum ad necessitatem, ignorantiam vel utilitatem materialem redigi non potest, quia voluntas etiam statum transgressionis quaerit.
Epistemologia fundata in superficie sensibili, splendore sermonis aut nomine sacro veritatem discernere non potest.
Ordo moralis neque conventionalismo locali neque uniformitate materialis praecepti per omnia tempora continetur.
Gratia non potest esse mera responsio posterior subiecto iam ad conversionem sufficienti, quia ipsa excitatio, abstinentia et correctio ei attribuuntur.
Praeteritum autobiographicum non est materia moraliter iners, quia recordatio aut veterem delectationem renovat aut causalitatem confessionis constituit.
Nullum extra Deum spatium ontologicum datur in quo creatura stabilitatem, libertatem aut bonum sibi independenter constituat.
Principium mali autonomum est ontologice inadmissibile; etiam deformitas indiget bonitate quam imminuit et imitatur.
Reditus sui causa et sermo Deo adaequatus indisponibiles sunt; confessio procedit intra donum fidei et limitationem linguae.
Transparentia totalis originum, intentionum et providentiae homini negatur, unde memoria, testimonium et auctoritas operantur sine comprehensione exhaustiva.
Clausura conversionis plena adhuc indisponibilis est: promissio reditus ex somnio, lacrimis et providentia vim accipit, sed legem universalem nondum constituit.
Peccatum per aetates eandem structuram aversionis servat, sed ab appetitu elementari ad voluntatem transgressivam et cognitionem captam crescit.
Schola, sodalitas et secta sunt mutationes unius machinae socialis quae pudorem, gloriam et credibilitatem ita distribuit ut inordinatio se confirmet.
Bona et signa possunt captationis instrumenta fieri non quia bonitatem amittunt, sed quia eorum similitudo cum bono quaesito substitutionem credibilem efficit.
Furtum et error Manichaeus variantes eiusdem imitationis sunt: alter omnipotentiam per transgressionem, alter veritatem per nomina et phantasmata usurpat.
Cum Deus non spatialiter absit et malum substantia non sit, alienatio necessario fit imminutio relationis, ordinis et participationis potius quam migratio ad alteram realitatem.
Confessio causalitatem bifurcat: culpam voluntati restituit, sed facultatem agnoscendi, abstinendi et redeundi misericordiae antecedenti attribuit.
Dilatio est operator ambivalens: sine recta ordinatione spatium licentiae aperit, sub providentia autem immaturam disputationem suspendit et correctionem praeparat.
Universalitas iustitiae non ex identitate factorum externorum, sed ex stabilitate ordinis qui intentiones, officia et tempora distinguit, derivatur.
Conversio intellectus pars conversionis affectus est, quia superbia non solum bonum male eligit, sed etiam instrumenta quibus verum agnoscitur deformat.
Subiectum autobiographicum non est conscientia sui transparens, sed ens acceptum, socialiter mediatum et confessione retrospectiva recollectum.
Tempus humanum est campus mutationis, distributionis moralium officiorum et dilationis providentialis, totum tamen sub immutabili praesentia divina continetur.
Causalitas moralis asymmetrica est: homo defectum producit per aversionem, Deus autem bona antecedentia et reordinationem consequentium praebet sine auctoritate mali.
Institutio politica et culturalis efficitur regimen affectuum, quia honorem, pudorem, eloquentiam et auctoritatem ita distribuit ut aliqua desideria probabilia atque laudabilia videantur.
Cognitio Dei non acquiritur sola accumulatione propositionum, sed mutatione subiecti cognoscentis ab exterioritate superba ad humilem capacitatem recipiendi.
Forma confessionis ipsa doctrinam perficit, quia eadem memoria quae dispersionem refert eam sub attributione culpae et misericordiae reordinat.
Vera libertas non est sui fundatio, sed capacitas boni summi recipiendi; licentia contra ordinem fit servitus imagini mutilae potentiae.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Fames Dei non agnita bonum creatum absolutum eligit; substitutum insufficiens inanitatem auget, quae novam fugam ad exteriora parit.
Laus socialis inordinationem remunerat, remuneratio eius publicam imitationem producit, et imitatio novam laudem atque ampliorem normarum inversionem stabilit.
Superbia formam humilem respuit, cognitio ad corpora restringitur, phantasma pro veritate accipitur, et falsa doctrina superbiam initialem doctrinaliter confirmat.
Correctio sequitur circuitum quo delectatio illicita amaritudinem parit, amaritudo memoriam excitat, memoria confessionem, confessio autem novam ordinationem desiderii.
Memoria est circuitus bifurcus: crimen recollectum vel delectationem repetit vel, sub confessione, culpam retinens eius vim affectivam convertit.
Requies in Deo est attractor occultus circa quem inquietudo, dispersio et fames negativam suam formam accipiunt.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Donum essendi et bonitatis → dependentia creaturae → appetitus constitutivus summi boni.
Oblivio principii → desiderium non intellectum → quaestus alimenti in rebus insufficientibus.
Bonum inferius absolutum → aversio a bono universali → dispersio → poena immanens egestatis.
Institutio vel consortium → distributio laudis et pudoris → confirmatio affectus inordinati → amplificatio socialis.
Appetitus elementaris → transgressio volita → imitatio libertatis → captatio intellectus sub specie veritatis.
Negatio mali substantialis et Dei corporei → reclassificatio alienationis → correctio modi cognoscendi et iudicandi.
Misericordia antecedens → correptio et dilatio → memoria confessionalis → recollectio bonorum → reditus promissus ad requiem.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Dependentia creata → oblivio principii → appetitus infantilis → disciplina socialis → dispersio adolescentiae → transgressio gratuita → fames sapientiae → error doctrinalis → praeparatio reditus.
Bonum creatum → usus inordinatus → imitatio perversa boni divini → privatio et egestas → correctio ontologica → reordinatio amoris.
Misericordia antecedens → fides et testimonium → correptio → memoria → confessio → dilatio formativa → promissio requiei.
Peccatum reclassificatur ex serie actuum separatorum in continuum affectivum quod aetates, institutiones et doctrinas per formas crescentes transit.
Familia, schola, sodalitas, theatrum et secta fiunt species unius agri mediatorii in quo facultates, honores et verisimilitudines ordinantur.
Libertas transfertur ab immunitate legis ad participationem recti ordinis, dum transgressio sui fundatrix ut servitus imitationis detegitur.
Epistemologia fit pars asceseos moralis, quia modus videndi Deum, malum et Scripturam ab ordine affectus et humilitate cognoscentis pendet.
Oppositio inter iustitiam universalem et varietatem historicam corruit, quia lex stabilis per officia, personas et tempora distributive operatur.
Malum et providentia non amplius ut causae symmetricae describuntur: privatio ab agente oritur, dum Deus bona servat et consequentia ad correctionem ordinat.
Gradus superficiei continet originem, infantiam, scholam, baptismum dilatum, adolescentiam, furtum, spectacula, studia, Manichaeismum et intercessionem Monnicae.
Gradus structuralis continet circulationem donorum, appetituum, institutionum, imitationum et correctionum quae sub diversis casibus eandem aversionis machinam efficiunt.
Gradus metastrategicus iudicium transfert ab honore, utilitate, affectus vehementia et specie externa ad ordinem amoris, intentionem et auctoritatem divinam.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem ut dependentiam a Deo incorporeo, malum ut privationem et tempus ut campum providentiae distributivae constituit.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus confessionem facit operationem conversionis, quia narratio ipsa culpam, donum et memoriam ad rectas causas refert.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Culpabilis voluntas et misericordia decisive antecedens simul servantur, sed modus concursus earum causaliter non explicatur.
Omne vitium speciem boni imitari dicitur, furtum tamen malitiam ipsam appetere videtur; defectus et bonum apparens imperfecte conciliantur.
Providentia ex actibus pravis utilitatem elicit, sed discrimen inter ordinationem effectuum et participationem causalitatis mali formula completa caret.
Iustitia immutabilis mandata temporaliter diversa sustinet, sed authenticatio mandati divini ab auctoritate pendet cuius criterium intra synthesim incompletum manet.
Phantasmata corporea ut fontes erroris reiciuntur, somnium tamen vim providentialem accipit; distinctio generali regula epistemica non stabilitur.
Appetitus infantilis in adolescentia mutatur ex impulsu instrumentis infirmo in voluntatem quae ipsam positionem contra legem quaerit.
Lingua transit ab instrumento socialiter acquisito ad medium gloriae, deinde ad superficiem doctrinalem qua nomina vera errorem tegunt.
Dilatio mutat valorem structuralem: circa baptismum permissionem peccandi minatur, circa disputationem autem correctionem maturam praeparat.
Eloquentia ab instrumento vanitatis in Hortensio fit excitatio ad sapientiam, sed iterum in splendorem falsae doctrinae labi potest.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est campus participationis non spatialis, in quo omnia a Deo continentur et alienatio intra ipsam dependentiam accidit.
Subiectum est appetitus memoriam excedens, per corpora, signa et societates permeabilis, qui se tantum confessione sub gratia recollegit.
Tempus est distributio mutationum sub aeterno Dei hodie, ubi mora potest lapsum amplificare vel facultatem futurae conversionis formare.
Certamen possibile est navigatio inter bona vera et substitutiones eorum, cuius discrimen requirit ordinationem amoris, humilitatem cognitionis et misericordiam antecedentem.
Axiomata extracta sufficiunt ad restituendum motum ab ontologica dependentia per amplificationes affectivas, sociales et epistemicas ad confessionem reditus dilati.
Structura firmissima est distinctio inter bonum datum et usum inordinatum, una cum malo privativo et veritate quae formam socialem transcendit.
Cohaerentia praesentis gradus non ordine chronologico solo, sed reditu spirali eiusdem aversionis sub formis affectivis, voluntariis et doctrinalibus sustentatur.
Indeterminata manet relatio exacta inter libertatem culpabilem et misericordiam antecedentem, quam synthesis distinguere potest sed non causaliter absolvere.
Indeterminatum etiam manet criterium generale quo mandatum, somnium vel testimonium providentiale ab imaginatione falsa certo discernatur.
Reductioni axiomaticae resistit actus confessionis ipse, quia systema non tantum propositiones de conversione enuntiat, sed memoriam narrando causaliter et affective convertit.
The system asks how a human being alienated from his origin may recognize the cause of sin, error, and restlessness and turn toward God, whom he knows imperfectly.
The global thesis holds that every good proceeds from God, whereas sin arises from the conversion of the will toward a created good outside the order of the highest good.
The argument combines autobiographical confession, analysis of the affects, critique of institutions, and ontological correction into a single genealogy of aversion.
The movement proceeds from the hidden origin of memory through infancy, adolescence, and doctrinal error, but transforms chronological order into a recursion of the same disordered love.
Disorder grows from desire not yet effectively moderated to transgression for the sake of transgression itself, then to the capture of the intellect by a false appearance of truth.
Confession does not simply report the past, but reorders memory so that culpable dispersion is read within antecedent providence.
Mercy not only remits after a fall, but through faith, correction, testimony, punishment, and delay prepares the very capacity for confession.
The closure is attractive rather than consummated: rest in God establishes the end, but conversion is still promised through providential delay, not narrated as complete.
[Persistent] God is the principle of all being and good, the stable highest good, immutable truth, and ruler of the universe.
[Attractor] The human creature is ordered toward God and, whether it recognizes or ignores this desire, persists outside him in restlessness and hunger.
[Persistent] Created goods, faculties, and signs retain their goodness, but can neither replace the highest good nor guarantee their own right use.
[Mutating] Sin is an ordering of love by which the will turns from God toward particular goods, flows out into multiplicity, and usurps a private part as a universal good.
[Mutating] Evil is not a positive substance, but disorder, defect, and privation of good that really deform the agent and the social order.
[Emergent] Vice operates parasitically, because it imitates the appearance of divine good and converts freedom, power, society, or truth into a diminished form.
[Persistent] Alienation from God is neither local distance nor ontological independence, but a deformed affective relation within the creature's enduring dependence.
[Mutating] The moral species of an act is judged from the end of the affect, intention, use, and time, while useful effects may be attributed to providence without absolving the agent.
[Mutating] Family, school, association, and doctrinal community not only restrain desires, but also amplify them by distributing rewards, shame, and criteria of truth.
[Emergent] Knowledge is morally ordered: eloquence, correctness of signs, meanings, and sacred names do not secure truth if the mind is subject to phantasms and pride.
[Mutating] Confessional memory restores identity beyond direct recollection and transfers the past from delight or neutrality into judgment and conversion.
[Persistent] Divine mercy precedes confession and orders errors, corrections, punishments, and delays to benefit without approving guilt.
[Emergent] Return requires at once conversion of love and of the mode of knowing, sustained by faith, Christ, humility, and mediations of providence.
[Terminal] Rest, truth, and secure delight are found only in stable God; every created substitute returns to indigence.
Restlessness is initially an ontological condition, becomes affective dispersion in adolescence, then returns as epistemic hunger seeking truth in sensible things.
Created good persists, but its function changes from an instrument badly used to an appearance of good imitated by vice and finally to a surface through which doctrinal error captures.
Infantile disorder is not repeated identically: in adolescence it becomes voluntary transgression, while in doctrinal error it migrates into an intellect that embraces false truth.
Social mediation is transferred from the discipline of family and school to the association of delinquents, thence to rhetorical and sectarian authority.
Memory changes from an instrument of reconstructing origins into a moral operation by which delight in crime or neutrality toward the past is excluded.
Freedom, first placed under tension between curiosity and coercion, is inverted into license for transgression, then reconstituted through humility as receptivity to truth.
Delay of baptism locally increases the danger of license, but delay of doctrinal correction later changes into an instrument of providence and epistemic maturity.
The distinction between guilt and useful effect is amplified into a dual causality of history, in which the will sins and mercy orders the same sequence toward confession.
