Infancy, pear theft, spectacles, and Manichaean controversies remain local cases; at this level they function as proofs of distinct forms of one aversion.
The denial of infantile innocence is amplified upward into the thesis of affective continuity, according to which instruments and contexts change, not the root of the desire to dominate.
The material uselessness of theft remains a particular proof, but effects a global transition from explanation by the desired object to explanation by the state of the will.
The correction of Manichaeism does not remain a local polemic, but makes explicit the structure already implied in God's non-spatial presence and in non-substantial evil.
Delay of baptism and delay of disputation are not equivalent: the former can involuntarily engender license, the latter providentially preserves the future capacity to learn.
Critique of school, association, and sect is joined in the proposition at the present level that social formation distributes together the order of love and criteria of truth.
The creature is the principle neither of its own being nor of its own salvation; every absolute autonomy denies ontological dependence.
God neither occupies space nor is a body or phantasm; his nearness cannot be defined by local measure.
Evil is neither a created substance nor an autonomous principle opposed to God.
Created goods and cultural instruments are neither condemned in themselves nor can be held as the ultimate end.
Grammatical correctness, intensity of affect, the external appearance of a deed, and an abundance of sacred names do not prove moral rectitude or truth.
Custom, social praise, and association possess no ultimate authority, because the end and divine law judge the moral form of society.
Transgression does not constitute freedom, but conceals dependence upon good under the appearance of autonomy.
Providence can order a useful effect, but utility neither makes a depraved intention good nor removes the agent's guilt.
The system would collapse if the subject were author of itself, a self-sufficient possessor, or an autonomous restorer.
Desire, language, education, and society cannot be neutral, because each effects an order of love or truth.
Sin cannot be reduced to necessity, ignorance, or material utility, because the will also seeks the state of transgression.
An epistemology founded on sensible surface, splendor of speech, or sacred name cannot discern truth.
Moral order is contained neither by local conventionalism nor by the uniformity of a material precept across all times.
Grace cannot be a mere subsequent response to a subject already sufficient for conversion, because awakening itself, abstinence, and correction are attributed to it.
The autobiographical past is not morally inert material, because recollection either renews old delight or constitutes the causality of confession.
No ontological space outside God is given in which the creature might independently establish stability, freedom, or good for itself.
An autonomous principle of evil is ontologically inadmissible; even deformity requires the goodness that it diminishes and imitates.
Return caused by oneself and speech adequate to God are unavailable; confession proceeds within the gift of faith and the limitation of language.
Total transparency of origins, intentions, and providence is denied to the human being, whence memory, testimony, and authority operate without exhaustive comprehension.
The full closure of conversion is still unavailable: the promise of return receives force from dream, tears, and providence, but does not yet establish a universal law.
Across ages, sin preserves the same structure of aversion, but grows from elementary desire to transgressive will and captured knowledge.
School, companionship, and sect are mutations of one social machine that distributes shame, glory, and credibility so that disorder confirms itself.
Goods and signs can become instruments of capture not because they lose their goodness, but because their likeness to the good sought makes substitution credible.
Theft and Manichaean error are variants of the same imitation: the one usurps omnipotence through transgression, the other truth through names and phantasms.
Since God is not spatially absent and evil is not a substance, alienation necessarily becomes a diminution of relation, order, and participation rather than a migration to another reality.
Confession bifurcates causality: it restores guilt to the will, but attributes the capacity to recognize, abstain, and return to antecedent mercy.
Delay is an ambivalent operator: without right ordering it opens a space for license, but under providence it suspends immature disputation and prepares correction.
The universality of justice is derived not from identity of external deeds, but from the stability of the order that distinguishes intentions, duties, and times.
Conversion of the intellect is part of conversion of affect, because pride not only chooses good badly, but also deforms the instruments by which truth is recognized.
The autobiographical subject is not self-transparent consciousness, but a received being, socially mediated and recollected by retrospective confession.
Human time is a field of change, distribution of moral duties, and providential delay, yet is wholly contained under God's immutable presence.
Moral causality is asymmetric: the human being produces defect through aversion, while God provides antecedent goods and reordering of consequences without authorship of evil.
Political and cultural institution becomes a governance of the affects, because it distributes honor, shame, eloquence, and authority so that certain desires appear probable and praiseworthy.
Knowledge of God is not acquired by accumulation of propositions alone, but by transformation of the knowing subject from proud exteriority to the humble capacity to receive.
The form of confession itself performs doctrine, because the same memory that reports dispersion reorders it under the attribution of guilt and mercy.
True freedom is not self-foundation, but the capacity to receive the highest good; license against order becomes slavery to a mutilated image of power.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Unrecognized hunger for God chooses created good as absolute; the insufficient substitute increases emptiness, which produces a new flight toward external things.
Social praise rewards disorder, its reward produces public imitation, and imitation establishes new praise and a broader inversion of norms.
Pride rejects the humble form, knowledge is restricted to bodies, phantasm is accepted as truth, and false doctrine doctrinally confirms the initial pride.
Correction follows a circuit in which illicit delight produces bitterness, bitterness awakens memory, memory confession, and confession a new ordering of desire.
Memory is a bifurcated circuit: recollected crime either repeats delight or, under confession, retains guilt while transforming its affective force.
Rest in God is the hidden attractor around which restlessness, dispersion, and hunger assume their negative form.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Gift of being and goodness → dependence of the creature → constitutive desire for the highest good.
Forgetting of the principle → desire not understood → pursuit of nourishment in insufficient things.
Lower good made absolute → aversion from universal good → dispersion → immanent punishment of indigence.
Institution or association → distribution of praise and shame → confirmation of disordered affect → social amplification.
Elementary desire → willed transgression → imitation of freedom → capture of the intellect under the appearance of truth.
Denial of substantial evil and corporeal God → reclassification of alienation → correction of the mode of knowing and judging.
Antecedent mercy → correction and delay → confessional memory → recollection of goods → promised return to rest.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Created dependence → forgetting of the principle → infantile desire → social discipline → adolescent dispersion → gratuitous transgression → hunger for wisdom → doctrinal error → preparation for return.
Created good → disordered use → perverse imitation of divine good → privation and indigence → ontological correction → reordering of love.
Antecedent mercy → faith and testimony → correction → memory → confession → formative delay → promise of rest.
Sin is reclassified from a series of separate acts into an affective continuum that passes through ages, institutions, and doctrines in growing forms.
Family, school, companionship, theater, and sect become forms of one mediating field in which faculties, honors, and verisimilitudes are ordered.
Freedom is transferred from immunity from law to participation in right order, while self-founding transgression is disclosed as slavery to imitation.
Epistemology becomes part of moral ascesis, because the manner of seeing God, evil, and Scripture depends on the order of affect and the humility of the knower.
The opposition between universal justice and historical variety collapses, because stable law operates distributively through duties, persons, and times.
Evil and providence are no longer described as symmetrical causes: privation arises from the agent, while God preserves goods and orders consequences toward correction.
The surface level contains origin, infancy, school, delayed baptism, adolescence, theft, spectacles, studies, Manichaeism, and Monnica's intercession.
The structural level contains the circulation of gifts, desires, institutions, imitations, and corrections that make the same machine of aversion under diverse cases.
The metastrategic level transfers judgment from honor, utility, intensity of affect, and external appearance to the order of love, intention, and divine authority.
The ontological and temporal level establishes reality as dependence on incorporeal God, evil as privation, and time as a field of distributive providence.
The methodological and performative level makes confession an operation of conversion, because narrative itself refers guilt, gift, and memory to their right causes.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Culpable will and decisively antecedent mercy are preserved together, but the mode of their concurrence is not causally explained.
Every vice is said to imitate an appearance of good, yet theft seems to desire malice itself; defect and apparent good are imperfectly reconciled.
Providence draws utility from depraved acts, but the distinction between ordering effects and participation in the causality of evil lacks a complete formula.
Immutable justice sustains temporally diverse commands, but authentication of the divine command depends on an authority whose criterion remains incomplete within the synthesis.
Corporeal phantasms are rejected as sources of error, yet dream receives providential force; the distinction is not established by a general epistemic rule.
Infantile desire changes in adolescence from an impulse weak in means into a will that seeks the very position against the law.
Language passes from a socially acquired instrument to a medium of glory, then to a doctrinal surface by which true names conceal error.
Delay changes structural value: concerning baptism it threatens permission to sin, but concerning disputation it prepares mature correction.
Eloquence changes from an instrument of vanity in Hortensius into an awakening to wisdom, but can again slip into the splendor of false doctrine.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a field of non-spatial participation, in which all things are contained by God and alienation occurs within dependence itself.
The subject is a desire exceeding memory, permeable through bodies, signs, and societies, which recollects itself only by confession under grace.
Time is a distribution of changes under God's eternal today, where delay can amplify a fall or form the capacity for future conversion.
Possible struggle is navigation between true goods and their substitutions, the discernment of which requires ordering of love, humility of knowledge, and antecedent mercy.
The extracted axioms suffice to restore the movement from ontological dependence through affective, social, and epistemic amplifications to confession of delayed return.
The firmest structure is the distinction between given good and disordered use, together with privative evil and truth that transcends social form.
The coherence of the present level is sustained not by chronological order alone, but by the spiral return of the same aversion under affective, voluntary, and doctrinal forms.
The exact relation between culpable freedom and antecedent mercy remains indeterminate, which the synthesis can distinguish but cannot causally resolve.
Also indeterminate remains the general criterion by which a command, dream, or providential testimony is certainly distinguished from false imagination.
The act of confession itself resists axiomatic reduction, because the system not only enunciates propositions about conversion, but by narrating memory transforms it causally and affectively.

identity.context: Book I. · Book II. · Book III.
identity.original_context: Liber Primus. · Liber Secundus. · Liber Tertius.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo anima ingenio, veritatibus localibus et bonis creatis praedita simul errore doctrinali, amore inordinato et voluntate servili teneatur.
Quaestio ita restituitur ut error non ex defectu bonorum creatorum, sed ex aversione finis, falsa interpretatione et consuetudine affectiva oriatur.
Argumentatio ab experientia luctus et erroris ad examen auctoritatis, inde ad rehabilitationem fidei atque postremo ad diagnosin voluntatis progreditur.
Probatio conversionis primum negativa est: certitudo falsa degradatur, obiectio contra fidem dissolvitur, et tantum post hanc purgationem impedimentum morale manifestatur.
Fundamentum totius motus est distinctio inter Creatorem incommutabilem et creaturam mutabilem, cuius mens veritatem non possidet autonome sed participatione et mediatione recipit.
Motus est recursivus et spiralis: aversio errores novos generat, sed eadem experientia erroris confessione retractata fit materia curationis et novi iudicii.
Mutationes loci, magistri et doctrinae non efficiunt conversionem linearem, sed seriem rupturarum quae subiectum a falsa firmitate ad agnitionem propriae infirmitatis cogunt.
Clausura huius gregis est limen: falsa auctoritas relicta est, fides rationabiliter necessaria apparet, voluntas autem nondum liberata necessitatem gratiae producit.
[Persistent] Ordo Creatoris incommutabilis et creaturae mutabilis simul limites amoris, cognitionis, temporis et quietis constituit.
[Persistent] Aversio a Deo non absentiam Dei, sed alienationem animae a se atque corruptionem finis affectivi et intellectualis generat.
[Mutating] Unus ordo aversionis mutatur ex fixatione amoris et phantasmate metaphysico in dependentiam ab auctoritate falsa, deinde in consuetudinem voluntatis resistente.
[Persistent] Veritas localis, facultas intellectualis vel bonum creatum salutare non fit nisi usus eius ad fontem veritatis et finem beatitudinis ordinetur.

[Mutating] Mediatio socialis, rhetorica, sacramentalis, scripturalis et eventuum neque intrinsece corruptiva neque autonome salvifica est, sed secundum ordinem recipientis et providentiae functionem mutat.
[Emergent] Conversio incipit per dissolutionem asymmetricam falsi, transit per habitationem provisionalem sub auctoritate, et demum voluntatem sanandam exhibet.
[Persistent] Malum neque substantia externa neque necessitas caelestis est, sed vitium agentis mutabilis cui culpa propria restitui debet.
[Attractor] Omnis inquisitio ad quietem in bono incommutabili attrahitur, quia nulla summa bonorum finitorum stabilitatem vel beatitudinem praestat.
[Mutating] Auctoritas ex potentia sociali errorem propagante in obiectum examinis mutatur, deinde ut mediatio medicinalis fidei restituitur.
[Emergent] Fides et ratio circuitum medicinalem constituunt: aliqua fiducia mentem purgat, mens purgata id quod credit intelligere et iudicare incipit.
[Persistent] Reditus non est ascensus autonomus, sed participatio mediationis Christi, cuius incarnatio vera, humilitas et victoria mortis exteriora ad interiora referunt.
[Terminal] Correctio doctrinalis, ruptura sectaria et cognitio miseriae conversionem nondum perficiunt, sed insufficientiam virium propriarum et necessitatem gratiae terminative constituunt.
Praesentia Dei identitatem stabilem retinet, sed eius functio ab fundamento ontologico ad negationem fugae et postremo ad interpretationem absentiae expertae ut caecitatis mutatur.

Imaginatio corporea redit functione amplificata: primum spiritualia falsificat, deinde dualismum sectarium et caricaturam Catholicismi sustinet, tandem remota impedimentum doctrinale cessat esse principale.
Mediatio socialis mutatur ex circuito laudis et erroris in rhetoricam causaliter ambiguam, deinde in campum ubi idem subiectum corrigi vel captivari potest.
Temporalitas ex causa amissionis affectivae in medium inquisitionis dilatae transit atque postremo vim inversionis accipit, quia mora ipsa servitutem auget.
Confessio ab ordinatione retrospectiva donorum et errorum amplificatur in formam quae casum, impedimentum et intentionem perversam sub providentia reclassificat.
Dubitatio, initio intervallum productivum post ruinam sectae, functionem terminalem amittit et sub necessitate fidei ac decisionis fit positio non stabilis.
Amicitia desinit esse sola relatio dyadica et in structuram latiorem mediationis absorbetur, ubi amor gratuitus ordinem bonorum indicat sed etiam habitum socialem format.

Astrologia post munus locale evanescit, sed eius structura persistit ut exemplar cuiuslibet doctrinae quae causalitatem confundit, culpam externalizat et auctoritatem examinabilem immunem facere conatur.
Luctus, astrologia, Faustus, migrationes et casus Alypii manent eventus locales; hoc gradu valent tantum quatenus diversos modos aversionis, mediationis et correctionis efficiunt.
Mors amici ex casu biographico amplificatur in probationem quod permanentia a re temporali exacta miseriam ante ipsam iacturam instituit.
Imperitia Fausti non sola falsitatem totius sectae probat, sed cum praetensione divina et discrepantia examinabili coniuncta transitum globalem ad discrimen auctoritatis efficit.
Casus Alypii inferiores manent quantum ad personas et eventus, sed sursum amplificantur in legem receptionis non linearis sub habitu, multitudine et providentia.
Exegesis spiritalis non constituit hoc gradu probationem positivam plenam, sed commissuram necessariam qua obiectio litteralis solvitur et fides rursus possibilis fit.
Defensibilitas Catholica localiter nondum est veritas demonstrata; currenti gradu tamen cum necessitate cotidiana credendi coniuncta transit in quaestionem de auctoritate medicinali.
Artes, scientia et eloquentia autonomiam structuralem amittunt atque sub distinctione inter veritatem, efficaciam causalitatemque, usum et finem denuo codificantur.
Nulla creatura mutabilis, relatio temporalis aut compositio bonorum saecularium finem stabilem animae constituere potest.
Nulla imago corporea, pars sensibilis vel categoria creata ambitum Dei aut substantiae spiritalis exhaurit.
Malum in substantiam adversam, naturam alienam, sidera aut necessitatem transferri non potest sine dissolutione responsabilitatis et confessionis.
Scientia creaturarum, eloquentia, ingenium et veritates locales neque auctoritatem divinam neque beatitudinem per se efficiunt.
Credere universaliter repudiari nequit, sed neque certitudo demonstrativa ante omnem transformationem tamquam condicio medicinae postulanda est.
Recta doctrina sola habitum cupiditatis, divisionem voluntatis aut impotentiam continentiae abolere non potest.
Nulla mutatio loci vel fuga exterior animam a corde suo, praesentia Dei aut ordine amoris quem secum fert separare potest.
Falsum esse oportet subiectum sibi principium veritatis, firmitatis et redemptionis esse posse.
Falsum esse oportet tempus dilationis medium vacuum esse: idem tempus res dissolvit, memoriam reformat et consuetudinem non interruptam corroborat.
Falsum esse oportet cognitionem veritatis nullo testimonio, magistro, Scriptura, Ecclesia aut fide antecedenti indigere.
Falsum esse oportet providentiam tantum per intentiones rectas, petitiones statim impletas et causas agentibus perspicuas operari.
Falsum esse oportet ambitum socialem neutralem esse, cum laus, eloquentia, multitudo et amicitia cognitionem atque appetitum recursive forment.
Falsum esse oportet novam dispositionem externam eadem cupiditate intacta conversionem efficere posse, quia desiderium perversum se honestis nominibus tegit.
Impossibilis est absentia Dei proprie localis vel ontologica; absentia experta tantum caecitas et aversio animae coram praesentia permanente est.
Indisponibilis est positio stabilis inter falsitatem iam relictam et conversionem indefinite recusatam.
Indisponibilis est certitudo totalis quae transformationem antecedat, quia ipsa facultas iudicandi indiget medicina quam postulatio certitudinis prohibet.
Impossibilis est beatitudo intra totalitatem finitorum, etiam si amissio eorum cogitatione removeatur.
Vetitus est reditus per assimilationem superbam, scientiam autonomam aut voluntatem sui iuris; conversio tantum ut participatio medicinae et gratiae cogitatur.
Tempus duplicem vim acquirit: obiectum dilectum dissolvit et, ubi conversio differtur, ipsum habitum qui obiecto inhaeret confirmat.
Error non residet in propositione singulari, sed distribuitur per imaginationem, auctoritatem, caricaturam doctrinalem et appetitum qui falsas imagines retinere cupit.
Adequatio epistemica non mensuratur copia veritatum localium, sed orientatione cognoscentis et sanatione facultatis qua verum in sapientiam ordinatur.
Restitutio culpae toti agenti excusationes externas tollit, sed simul ostendit confessionem responsabilitatis non sufficere sine dono quo voluntas continens fiat.
Nullum medium sociale vim univocam habet: auctoritas et rhetorica secundum habitum recipientis et ordinem superiorem errorem propagare, veritatem inferre aut correctionem producere possunt.
Providentia causas moraliter mixtas ordinare dicitur sine culpae humanae abolitione, sed nexus inter causalitatem superiorem et responsabilitatem agentis insolutus manet.
Auctoritas non simpliciter destruitur neque simpliciter restituitur: examen falsas praetensiones dissolvit, dum necessitas fidei auctoritatem medicinalem sub novo criterio requirit.
Dissolutio falsi conversionem tantum negative praeparat; cum obiectio doctrinalis removetur, residuum impeditivum in habitu voluntatis apparet et limen gratiae constituit.
Subiectum reclassificatur ex possessore autonomo veritatis in agentem culpabilem, patientem medicinae et participem luminis cuius fontem non constituit.
Tempus fit simul forma creaturae, medium curationis et periculum strategicum: successione solatur, sed dilatione voluntatem alligat et morti exponit.
Causalitas hierarchice ordinatur: intentiones particulares effectus locales producunt, dum providentia earum concursum ad finem agentibus ignotum reponit.
Cognitio transformativa procedit per refutationem, fiduciam provisionalem, purgationem facultatis et iudicium renovatum, non per demonstrationem totalem uno actu possessam.
Auctoritas et libertas non sunt opposita simpliciter, quia libertas ab errore ipsa mediatione formatur, quam tamen discrepantia, fructus et praetensio veritatis examinabilem faciunt.
Malum ontologice de-substantializatur et strategicam formam accipit: est perversio motus, finis, iudicii et habitus quae bona ipsa contra ordinem eorum convertit.
Conversio fit mutatio status totius systematis, quae ontologiam, auctoritatem, interpretationem, affectum et voluntatem simul reordinare debet, non mera substitutio opinionis.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Aversio → inquisitio exterior → phantasma → doctrina falsa → confirmatio aversionis constituit circuitum principalem erroris.
Amor finis temporalis → postulatio firmitatis → iactura vel anxietas → fuga exterior → reditus ad animam vulneratam constituit circuitum miseriae.
Laus vel eloquentia → affectus → auctoritas → transmissio doctrinae → nova laus constituit viam amplificationis socialis, cuius valor epistemicus semper indeterminatus manet.
Fides initialis → purgatio mentis → intellectus auctus → iudicium auctoritatis → fides distinctior constituit circuitum medicinalem cognitionis.
Consuetudo → consilium compromissorium → dilatio → consuetudo corroborata → libertas imminuta constituit escalationem voluntatis servilis.
Eventus ambiguus → interpretatio confessionalis → recognitio providentiae → humilitas → nova capacitas eventus legendi constituit circuitum curationis retrospectivae.
Quietis in Deo attractor lineas amoris, cognitionis, auctoritatis et voluntatis congregat, quia unaquaeque ad defectum firmitatis autonomae reducitur.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Aversio finis → dispersio amoris et cognitionis → bona creata tamquam fines aut principia autonoma usurpata.
Usurpatio boni creati → phantasma metaphysicum, auctoritas falsa vel appetitus stabilitatis → miseria et error recursive producti.
Contradictio experientiae, rationis aut exegesis → degradatio certitudinis → ruptura cum systemate priore sine possessione statim positiva novi.
Ruptura certitudinis → habitatio provisionalis → auctoritas medicinalis → fides quae facultatem ulterioris cognitionis purgat.
Correctio intellectus → detectio consuetudinis intactae → translatio impedimenti ad voluntatem → clausura consiliorum compromissoriorum.
Impotentia voluntatis + mors incerta + mediatio Christi → necessitas gratiae → conversio nondum effecta sed structuraliter inevitabilis.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Amor et ingenium aversa → luctus atque falsa metaphysica → examen doctrinae et magistri → ruina auctoritatis sectariae → defensibilitas Catholica → fides rehabilitata → servitus voluntatis → necessitas gratiae.
Phantasma corporeum → dualismus et caricatura fidei → exegesis spiritalis → remotio objectionis → auctoritas medicinalis → cognitio recursiva.
Appetitus quietis → bona temporalia → anxietas et iactura → consilia media → dilatio → mors ut terminus incertus → gratia ut sola clausura conversionis.
Veritas propositionis, forma sermonis, rectitudo finis et beatitudo cognoscentis in axes distinctos distribuuntur, quorum confusio errores inferiores generaverat.
Auctoritas reclassificatur ex dominio vel splendore rhetorico in mediationem examinabilem cuius munus est mentem ad iudicium maturius ducere.
Tempus desinit esse scaena neutra eventuum et fit operator qui res temporales dissolvit, curationem differt vel promovet atque consuetudinem auget.
Malum ex obiecto substantiali in relationem perversam inter facultatem, obiectum, finem et motum agentis transfertur.
Conversio ex mutatione doctrinae in reordinationem plurium graduum redescribitur, quia error ontologicus dissolvi potest dum affectus et voluntas manent captivi.
Mediatio ex impedimento libertatis in condicionem ambivalentem formationis mutatur, unde lectio semper intentionem agentis, dispositionem recipientis et ordinem providentialem distinguere debet.
In gradu superficiei agunt mors amici, astrologia, Faustus, migrationes, Ambrosius, consilia matrimonii et casus Alypii.
In gradu structurali aversio, imaginatio, auctoritas, habitus socialis, consuetudo et temporalitas distribuunt errores atque condiciones correctionis.
In gradu metastrategico quaestio ab electione inter doctrinas ad inventionem criterii, mediationis medicinalis et ordinis quo intellectus atque voluntas curentur transfertur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali realitas distinguitur inter praesentiam incommutabilem Dei et creaturam successive existentem, mortalem atque incapacem sibi firmitatem tribuendi.
In gradu methodologico et performativo confessio ipsa quod asserit efficit, quia fragmenta biographica retractando casum in providentiam, culpam in agnitionem et memoriam in medicinam convertit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Providentia causas perversas ordinat et tamen culpam agentibus relinquit, sed modus concursus divini et voluntarii affirmatur potius quam formaliter explicatur.
Fides rationem sanare debet ad auctoritatem iudicandam, sed auctoritas medicinae partim ipsa fide in institutionem divinam agnoscitur.
Refutatio caricaturae Catholicae et defensibilitas Scripturae probationem veritatis positivae non perficiunt, quamquam motus ad auctoritatem Scripturae vi confessionali acceleratur.
Amicitia, matrimonium et bona saecularia legitima manent, sed eadem bona sub cupiditate fiunt vincula; criterium inter usum ordinatum et tegumentum appetitus non semper explicatur.
Imaginatio corporea mutatur ex causa positiva dualismi in obiectum purgationis exegeticae; post eius dissolutionem locus conflictus ad voluntatem transfertur.
Rhetorica vim epistemicam amittit sed efficaciam causalem retinet, unde medium repudiatum tamquam criterium redit tamquam via ingressus veritatis.
Scepticismus mutatur ex tutela contra doctrinam falsam in impedimentum, ubi suspensio assensus medicinam fidei indefinite differt.
Punctum mutationis principale occurrit cum correctione intellectus perfecta relative, impedimentum conversionis non iam in obiecto credendo sed in habitu volendi reperitur.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite apparet ut ordo hierarchicus bonorum mutabilium circum praesentiam incommutabilem, in quo nulla creatura sibi principium aut terminum est.
Subiectum est nodus amoris, memoriae, habitus, testimonii et voluntatis, qui secundum id cui adhaeret aut dispergitur aut integratur.
Tempus est fluvius qui obiecta aufert, memoriam format, causas ad fines ignotos vehit et dilationem in servitutem convertit.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga ad exteriora, sed reditus interior per mediationes quarum finis est firmare animam in eo quod non transit.
Axiomata extracta sufficiunt ad restituendum motum ab aversione affectiva et falsa ontologia per ruinam auctoritatis ad fidem medicinalem atque necessitatem gratiae.
Structura firmissima est ubi phantasma corporeum doctrinam falsificat, discrepantia examinabilis auctoritatem destruit et correctione doctrinali peracta servitus voluntatis manifestatur.
Nondum satis determinantur criterium independens verae auctoritatis, concursus providentiae cum culpa et modus quo gratia voluntatem actu liberatura sit.
Cohaerentia huius gregis non ordine mere lineari, sed reditu variato aversionis, mediationis et firmitatis impossibilis constat; fragmenta biographica circa conversionem nondum effectam convergunt.

Reductioni resistunt singulares ambiguitates luctus, eloquentiae, bonorum coniugalium et providentiae; hae tamen machinam non dissolvunt, sed commissuras ubi transitus a signo ad ontologiam comprimitur indicant.
The system asks how the soul, endowed with intellect, local truths, and created goods, is at once held by doctrinal error, disordered love, and servile will.
The question is thus restored: error arises not from a defect in created goods, but from a turning away from the end, false interpretation, and affective habit.
The argument proceeds from the experience of grief and error to an examination of authority, thence to the rehabilitation of faith, and finally to a diagnosis of the will.
The proof of conversion is first negative: false certainty is degraded, the objection against faith is dissolved, and only after this purgation does the moral impediment become manifest.

The foundation of the whole movement is the distinction between the immutable Creator and mutable creature, whose mind does not possess truth autonomously but receives it through participation and mediation.
The movement is recursive and spiral: turning away generates new errors, yet the same experience of error, reconsidered through confession, becomes material for healing and new judgment.
Changes of place, teacher, and doctrine do not produce linear conversion, but a series of ruptures that compel the subject from false firmness to recognition of its own weakness.
The closure of this cluster is a threshold: false authority has been abandoned, faith appears rationally necessary, but the will, not yet liberated, yields the necessity of grace.
[Persistent] The order of the immutable Creator and mutable creature simultaneously establishes the limits of love, knowledge, time, and rest.
[Persistent] Turning away from God generates not God's absence, but the soul's alienation from itself and the corruption of the affective and intellectual end.
[Mutating] A single order of turning away changes from fixation of love and metaphysical phantasm into dependence on false authority, then into a habit of resistant will.
[Persistent] A local truth, intellectual faculty, or created good becomes salutary only if its use is ordered toward the source of truth and the end of blessedness.

[Mutating] Social, rhetorical, sacramental, scriptural, and evental mediation is neither intrinsically corrupting nor autonomously salvific, but changes function according to the order of the recipient and of providence.
[Emergent] Conversion begins through the asymmetric dissolution of falsity, passes through provisional dwelling under authority, and finally presents the will as requiring healing.
[Persistent] Evil is neither an external substance nor a celestial necessity, but a vice of the mutable agent to which its own guilt must be restored.
[Attractor] Every inquiry is drawn toward rest in the immutable good, because no sum of finite goods furnishes stability or blessedness.
[Mutating] Authority changes from a social power propagating error into an object of examination, then is restored as the medicinal mediation of faith.
[Emergent] Faith and reason constitute a medicinal circuit: some trust purges the mind; the purged mind begins to understand and judge what it believes.
[Persistent] Return is not autonomous ascent, but participation in Christ's mediation, whose true incarnation, humility, and victory over death refer exterior things to interior ones.
[Terminal] Doctrinal correction, sectarian rupture, and knowledge of misery do not yet complete conversion, but terminally establish the insufficiency of one's own powers and the necessity of grace.
God's presence retains stable identity, but its function changes from ontological foundation to negation of flight and finally to an interpretation of experienced absence as blindness.

Corporeal imagination returns with an amplified function: first it falsifies spiritual things, then sustains sectarian dualism and a caricature of Catholicism, and finally, once removed, ceases to be the principal doctrinal impediment.
Social mediation changes from a circuit of praise and error into causally ambiguous rhetoric, then into a field where the same subject can be corrected or captured.
Temporality passes from a cause of affective loss into a medium of delayed inquiry and finally acquires the force of inversion, because delay itself increases servitude.
Confession is amplified from retrospective ordering of gifts and errors into a form that reclassifies accident, impediment, and perverse intention under providence.
Doubt, initially a productive interval after the collapse of the sect, loses its terminal function and, under the necessity of faith and decision, becomes an unstable position.
Friendship ceases to be a merely dyadic relation and is absorbed into a broader structure of mediation, where gratuitous love indicates the order of goods but also forms social habit.
Astrology disappears after a local role, but its structure persists as a model for any doctrine that confuses causality, externalizes guilt, and seeks to render examinable authority immune.
Grief, astrology, Faustus, migrations, and Alypius's cases remain local events; at this level they matter only insofar as they produce diverse modes of turning away, mediation, and correction.
The death of a friend is amplified from a biographical event into proof that permanence demanded from a temporal thing establishes misery before the loss itself.
Faustus's incompetence does not alone prove the falsity of the entire sect, but, joined with divine pretension and examinable discrepancy, effects a global transition to a crisis of authority.
Alypius's cases remain lower with respect to persons and events, but are amplified upward into a law of nonlinear reception under habit, crowd, and providence.
Spiritual exegesis does not at this level constitute a full positive proof, but a necessary joint by which the literal objection is dissolved and faith again becomes possible.
The defensibility of Catholicism is not yet locally demonstrated truth; at the current level, however, joined with the everyday necessity of believing, it becomes a question of medicinal authority.
Arts, science, and eloquence lose structural autonomy and are recoded under the distinction between truth, efficacy, and causality, use and end.
No mutable creature, temporal relation, or composition of secular goods can constitute the stable end of the soul.
No corporeal image, sensible part, or created category exhausts the scope of God or of spiritual substance.
Evil cannot be transferred to an opposing substance, alien nature, stars, or necessity without dissolving responsibility and confession.
Knowledge of creatures, eloquence, intellect, and local truths produce neither divine authority nor blessedness through themselves.
Believing cannot be universally repudiated, but neither is demonstrative certainty before every transformation to be demanded as a condition of healing.
Right doctrine alone cannot abolish the habit of desire, division of the will, or impotence of continence.
No change of place or external flight can separate the soul from its own heart, God's presence, or the order of love that it bears with itself.
It must be false that the subject can be for itself the principle of truth, firmness, and redemption.
It must be false that the time of delay is an empty medium: that same time dissolves things, reforms memory, and strengthens uninterrupted habit.
It must be false that knowledge of truth requires no prior testimony, teacher, Scripture, Church, or faith.
It must be false that providence operates only through right intentions, immediately fulfilled petitions, and causes transparent to agents.
It must be false that the social environment is neutral, since praise, eloquence, crowd, and friendship recursively form knowledge and appetite.
It must be false that a new external arrangement, with the same desire intact, can effect conversion, because perverse desire conceals itself under honorable names.
The absence of God in a properly local or ontological sense is impossible; experienced absence is only the soul's blindness and turning away before enduring presence.
A stable position between falsity already abandoned and conversion indefinitely refused is unavailable.
Total certainty preceding transformation is unavailable, because the very faculty of judging requires the healing that the demand for certainty prevents.
Blessedness within the totality of finite things is impossible, even if their loss is removed in thought.
Return through proud assimilation, autonomous knowledge, or self-governing will is forbidden; conversion is conceived only as participation in healing and grace.
Time acquires a double force: it dissolves the beloved object and, where conversion is deferred, confirms the very habit that clings to the object.
Error does not reside in a single proposition, but is distributed through imagination, authority, doctrinal caricature, and the appetite that wishes to retain false images.
Epistemic adequacy is not measured by the quantity of local truths, but by the orientation of the knower and the healing of the faculty by which truth is ordered to wisdom.

The restoration of guilt to the whole agent removes external excuses, but at the same time shows that confession of responsibility does not suffice without the gift by which the will becomes continent.
No social medium has univocal force: authority and rhetoric can propagate error, convey truth, or produce correction according to the recipient's habit and the higher order.
Providence is said to order morally mixed causes without abolishing human guilt, but the nexus between higher causality and the responsibility of the agent remains unresolved.
Authority is neither simply destroyed nor simply restored: examination dissolves false pretensions, while the necessity of faith requires medicinal authority under a new criterion.

The dissolution of falsity prepares conversion only negatively; when the doctrinal objection is removed, the remaining impediment appears in the habit of the will and constitutes the threshold of grace.
The subject is reclassified from autonomous possessor of truth into a guilty agent, patient of healing, and participant in a light whose source it does not constitute.
Time becomes at once the form of creaturehood, a medium of healing, and a strategic danger: through succession it consoles, but through delay it binds the will and exposes it to death.
Causality is hierarchically ordered: particular intentions produce local effects, while providence places their concurrence toward an end unknown to the agents.
Transformative knowledge proceeds through refutation, provisional trust, purgation of faculty, and renewed judgment, not through total demonstration possessed in a single act.
Authority and freedom are not simply opposites, because freedom from error is itself formed through mediation, which discrepancy, fruits, and a claim to truth nevertheless render examinable.
Evil is ontologically de-substantialized and takes a strategic form: it is a perversion of movement, end, judgment, and habit that turns goods themselves against their order.
Conversion becomes a change in the state of the whole system, which must reorder ontology, authority, interpretation, affect, and will together, not a mere substitution of opinion.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Turning away → external inquiry → phantasm → false doctrine → confirmation of turning away constitutes the principal circuit of error.
Love of a temporal end → demand for firmness → loss or anxiety → external flight → return to the wounded soul constitutes the circuit of misery.
Praise or eloquence → affect → authority → transmission of doctrine → new praise constitutes a path of social amplification, whose epistemic value always remains indeterminate.
Initial faith → purgation of mind → increased understanding → judgment of authority → more distinct faith constitutes the medicinal circuit of knowledge.
Habit → compromising plan → delay → strengthened habit → diminished freedom constitutes the escalation of servile will.
Ambiguous event → confessional interpretation → recognition of providence → humility → new capacity for reading events constitutes the circuit of retrospective healing.
The attractor of rest in God gathers the lines of love, knowledge, authority, and will, because each is reduced to the defect of autonomous firmness.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Turning away from the end → dispersion of love and knowledge → created goods usurped as autonomous ends or principles.
Usurpation of a created good → metaphysical phantasm, false authority, or appetite for stability → recursively produced misery and error.
Contradiction by experience, reason, or exegesis → degradation of certainty → rupture with the prior system without immediate positive possession of the new.
Rupture of certainty → provisional dwelling → medicinal authority → faith that purges the faculty for further knowledge.
Correction of intellect → detection of intact habit → transfer of impediment to the will → closure of compromising plans.
Impotence of the will + uncertain death + mediation of Christ → necessity of grace → conversion not yet effected but structurally inevitable.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Turned-away love and intellect → grief and false metaphysics → examination of doctrine and teacher → collapse of sectarian authority → defensibility of Catholicism → rehabilitated faith → servitude of the will → necessity of grace.
Corporeal phantasm → dualism and caricature of faith → spiritual exegesis → removal of objection → medicinal authority → recursive knowledge.
Appetite for rest → temporal goods → anxiety and loss → intermediate plans → delay → death as an uncertain limit → grace as the sole closure of conversion.
The truth of a proposition, form of speech, rectitude of the end, and blessedness of the knower are distributed across distinct axes, whose confusion had generated lower errors.
Authority is reclassified from dominion or rhetorical splendor into examinable mediation whose role is to lead the mind toward more mature judgment.
Time ceases to be a neutral stage of events and becomes an operator that dissolves temporal things, delays or advances healing, and increases habit.
Evil is transferred from a substantial object to a perverse relation among the agent's faculty, object, end, and movement.
Conversion is redescribed from a change of doctrine into a reordering of multiple levels, because ontological error can be dissolved while affect and will remain captive.

Mediation changes from an impediment to freedom into an ambivalent condition of formation, whence reading must always distinguish the agent's intention, the recipient's disposition, and the providential order.
At the surface level operate the death of the friend, astrology, Faustus, migrations, Ambrose, marriage plans, and Alypius's cases.
At the structural level, turning away, imagination, authority, social habit, custom, and temporality distribute errors and conditions of correction.
At the metastrategic level, the question shifts from choosing among doctrines to discovering criterion, medicinal mediation, and the order by which intellect and will are healed.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality is distinguished between God's immutable presence and creature existing successively, mortal, and incapable of bestowing firmness upon itself.

At the methodological and performative level, confession itself effects what it asserts, because by reconsidering biographical fragments it converts accident into providence, guilt into recognition, and memory into healing.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Providence orders perverse causes and yet leaves guilt to agents, but the mode of concurrence between divine and voluntary action is affirmed rather than formally explained.
Faith must heal reason in order to judge authority, but the authority of healing is itself partly recognized through faith in divine institution.

The refutation of the caricature of Catholicism and the defensibility of Scripture do not accomplish a positive proof of truth, although the movement toward the authority of Scripture is accelerated by confessional force.
Friendship, marriage, and secular goods remain legitimate, but the same goods become bonds under desire; the criterion between ordered use and the covering of appetite is not always explained.
Corporeal imagination changes from a positive cause of dualism into an object of exegetical purgation; after its dissolution, the locus of conflict is transferred to the will.
Rhetoric loses epistemic force but retains causal efficacy, whence a repudiated medium returns as criterion and as a path of entry for truth.
Skepticism changes from protection against false doctrine into an impediment, where suspension of assent indefinitely delays the healing of faith.

The principal point of mutation occurs when, with correction of intellect relatively complete, the impediment to conversion is found no longer in the object to be believed but in the habit of willing.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality implicitly appears as a hierarchical order of mutable goods around immutable presence, in which no creature is its own principle or end.
The subject is a node of love, memory, habit, testimony, and will, which according to that to which it adheres is either dispersed or integrated.
Time is a river that carries away objects, forms memory, bears causes toward unknown ends, and converts delay into servitude.
Navigation is possible not through flight toward exterior things, but through interior return by mediations whose end is to establish the soul in what does not pass away.
The extracted axioms suffice to reconstruct the movement from affective turning away and false ontology through the collapse of authority to medicinal faith and the necessity of grace.

The structure is strongest where corporeal phantasm falsifies doctrine, examinable discrepancy destroys authority, and, doctrinal correction having been completed, the servitude of the will becomes manifest.
The independent criterion of true authority, the concurrence of providence with guilt, and the manner in which grace will actually liberate the will are not yet sufficiently determined.

The coherence of this cluster consists not in a merely linear order, but in the varied recurrence of turning away, mediation, and impossible firmness; biographical fragments converge around conversion not yet effected.

The particular ambiguities of grief, eloquence, marital goods, and providence resist reduction; these nevertheless do not dissolve the mechanism, but indicate the joints where the transition from sign to ontology is compressed.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo creatura, cui veritas de bono immutabili iam patet, a malo non substantiali sed voluntarie sedimentato liberetur atque libertatem in vita temporali, ecclesiali et mortali perficiat.

Thesis globalis malum ex ordine naturarum removet, in privatione et voluntate perverso habitu ligata collocat, liberationem autem gratiae sananti atque mediationibus Christi, Scripturae et Ecclesiae attribuit.

Argumentatio diagnostica et reconstructiva falsas ontologias excludit, divisionem voluntatis genealogice explicat, deinde effectus liberationis confessione, sacramento, providentia et intercessione probat.
Motus ab ascensu ad veritatem incorpoream transit ad detectionem impotentiae practicae, inde ad voluntatem integratam, vitam ecclesialiter formatam et mortem sub spe resurrectionis intellectam.

Progressio est cumulativa et mutatione acta: visio infirmitatem detegit, infirmitas historiam consuetudinis aperit, historia limen gratiae parat, actus autem conversus ulteriorem formationem requirit.

Mediatio successive amplificatur ab incarnatione sanante ad allocutionem scripturalem, sacramentum, cantum, communionem et memoriam liturgicam, sine quibus veritas in possessionem temporaliter ordinatam non transit.

Conversio simul est eventus punctiformis et processus multistratus: voluntas uno limine integratur, sed intellectus, affectus, professio, consuetudo et relatio socialis temporibus diversis reformantur.
Clausura non possessionem definitivam sed precem producit: mediatio temporalis ad Sapientiam stabilem ordinatur, dum misericordia et intercessio etiam post vitam laudabilem necessariae manent.
[Persistent] Deus est bonum immutabile et fons omnis naturae; ideo nihil creatum rationem substantiae adversae ex se habet.
[Persistent] Quidquid est bonitatem aliquam retinet; malum igitur non est natura positiva, sed diminutio boni et aversio voluntatis.
[Mutating] Ordo creatus primo inaequalitatem naturarum complectitur, deinde discordias voluntatis et eventuum intra providentiam ordinantem absorbet.
[Persistent] Culpa in voluntate creaturae locatur neque ad naturam contrariam, astra aut effectum providentialiter bonum transferri potest.
[Mutating] Cognitio veritatis obiectum ostendit, sed neque adhesionem stabilem neque maturitatem voluntatis et intellectus efficit nisi subiectum sanetur.
[Attractor] Veritas et Sapientia incommutabiles supra mentem temporalem permanent atque normam iudicii et terminum desiderii praebent.
[Persistent] Gratia voluntatem non delet, sed vincula eius rumpit, consensum excitat et voluntates partiales in actum integrum perducit.
[Mutating] Mediatio a Christo et Scriptura ad sacramenta, cantum, communionem et intercessionem extenditur, quia sanatio subiecti formam distributam requirit.
[Mutating] Actus voluntarii tempore sedimentantur in consuetudinem necessitatis similem, quae etiam post correctionem rationalem vestigia affectiva relinquere potest.
[Emergent] Conversio est limen decisivum intra processum longum, cuius effectus voluntatem, intellectum, habitum, statum socialem et incorporationem ecclesialem diversis temporibus mutant.
[Emergent] Providentia effectum salutarem ex eventu adverso vel intentione mala producere potest, quin culpam agentis in bonitatem effectus dissolvat.
[Emergent] Confessio causalitatem asymmetrice distribuit: voluntas peccati responsabilitatem gerit, sed initium, medicina et fructus liberationis Deo redduntur.
[Terminal] Baptismus conversionem in regenerationem ecclesialem stabilit, non tamen futuram culpam aut permanentem misericordiae necessitatem aufert.
[Attractor] Mens temporaliter Sapientiam tangere potest, sed stabilis praesentiae aeternae possessio intra successionem vitae praesentis indisponibilis manet.
[Terminal] Nulla sanctitas humana iudicium claudit; sacrificium Christi, misericordia et intercessio ultimam formam memoriae et spei constituunt.

Malum ab hypothesi substantiae adversae ad privationem, inde ad voluntatem perversam, consuetudinem et reliquias affectivas transfertur; identitas negativa manet, sed locus operationis temporaliter densatur.
Voluntas primo locus aversionis est, deinde campus divisionis, postremo consensus a gratia excitatus; eadem facultas culpam et liberationem recipit, non eodem tamen principio causali.
Veritas incorporea identitatem retinet, sed munus mutat: ex termino ascensus fit accusatio impotentiae, deinde norma formationis et attractor eschatologicus.
Consuetudo ex impedimento carnali in genealogiam servitutis explicatur atque post conversionem ut memoria affectiva persistit; non destruitur uno actu, sed ad novum ordinem paulatim traducitur.
Mediatio a via Christi adversus superbiam ad vocem scripturalem personalem et ad apparatus ecclesiales plurales migrat, dum functio sanandi et adhaesionem stabiliendi permanet.
Ascensus interior bis redit functione mutata: primum veritatem demonstrat sed contemplantem infirmum relinquit; postea aeternitatem breviter tangit atque statum viatoris manifestat.
Anti-dualismus ab exclusionibus cosmologicis ad unitatem animae et responsabilitatem moralem extenditur, deinde in distinctionem inter intentionem malam et effectum providentialem absorbetur.
Exemplum ex comparatione doctrinarum in machinam conversionis mutatur: narrationes alienae dissolvunt excusationes, conversio visibilis autem novas imitationes gignit.
Tempus ex successione creata fit medium sedimentationis culpae, discrimen inter nunc et dilationem, atque spatium sacramentalis formationis, luctus et spei.
Ordo universalis mutatur in providentiam narrativam: bonitas totius non solum inconvenientias metaphysicas continet, sed etiam eventus adversos ad salutem convertit sine confusione morali.

Astrologia postquam causalitatem externam infirmavit e campo manifesto recedit; eius opus structuraliter persistit in omni ulteriori recusatione qua culpa ad naturam, necessitatem vel casum transfertur.

Imagines Dei corporeae et astrologia manent refutationes locales; ad gradum praesentem ascendit earum functio communis, scilicet exclusio omnis causalitatis quae bonum immutabile minuat aut responsabilitatem voluntatis extrinsecus solvat.
Distinctio localis inter Platonicos et Scripturam sursum amplificatur in discrimen generale inter cognitionem termini et viam quae subiectum ad fruitionem idoneum reddit.

Delimitationes Christologicae particulares non integrae doctrinae unionem hoc gradu constituunt; earum vis superior est mediatorem nec purum magistrum nec apparentiam sine plena humanitate esse posse.
Victorinus, Antonius et aulici casus inferiores manent, sed coniuncti ostendunt exemplum alienum facultatem praesentis mutationis probare, excusationes destruere et conversionem socialiter propagare.
Vita Monicae non est appendix biographica, sed probatio praesentis gradus qua virtus, correctio, providentia, contemplatio, mors et intercessio sub eadem ratione doni ordinantur.
Duo ascensus interiores unitates coniungunt: prior necessitatem mediationis aperit, posterior terminum mediationum praegustat sed eius possessionem adhuc differt.

Actus conversionis qui in discrimine voluntatis localiter clauditur ad gradum praesentem non est finis, sed transitus in formationem, sacramentum, communitatem, disciplinam affectuum et intelligentiam mortis.
Baptismus terminalis est respectu culpae antecedentis et incorporationis ecclesialis, non respectu totius itineris; ulterior culpa, luctus et misericordia vetant eum in clausuram absolutam converti.
Systema nullam materiam increatam aut substantiam malam admittit ex qua defectus voluntatis causaliter derivetur.
Pluralitas affectuum et voluntatum neque pluralitatem animarum neque principium ontologice contrarium probat.
Deus nec spatio dividitur nec per imaginem, sonum aut mensuram corporalem ut terminus cognitionis definitur.
Causalitas astralis vel externa culpam non aufert, quia praedictio incerta et necessitas acquisita actum voluntarium antecedentem non abolent.
Cognitio philosophica, certitudo metaphysica et doctrina recta non sunt causa sufficiens adhaesionis, actionis aut maturitatis spiritualis.
Voluntas nullum fundamentum autonomum possidet quo consuetudinem suam rumpat aut continentiam ex propria virtute producat.
Dilatio conversionis non est spatium neutrum; promissum futuri indefiniti praesentem retentionem veteris ordinis operatur.
Interioritas privata et mediatio exterior separatim sumptae conversionem non perficiunt; sanatio interna incorporationem, confessionem et communionem postulat.
Effectus providentialiter bonus intentionem malam non iustificat, neque successus eventus mensuram moralem agentis constituit.
Virtus, baptismus et vita laudabilis neque innocentiam absolutam neque ius salutis sine misericordia constituunt.
Nulla creatura, professio, propinquitas corporalis aut patria terrestris potest terminum ultimum desiderii vel communionis praebere.
Falsum esse oportet esse cum extensione spatiali converti; aliter Deus incorporeus et veritas supra mentem in nihilum redigerentur.
Falsum esse oportet mentem mutabilem normam sui iudicii producere; aliter ascensus ad veritatem incommutabilem fundamentum amitteret.
Falsum esse oportet cognitionem termini facultatem perveniendi secum ferre; aliter transitus a metaphysica ad voluntatem et gratiam supervacuus fieret.
Falsum esse oportet consuetudinem naturam alienam vel necessitatem primariam esse; aliter simul imputabilitas praeterita et sanabilitas praesens corruerent.
Falsum esse oportet gratiam voluntatem coactione substituere; systema indiget voluntate vere consentiente, quamvis principium liberationis ipsa non praebeat.
Falsum esse oportet conversionem uno decreto omnes ordines subiecti consummare; aliter formatio intellectualis, sacramentalis et affectiva structuram necessariam amitteret.
Falsum esse oportet bonum effectum bonitatem intentionis demonstrare; aliter providentia et retributio moralis indistinguibiles fierent.
Falsum esse oportet regenerationem sacramentalem omnem culpam futuram excludere; aliter misericordia post baptismum et intercessio pro laudabilibus incohaerentes essent.
Falsum esse oportet immediationem Dei mediationes temporales supervacaneas facere; status viatoris signis eget, quamvis terminus eorum transcensum promittat.
Nulla exterioritas ontologica relinquitur in qua malum, materia aut natura contraria ordini creato coordinari possit.
Nullum ego neutrum et nullum futurum vacuum inter voluntates contendentes datur; ipsa dilatio iam pars ordinis veteris est.
Possibilitas subiecti se ipsum ex nihilo moraliter regenerantis inadmissibilis est; libertas recipitur ut sanata, non producitur ut causa sui.
Stabilis immediataque possessio Sapientiae intra vitam temporalem abest; haec indisponibilitas mediationibus praesentibus directionem et terminum dat.
Nulla ratio meritorum potest iudicium claudere aut misericordiam superfluam facere; absentia innocentiae absolutae precem terminalem generat.
Plena transparentia sui et providentiae indisponibilis manet; confessio causam ultimam Deo tribuit sine cognitione exhaustiva omnium mediorum.
Patria ultima nec loco, sepultura, successu nec propinquitate corporali continetur; communionis forma terminalis resurrectionem et memoriam liturgicam postulat.
Privatio ontologica, consuetudo moralis et persistentia affectiva componuntur in unam theoriam mali quod essentia propria caret, sed efficaciam temporalem per actus sedimentatos acquirit.
Ascensus ad veritatem, impotentia conversionis et immaturitas post conversionem demonstrant cognitionem salutarem non simplicem informationem, sed transformationem capacitatis subiecti esse.
Responsabilitas et dependentia a gratia cohaerent asymmetrice: subiectum servitutem per actus suos fabricat, sed principium quo vincula rumpuntur sibi non potest praebere.
Incarnatio, allocutio scripturalis et incorporatio sacramentalis constituunt unam seriem qua veritas superior ad facultates temporales subiecti descendit easque ad se elevat.
Conversio uno actu divisionem voluntatis claudit, sed non uno tempore omnes eius causas, habitus et effectus; eventus est forma compressionis processus, non negatio processus.
Ordo universalis et providentia asymmetrica sinunt effectum bonum ex discordia oriri sine substantializatione mali neque absolutione intentionis pravae.

Exemplum conversi et communio ecclesialis efficiunt circuitum propagationis: liberatio visibilis imitationem accendit, communitas eam stabilit, narratio autem novum lectorem intra eundem circuitum trahit.
Duo ascensus interiores statuunt contemplationem veram sed instabilem esse; brevitas tactus non cognitionem evacuat, sed necessitatem formationis praesentis et possessionis eschatologicae distinguit.
Liberatio interior separationem externam regere debet, sed conversio privatam invisibilitatem retinere non potest; humilitas spectaculum recusat, communio tamen formam publicam requirit.
Baptismus remissionem et regenerationem efficit, sed laus post baptismum in intercessionem transit; sacramentum ordinem misericordiae instituit, non necessitatem eius terminat.
Sanatio voluntatis ordinem affectuum mutat, non vulnerabilitatem temporalem delet; consuetudo correcta adhuc in memoria, separatione et luctu operatur.
Reiectio astrologiae et dualismi in eandem structuram convergit: causalitas externa non potest voluntatem a culpa eximere, quamvis providentia eventuum ordinem excedat cognitionem agentis.
Bonitas ontologica creaturae condicionem sanabilitatis constituit: quia malum naturam propriam non efficit, voluntas aegra restitui potest sine destructione subiecti.
Subiectum non est punctum voluntatis atemporale, sed historia actuum, habituum, exemplorum, sacramentorum et affectuum, quae responsabilitatem et transformationem simul portat.
Causalitas in quattuor ordines distribuitur: intentio mala creaturae, effectus providentialiter ordinatus, liberatio a gratia inchoata et consensus voluntatis ecclesialiter stabilitus.
Tempus conversionis est catastrophicum intra accumulationem: diuturna sedimentatio et mediatio in unum nunc comprimuntur, cuius effectus postea per formationem explicantur.
Epistemologia fit soteriologica: veritas cognita statum subiecti iudicat, sed cognitio plena tantum emergit cum voluntas et affectus ad obiectum cognitum formantur.
Ecclesia operatur ut apparatus temporalis transitus ad aeternum, quia propositionem in allocutionem, affectum in cantum, remissionem in sacramentum et memoriam in intercessionem convertit.
Confessio non solum acta narrat, sed eorum causalitatem performative reordinat et lectorem ex spectatore in gratias agentem, imitatorem atque intercessorem mutat.
Mors relationem non annihilat, sed eam a consuetudine corporali ad dolorem ordinandum, spem resurrectionis et memoriam liturgicam transfert.
Clausura huius gregis aperta manet: conversionem sacramentaliter stabilitam sequuntur vulnerabilitas, iudicium et oratio, dum possessio Sapientiae in terminum eschatologicum differtur.

items.text: Voluntas perversa libidinem gignit, libido consuetudinem, consuetudo divisionem, divisio dilationem, dilatio autem eandem consuetudinem roborat.
Veritas cognita impotentiam manifestat; impotentia exemplis alienis fit inexcusabilis; pudor implorationem aperit; gratia voluntatem ad veritatem iam cognitam reducit.
Conversio visibilis imitationem generat, imitatio novos conversos producit, quorum gaudium commune vim exemplarem ulterioris conversionis amplificat.
Scriptura a textu generali ad allocutionem praesentem transit; allocutio actum efficit; actus narratus vicissim Scripturam alteri lectori ut possibilem allocutionem restituit.
Donum Dei confessionem causalitatis generat, confessio gratiarum actionem, gratiarum actio intercessionem; intercessio agnoscit etiam sanctitatem receptum donum manere.
Eventus adversus effectum salutarem parit; effectus ad providentiam refertur, culpa intentioni relinquitur, atque eadem distinctio novos eventus legendi modum format.
Mens a sensibilibus ad se et supra se ascendit, Sapientiam tangit, ad successionem verborum redit atque ex reditu desiderium stabilioris praesentiae auget.
Vinculum familiare per mortem abrumpitur, abruptio dolorem aperit, dolor coram Deo ordinatur, memoria autem in spem resurrectionis et intercessionem convertitur.
Attractor totius motus est stabilis fruitio Sapientiae: quia nunc indisponibilis manet, omnes mediationes, conversiones et luctus ad praesentiam nondum possessam convergunt.
