sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Invariantes statuuntur: bonum immutabile, creatio omnis naturae et bonitas essendi nullam substantiam malam relinquunt.
Exemplaria corporea, dualistica et deterministica contra invariantes probantur atque ut modos exteriorizandi defectum eliminantur.
Ascensus veritatem supra mentem demonstrat; defectus adhesionis cognitionem ab efficacia salutari separat.
Defectus in historiam voluntatis resolvitur: aversio actus producit, actus consuetudinem, consuetudo necessitatem et voluntatem partialem.
Exempla et Scriptura divisionem voluntatis ad limen adducunt, ubi dilatio suam vim servilem patefacit.
Gratia vincula rumpit et voluntatem sine substitutione integrat; cognitio iam acquisita in consensum et novum ordinem vitae transit.
Liberatio interna professionem, disciplinam, sacramentum et communionem ordinat, unde conversio punctiformis in processum ecclesialem explicatur.
Providentia eventus adversos sine confusione intentionum assumit, dum contemplatio breviter terminum aeternum aperit et ad tempus remittit.
Mors et sanctitas omnem clausuram meritoriam dissolvunt; narratio in misericordiam, sacrificium et intercessionem convertitur.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Imaginatio corporea → exclusio dualismi → veritas incorporea → malum ut privatio → insufficientia cognitionis → genealogia consuetudinis → voluntas divisa → gratia integrans → conversio.
Conversio punctiformis → renuntiatio ordinata → formatio intellectualis → baptismus → communio ecclesialis → providentia narrata → contemplatio brevis → luctus → intercessio.
Exteriorizatio culpae → responsabilitas voluntatis → impossibilitas autonomiae → mediatio sanans → causalitas Deo restituta → possessio aeterna adhuc dilata.
Malum ex classe naturarum in structuram triplicem reclassificatur: privatio ontologica, aversio voluntaria et inertia temporaliter sedimentata.
Subiectum ex substantia contra substantiam pugnantem in unam voluntatem historicam, partialem, culpabilem et sanabilem redescribitur.
Conversio ex mutatione opinionis in integrationem voluntatis et processum formationis sacramentalis, affectivae ac socialis expanditur.
Cognitio dividitur in demonstrationem obiecti, capacitatem adhaerendi et stabilitatem fruitionis; philosophia prioris ordinis sufficientiam amittit.
Tempus ex recipiente neutro in machinam moralem mutatur: actus sedimentat, dilatio servitutem auget, momentum decisivum comprimit, formatio autem effectus explicat.
Scriptura ex deposito propositionum in eventum allocutionis reclassificatur, cuius vis ex tempore, receptione et praeparatione subiecti oritur.
Ecclesia fit apparatus distribuentis cognitionem, affectum, confessionem, sacramentum, resistentiam communem et memoriam defunctorum.
Providentia causalitatem moralem a causalitate eventuum distinguit, ita ut bonum ex malo provenire possit sine conversione malae intentionis in bonam.
Mors et vita sancta reordinantur: mors fit separatio temporalis intra resurrectionem, sanctitas autem materia gratiarum actionis et intercessionis, non titulus debiti.
Gradus superficiei coniungit dissolutionem errorum de malo, discrimen conversionis, renuntiationem, baptismum, contemplationem Ostiensem, mortem Monicae et precem pro ea.
Gradus structuralis componit participationem essendi, voluntatem, consuetudinem, gratiam, providentiam et mediationes ecclesiales in unam machinam formationis temporalis.
Gradus metastrategicus interpretationem a quaestione obiecti ad quaestionem capacitatis transfert atque exemplum, confessionem et intercessionem modos interventionis efficit.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem inter creaturas mutabiles et Sapientiam aeternam distinguit, dum subiectum per successionem ligatur, sanatur et ad praesentiam eschatologicam dirigitur.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus ipsam confessionem adhibet ut redistributionem causalitatis: narratio bonum Deo reddit, culpam voluntati, lectorem autem imitationi et precationi inserit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Gratia principium liberationis praebet et voluntas vere consentit, sed modus quo actio divina consensum efficit sine coactione formaliter indeterminatus manet.
Conversio tamquam actus integer et tamquam processus multistratus cohaeret tantum si limen voluntatis ab ulteriori transformatione intellectus et affectus distinguatur.
Mediationes ecclesiales necessariae sunt, sed immediatio Sapientiae desideratur ut earum terminus; relatio inter necessitatem praesentem et futuram superationem signorum manet tensionis locus.
Remissio baptismalis et culpa posterior simul affirmantur, sed limes inter regenerationem, reliquias habitus et novam culpam non perfecte explicatur.
Providentia bonum ex intentione mala producit, sed modus concursus quo effectus Deo et culpa agenti distribuuntur assertione firmatur potius quam analysi exhaustiva.
Conversio publicam confessionem requirit, dum renuntiatio Augustini spectaculum magnitudinis recusat; visibilitas necessaria a iactantia distinguenda manet.
Fides desperationem luctus excludit, non ipsum dolorem; discrimen inter consuetudinem carnalem et lacrimas recte ordinatas mobile manet.
Deus invariabilis affirmatur, dum gaudium de conversione sermone affectivo variatur; relatio inter immutabilitatem divinam et variationem gaudii in creaturis compressa manet.
Malum sensum mutat cum a substantia ad privationem, ab illa ad aversionem voluntatis atque inde ad consuetudinem temporalem transfertur.
Veritas ex obiecto demonstrabili mutatur in normam quae capacitatem contemplantis iudicat et liberationem ad novum ordinem vitae exigit.
Voluntas ex pluralitate partialium appetituum ad integrum velle transit; in hoc puncto deliberatio cessat et actus incipit.
Scriptura functionem mutat cum ex propositione generali in allocutionem temporalem et personalem recipitur.
Conversio a clausura discriminali ad principium formationis mutatur; quod voluntatem terminat, processum sacramentalem et affectivum aperit.
Vinculum familiare a possessione corporali ad memoriam liturgicam et spem resurrectionis transfertur, sine abolitione doloris separationis.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est campus ordinatus circa fontem immutabilem, in quo defectus ordinem vulnerare potest sed naturam contrariam producere nequit.
Subiectum est nodus diachronicus voluntatum, habituum et relationum: se ligat per repetitionem, ab alio principio solvitur et consensu sanato novum ordinem suscipit.
Tempus est simul sedimentum, limen et peregrinatio: praeteritum consuetudinem format, praesens decisionem comprimit, futurum autem possessionem aeternam differt.
Ecclesia est rete mediationum quod veritatem per textum, vocem, aquam, cantum, exemplum et memoriam distribuit atque subiecta singularia in communionem format.
Navigatio est spiralis: mens ascendit, redit, consuetudinem patitur, iterum per gratiam elevatur et ex singulis reditibus desiderium stabilis praesentiae auget.
Mors est limen quod communionem corporalem frangit sed relationem non delet; affectum in luctum, luctum in precem et memoriam in spem resurrectionis convertit.
Axiomata extracta sufficiunt ad restituendum motum a correctione ontologiae mali per sanationem voluntatis ad incorporationem ecclesialem, mortem et intercessionem.
Systema hoc gradu cohaeret quia bonitatem creaturae, responsabilitatem voluntatis, necessitatem gratiae et permanentem misericordiae rationem sine dualismo componit.
Firmissima structura est coniunctio inter genealogiam consuetudinis et redistributionem causalitatis, qua culpa voluntati, liberatio et bonum Deo tribuuntur.
Minus determinata manet efficientia qua gratia voluntatem integram producit sine coactione; narratio effectum ostendit, sed nexum causaliter non formalizat.
Ordo universalis et providentia firmiter postulantur, sed congruentia omnium particularium et modus quo bonum ex malo elicitur non universaliter demonstrantur.
Quaedam commissurae auctoritate narrationis, analogia conversionum, testimonio signorum et fide eschatologica nituntur potius quam deductione interna completa.
Restitutio verum motum servat: falsas exterioritates excludit, defectum intra voluntatem temporalem localizat, liberationem per mediationem efficit et clausuram in misericordiam aperit.
Reductioni axiomaticae resistunt densitas affectuum, temporalitas allocutionis et singularitas luctus, quia hae non exempla accidentalia sed media sunt quibus systema suam doctrinam efficit.

The system asks how the creature, to whom the truth concerning the immutable good is already manifest, may be freed from evil—not substantial, but voluntarily sedimented—and perfect freedom in temporal, ecclesial, and mortal life.

The global thesis removes evil from the order of natures, situates it in privation and in the will bound by a perverse habit, and attributes liberation to healing grace and to the mediations of Christ, Scripture, and the Church.

The diagnostic and reconstructive argument excludes false ontologies, genealogically explains the division of the will, then demonstrates the effects of liberation through confession, sacrament, providence, and intercession.

The movement proceeds from ascent to incorporeal truth to the detection of practical impotence, thence to an integrated will, an ecclesially formed life, and death understood under the hope of resurrection.

The progression is cumulative and effected through mutation: vision detects weakness, weakness discloses the history of habit, history prepares the threshold of grace, while the converted act requires further formation.

Mediation is progressively amplified from the healing incarnation to scriptural address, sacrament, chant, communion, and liturgical memory, without which truth does not pass into temporally ordered possession.

Conversion is at once a point-like event and a multilayered process: the will is integrated at a single threshold, but intellect, affect, profession, habit, and social relation are reformed at different times.
The closure produces not definitive possession but prayer: temporal mediation is ordered toward stable Wisdom, while mercy and intercession remain necessary even after a praiseworthy life.
[Persistent] God is the immutable good and the source of every nature; therefore nothing created has in itself the character of an opposed substance.
[Persistent] Whatever exists retains some goodness; evil, therefore, is not a positive nature, but a diminution of good and a turning-away of the will.
[Mutating] The created order first encompasses the inequality of natures, then absorbs the discordances of wills and events within ordering providence.
[Persistent] Fault is located in the will of the creature and cannot be transferred to a contrary nature, the stars, or an effect providentially good.
[Mutating] Knowledge of truth shows the object, but produces neither stable adhesion nor maturity of will and intellect unless the subject is healed.
[Attractor] Immutable Truth and Wisdom remain above the temporal mind and furnish the norm of judgment and the end of desire.
[Persistent] Grace does not abolish the will, but breaks its bonds, arouses consent, and brings partial wills into an integral act.
[Mutating] Mediation extends from Christ and Scripture to sacraments, chant, communion, and intercession, because the healing of the subject requires a distributed form.
[Mutating] Voluntary acts are sedimented in time into a habit resembling necessity, which can leave affective traces even after rational correction.
[Emergent] Conversion is a decisive threshold within a long process, whose effects alter will, intellect, habit, social condition, and ecclesial incorporation at different times.
[Emergent] Providence can produce a salutary effect from an adverse event or evil intention without dissolving the agent's fault into the goodness of the effect.
[Emergent] Confession distributes causality asymmetrically: the will bears responsibility for sin, but the beginning, remedy, and fruit of liberation are rendered to God.
[Terminal] Baptism establishes conversion in ecclesial regeneration, yet does not remove future fault or the enduring necessity of mercy.
[Attractor] The mind can touch Wisdom temporally, but stable possession of eternal presence remains unavailable within the succession of present life.
[Terminal] No human holiness closes judgment; Christ's sacrifice, mercy, and intercession constitute the ultimate form of memory and hope.

Evil is transferred from the hypothesis of an opposed substance to privation, thence to the perverse will, habit, and affective residues; its negative identity remains, but its locus of operation becomes temporally denser.
The will is first the locus of turning-away, then the field of division, finally consent aroused by grace; the same faculty receives fault and liberation, though not under the same causal principle.
Incorporeal truth retains its identity, but changes its function: from the end of ascent it becomes an accusation of impotence, then a norm of formation and an eschatological attractor.

Habit is unfolded from a carnal impediment into a genealogy of bondage and persists after conversion as affective memory; it is not destroyed by a single act, but gradually transferred to a new order.
Mediation migrates from the way of Christ against pride to the personal scriptural voice and to multiple ecclesial apparatuses, while its function of healing and stabilizing adhesion remains.
Interior ascent returns twice with a changed function: first it demonstrates truth but leaves the contemplator weak; later it briefly touches eternity and reveals the condition of the wayfarer.
Anti-dualism extends from cosmological exclusions to the unity of the soul and moral responsibility, then is absorbed into the distinction between evil intention and providential effect.
Example is transformed from a comparison of doctrines into a machine of conversion: alien narratives dissolve excuses, whereas visible conversion generates new imitations.
Time changes from created succession into the medium of the sedimentation of fault, the crisis between now and delay, and the space of sacramental formation, mourning, and hope.
Universal order changes into narrative providence: the goodness of the whole not only contains metaphysical incongruities, but also turns adverse events toward salvation without moral confusion.

After undermining external causality, astrology recedes from the manifest field; its work structurally persists in every subsequent refusal by which fault is transferred to nature, necessity, or chance.

Corporeal images of God and astrology remain local refutations; at the present level their common function rises, namely, the exclusion of every causality that diminishes the immutable good or extrinsically dissolves the responsibility of the will.
The local distinction between Platonists and Scripture is amplified upward into the general difference between knowledge of the end and the way that renders the subject fit for fruition.

Particular Christological delimitations do not constitute the union of the integral doctrine at this level; their higher force is that the mediator can be neither a mere teacher nor an appearance without full humanity.
Victorinus, Anthony, and the courtiers remain lower cases, but together show that another's example can prove the capacity for present change, destroy excuses, and socially propagate conversion.

Monica's life is not a biographical appendix, but a demonstration at the present level by which virtue, correction, providence, contemplation, death, and intercession are ordered under the same rationale of gift.
The two interior ascents unite the units: the former discloses the necessity of mediation, the latter anticipates the end of mediations but still defers its possession.

The act of conversion that locally closes in the crisis of the will is not, at the present level, an end, but a transition into formation, sacrament, community, discipline of the affects, and an understanding of death.

Baptism is terminal with respect to antecedent fault and ecclesial incorporation, not with respect to the whole journey; further fault, mourning, and mercy prevent its being turned into an absolute closure.
The system admits no uncreated matter or evil substance from which the defect of the will may be causally derived.
The plurality of affects and wills proves neither a plurality of souls nor an ontologically contrary principle.
God is neither divided by space nor defined as the end of cognition through a bodily image, sound, or measure.
Astral or external causality does not remove fault, because uncertain prediction and acquired necessity do not abolish the antecedent voluntary act.
Philosophical knowledge, metaphysical certainty, and correct doctrine are not a sufficient cause of adhesion, action, or spiritual maturity.
The will possesses no autonomous foundation by which it may break its habit or produce continence from its own strength.
The delay of conversion is not a neutral space; the promise of an indefinite future effects the present retention of the old order.
Private interiority and external mediation, taken separately, do not complete conversion; internal healing requires incorporation, confession, and communion.
A providentially good effect does not justify an evil intention, nor does the success of an event constitute the moral measure of the agent.
Virtue, baptism, and a praiseworthy life establish neither absolute innocence nor a right to salvation without mercy.
No creature, profession, bodily proximity, or earthly homeland can provide the ultimate end of desire or communion.
It must be false that being is convertible with spatial extension; otherwise incorporeal God and truth above the mind would be reduced to nothing.
It must be false that the mutable mind produces the norm of its own judgment; otherwise ascent to immutable truth would lose its foundation.
It must be false that knowledge of the end carries with it the capacity to attain it; otherwise the transition from metaphysics to will and grace would become superfluous.
It must be false that habit is an alien nature or primary necessity; otherwise both past imputability and present healability would collapse.
It must be false that grace replaces the will by compulsion; the system requires a will that truly consents, although it does not itself furnish the principle of liberation.
It must be false that conversion consummates all orders of the subject by a single decree; otherwise intellectual, sacramental, and affective formation would lose their necessary structure.
It must be false that a good effect demonstrates the goodness of intention; otherwise providence and moral recompense would become indistinguishable.
It must be false that sacramental regeneration excludes every future fault; otherwise post-baptismal mercy and intercession for the praiseworthy would be incoherent.
It must be false that God's immediacy makes temporal mediations superfluous; the state of the wayfarer needs signs, although their end promises transcendence.
No ontological exteriority remains in which evil, matter, or a contrary nature could be coordinated with the created order.
There is no neutral self and no empty future between contending wills; delay itself is already part of the old order.
The possibility of a subject morally regenerating itself from nothing is inadmissible; freedom is received as healed, not produced as its own cause.
Stable and immediate possession of Wisdom is absent within temporal life; this unavailability gives direction and an end to present mediations.
No account of merits can close judgment or make mercy superfluous; the absence of absolute innocence generates terminal prayer.
Full transparency of self and providence remains unavailable; confession attributes the ultimate cause to God without exhaustive knowledge of all means.
The ultimate homeland is contained neither in place, burial, success, nor bodily proximity; the terminal form of communion requires resurrection and liturgical memory.
Ontological privation, moral habit, and affective persistence are composed into one theory of evil that lacks its own essence but acquires temporal efficacy through sedimented acts.
Ascent to truth, the impotence of conversion, and immaturity after conversion demonstrate that salvific knowledge is not mere information, but transformation of the subject's capacity.
Responsibility and dependence on grace cohere asymmetrically: the subject fabricates bondage through its own acts, but cannot provide for itself the principle by which its bonds are broken.
Incarnation, scriptural address, and sacramental incorporation constitute one series by which higher truth descends to the temporal capacities of the subject and raises them to itself.
Conversion closes the division of the will in one act, but not all its causes, habits, and effects at one time; the event is a form of compression of a process, not the negation of a process.
Universal order and asymmetric providence allow a good effect to arise from discord without substantializing evil or absolving perverse intention.

The example of the convert and ecclesial communion effect a circuit of propagation: visible liberation kindles imitation, community stabilizes it, and narrative draws a new reader into the same circuit.

The two interior ascents establish contemplation as true but unstable; the brevity of the touch does not empty knowledge, but distinguishes the necessity of present formation from eschatological possession.
Interior liberation must govern external separation, but conversion cannot retain private invisibility; humility refuses spectacle, yet communion requires a public form.
Baptism effects remission and regeneration, but praise after baptism passes into intercession; sacrament establishes the order of mercy, not the end of its necessity.
The healing of the will changes the order of affects, not temporal vulnerability; corrected habit still operates in memory, separation, and mourning.
The rejection of astrology and dualism converges in the same structure: external causality cannot exempt the will from fault, even though the providence of events exceeds the agent's knowledge.

The ontological goodness of the creature constitutes the condition of healability: because evil does not produce a nature of its own, the sick will can be restored without the destruction of the subject.
The subject is not an atemporal point of will, but a history of acts, habits, examples, sacraments, and affects, which bears responsibility and transformation together.
Causality is distributed across four orders: the evil intention of the creature, the providentially ordered effect, liberation initiated by grace, and the consent of the will stabilized ecclesially.
The time of conversion is catastrophic within accumulation: prolonged sedimentation and mediation are compressed into a single now, whose effects are subsequently unfolded through formation.
Epistemology becomes soteriological: known truth judges the condition of the subject, but full knowledge emerges only when will and affect are formed toward the known object.
The Church operates as a temporal apparatus of passage to the eternal, because it turns proposition into address, affect into chant, remission into sacrament, and memory into intercession.
Confession not only narrates deeds, but performatively reorders their causality and changes the reader from spectator into one giving thanks, an imitator, and an intercessor.
Death does not annihilate relation, but transfers it from bodily habit to ordered grief, the hope of resurrection, and liturgical memory.
The closure of this group remains open: sacramentally stabilized conversion is followed by vulnerability, judgment, and prayer, while possession of Wisdom is deferred to the eschatological end.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: A perverse will generates lust, lust habit, habit division, division delay, and delay in turn strengthens the same habit.
Known truth reveals impotence; through the examples of others impotence becomes inexcusable; shame opens supplication; grace returns the will to truth already known.
Visible conversion generates imitation; imitation produces new converts, whose common joy amplifies the exemplary force of further conversion.
Scripture passes from a general text to a present address; the address effects an act; the narrated act in turn restores Scripture to another reader as a possible address.
God's gift generates confession of causality, confession thanksgiving, thanksgiving intercession; intercession recognizes that even holiness remains a received gift.
An adverse event produces a salutary effect; the effect is referred to providence, fault is left to intention, and the same distinction forms a way of reading new events.
The mind ascends from sensible things to itself and above itself, touches Wisdom, returns to the succession of words, and through that return increases its desire for a more stable presence.
The familial bond is broken by death, the break opens grief, grief is ordered before God, while memory is transformed into hope of resurrection and intercession.
The attractor of the entire movement is stable fruition of Wisdom: because it remains unavailable now, all mediations, conversions, and griefs converge upon a presence not yet possessed.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: The invariants are established: the immutable good, the creation of every nature, and the goodness of being leave no evil substance.
Corporeal, dualistic, and deterministic models are tested against the invariants and eliminated as modes of externalizing defect.
Ascent demonstrates truth above the mind; the failure of adhesion separates knowledge from salvific efficacy.
Defect is resolved into the history of the will: turning-away produces act, act habit, habit necessity and a partial will.
Examples and Scripture bring the division of the will to a threshold, where delay reveals its servile force.
Grace breaks bonds and integrates the will without substitution; knowledge already acquired passes into consent and a new order of life.
Internal liberation orders profession, discipline, sacrament, and communion, whence point-like conversion is unfolded into an ecclesial process.
Providence assumes adverse events without confusion of intentions, while contemplation briefly opens the eternal end and sends one back to time.
Death and holiness dissolve every meritorious closure; narrative turns into mercy, sacrifice, and intercession.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Corporeal imagination → exclusion of dualism → incorporeal truth → evil as privation → insufficiency of knowledge → genealogy of habit → divided will → integrating grace → conversion.
Point-like conversion → ordered renunciation → intellectual formation → baptism → ecclesial communion → narrated providence → brief contemplation → mourning → intercession.
Externalization of fault → responsibility of the will → impossibility of autonomy → healing mediation → causality restored to God → eternal possession still deferred.
Evil is reclassified from the class of natures into a threefold structure: ontological privation, voluntary turning-away, and temporally sedimented inertia.
The subject is redescribed from a substance struggling against a substance into one historical, partial, culpable, and healable will.
Conversion is expanded from a change of opinion into integration of the will and a process of sacramental, affective, and social formation.
Knowledge is divided into demonstration of the object, capacity for adhesion, and stability of fruition; philosophy loses the sufficiency of the first order.
Time changes from a neutral receptacle into a moral machine: act sediments, delay increases bondage, the decisive moment compresses, while formation unfolds the effects.
Scripture is reclassified from a deposit of propositions into an event of address, whose force arises from time, reception, and the preparation of the subject.
The Church becomes an apparatus distributing knowledge, affect, confession, sacrament, common resistance, and the memory of the dead.
Providence distinguishes moral causality from the causality of events, such that good can result from evil without the conversion of evil intention into good.
Death and holy life are reordered: death becomes temporal separation within resurrection, while holiness becomes matter for thanksgiving and intercession, not a title of debt.
The surface level joins the dissolution of errors concerning evil, the crisis of conversion, renunciation, baptism, the Ostian contemplation, Monica's death, and prayer for her.
The structural level composes participation in being, will, habit, grace, providence, and ecclesial mediations into a single machine of temporal formation.
The metastrategic level transfers interpretation from the question of the object to the question of capacity and makes example, confession, and intercession modes of intervention.

The ontological and temporal level distinguishes reality between mutable creatures and eternal Wisdom, while the subject is bound, healed, and directed toward eschatological presence through succession.

The methodological and performative level employs confession itself as a redistribution of causality: narrative renders good to God, fault to the will, and inserts the reader into imitation and prayer.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Grace provides the principle of liberation and the will truly consents, but the manner in which divine action effects consent without compulsion remains formally indeterminate.
Conversion as an integral act and as a multilayered process cohere only if the threshold of the will is distinguished from the further transformation of intellect and affect.
Ecclesial mediations are necessary, but the immediacy of Wisdom is desired as their end; the relation between present necessity and the future overcoming of signs remains a locus of tension.
Baptismal remission and subsequent fault are simultaneously affirmed, but the boundary between regeneration, residuals of habit, and new fault is not perfectly explained.
Providence produces good from evil intention, but the mode of concurrence by which effect is distributed to God and fault to the agent is affirmed rather than exhaustively analyzed.
Conversion requires public confession, while Augustine's renunciation refuses a spectacle of greatness; necessary visibility remains to be distinguished from boastfulness.
Faith excludes the despair of mourning, not pain itself; the distinction between carnal habit and rightly ordered tears remains mobile.
God is affirmed as invariable, while joy concerning conversion is varied in affective discourse; the relation between divine immutability and variation of joy in creatures remains compressed.
Evil changes meaning when it is transferred from substance to privation, from that to turning-away of the will, and thence to temporal habit.
Truth changes from a demonstrable object into a norm that judges the capacity of the contemplator and demands liberation toward a new order of life.
The will passes from a plurality of partial desires to integral willing; at this point deliberation ceases and action begins.
Scripture changes function when it is received from a general proposition into a temporal and personal address.
Conversion changes from crisis closure into the beginning of formation; what ends the will opens the sacramental and affective process.
The familial bond is transferred from bodily possession to liturgical memory and the hope of resurrection, without abolition of the pain of separation.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly an ordered field around an immutable source, in which defect can wound order but cannot produce a contrary nature.
The subject is a diachronic node of wills, habits, and relations: it binds itself through repetition, is loosed by another principle, and receives a new order through healed consent.
Time is at once sediment, threshold, and pilgrimage: the past forms habit, the present compresses decision, while the future defers eternal possession.
The Church is a network of mediations that distributes truth through text, voice, water, chant, example, and memory, and forms individual subjects into communion.
Navigation is spiral: the mind ascends, returns, suffers habit, is again raised through grace, and from individual returns increases its desire for stable presence.
Death is a threshold that breaks bodily communion but does not destroy relation; it transforms affect into mourning, mourning into prayer, and memory into hope of resurrection.
The extracted axioms suffice to restore the movement from the correction of the ontology of evil through the healing of the will to ecclesial incorporation, death, and intercession.
The system coheres at this level because it combines the goodness of the creature, responsibility of the will, the necessity of grace, and the enduring rationale of mercy without dualism.
The strongest structure is the conjunction between the genealogy of habit and the redistribution of causality, by which fault is attributed to the will, liberation and good to God.
Less determined remains the efficacy by which grace produces an integral will without compulsion; the narrative shows the effect, but does not formalize the causal nexus.
Universal order and providence are firmly posited, but the congruity of all particulars and the manner in which good is elicited from evil are not universally demonstrated.
Certain joints rely on the authority of narrative, the analogy of conversions, the testimony of signs, and eschatological faith rather than on complete internal deduction.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement: it excludes false exteriorities, locates defect within the temporal will, effects liberation through mediation, and opens closure into mercy.

The density of affects, the temporality of address, and the singularity of mourning resist axiomatic reduction, because these are not accidental examples but the media through which the system effects its doctrine.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo subiectum, sibi opacum et successione distractum, intra cognitionem Dei omniscientis veritatem de se, mundo et tempore recipere possit.
Introspectio non autonomiam constituit, sed dependentiam epistemicam, ontologicam et soteriologicam a veritate immutabili detegit.

Argumentatio confessionem, exclusionem apophaticam, analysim experientiae et reconstructionem metaphysicam coniungit, ut errores voluntatis et errores grammaticae sub eadem disciplina veritatis corrigantur.
Motus a signis exterioribus in memoriam et operationes animi descendit, sed interioritatem transcendit versus veritatem, aeternitatem et unitatem divinam.
Progressio est recursiva et spiralis: confessio atque analysis solvunt falsas clausuras, sed singulae solutiones novam opacitatem et ulteriorem conversionem aperiunt.
Dispersio moraliter ut cupiditas et temporaliter ut distentio apparet; utraque attentionem a fine uno in multa obiecta vel momenta distribuit.
Introspectio distantiam inter creaturam mutabilem et Deum immutabilem detegit, sed sola mediatio Christi eam in viam reconciliationis et collectionis convertit.
Clausura definitiva differtur: subiectum manet inter sanationem incohatam, cognitionem non exhaustam, praesentem distentionem et pacem futuram.
[Persistent] Veritas divina immutabilis et aeternitas tota praesens mensuram praebent qua mens mutabilis, voluntas divisa et successio creata iudicantur.
[Persistent] Creatura, quia mutabilis et facta, nec causa sui nec principium sufficiens cognitionis, ordinis aut collectionis suae est.
[Persistent] Confessio Deo scientiam non addit, sed confitentem et audientem intra ordinem veritatis, illuminationis et affectus recti constituit.
[Mutating] Memoria ex campo imaginum, notionum et agnitionis in operationem praesentem convertitur, qua praeteritum absentem vitam temporalem adhuc format.
[Emergent] Interiorem sequi non est in mente claudi: interioritas est limes ubi signa creata, vestigia temporalia et iudicium veritatis supra subiectum concurrunt.
[Persistent] Proximitas animi sibi ipsi nec plenam sui comprehensionem nec integrum sui praesentem efficit.
[Emergent] Dispersio est una structura moraliter et temporaliter expressa: amor in multa dividitur sicut vita inter memoriam, attentionem et exspectationem distenditur.
[Mutating] Attentio transit a facultate praesentem successionem metiente ad locum strategicum ubi amor aut finem ordinat aut a bono creato captivatur.
[Persistent] Res creatae, corpus, motus et tempus bona dependentia sunt; error incipit cum medium in finem, signum in rem ultimam aut creaturam in principium autonomum mutatur.
[Persistent] Gratia et illuminatio actionem creatam non annihilant, sed facultatem cognoscendi, resistendi et ordinandi praebent quam subiectum sibi dare nequit.
[Attractor] Unitas ad Deum est attractor communis continentiae et intentionis: amores dispersi atque tempora animi non delentur, sed ad unum finem colliguntur.
[Terminal] Christus mediator coniungit mortalitatem cum iustitia atque vitam distentam ad Deum dirigit, sine confusione distantiae Creatoris et creaturae.
[Emergent] Eadem forma transitionis per gradus recurrit: pars in totum transit, praesentia in vestigium, appetitus in consuetudinem, actus in vitam.
[Terminal] Cognitio fidelis non comprehensione exhaustiva clauditur, sed confessione limitis, petitione illuminationis et spe consummationis nondum praesentis.
Confessio identitatem functionalem retinet: in utroque campo informatio Dei excluditur, dum actus confitentis ad veritatem et affectum rectum convertitur.
Memoria mutatur ab amplitudine contentorum interiorum in praesentem operationem temporalem; functio agnitionis persistit, sed eius obiectum fit vestigium rei absentis.
Veritas interior identitatem stabilem servat, sed a mensura amoris et beatitudinis ad criterium exegeseos, causalitatis et sermonis de tempore extenditur.
Dispersio migrat ex campo cupiditatis in structuram temporis: quod prius divisio amoris erat, fit divisio praesentiae inter multa tempora animi.
Continentia functionem mutat in intentionem: privatio voluptatis iam recusata in recollectionem amorum, deinde in collectionem vitae temporalis convertitur.
Mediator ab agente reconciliationis ad principium directionis temporalis amplificatur; mortalitas eius ad creaturam distentam pertinet, iustitia ad finem immutabilem.
Praesens mutatur a statu morali examinando in operationem quae memoriam et exspectationem coniungit; examinatio conscientiae fit examinatio ipsius praesentiae.
Veritas beatitudinem definiens in Verbum creatorium absorbetur: finis desiderii et principium essendi non confunduntur, sed eadem stabilitate divina ordinantur.
Creaturae a signis Conditoris in universum ordinem temporalem migrant; significatio earum nunc etiam dependentiam causalitatis, loci et temporis ostendit.
Applicatio anti-Donatistica munere locali peracto evanescit: regulam contra iudicium cordis confirmat, sed structuram creationis et temporis non gubernat.
Taxonomia imaginum, affectionum et disciplinarum memoriae localis manet; ad gradum praesentem ascendit sola functio memoriae ut retentio, agnitio et relatio ad absentiam.
Triplex cupiditas, localiter per genera tentationis ordinata, sursum amplificatur in legem generalem captationis attentionis atque dispersionis vitae.
Aporiae de longitudine praesentis et motu corporali localiter tempus examinant; praesentis gradus conclusio est nullam praesentiam creatam integre possideri.

Enumeratio angelorum, daemonum et artium falsarum localis est; ad gradum praesentem ascendit exclusio omnis mediationis quae distantiam sine coniunctione mortalitatis et iustitiae superare praetendit.
Analysis beatitudinis non manet argumentum separatum, sed attractorem collectionis definit: gaudium verum est finis ad quem attentio et vita distenta ordinantur.
Refutatio circuituum caelestium ut essentiae temporis localis manet; effectus superior est demotio omnis creaturae visibilis a munere mensurae ultimae.
Polemica adversus iudicium ad hominem structuram confessionis illustrat, sed novo campo temporis non integratur atque ideo praemissa generatrix gregis non fit.
Creatio ex nihilo argumentum localiter cosmologicum est, sed sursum transit in principium universale dependentiae, quod etiam cognitionem et facultatem moralem ordinat.
Auditores caritate coniuncti et lectores affectu excitati duas figuras locales praebent; gradus praesens eas coniungit in communitatem cui confessio cognitionem performative ordinat.
Confessio neque informatio Dei neque narratio externa est; eius veritas in conversione affectus et subiecti consistit.
Subiectum nec sibi plene transparens nec sibi integraliter praesens est; introspectio igitur iudicium ultimum sui praebere non potest.
Deus non continetur memoria sicut obiectum locale, nec tempus continet Deum sicut receptaculum universale.
Sensus, sonus exterior et auctoritas locutoris veritatem ultimam non constituunt; omnia iudicio veritatis interioris subiciuntur.
Corpus et creaturae non sunt per se mala, sed neque principia coaeterna aut fines ultimi; malum ex inordinatione dependentiae oritur.
Tempus neque motus corporis neque series rerum in regionibus praeteriti et futuri reposita est.
Nec oboedientia autonoma nec superioritas spiritualis reconciliationem efficit; utraque gratiam et structuram verae mediationis praeterit.
Vita praesens neque perfectionem stabilem neque praesens sine transitu admittit; omnis clausura intra statum mortalem revocatur.
Ut systema constet, falsum esse debet subiectum sui causam, mensuram, medicum et iudicem sufficientem esse.
Falsum esse debet veritatem immutabilem ex consensu, affectu vel operatione mentis mutabilis produci.
Falsum esse debet tempus esse campum neutralem et independentem in quo Deus, mundus et anima eodem modo collocentur.
Falsum esse debet pluralitatem bonorum vel momentorum per se ordinem efficere; sine fine uno multiplicitas in dispersionem transit.
Falsum esse debet desiderium veri aut familiaritatem vocabuli sufficere ad cognitionem rectam; voluntas et ratio illuminatione atque correctione egent.
Falsum esse debet praesentiam rei apud animum possessionem rei vel transparantiam animi efficere; mensuratio et agnitio per vestigia operantur.
Falsum esse debet transitum a mutabilitate ad immutabilitatem ex sola introspectione vel analysi temporis deduci posse; utrumque mediatorem theologice requirit.
Possibilitas maxime indisponibilis est praesens creatum quod se totum possideat: vita semper iam memoratur, adhuc exspectatur aut attentione transit.
Systema circum absentiam originis propriae ordinatur: subiectum neque esse, veritatem, bonum neque perseverantiam ex se producit.
Omne alterum coaeternum Deo excluditur; neque materia, tempus, locus, memoria neque mens potest intervallum independentem praebere.
Comprehensio positiva plena animae, temporis et aeternitatis inadmissibilis manet; cognitio vera potest limitem constituere quem transcendere non potest.
Salus ut fuga autonoma ex corpore, successione aut relatione sociali impossibilis est; navigatio manet intra mortalitatem, gratiam et mediationem.
Absentia ordinans est pax plena nondum possessa: eam confessio, continentia, intentio et mediatio appetunt sine praesentem statum pro consummatione sumendo.
Confessio est operatio epistemico-affectiva quae opacitatem subiecti et ignorantiam temporis sub iudicio veritatis ponit, non simplex relatio factorum.
Memoria identitatem personalem non ut archivum clausum sed ut retentionem praesentem constituit, qua agnitio et temporalitas eodem vestigio operantur.
Cupiditas est distentio moraliter qualificata: multa non tantum successionem vitae componunt, sed attentionem a fine uno captivam faciunt.
Continentia est forma temporalis intentionis, quia amores colligere idem fit ac exspectationem, attentionem et memoriam ad unum finem ordinare.
Veritas interior simul errores amoris et errores interpretationis corrigit; ideo epistemologia et disciplina voluntatis structuram iudicii communem habent.
Bonum creatum et tempus creatum eadem lege dependentiae reguntur: neutrum malum est, sed utrumque falsum principium fit si a causa et fine separatur.
Interioritas tensionem constitutivam gerit: ibi veritas certissime iudicat, quamvis animus qui iudicatur neque se totum comprehendat neque sibi totus praesens sit.
Mediatio Christi non solum culpam reconciliat, sed mortalitatem temporalem ad iustitiam et praesentiam divinam dirigit, sine successionis abolitione immediata.
Forma minima transitionis per totum systema replicatur: quod futurum est per attentionem transit, quod appetitur per usum transit, et uterque transitus memoriam vel consuetudinem format.
Ignorantia virium moralium et aporia temporis eandem disciplinam exigunt: simulatio certitudinis excluditur, dum actio sub illuminatione et misericordia continuatur.
Subiectum non est punctum simplex conscientiae, sed nexus appetitus, memoriae, attentionis et exspectationis, quem veritas transcendens iudicat.
Tempus fit medium ethicum, quia qualitas vitae pendet non solum ab obiectis electis, sed a modo quo attentio inter praesentia, vestigia et fines distribuitur.
Sanatio est reconfiguratio temporalis voluntatis: gratia non praeteritum delet aut successionem sistit, sed memoriam, usum praesentem et exspectationem ad unum ordinat.
Confessio praesentem statum contra duas falsas temporalitates tuetur: defensionem per praeteritum meritum et praesumptionem futurae perseverantiae.
Creatio et gratia analogam, non identicam, asymmetriam exhibent: sicut creatura esse sibi non dat, ita voluntas dispersa collectionem sibi sufficienter non confert.
Mediatio distantiam Creatoris et creaturae non aufert, sed eam in relationem traversabilem mutat, quia idem mediator mortalitatem participat et ad iustitiam immutabilem refert.
Certitudo veritatis et provisionalitas sui-examinis simul constant: mens certum principium iudicii recipit, sed applicationem eius ad motiva et durationes imperfecte metitur.
Historia personalis et historia creata eadem forma transitus leguntur: exspectata per praesentem actionem in memoriam transeunt, dum finis aeternus successionem sine successione ordinat.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Opacitas sui confessionem generat; confessio illuminationem petit; illuminatio subtiliorem opacitatem detegit; nova cognitio igitur ad confessionem redit.
Bonum creatum attentionem allicit; attentio finem ei concedit; finis falsus animam dispergit; dispersio infirmitatem manifestat; infirmitas misericordiam petit.
Exspectatio per attentionem in memoriam transit; multiplicatio transituum distentionem vitae producit; distentio desiderium collectionis auget.
Gratia resistendi facultatem dat; resistentia vulnus residuum manifestat; vulnus petitionem renovat; petitio dependentiam a gratia confirmat.
Sonus exterior ad iudicium interius remittitur; iudicium Verbum aeternum quaerit; Verbum rursus sonum Scripturae interpretandum restituit.
Quaestio agnitionem praesupponit, agnitio memoriam, memoria vestigium, vestigium rem absentem; quaerere igitur praesentiam per absentiam recursive operatur.
Attractor totius gregis est unum immutabile, ad quod amores per continentiam et tempora animi per intentionem colliguntur.
Superbia circuitum fugae impedit: subiectum etiam de negatione laudis gloriatur atque mediatorem secundum propriam excellentiam fingit, separationem sic reproducens.
