sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Creatura mutabilis + veritas immutabilis → differentia ontologica quae introspectionem, confessionem et analysim temporis necessarias facit.
Signum exterior → iudicium interior → exclusio falsae ontologiae → agnitio principii transcendentis.
Memoria + exspectatio + attentio → praesentia vestigiorum → identitas temporalis sine possessione plena sui.
Bonum creatum + attentio inordinata → mutatio medii in finem → cupiditas → dispersio moraliter et temporaliter amplificata.
Dispersio + opacitas → confessio limitis → petitio illuminationis et misericordiae → facultas partialis correctionis.
Gratia + attentio rectificata → continentia/intentione → recollectio plurium sub fine uno → renovata probatio per successionem.
Distantia irreducibilis + mediator mortalis et iustus → reconciliatio sine confusione → sanatio incohata → consummatio extra clausuram praesentis.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Omniscientia divina → inutilitas informationis → confessio performativa → interioritatis exploratio → memoria et vestigia → opacitas sui → analysis praesentiae → distentio temporalis.
Distentio → captatio attentionis a bonis creatis → triplex cupiditas → confessio infirmitatis → gratia et illuminatio → continentia sive intentio → collectio ad unum.
Distinctio Creatoris et creaturae → exclusio autocausationis et temporis coaeterni → impossibilitas ascensus autonomi → mediatio Christi → sanatio temporalis → pax futura sine clausura exhaustiva.
Interiority ex spatio autonomiae in locum relationis reclassificatur, ubi subiectum a veritate quam non producit iudicatur.
Memoria ex receptaculo contentorum in infrastructuram agnitionis, identitatis et temporalitatis mutatur.
Tempus ex receptaculo cosmico in distributionem praesentium operationum animi transfertur, sine reductione ad fictionem privatam.
Peccatum ex proprietate rei sensibilis in modum captationis attentionis reclassificatur, quo usus, cognitio vel societas finem usurpat.
Continentia ex suppressione voluptatis in artem collectionis amorum et temporum sub uno fine convertitur.
Confessio ex relatione praeteritorum in methodum cognitionis praesentis mutatur, quae affectum, lecturam et iudicium intentionum simul exercet.
Mediatio ex scala superioritatis spiritualis in structuram coniunctionis reconstituitur, quae mortalitatem, iustitiam et directionem ad aeternitatem complectitur.
Distinctio Creatoris et creaturae agrum integrum reordinat: eadem asymmetria esse, causalitatem, cognitionem, voluntatem et tempus permeat.
Gradus superficiei confessionem praesentis status, memoriam, tentationes, creationem et naturam temporis tamquam quaestiones expressas proponit.
Gradus structuralis memoriam, attentionem, exspectationem, appetitum et gratiam tamquam distributiones quibus subiectum dispergitur aut colligitur coordinat.
Gradus metastrategicus quaestiones non intra praesuppositiones adversas solvit, sed curiositatem, autonomiam et tempus praevium tamquam falsas constitutiones quaestionis destruit.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem creatam ut dependentiam mutabilem, subiectum ut distentionem praesentium operationum et Deum ut praesentiam sine successione constituit.

Gradus methodologicus et performativus ipsam formam confessionis efficacem facit: reditus, aporiae et negationes lectorem ab informatione ad illuminationem atque ab dispersione ad intentionem transferunt.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Deus in memoria agnoscitur, sed memoria eum localiter non continet; relatio inter notitiam retentam et praesentiam transcendentem manet structuraliter ambigua.
Veritas interior certitudinem praebet, quamvis animus interior sibi opacus maneat; systema criterium certum cum applicatione fallibili componere debet.
Incertum manet utrum tempus sit ipsa affectio animi an res distincta quae tantum per affectionem praesentem mensuratur.
Praesens omni spatio carens cum attentione perdurante componitur, sed modus quo attentio transitionem sustineat sine extensione praesentis non absolvitur.
Gratia omne bonum facultatis tribuit, dum subiectum responsabilitatem resistendi vel cedendi retinet; modus cooperationis non formaliter determinatur.
Analysis distentionis collectionem desiderabilem reddit, sed necessitatem mediatoris ex sola phaenomenologia temporis non demonstrat.
Punctum mutationis memoriae occurrit cum contenta interiora in operationem praesentem retinentem res absentes convertuntur.
Punctum mutationis dispersionis occurrit cum triplex cupiditas desinit esse sola divisio moralium obiectarum et fit forma temporalis vitae in multa.
Punctum mutationis attentionis occurrit cum functio mensurationis temporalis in intentionem normativam ad Deum convertitur.
Punctum mutationis mediationis occurrit cum reconciliatio peccatoris etiam collectionem vitae temporalis ad aeternum finem sustinere incipit.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est machina dependentiarum mutabilium circa centrum immutabile, non planum entium sibi aequaliter praesentium.
Subiectum est nodus appetitus, memoriae, attentionis et exspectationis, cuius unitas effecta potius quam naturaliter possessa est.
Tempus est fluvius non exterior, sed translatio continua qua exspectatum per attentionem in memoratum transit et praesentiam in vestigium mutat.
Certamen principale est distributio attentionis inter multa bona captantia et unum finem ordinantem; cupiditas et distentio sunt duae imagines eiusdem discerptionis.
Navigatio possibilis procedit per confessionem, illuminationem, gratiam et mediatorem; fuga ex condicione creata substituitur directione eius ad Deum.
Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad restituendam structuram communem confessionis, interioritatis, memoriae, dispersionis, temporis, gratiae et mediationis.
Structura firmissima est coniunctio opacitatis sui cum confessione, mutabilitatis cum dependentia et dispersionis cum collectione gratiae sustentata.
Nondum satis determinatur quomodo prima cognitio Dei in memoria adsit neque quomodo tempus ad affectionem animi ontologice referatur.
Cooperatio inter gratiam et voluntatem manet insufficiens ad formulam reducta, quamvis dependentia doni et responsabilitas subiecti simul necessariae sint.
Clausura christologica cohaeret cum condicionibus mediationis, sed ex analysi memoriae et temporis sola non sequitur atque praemissis revelatis nititur.
Cohaerentia gregis ordine lineari minus quam forma recursiva nititur: transitus localis in memoriam, consuetudinem vel vestigium per gradus maiores replicatur.
Reductioni axiomaticae resistunt paradoxum oblivionis et productio successionis ex causa non successiva; utraque limitem explicationis positivae servat.
Restitutio verum motum servat si confessionem, exclusionem, recursionem et mediationem tamquam operationes generatrices retinet, non tamquam argumenta iuxta posita.
The system asks how a subject, opaque to itself and dispersed by succession, can receive within the knowledge of an omniscient God truth about itself, the world, and time.
Introspection establishes not autonomy, but uncovers epistemic, ontological, and soteriological dependence upon immutable truth.

The argumentation joins confession, apophatic exclusion, analysis of experience, and metaphysical reconstruction, so that errors of will and errors of grammar may be corrected under the same discipline of truth.
The movement descends from external signs into memory and the operations of the mind, but transcends interiority toward divine truth, eternity, and unity.
The progression is recursive and spiral: confession and analysis dissolve false closures, but each solution opens a new opacity and a further conversion.
Dispersion appears morally as cupidity and temporally as distention; both distribute attention from one end among many objects or moments.
Introspection uncovers the distance between mutable creature and immutable God, but only Christ's mediation transforms it into a path of reconciliation and gathering.
Definitive closure is deferred: the subject remains between begun healing, unexhausted knowledge, present distention, and future peace.
[Persistent] Immutable divine truth and eternity wholly present provide the measure by which mutable mind, divided will, and created succession are judged.
[Persistent] The creature, because mutable and made, is neither the cause of itself nor a sufficient principle of its own knowledge, order, or gathering.
[Persistent] Confession adds no knowledge to God, but places the confessor and hearer within the order of truth, illumination, and right affection.
[Mutating] Memory is transformed from a field of images, notions, and recognition into a present operation by which the past continues to shape absent temporal life.
[Emergent] To follow the inner is not to be shut up in the mind: interiority is the boundary where created signs, temporal traces, and the judgment of truth above the subject converge.
[Persistent] The mind's proximity to itself produces neither full comprehension of itself nor its complete presence to itself.
[Emergent] Dispersion is one structure expressed morally and temporally: love is divided among many things just as life is distended among memory, attention, and expectation.
[Mutating] Attention passes from a faculty measuring present succession to the strategic place where love either orders an end or is captivated by a created good.

[Persistent] Created things, body, motion, and time are dependent goods; error begins when a means is transformed into an end, a sign into the ultimate thing, or a creature into an autonomous principle.
[Persistent] Grace and illumination do not annihilate created action, but provide a capacity for knowing, resisting, and ordering which the subject cannot give itself.
[Attractor] Unity toward God is the common attractor of continence and intention: dispersed loves and the times of the mind are not erased, but gathered toward one end.
[Terminal] Christ the mediator joins mortality with justice and directs distended life toward God, without confusing the distance between Creator and creature.
[Emergent] The same form of transition recurs through degrees: part passes into whole, presence into trace, appetite into habit, act into life.
[Terminal] Faithful knowledge is not closed by exhaustive comprehension, but by confession of limit, petition for illumination, and hope for a consummation not yet present.
Confession retains its functional identity: in both fields information about God is excluded, while the act of the confessor is turned toward truth and right affection.
Memory is transformed from an amplitude of inner contents into a present temporal operation; the function of recognition persists, but its object becomes the trace of an absent thing.
Inner truth maintains a stable identity, but is extended from a measure of love and blessedness to a criterion of exegesis, causality, and discourse about time.
Dispersion migrates from the field of cupidity into the structure of time: what was formerly a division of love becomes a division of presence among the many times of the mind.
Continence changes function into intention: the previously rejected privation of pleasure is transformed into recollection of loves, then into the gathering of temporal life.
The mediator is enlarged from an agent of reconciliation into a principle of temporal direction; his mortality pertains to the distended creature, justice to the immutable end.
The present is transformed from a moral state to be examined into an operation joining memory and expectation; examination of conscience becomes examination of presence itself.
Truth defining blessedness is absorbed into the creative Word: the end of desire and the principle of being are not confused, but are ordered by the same divine stability.
Creatures migrate from signs of the Creator into the universal temporal order; their significance now also shows the dependence of causality, place, and time.
The anti-Donatist application vanishes once its local role has been performed: it confirms the rule against judgment of the heart, but does not govern the structure of creation and time.
The taxonomy of images, affections, and disciplines of local memory remains; only the function of memory as retention, recognition, and relation to absence rises to the present level.
The triple cupidity, locally ordered through kinds of temptation, is amplified upward into a general law of the capture of attention and the dispersion of life.
Aporias concerning the length of the present and bodily motion examine time locally; the conclusion of the present level is that no created presence is possessed integrally.

The enumeration of angels, demons, and false arts is local; what rises to the present level is the exclusion of every mediation claiming to overcome distance without the conjunction of mortality and justice.
The analysis of blessedness does not remain a separate argument, but defines the attractor of gathering: true joy is the end toward which attention and distended life are ordered.
The refutation of celestial circuits as the essence of time remains local; the higher effect is the demotion of every visible creature from the role of ultimate measure.
The polemic against judgment of a person illustrates the structure of confession, but is not integrated into the new field of time and therefore does not become a generative premise of the cluster.
Creation from nothing is locally a cosmological argument, but passes upward into a universal principle of dependence, which also orders knowledge and moral capacity.
Hearers joined by charity and readers stirred by affection furnish two local figures; the present level joins them in a community for which confession performatively orders knowledge.
Confession is neither information about God nor an external narrative; its truth consists in the conversion of affection and subject.
The subject is neither fully transparent to itself nor integrally present to itself; introspection therefore cannot provide its final judgment of itself.
God is not contained in memory like a local object, nor does time contain God like a universal receptacle.
Sense, external sound, and the authority of the speaker do not establish ultimate truth; all are subjected to the judgment of inner truth.
Body and creatures are not evil in themselves, but neither are they coeternal principles or ultimate ends; evil arises from the disordering of dependence.
Time is neither the motion of a body nor a series of things stored in the regions of past and future.
Neither autonomous obedience nor spiritual superiority produces reconciliation; both bypass grace and the structure of true mediation.
Present life admits neither stable perfection nor a present without passage; every closure within the mortal state is revoked.
For the system to stand, it must be false that the subject is its own sufficient cause, measure, physician, and judge.
It must be false that immutable truth is produced from the consensus, affection, or operation of mutable mind.
It must be false that time is a neutral and independent field in which God, world, and soul are situated in the same manner.
It must be false that a plurality of goods or moments produces order in itself; without one end, multiplicity passes into dispersion.
It must be false that desire for truth or familiarity with a word suffices for right knowledge; will and reason need illumination and correction.
It must be false that the presence of a thing to the mind produces possession of the thing or transparency of mind; measurement and recognition operate through traces.
It must be false that passage from mutability to immutability can be deduced from introspection or analysis of time alone; both theologically require a mediator.
The most unavailable possibility is a created present that possesses itself whole: life is always already remembered, still expected, or passes through attention.
The system is ordered around the absence of its own origin: the subject produces neither being, truth, good, nor perseverance from itself.
Every other thing coeternal with God is excluded; neither matter, time, place, memory, nor mind can furnish an independent interval.
Full positive comprehension of soul, time, and eternity remains inadmissible; true knowledge can establish a limit which it cannot transcend.
Salvation as an autonomous escape from body, succession, or social relation is impossible; navigation remains within mortality, grace, and mediation.
The ordering absence is full peace not yet possessed: confession, continence, intention, and mediation seek it without taking the present state for consummation.
Confession is an epistemic-affective operation that places the opacity of the subject and ignorance of time under the judgment of truth, not a simple report of facts.
Memory constitutes personal identity not as a closed archive but as present retention, through which recognition and temporality operate by the same trace.
Cupidity is morally qualified distention: the many do not merely compose the succession of life, but make attention captive away from the one end.
Continence is a temporal form of intention, because gathering loves is the same as ordering expectation, attention, and memory toward one end.
Inner truth simultaneously corrects errors of love and errors of interpretation; therefore epistemology and discipline of the will have a common structure of judgment.
Created good and created time are governed by the same law of dependence: neither is evil, but each becomes a false principle if separated from cause and end.
Interiority bears a constitutive tension: there truth judges most certainly, although the mind that is judged neither comprehends itself wholly nor is wholly present to itself.
Christ's mediation not only reconciles guilt, but directs temporal mortality toward justice and divine presence, without immediate abolition of succession.
The minimal form of transition is replicated throughout the whole system: what is future passes through attention, what is desired passes through use, and each transition forms memory or habit.
Ignorance of moral powers and the aporia of time demand the same discipline: the simulation of certainty is excluded, while action continues under illumination and mercy.
The subject is not a simple point of consciousness, but a nexus of appetite, memory, attention, and expectation, judged by transcendent truth.
Time becomes an ethical medium, because the quality of life depends not only on chosen objects, but on the manner in which attention is distributed among presences, traces, and ends.
Healing is a temporal reconfiguration of the will: grace does not erase the past or stop succession, but orders memory, present use, and expectation toward one.
Confession protects the present state against two false temporalities: self-defense through past merit and presumption of future perseverance.
Creation and grace exhibit an analogous, not identical, asymmetry: just as the creature does not give being to itself, so the dispersed will does not sufficiently confer gathering upon itself.

Mediation does not remove the distance between Creator and creature, but transforms it into a traversable relation, because the same mediator participates in mortality and refers it to immutable justice.
Certainty of truth and the provisionality of self-examination coexist: the mind receives a certain principle of judgment, but measures its application to motives and durations imperfectly.
Personal history and created history are read in the same form of transition: what is expected passes through present action into memory, while the eternal end orders succession without succession.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Opacity of self generates confession; confession seeks illumination; illumination uncovers a subtler opacity; new knowledge therefore returns to confession.
Created good attracts attention; attention grants it the status of end; the false end disperses the soul; dispersion manifests weakness; weakness seeks mercy.
Expectation passes through attention into memory; multiplication of transitions produces the distention of life; distention increases the desire for gathering.
Grace gives the capacity to resist; resistance manifests the remaining wound; the wound renews petition; petition confirms dependence upon grace.
External sound is referred back to inner judgment; judgment seeks the eternal Word; the Word in turn restores the sound of Scripture to be interpreted.
Questioning presupposes recognition, recognition memory, memory a trace, a trace an absent thing; therefore seeking operates recursively through presence by absence.
The attractor of the whole cluster is the one immutable, toward which loves are gathered through continence and the times of the mind through intention.
Pride obstructs the circuit of escape: the subject glories even in the denial of praise and fashions the mediator according to its own excellence, thereby reproducing separation.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Mutable creature + immutable truth → ontological difference that makes introspection, confession, and analysis of time necessary.
External sign → inner judgment → exclusion of false ontology → recognition of transcendent principle.
Memory + expectation + attention → presence of traces → temporal identity without full possession of self.
Created good + disordered attention → transformation of means into end → cupidity → dispersion amplified morally and temporally.
Dispersion + opacity → confession of limit → petition for illumination and mercy → partial capacity for correction.
Grace + rectified attention → continence/intention → recollection of the many under one end → renewed trial through succession.
Irreducible distance + mortal and just mediator → reconciliation without confusion → begun healing → consummation beyond the closure of the present.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Divine omniscience → uselessness of information → performative confession → exploration of interiority → memory and traces → opacity of self → analysis of the present → temporal distention.
Distention → capture of attention by created goods → triple cupidity → confession of weakness → grace and illumination → continence or intention → gathering toward one.

Distinction between Creator and creature → exclusion of self-causation and coeternal time → impossibility of autonomous ascent → mediation of Christ → temporal healing → future peace without exhaustive closure.
Interiority is reclassified from a space of autonomy into a place of relation, where the subject is judged by a truth it does not produce.
Memory is transformed from a receptacle of contents into an infrastructure of recognition, identity, and temporality.
Time is transferred from a cosmic receptacle into the distribution of present operations of the mind, without reduction to a private fiction.
Sin is reclassified from a property of the sensible thing into a mode of capturing attention, by which use, knowledge, or society usurps the status of end.
Continence is transformed from suppression of pleasure into an art of gathering loves and times under one end.
Confession is transformed from a report of past things into a method of present knowledge, which simultaneously exercises affection, reading, and judgment of intentions.
Mediation is reconstituted from a scale of spiritual superiority into a structure of conjunction, encompassing mortality, justice, and direction toward eternity.
The distinction between Creator and creature reorders the entire field: the same asymmetry permeates being, causality, knowledge, will, and time.
The surface level presents confession of the present state, memory, temptations, creation, and the nature of time as explicit questions.
The structural level coordinates memory, attention, expectation, appetite, and grace as distributions through which the subject is dispersed or gathered.
The metastrategic level solves questions not within opposing presuppositions, but by destroying curiosity, autonomy, and prior time as false constructions of the question.
The ontological and temporal level establishes created reality as mutable dependence, the subject as distention of present operations, and God as presence without succession.

The methodological and performative level renders the very form of confession effective: returns, aporias, and negations transfer the reader from information to illumination and from dispersion to intention.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: God is recognized in memory, but memory does not contain him locally; the relation between retained knowledge and transcendent presence remains structurally ambiguous.
Inner truth provides certainty, although the inner mind remains opaque to itself; the system must reconcile a certain criterion with fallible application.
It remains uncertain whether time is the very affection of the mind or a distinct thing measured only through present affection.
The present lacking all extension is reconciled with enduring attention, but the manner in which attention sustains transition without extension of the present is not resolved.
Grace grants every good of capacity, while the subject retains responsibility for resisting or yielding; the mode of cooperation is not formally determined.
The analysis of distention renders gathering desirable, but does not demonstrate the necessity of a mediator from the phenomenology of time alone.
The mutation point of memory occurs when inner contents are transformed into a present operation retaining absent things.
The mutation point of dispersion occurs when triple cupidity ceases to be merely a division of moral objects and becomes the temporal form of life among many things.
The mutation point of attention occurs when the function of temporal measurement is transformed into normative intention toward God.
The mutation point of mediation occurs when reconciliation of the sinner also begins to sustain the gathering of temporal life toward the eternal end.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a machine of mutable dependencies around an immutable center, not a plane of beings equally present to themselves.
The subject is a node of appetite, memory, attention, and expectation, whose unity is effected rather than naturally possessed.
Time is a river not external, but a continuous translation through which what is expected passes through attention into what is remembered and transforms presence into trace.
The principal conflict is the distribution of attention between many captivating goods and one ordering end; cupidity and distention are two images of the same tearing apart.
Possible navigation proceeds through confession, illumination, grace, and the mediator; escape from the created condition is replaced by its direction toward God.
The present axioms suffice to restore the common structure of confession, interiority, memory, dispersion, time, grace, and mediation.
The firmest structure is the conjunction of opacity of self with confession, mutability with dependence, and dispersion with gathering sustained by grace.
It is not yet sufficiently determined how the first knowledge of God is present in memory, nor how time is ontologically related to affection of the mind.
Cooperation between grace and will remains reduced to an insufficient formula, although dependence upon gift and responsibility of the subject are simultaneously necessary.
The Christological closure coheres with the conditions of mediation, but does not follow from analysis of memory and time alone and rests upon revealed premises.
The coherence of the cluster rests less on linear order than on recursive form: local transition into memory, habit, or trace is replicated through larger degrees.
The paradox of forgetting and the production of succession from a non-successive cause resist axiomatic reduction; both preserve the limit of positive explanation.
Reconstruction preserves the true movement if it retains confession, exclusion, recursion, and mediation as generative operations, not as juxtaposed arguments.
Systema quaerit quomodo dependentia creationis ante omnem successionem in historiam formationis temporalis, ecclesialis et hermeneuticae transeat atque in requiem aeternam terminetur.
Omne esse, formari, illuminari, intelligere, bene operari et quiescere fit distributio unius donationis divinae, cui grammatica creationis per diversos ordines creaturae recurrit.
Argumentatio est reconstructio transversalis quae metaphysicam creationis, disciplinam interpretationis, formationem Ecclesiae et consummationem coniungit sine horum graduum aequatione.
Motus ab origine ontologica non chronologica per formationem et tempus ad ordinem dierum ecclesialiter recodificatum procedit.
Multiplicitas rerum et multiplicitas sensuum eandem structuram participant: unitas fontis diversitatem ordinatam generat, veritate exclusiones eius circumscribente.
Motus verus est recursivus et spiralis, quia narratio creationis regulam formationis Ecclesiae gignit, dum Ecclesia finem latentem ordinis creati retrospecte manifestat.
Caritas axem communem constituit quo interpretatio ad veritatem ordinatur et creatura rationalis ad locum quietis suae fertur.
Clausura systematis non est exhaustio sensuum, sed sabbatum sine vespera, ubi opera temporalia cessant sine reditu ad novum cyclum mutabilitatis.
[Persistent] Deus aeternus, incommutabilis et sibi sufficiens neque creatione augetur neque temporalibus actibus perficitur.
[Persistent] Omnis creatura ex nihilo procedit, nulla substantia divina, materia coaeterna aut natura hostili tamquam principio secundo admissa.
[Persistent] Esse creatum a forma, sapientia et beatitudine distinguitur; ideo omnis creatura mutabilis est et ulterioris formationis capax.
[Mutating] Informitas a capacitate ontologica prope nihil ad statum spiritualem aversionis, obscuritatis et formationis nondum completae extenditur.
[Emergent] Tempus non creationem continet, sed ex mutationibus ordinatis et ex modo temporali quo creatura formam recipit emergit.
[Attractor] Creatura rationalis stabilitatem participat non per immutabilitatem propriam, sed per inhaesionem continuatam et satiationem in Deo.
[Persistent] Verbum increatum est principium creationis et vocatio formativa qua creatura dispersa ad unitatem revocatur.
[Mutating] Spiritus a plenitudine intentionis divinae in Scriptura ad donum cognitionis, caritatis et elevationis creaturae explicatur.
[Attractor] Caritas simul est norma interpretationis, pondus motus spiritualis et principium quietis in bono proprio creaturae.
[Persistent] Unitas fontis potest multiplicitatem veram rerum, enuntiationum et intellectuum generare sine divisione veritatis.
[Emergent] Scriptura est medium temporale et humile Verbi aeterni quod auctoritatem stabilem cum accommodatione multiplici coniungit.
[Mutating] Pluralitas sensuum transit a concordia interpretum ad oeconomiam ecclesialem quae media et intellectus secundum diversas capacitates distribuit.
[Terminal] Fides, signa et opera temporalia ad statum transeuntem pertinent cui sabbatum aeternum sine vespera terminum imponit.
[Emergent] Divina causalitas operationem creaturae participative constituit, ita ut Deus in creatura agat neque actum creatum simpliciter supprimat.
[Attractor] Bonitas singulorum ad bonitatem ordinatam totius et inde ad fruitionem Dei colligitur, non ad autosufficientiam universi.
Creatio ex nihilo identitatem stabilem retinet et tam cosmologiam quam refutationem dualismi regit.
Informitas functionem mutat: primo capacitatem formarum designat, deinde modum aversionis et dependentiae spiritualis.
Lux ab effectu formationis ontologicae ad conversionem ecclesialem migrat, obscuritate residua statum nondum consummatum indicante.
Tempus ab effectu mutationis ad modum receptionis et institutionis creaturae amplificatur.
Inhaesio intellectualis in caritatem gravitantem mutatur: stabilitas super vicissitudinem fit motus recte directus ad requiem.
Pluralitas sensuum retinet veritatem multiplicem, sed ex concordia defensiva in fecunditatem activam sub auctoritate Scripturae extenditur.
Intentio conscia ministri humani in ampliorem operationem Spiritus absorbetur, qui in creatura cognoscit et loquitur.
Ordo dierum a structura originis non chronologica in figuram formationis Ecclesiae transfertur.
Duplex carentia temporis transformationem terminalem patitur: plenitudo per inhaesionem in sabbatum sine vespera colligitur, defectus formae in initium formationis transit.
Status metaphysicus materiae informis manet quaestio localis, dum gradu praesenti capacitas nondum formata fit conditio generalis omnis formationis.
Correspondentiae singulorum dierum cum ministeriis manent locales; distributio mediorum secundum capacitatem sola ad structuram gregis ascendit.
Prioritas originis sine intervallo temporali e quaestione de materia amplificatur in regulam generalem causalitatis divinae.
Distinctio inter veritatem rei et intentionem humanam cum multiplici intelligibilitate enuntiationis pontem inter ontologiam et hermeneuticam constituit.
Recapitulatio ecclesialis grammaticae creationis est emergentia propria huius gradus, non simplex allegoriarum localium aggregatio.
Limites particularis iudicii spiritualis in axiomate superiore auctoritatem participatam, corrigibilem et Scripturae subiectam constituunt.
Tenebrae cosmologicae ut privatio formae opere structuraliter peracto non evanescunt, sed in obscuritatem aversionis et conversionis nondum plenae recodificantur.
Systema excludit Deum temporaliter deliberantem, nova voluntate motum, indigentem aut post laborem quiescentem.
Creatio neque emanatio substantiae divinae neque ordinatio materiae aut naturae hostilis coaeternae est.
Malum et informitas principia positiva Deo adversa esse non possunt, sed privationem et aversionem boni creati significant.
Tempus non est receptaculum in quo Deus, informitas et creatura formata aequaliter locentur.
Nulla creatura se ipsam efficere, illuminare, satiare aut bono creato tamquam fine ultimo compleri potest.
Pluralitas hermeneutica neque univocitatem exclusivam neque licentiam sensuum falsorum vel indiscriminatorum admittit.
Iudicium spirituale non potest auctoritatem Scripturae, occulta hominum aut destinum exteriorum sibi subicere.
Nulla fruitio temporalium neque perpetuatio operum praesentium consummationem creaturae constituit.
Aequatio essendi cum forma actuali falsa esse debet, alioquin neque materia informis neque vita nondum sapiens cogitari posset.
Omnis mutabilitas possibilis in mutationem actualem converti non potest, quia inhaesio impedit lapsum sine naturae creatae abolitione.
Differentia a Deo non potest rivalitatem substantialem efficere; alioquin malum et materia in principia ontologica independentia converterentur.
Causalitas divina et actio humana relatione aemula contineri non possunt, quia gratia operationem participative constituit.
Significatio divina non potest ambitu intentionis consciae ministri humani terminari.
Mediatio per verba, signa, fidem et gradus capacitatis non est merus defectus tollendus, sed modus ordinarius formationis temporalis.
Successio narrationis non potest successionem cognitionis aut voluntatis divinae probare, quamvis relationem actus aeterni ad effectus temporales systema non absolvat.
Origo ante tempus nullo schemate successionis repraesentari potest, sicut requies ultima nullo die posteriori clauditur.
Nullus locus ontologicus extra causalitatem creatoris relinquitur ex quo res aut malum independentem originem accipiant.
Informitas pura cogitationi imaginativae indisponibilis manet et tantum per subtractionem formarum attingitur.
Prospectus qui omnem sensum Scripturae aut cognitionem Dei exhauriat creaturae praecluditur.
Orientatio affectiva neutralis indisponibilis est, quia omnis amor aut ad fontem convertit aut ad inferiora deicit.
Consummatio quae in novum cyclum laboris, vesperae et mutabilitatis redeat ontologice inadmissibilis est.
Capacitas materiae ad formas et capacitas verborum ad plures intellectus structuram homologam constituunt: unitas receptiva diversitatem ordinatam sustinet sine indeterminatione absoluta.
Tempus inter duos limites non temporales tenditur: originem quae successionem antecedit et requiem terminalem cui nulla vespera succedit.
Stabilitas creaturae rationalis non est immobilitas absoluta, sed directio continenter renovata qua mutabilitas ad inhaesionem et requiem ordinatur.
Caritas idem principium in duobus campis exercet: motum creaturae ad Deum dirigit et pluralitatem interpretum ad veritatem communem ordinat.
Incertitudo de intentione Moysi in cognitionem participativam transfertur: plenitudo Spiritus non statum mentalem auctoris replicat, sed veritatem in creatura operatur.
Sicut differentia creaturae a Deo substantiam adversam non gignit, ita multiplicitas intellectuum errorem necessario non gignit; utrumque ordine positivo continetur.
Historia temporalis est apparatus formationis cui propria obsolescentia inscribitur, quia mutationes opera producunt quae in requiem transire debent.
Scriptura ut firmamentum stabilitatem supra ministros servat, sed eadem stabilitas accommodationem et pluralitatem sensuum generat potius quam interpretationem unicam immobilit.
Bonitas totius non simplicitate vacua, sed compositione ordinata plurium rerum, facultatum et intellectuum efficitur.
Realitas creata est participatio dependens: accipit esse, formam et stabilitatem sine conversione in substantiam divinam.
Tempus est index interior formationis creaturae et medium historiae salutis, non mensura actus creatoris; eius finis est propria transcensio in requiem.
Actio finita non est regio causaliter relicta a Deo, sed effectus in quo causalitas divina voluntatem et operationem creatam participative producit.
Cognitio vera est communis et participata, sed semper signis, fide, auctoritate et gradu capacitatis mediatur.
Auctoritas ecclesialis distribuitur secundum capacitatem et corrigibilitatem; maturitas auget iudicium sine productione autonomiae a Scriptura.
Allegoria legitima non naturas delet, sed grammaticam creationis in formationem ecclesialem transfert servata distinctione graduum.
Subiectum non est centrum sibi sufficiens, sed capacitas mutabilis cuius status ab orientatione amoris et a gratia formante constituitur.
Visio bonitatis consummatur cum bonum singulare ad auctorem et ad ordinem totius refertur.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Bonitas desiderium inspirat, desiderium invocationem parit, invocatio conversionem aperit, conversio ampliorem receptionem eiusdem gratiae efficit.
Vita illuminabilis lucem recipit, lux visum bonitatis producit, visus bonum ad auctorem refert et relatio ulteriorem conformitatem generat.
Verbum unum plures sensus candidatos generat, veritas falsos excludit, caritas veros componit, compositio fecunditatem textus iterum auget.
Genesis Ecclesiam figurat, Ecclesia ordinem Geneseos in se recapitulat, et haec recapitulatio creationem ut historiam sanctificationis denuo legibilem facit.
Via amplificationis a conversione initiali per signa, disciplinam et exempla ad iudicium renovatae mentis ascendit, auctoritate Scripturae permanente.
Amor est attractor dynamicus: cupiditas inferiora repetit et inquietudinem auget, caritas ad Deum elevat et requiem appropinquat.
Requies sine vespera est attractor terminalis qui totam seriem operum ordinat neque in aliam vicissitudinem reingreditur.
Exclusio autonomiae recurrit ad singulos gradus, quia neque initium, formatio, illuminatio neque consummatio merito antecedente aut virtute propria producitur.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Deus sibi sufficiens + nulla materia coaeterna → donatio gratuita essendi → dependentia universalis creati.
Capacitas informis → vocatio Verbi → conversio ad unitatem → forma, lumen et conformitas sine aequalitate.
Forma recepta → mutationes ordinatae → tempus → historia graduum formationis secundum capacitatem.
Verbum aeternum per verba temporalia → sensus veri multiplices → examen veritatis → exclusio falsi → concordia caritatis.
Ordo creationis lectus → translatio ecclesialis → distributio signorum, ministeriorum et intellectuum → renovatio iudicii.
Spiritus ut donum → caritas ut pondus → operatio divina participata → motus creaturae ad locum quietis.
Opera temporalia ordinata → bonitas totius → transitus operum → sabbatum sine vespera.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Deus incommutabilis → creatio ex nihilo → informitas capax → formatio per Verbum → mutationes ordinatae → tempus creatum → quies non temporalis.
Sermo humilis → sensus veri multiplices → distinctio veritatis ab intentione humana → exclusio falsi → concordia caritatis → fecunditas sub auctoritate.
Creatio recapitulate lecta → conversio ecclesialis → distributio mediorum secundum capacitatem → renovatio mentis → transitus operum → sabbatum aeternum.
Tempus ex continente universali in effectum mutationis et modum receptionis creaturae reclassificatur.
Carentia temporis duplicem tabulam aperit: stabilitatem per plenitudinem inhaesionis et terminum eschatologicum sine vespera.
Multiplicitas interpretativa ex ambiguitate suspecta in fecunditatem veram, ordinatam et auctoritate limitatam convertitur.
Oppositio boni et mali a conflictu substantiarum ad directiones conversionis et aversionis intra bonum creatum transfertur.
Ecclesia fit non thema additum creationi, sed locus in quo grammatica creationis temporaliter recapitulari potest.
Oppositio inter gratiam et actionem propriam reordinatur ut causalitas participativa, quamvis ratio responsabilitatis incompleta maneat.
Auctoritas canonica ex clausura semantica in firmamentum generativum mutatur quod ministros transcendit et intellectus multiplices sustinet.
Bonitas universi non in perpetuitate operum, sed in ordine quo bona temporalia ad fruitionem Dei transeunt collocatur.
In gradu superficiei vocabula caeli, terrae, tenebrarum, lucis, dierum et sabbati ut obiecta narrationis Geneseos interpretantur.
In gradu structurali capacitas, forma, mutatio, tempus, conversio, media institutionis et iudicium in unam machinam formationis connectuntur.
In gradu metastrategico certamen de sensu mutatur in disciplinam pluralitatis verae, dum potestas ecclesialis intra auctoritatem et corrigibilitatem restringitur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali Deus aeternaliter causat, creatura temporaliter recipit et mutabilitas per conversionem ad requiem ordinatur.
In gradu methodologico et performativo textus eadem vocabula per campos metaphysicos, hermeneuticos et ecclesiales variat, atque sic fecunditatem quam affirmat actu efficit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Materia informis aliquid et tamen omni forma actuali carens dicitur; capacitas hanc medietatem sustinet, sed eius status ulterius non resolvitur.
Creatura intellectualis naturaliter mutabilis manet, quamvis inhaesio eius mutationem actualem impediat; nexus inter potentiam permanentem et immobilitatem participatam fragilis est.
Actus aeternus Dei successionem creatam producit sine successione divina, sed modus huius causalitatis non plene formalizatur.
Operatio divina voluntatem humanam constituit, dum responsabilitas actus proprii retinetur; articulatio utriusque causalitatis incompleta manet.
Pluralitas sensuum verorum auctoritate, Spiritu et caritate circumscribitur, sed criterium compatibilitatis plurium sensuum non in regulam plenam convertitur.
Allegoria naturas proprias servare profitetur, sed propositio creationem universaliter ad Ecclesiam ordinans latius patet quam demonstratio singularium correspondentiarum.
Intentio Moysi quaerenda manet, quamvis plenitudo Spiritus et possibilitas unius tantum sensus conscii eius necessitatem structuralem imminuant.
Ambitus iudicii spiritualis exemplis et exclusionibus restringitur, sed regula generalis quae omnia iudicabilia definit non explicatur.
Informitas mutatur ex limite privativo cosmologico in statum conversionis, aversionis et dependentiae spiritualis.
Caritas mutatur ex norma finis hermeneutici in principium gravitatis ontologicae et motus creaturae.
Tempus mutatur ex effectu mutationum formatarum in intervallum pedagogicum receptionis, fidei et operum transeuntium.
Spiritus mutatur ex amplitudine intentionis divinae in principium quo Deus in creatura cognoscit, amat et operatur.
Requies mutatur ex stabilitate creaturae inhaerentis in transformationem terminalem totius ordinis temporalium operum.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est machina donationis et conversionis: esse effluit non ex indigentia, forma revocat dispersum, amor dirigit et requies colligit.
Subiectum intra hanc machinam est capacitas mutabilis pondere amoris mota, non substantia sibi sufficiens aut centrum causalitatis clausum.
Tempus est vestigium motus formativi: cum formae variantur historia aperitur, cum opera in requiem transeunt eius functio terminatur.
Scriptura est firmamentum et prisma: auctoritatem stabilem ministrat, sed unitatem suam in pluralitatem intellectuum verorum refringit.
Certamen fundamentale non est inter duas substantias, sed inter conversionem boni creati ad fontem et aversionem eius ad inferiora.
Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad restituendam seriem a creatione ex nihilo per formationem, interpretationem et Ecclesiam ad requiem aeternam.
Structura firmissima est oppositio inter Deum sibi sufficientem et creaturam cui esse, forma, lumen, actio et quies donantur.
Restitutio verum motum servat, quia transitum ab ontologia formae et temporis ad fecunditatem hermeneuticam, sanctificationem ecclesialem et consummationem retinet.
Status materiae informis et relatio actus aeterni ad successionem creatam nondum satis determinantur.
Systema cohaeret per distinctiones originis a tempore, mutabilitatis a mutatione, unitatis a univocitate et causalitatis divinae ab autonomia creaturae.

Reductioni axiomaticae resistunt plena regula discernendi sensus multiplices et demonstratio exhaustiva translationis ab ordine creationis ad Ecclesiam; utraque auctoritate et analogia amplius quam formalizatione nititur.
The system asks how the dependence of creation prior to all succession passes into the history of temporal, ecclesial, and hermeneutical formation and culminates in eternal rest.
All being, formation, illumination, understanding, good action, and rest become the distribution of one divine gift, to which the grammar of creation recurs through diverse orders of creature.
The argument is a transversal reconstruction that joins the metaphysics of creation, the discipline of interpretation, the formation of the Church, and consummation without equating these levels.
The movement proceeds from an ontological, non-chronological origin through formation and time to an ecclesially recoded order of days.
The multiplicity of things and the multiplicity of meanings share the same structure: unity of source generates ordered diversity, with truth circumscribing its exclusions.

The movement is genuinely recursive and spiral, because the narrative of creation generates the rule of the Church's formation, while the Church retrospectively discloses the hidden end of the created order.
Charity constitutes the common axis by which interpretation is ordered to truth and the rational creature is borne toward the place of its rest.
The system's closure is not an exhaustion of meanings, but a sabbath without evening, where temporal works cease without return to a new cycle of mutability.
[Persistent] The eternal, immutable, and self-sufficient God is neither increased by creation nor perfected by temporal acts.
[Persistent] Every creature proceeds from nothing, with no divine substance, coeternal matter, or hostile nature admitted as a second principle.
[Persistent] Created being is distinct from form, wisdom, and blessedness; therefore every creature is mutable and capable of further formation.
[Mutating] Formlessness extends from an ontological capacity close to nothing to a spiritual state of aversion, darkness, and not-yet-completed formation.
[Emergent] Time does not contain creation, but emerges from ordered changes and from the temporal mode by which the creature receives form.
[Attractor] The rational creature participates in stability not through an immutability of its own, but through continuous adherence to and satiation in God.
[Persistent] The uncreated Word is the principle of creation and the formative call by which the dispersed creature is recalled to unity.
[Mutating] The Spirit is unfolded from the fullness of divine intention in Scripture into the gift of knowledge, charity, and the elevation of the creature.
[Attractor] Charity is at once the norm of interpretation, the weight of spiritual motion, and the principle of rest in the creature's proper good.
[Persistent] Unity of source can generate a true multiplicity of things, propositions, and understandings without division of truth.
[Emergent] Scripture is the temporal and humble medium of the eternal Word, joining stable authority with manifold accommodation.
[Mutating] The plurality of meanings passes from the concord of interpreters to an ecclesial economy that distributes means and understandings according to diverse capacities.
[Terminal] Faith, signs, and temporal works belong to a transitory state to which the eternal sabbath without evening imposes an end.
[Emergent] Divine causality participatively constitutes the creature's operation, so that God acts in the creature without simply suppressing the created act.
[Attractor] The goodness of individual things is joined to the ordered goodness of the whole and thence to the enjoyment of God, not to the self-sufficiency of the universe.
Creation from nothing retains a stable identity and governs both cosmology and the refutation of dualism.
Formlessness changes function: first it denotes the capacity for forms, then the mode of spiritual aversion and dependence.
Light migrates from the effect of ontological formation to ecclesial conversion, with residual darkness indicating a state not yet consummated.
Time is expanded from an effect of change into a mode of the creature's reception and instruction.
Intellectual adherence changes into gravitating charity: stability above vicissitude becomes motion rightly directed toward rest.
The plurality of meanings retains manifold truth, but extends from defensive concord into active fecundity under the authority of Scripture.
The conscious intention of the human minister is absorbed into the broader operation of the Spirit, who knows and speaks in the creature.
The order of days is transferred from a structure of non-chronological origin into a figure of the Church's formation.
The twofold absence of time undergoes terminal transformation: fullness through adherence is gathered into the sabbath without evening, while lack of form passes into the beginning of formation.
The metaphysical status of formless matter remains a local question, while at the present level not-yet-formed capacity becomes the general condition of all formation.
Correspondences of individual days with ministries remain local; only the distribution of means according to capacity rises to the structure of the flock.
The priority of origin without temporal interval is expanded from a question about matter into a general rule of divine causality.
The distinction between the truth of the thing and human intention, together with the manifold intelligibility of an utterance, constitutes a bridge between ontology and hermeneutics.
The ecclesial recapitulation of the grammar of creation is an emergence proper to this level, not a mere aggregation of local allegories.
The limits of particular spiritual judgment establish, at the higher axiom, an authority that is participatory, corrigible, and subject to Scripture.
Cosmological darkness as privation of form does not vanish when its structural work is completed, but is recoded into the darkness of aversion and not-yet-full conversion.
The system excludes a God who deliberates temporally, is moved by a new will, is needy, or rests after labor.
Creation is neither an emanation of divine substance nor an ordering of coeternal matter or hostile nature.
Evil and formlessness cannot be positive principles opposed to God, but signify privation and aversion from created good.
Time is not a receptacle in which God, formlessness, and the formed creature are equally situated.
No creature can make, illuminate, or satisfy itself, or be fulfilled in a created good as its ultimate end.
Hermeneutical plurality admits neither exclusive univocity nor license for false or indiscriminate meanings.
Spiritual judgment cannot subject to itself the authority of Scripture, the hidden things of human beings, or the destiny of outsiders.
No enjoyment of temporal things or perpetuation of present works constitutes the creature's consummation.
The equation of being with actual form must be false; otherwise neither formless matter nor life not yet wise could be conceived.
Every possible mutability cannot be converted into actual change, because adherence prevents falling without abolishing created nature.
Difference from God cannot produce substantial rivalry; otherwise evil and matter would be converted into independent ontological principles.
Divine causality and human action cannot be contained in a rival relation, because grace participatively constitutes operation.
Divine signification cannot be delimited by the scope of the conscious intention of the human minister.
Mediation through words, signs, faith, and degrees of capacity is not a mere defect to be removed, but the ordinary mode of temporal formation.
The succession of narrative cannot prove a succession of divine knowledge or will, although the system does not resolve the relation of the eternal act to temporal effects.
Origin before time can be represented by no schema of succession, just as final rest is not closed by any later day.
No ontological place outside the causality of the creator is left from which things or evil might receive an independent origin.
Pure formlessness remains unavailable to imaginative thought and is reached only through the subtraction of forms.
A perspective that would exhaust every meaning of Scripture or knowledge of God is precluded to the creature.
A neutral affective orientation is unavailable, because every love either turns toward the source or casts down toward lower things.
A consummation that returns to a new cycle of labor, evening, and mutability is ontologically inadmissible.
The capacity of matter for forms and the capacity of words for several understandings constitute a homologous structure: receptive unity sustains ordered diversity without absolute indetermination.
Time is stretched between two non-temporal limits: an origin that precedes succession and a terminal rest to which no evening succeeds.
The stability of the rational creature is not absolute immobility, but a continuously renewed direction by which mutability is ordered toward adherence and rest.
Charity exercises the same principle in two fields: it directs the creature's motion toward God and orders the plurality of interpreters toward common truth.
Uncertainty concerning the intention of Moses is transferred into participatory knowledge: the fullness of the Spirit does not replicate the author's mental state, but works truth in the creature.
Just as the creature's difference from God does not generate an opposing substance, so the multiplicity of understandings does not necessarily generate error; both are contained in a positive order.
Temporal history is an apparatus of formation inscribed with its own obsolescence, because changes produce works that must pass into rest.
Scripture as firmament preserves stability above ministers, yet this same stability generates accommodation and plurality of meanings rather than immobilizing a single interpretation.
The goodness of the whole is effected not by empty simplicity, but by the ordered composition of many things, faculties, and understandings.
Created reality is dependent participation: it receives being, form, and stability without conversion into divine substance.
Time is the inner index of the creature's formation and the medium of the history of salvation, not the measure of the creator's act; its end is its own transcendence into rest.
Finite action is not a region causally abandoned by God, but an effect in which divine causality participatively produces created will and operation.
True knowledge is common and participatory, but is always mediated by signs, faith, authority, and degree of capacity.
Ecclesial authority is distributed according to capacity and corrigibility; maturity increases judgment without producing autonomy from Scripture.
Legitimate allegory does not erase natures, but transfers the grammar of creation into ecclesial formation while preserving the distinction of levels.
The subject is not a self-sufficient center, but a mutable capacity whose state is constituted by the orientation of love and by forming grace.
The vision of goodness is consummated when a particular good is referred to its author and to the order of the whole.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Goodness inspires desire, desire produces invocation, invocation opens conversion, and conversion effects a broader reception of the same grace.
Illuminable life receives light, light produces the sight of goodness, sight refers the good to its author, and this relation generates further conformity.
One Word generates several candidate meanings, truth excludes the false, charity composes the true, and the composition again increases the fecundity of the text.
Genesis figures the Church, the Church recapitulates in itself the order of Genesis, and this recapitulation makes creation newly legible as a history of sanctification.
The path of amplification rises from initial conversion through signs, discipline, and examples to the judgment of the renewed mind, with the authority of Scripture remaining.
Love is a dynamic attractor: cupiditas repeats lower things and increases restlessness, while charity elevates toward God and approaches rest.
Rest without evening is a terminal attractor that orders the entire series of works and does not re-enter another vicissitude.
The exclusion of autonomy recurs at every level, because neither beginning, formation, illumination, nor consummation is produced by antecedent merit or one's own power.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Self-sufficient God + no coeternal matter → gratuitous gift of being → universal dependence of the created.
Formless capacity → call of the Word → conversion to unity → form, light, and conformity without equality.
Received form → ordered changes → time → history of stages of formation according to capacity.
Eternal Word through temporal words → manifold true meanings → examination of truth → exclusion of the false → concord of charity.
Order of creation read → ecclesial translation → distribution of signs, ministries, and understandings → renewal of judgment.
Spirit as gift → charity as weight → participatory divine operation → motion of the creature toward the place of rest.
Ordered temporal works → goodness of the whole → passage of works → sabbath without evening.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Immutable God → creation from nothing → capable formlessness → formation through the Word → ordered changes → created time → non-temporal rest.
Humble speech → manifold true meanings → distinction of truth from human intention → exclusion of the false → concord of charity → fecundity under authority.
Creation read recapitulatorily → ecclesial conversion → distribution of means according to capacity → renewal of mind → passage of works → eternal sabbath.
Time is reclassified from a universal container into an effect of change and a mode of the creature's reception.
The absence of time opens a twofold tableau: stability through the fullness of adherence and an eschatological end without evening.
Interpretative multiplicity is converted from suspect ambiguity into true, ordered fecundity limited by authority.
The opposition of good and evil is transferred from a conflict of substances to directions of conversion and aversion within created good.
The Church becomes not a theme added to creation, but the place in which the grammar of creation can be temporally recapitulated.
The opposition between grace and one's own action is reordered as participatory causality, although the account of responsibility remains incomplete.
Canonical authority changes from semantic closure into a generative firmament that transcends ministers and sustains manifold understandings.
The goodness of the universe is situated not in the perpetuity of works, but in the order by which temporal goods pass into the enjoyment of God.
At the surface level, the terms heaven, earth, darkness, light, days, and sabbath are interpreted as objects of the Genesis narrative.
At the structural level, capacity, form, change, time, conversion, means of instruction, and judgment are connected into one machinery of formation.
At the metastrategic level, conflict over meaning changes into a discipline of true plurality, while ecclesial power is restricted within authority and corrigibility.
At the ontological and temporal level, God causes eternally, the creature receives temporally, and mutability is ordered through conversion toward rest.
At the methodological and performative level, the text varies the same terms across metaphysical, hermeneutical, and ecclesial fields, and thus actually effects the fecundity that it affirms.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Formless matter is said to be something and yet to lack every actual form; capacity sustains this middle position, but its status is not further resolved.
The intellectual creature remains naturally mutable, although adherence prevents its actual change; the connection between enduring potentiality and participated immobility is fragile.
God's eternal act produces created succession without divine succession, but the mode of this causality is not fully formalized.
Divine operation constitutes human will while responsibility for one's own act is retained; the articulation of the two causalities remains incomplete.
The plurality of true meanings is circumscribed by authority, Spirit, and charity, but the criterion for compatibility among several meanings is not converted into a complete rule.
Allegory professes to preserve proper natures, but the proposition ordering creation universally to the Church extends more broadly than the demonstration of individual correspondences.
The intention of Moses remains to be sought, although the fullness of the Spirit and the possibility of only one conscious meaning diminish its structural necessity.
The scope of spiritual judgment is restricted by examples and exclusions, but the general rule defining all things subject to judgment is not explained.
Formlessness changes from a cosmological privative limit into a state of conversion, aversion, and spiritual dependence.
Charity changes from a norm of hermeneutical end into a principle of ontological gravity and creaturely motion.
Time changes from an effect of formed changes into a pedagogical interval of reception, faith, and transitory works.
The Spirit changes from the breadth of divine intention into the principle by which God knows, loves, and works in the creature.
Rest changes from the stability of the adhering creature into the terminal transformation of the whole order of temporal works.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a machinery of gift and conversion: being flows forth not from need, form recalls what is dispersed, love directs, and rest gathers.
The subject within this machinery is a mutable capacity moved by the weight of love, not a self-sufficient substance or a closed center of causality.
Time is the trace of formative motion: when forms vary, history opens; when works pass into rest, its function ends.
Scripture is firmament and prism: it provides stable authority, but refracts its unity into a plurality of true understandings.
The fundamental conflict is not between two substances, but between the conversion of created good toward the source and its aversion toward lower things.
The axioms presented suffice to restore the sequence from creation from nothing through formation, interpretation, and the Church to eternal rest.
The firmest structure is the opposition between the self-sufficient God and the creature to which being, form, light, action, and rest are given.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement, because it retains the transition from the ontology of form and time to hermeneutical fecundity, ecclesial sanctification, and consummation.
The status of formless matter and the relation of the eternal act to created succession are not yet sufficiently determined.
The system coheres through distinctions of origin from time, mutability from change, unity from univocity, and divine causality from creaturely autonomy.

The full rule for discerning manifold meanings and an exhaustive demonstration of the translation from the order of creation to the Church resist axiomatic reduction; both rely more on authority and analogy than on formalization.
Systema quaerit quomodo creatura a principio et fine suo alienata culpam affectivam, epistemicam atque voluntariam agnoscat et ad bonum immutabile convertatur.
Thesis globalis statuit omne esse creatum bonum esse, malum autem ex aversione voluntatis oriri atque per consuetudinem efficaciam temporalem sine substantia propria adipisci.
Argumentatio confessionem, analysim affectuum, refutationem ontologicam et historiam mediationum componit, ut exteriorizatio mali in genealogiam subiecti culpabilis sed sanabilis convertatur.
Motus chronologiam biographicam in recursionem aversionis transformat, cuius formae ab appetitu per errorem doctrinalem et servitutem voluntatis ad formationem ecclesialem mutantur.
Correctio primum falsas certitudines et ontologias dissolvit, deinde ostendit doctrinam emendatam conversionem non efficere dum habitus volendi integer non est.
Conversio emergit ut limen punctiforme quod deliberationem claudit, sed simul processum intellectualem, affectivum, sacramentalem et socialem aperit.
Confessio doctrinam performative exercet, quia memoriam reordinat, causalitatem inter culpam et gratiam distribuit atque lectorem in imitationem et intercessionem inducit.
Clausura est aperta et attractiva: conversio stabilitur, sed plena fruitio Sapientiae differtur, dum mors, misericordia et intercessio omnem consummationem praesentem vetant.
[Persistent] Deus est fons immutabilis omnis esse et boni; omnis natura creata bonitatem participat nec principium contrarium coordinatum admittit.
[Attractor] Creatura ad quietem in bono incommutabili ordinatur, unde inquietudo, inquisitio et desiderium formam negativam termini divini gerunt.
[Persistent] Bona creata et veritates locales bonitatem retinent, sed salutaria fiunt tantum cum usus, finis et receptio eorum recte ordinantur.
[Mutating] Malum est privatio boni quae, quamvis essentia propria careat, per aversionem, repetitionem et habitum efficaciam temporalem acquirit.
[Mutating] Una aversionis structura transit ab appetitu disperso ad imitationem libertatis, captationem intellectus, auctoritatem falsam et voluntatem consuetudine ligatam.
[Emergent] Subiectum est nodus diachronicus amoris, memoriae, societatis, habitus et actuum, non conscientia sui simpliciter praesens aut transparens.
[Mutating] Mediationes sociales, rhetoricae, scripturales, sacramentales et ecclesiales neque univoce corrumpunt neque autonome salvant, sed affectum, credibilitatem et receptionem distribuunt.
[Emergent] Cognitio est moraliter et soteriologice ordinata: veritas ad sapientiam non transit nisi facultas cognoscens humilitate, fide et sanatione transformetur.
[Mutating] Tempus est operator moralis qui mutationes distribuit, obiecta dissolvit, habitus sedimentat, dilationem amplificat et curationem explicat.
[Emergent] Gratia conversionem antecedit et voluntates partiales in consensum integrum perducit, voluntatem sanans sine eius actu consensuali abolendo.
[Emergent] Conversio est limen decisivum intra processum longum: unum nunc divisionem voluntatis claudit, sed formationem plurium ordinum subiecti non consummat.
[Emergent] Causalitas confessionalis asymmetrica est: voluntas defectum et culpam gerit, providentia autem bona servat, eventus ordinat et liberationem inchoat.
[Emergent] Confessio memoriam et narrationem in machinam conversionis mutat, quia identitatem restituit, causas redistribuit et lectorem intra eundem motum format.
[Terminal] Sapientia stabiliter possessa intra vitam temporalem indisponibilis manet; ideo misericordia, sacrificium et intercessio ultimam potius quam meritoria clausuram constituunt.
Inquietudo ab indice dependentiae ontologicae in famem epistemicam, desiderium quietis et attractorem Sapientiae nondum possessae mutatur.
Bonum creatum ab obiecto male usurpato in speciem boni imitabilem et deinde in medium sanationis transit; bonitas persistit, functio relatione mutatur.
Mediatio migrat a disciplina et consortio ad rhetoricam, magistrum, Scripturam et apparatus ecclesiales, servata potestate formandi receptionem.
Auctoritas ex potentia sociali captante fit obiectum examinis, deinde mediatio medicinalis quae iudicium format potius quam suspendit.
Dilatio invertitur secundum ordinem: baptismum differens licentiam aperit, doctrinam suspendens correctionem praeparat, conversionem procrastinans consuetudinem roborat.
Memoria ab reconstructione originum ad iudicium morale et tandem ad operationem performativam transit, qua casus, culpa et providentia reclassificantur.
Veritas ex obiecto quaesito fit iudicium impotentiae cognoscentis, norma formationis et attractor cui adhaesio stabilis adhuc deest.
Conversio ex clausura biographica in principium formationis mutatur; baptismus eam ecclesialiter stabilit, sed misericordiae et transformationis ulterioris necessitatem non terminat.
Infantia, furtum, luctus, magistri, astrologia, conversiones exemplares et mors manent casus locales; praesentem gradum constituunt tantum ut mutationes aversionis, mediationis et reditus.
Correctiones anti-Manichaeae et exegeticae transcendent polemicam localem, quia constituunt transitum ab exteriorizatione mali ad discrimen inter cognitionem termini et viam sanantem.
Schola, sodalitas, multitudo et exemplum singulare amplificantur in unam theoriam receptionis socialiter distributae, qua laus, pudor et imitatio statum subiecti mutant.
Astrologia ut doctrina localis evanescit, sed eius functio persistit in omni conatu causalitatem confundendi et culpam ad necessitatem externam transferendi.
Ascensus interiores non manent episodicae contemplationes, sed coniunctim distinguunt cognitionem veri, incapacitatem adhaesionis et brevem anticipationem possessionis eschatologicae.
Baptismus, vita Monicae et mors eius amplificant conversionem ultra actum singularem in regenerationem, disciplinam affectuum, memoriam liturgicam et intercessionem.
Nulla exterioritas ontologica datur in qua creatura, materia vel malum extra dependentiam a Deo subsistere possit.
Malum neque substantia creata neque materia increata neque principium Deo coordinatum est.
Nullum bonum finitum per se damnatur, sed nulla creatura mutabilis terminum stabilem desiderii praebere potest.
Desiderium, societas, rhetorica et dilatio neutralia esse non possunt, quia statum recipientis et directionem voluntatis iam efficiunt.
Eloquentia, scientia, doctrina recta et certitudo metaphysica neque veritatem salutarem neque adhaesionem moralem per se efficiunt.
Subiectum neque reparator autonomus neque fundamentum sui consensus liberantis est.
Virtus, baptismus et vita laudabilis neque innocentiam absolutam neque clausuram meritoriam constituunt.
Falsum esse oportet mentem principium propriae veritatis et normam ultimam sui iudicii esse posse.
Falsum esse oportet affectus et ambitus sociales materiam neutralem constituere, quia cognitionem et voluntatem recursive formant.
Falsum esse oportet originum, intentionum et providentiae transparentiam totalem ante confessionem vel fidem praesto esse.
Falsum esse oportet cognitionem termini facultatem perveniendi secum ferre, quia recta doctrina habitum cupiditatis intactum relinquere potest.
Falsum esse oportet dilationem medium vacuum esse; inter veterem et novam voluntatem nullum futurum moraliter neutrum datur.
Falsum esse oportet gratiam meram responsionem posteriorem aut voluntatis substitutionem coactivam esse; ipsa initium praebet voluntati tamen consentienti.
Falsum esse oportet effectum bonum bonitatem intentionis probare, aliter providentia et imputatio moralis confunderentur.
Systema circum absentiam impossibilem Dei ordinatur: nulla creatura eum localiter fugit nec extra ordinem participationis subsistit.
Inter falsitatem relictam et conversionem recusatam nulla positio stabilis aut voluntas neutralis conceditur.
Plena conversio et stabilis possessio Sapientiae intra praesentem temporalitatem indisponibiles manent, unde clausura vim ex futuro nondum possesso accipit.
Regeneratio subiecti a se ipso producta est possibilitas inadmissibilis; reditus tantum ut participatio medicinae et gratiae cogitatur.
Innocentia absoluta, meritum clausum et transparentia providentiae excluduntur; earum absentia confessionem, misericordiam et intercessionem terminales reddit.
Bonitas ontologica creaturae et carentia substantiae propriae mali efficiunt ut servitus temporalis realis sit, sed subiectum sine destructione naturae sanari possit.
Aversio non in actu singulari residet, sed per institutiones, imagines, auctoritates et habitus distribuitur, quos subiectum diachronicum simul recipit et corroborat.
Auctoritas medicinalis circuitum constituit: fides facultatem iudicandi sanat, sed agnitio medicinae ipsa fiducia in auctoritatem iam indiget.
Correctio obiecti cogniti impedimentum ad capacitatem cognoscentis transfert: veritas demonstrata impotentiam manifestat et conversionem facultatis postulat.
Dilatio est causalitas temporalis activa: secundum ordinem potest correctionem maturare, sed voluntati conversionem recusanti consuetudinem et servitutem amplificat.
Responsabilitas et gratia cohaerent asymmetrice: subiectum vincula per actus suos fabricat, sed principium quo consentire integre potest sibi non praebet.
Eventus conversionis processum non tollit sed comprimit: voluntatem uno actu integrat, cuius effectus sacramento, disciplina et communione temporaliter explicantur.
Confessio providentiam non tantum interpretatur, sed ordinem causalitatis narrando exercet atque lectorem in gratiarum actionem, imitationem et intercessionem inserit.
Subiectum autobiographicum fit agens culpabile, patiens medicinae et historia relationum, cuius identitas memoria et confessione potius quam introspectione immediata constituitur.
Malum de-substantializatum non fit inefficax, sed vim strategicam ex conversione bonorum in fines falsos et ex sedimentatione actuum haurit.
Tempus reclassificatur ut medium morale in quo obiecta transeunt, habitus augentur, conversio catastrophicum momentum accipit et formatio eius effectus explicat.
Epistemologia fit soteriologia: cognitio vera procedit per purgationem facultatis et transformationem affectus, non per solam accumulationem propositionum.
Institutio socialis est regimen affectuum et credibilitatis, cuius media secundum recipientem captivare, corrigere aut conversionem propagare possunt.
Ecclesia emergit ut apparatus temporalis qui veritatem in allocutionem, consensum in sacramentum, affectum in cantum et memoriam in intercessionem transfert.
Mors non relationem delet sed formam eius mutat, dum possessionem corporalem in luctum ordinatum, spem resurrectionis et memoriam liturgicam convertit.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Fames boni immutabilis non agnita substitutum finitum absolutizat; insufficientia substituti inanitatem auget et novam fugam ad exteriora parit.
Laus socialis auctoritatem generat, auctoritas imitationem movet, imitatio novam laudem stabilit; conversio visibilis eundem circuitum inversum ad liberationem adhibet.
Superbia imaginem corporalem eligit, imago doctrinam falsam sustinet, doctrina aversionem confirmat, et appetitus veritatem correctionis recusat.
Actus perversus consuetudinem gignit, consuetudo divisionem, divisio consilium medium, consilium dilationem, dilatio autem libertatem ulterius imminuit.
Veritas cognita impotentiam detegit, impotentia excusationes dissolvit, dissolutio implorationem aperit, gratia autem voluntatem ad veritatem iam visam reducit.
Eventus confessione retractatus providentiam manifestat, confessio imitationem generat, et narratio conversionis textum alteri lectori in allocutionem praesentem mutat.
Stabilis fruitio Sapientiae est attractor communis inquietudinis, cognitionis, conversionis, mediationum et luctus, quia praesentia quaesita vera sed nondum possessa manet.
