sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Donum essendi et bonitatis → dependentia creaturae → desiderium constitutivum boni immutabilis.
Oblivio principii → bonum finitum absolutum → dispersio affectus → egestas et inquietudo.
Dispersio → mediatio socialis et imaginativa → auctoritas falsa → captatio intellectus et confirmatio aversionis.
Discrepantia experientiae et refutatio ontologica → dissolutio falsi → rehabilitatio fidei → auctoritas medicinalis.
Veritas intellecta → detectio habitus intacti → voluntas divisa → dilatio servilis → necessitas gratiae.
Gratia antecedens → consensus integratus → conversio punctiformis → baptismus et formatio ecclesialis → disciplina affectuum.
Confessio causalitatis → gratiae actio → memoria liturgica → intercessio → possessio Sapientiae eschatologice dilata.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Dependens bonitas creata → aversio affectiva → amplificatio socialis → error doctrinalis → refutatio ontologica → responsabilitas voluntatis.
Ruina certitudinis falsae → fides provisionalis → veritas incorporea → detectio impotentiae → gratia integrans → conversio.
Conversio punctiformis → renuntiatio et baptismus → communio ecclesialis → contemplatio instabilis → mors et luctus → misericordia atque intercessio.
Malum reclassificatur ex natura adversa in structuram coniunctam privationis ontologicae, aversionis voluntariae et inertiae temporaliter acquisitae.
Subiectum reclassificatur ex anima sibi transparente in historiam culpabilem et sanabilem, per corpora, signa, societates, habitus et sacramenta formatam.
Libertas transfertur ab autonomia et facultate eligendi ad participationem recti ordinis et consensum a gratia sanatum.
Auctoritas desinit esse oppositum libertatis et fit mediatio examinabilis, cuius validitas ex ordine, fructu et facultate formandi iudicium pendet.
Tempus ex recipiente neutro in machinam moralem mutatur, quae habitum sedimentat, momentum conversionis comprimit et possessionem aeternam differt.
Conversio ex substitutione opinionis in integrationem voluntatis et processum intellectualem, sacramentalem, affectivum atque socialem expanditur.
Narratio reclassificatur ex relatione praeteriti in interventionem quae memoriam, causalitatem, imitationem et precationem praesentem ordinat.
Gradus superficiei continet infantiam, institutiones, furtum, luctus, sectam, migrationes, ascensus interiores, conversionem, baptismum, mortem Monicae et intercessionem.
Gradus structuralis componit participationem essendi, aversionem, mediationem, habitum, temporalitatem, gratiam et providentiam in unam machinam formationis.
Gradus metastrategicus certamen transfert ab electione inter obiecta vel doctrinas ad formationem facultatis quae amare, credere, iudicare et consentire potest.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis realitatem ut participationem boni immutabilis constituit, in qua subiectum per successionem ligatur, sanatur et ad aeternitatem dirigitur.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus confessione efficit quod asserit, quia narratione culpam voluntati, bonum Deo et lectorem imitationi atque intercessioni distribuit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Voluntas culpabilis et gratia antecedens simul requiruntur, sed modus quo actio divina consensum efficit sine coactione formaliter indeterminatus manet.
Providentia eventus pravos ad bonum ordinat et culpam agenti relinquit, sed distinctio causalitatum affirmatur firmius quam explicatur.
Fides auctoritatem medicinalem recipit ut rationem sanet, ratio autem auctoritatem sanantem iudicare debet; circulus medicinalis criterio omnino externo caret.
Bona creata legitima manent, sed eadem sub cupiditate vincula fiunt; limes inter usum ordinatum et tegumentum appetitus non semper explicitus est.
Conversio ut actus integer et processus multistratus cohaeret tantum distinctione inter integrationem voluntatis et transformationem ulteriorem intellectus atque affectus.
Malum sensum mutat ab adversario substantiali ad privationem, inde ad aversionem voluntatis et postremo ad consuetudinem temporaliter efficacem.
Mediatio mutatur ab instrumento captationis in condicionem medicinae, deinde in rete ecclesiale quod conversionem temporaliter stabilit.
Veritas mutatur ex obiecto doctrinae in normam quae cognoscentem iudicat, impotentiam detegit et novum ordinem vitae requirit.
Dilatio mutat valorem a patientia providentiali ad mechanismum servitutis, ubi mora non amplius praeparat sed veterem consuetudinem confirmat.
Clausura conversionis mutatur in principium formationis, et clausura vitae laudabilis in memoriam liturgicam, misericordiam atque spem resurrectionis.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas est campus participationis circa fontem immutabilem, in quo defectus ordinem vulnerat sed naturam contrariam producere nequit.
Subiectum est nodus diachronicus permeabilis, qui se repetitione ligat, ab alio principio solvitur et memoria confessionali recollegitur.
Tempus est fluvius, sedimentum et limen: aufert obiecta, format consuetudinem, comprimit decisionem et futuram possessionem Sapientiae differt.
Mediatio est rete navigabile quod veritatem per voces, textus, corpora, exempla, sacramenta et memoriam distribuit, dum iter ab exterioribus ad interiora regit.
Mors est limen quod communionem corporalem frangit sine relationis abolitione, eamque in luctum, precem et expectationem stabilis praesentiae transfert.
Axiomata extracta sufficiunt ad restituendum motum ab ontologica dependentia per aversionem affectivam, captationem doctrinalem et servitutem voluntatis ad conversionem ecclesialiter formatam.
Structura firmissima coniungit bonitatem creaturae, malum privativum, responsabilitatem voluntatis et redistributionem causalitatis inter culpam atque gratiam.
Cohaerentia huius gradus reditu spirali constat: eadem aversio per affectum, intellectum et habitum mutatur, dum mediatio ab instrumento captationis in apparatus liberationis invertitur.
Minus determinata manent efficientia gratiae sine coactione, criterium ultimum verae auctoritatis et concursus providentiae cum culpa particulari.
Reductioni axiomaticae resistunt actus confessionis, densitas affectuum, allocutio temporalis et singularitas luctus, quia ipsa sunt media quibus doctrina conversionis efficitur.
The system asks how a creature alienated from its beginning and end may acknowledge affective, epistemic, and volitional guilt and turn toward the immutable good.
The global thesis holds that all created being is good, whereas evil arises from the will's aversion and, through habit, acquires temporal efficacy without a substance of its own.

The argument composes confession, analysis of the affections, ontological refutation, and a history of mediations, so that the externalization of evil may be converted into a genealogy of the culpable yet healable subject.
The movement transforms biographical chronology into a recursion of aversion, whose forms change from appetite through doctrinal error and servitude of the will to ecclesial formation.
Correction first dissolves false certainties and ontologies, then shows that corrected doctrine does not effect conversion so long as the habit of willing is not whole.
Conversion emerges as a point-like threshold that closes deliberation, yet at the same time opens an intellectual, affective, sacramental, and social process.
Confession performatively enacts doctrine, because it reorders memory, distributes causality between guilt and grace, and leads the reader into imitation and intercession.
The closure is open and attractive: conversion is stabilized, but full enjoyment of Wisdom is deferred, while death, mercy, and intercession prevent every present consummation.
[Persistent] God is the immutable source of all being and good; every created nature participates in goodness and admits no coordinated contrary principle.
[Attractor] The creature is ordered toward rest in the immutable good, whence restlessness, inquiry, and desire bear the negative form of the divine end.
[Persistent] Created goods and local truths retain goodness, but become salvific only when their use, end, and reception are rightly ordered.
[Mutating] Evil is a privation of good which, although lacking an essence of its own, acquires temporal efficacy through aversion, repetition, and habit.
[Mutating] A single structure of aversion passes from dispersed appetite to the imitation of freedom, the capture of intellect, false authority, and a will bound by habit.
[Emergent] The subject is a diachronic nexus of love, memory, society, habit, and acts, not a consciousness of itself simply present or transparent.
[Mutating] Social, rhetorical, scriptural, sacramental, and ecclesial mediations neither corrupt univocally nor save autonomously, but distribute affect, credibility, and reception.
[Emergent] Knowledge is morally and soteriologically ordered: truth does not pass into wisdom unless the knowing faculty is transformed by humility, faith, and healing.
[Mutating] Time is a moral operator that distributes changes, dissolves objects, sediments habits, amplifies delay, and unfolds healing.
[Emergent] Grace precedes conversion and brings partial wills into integral consent, healing the will without abolishing its consensual act.
[Emergent] Conversion is a decisive threshold within a long process: one now closes the division of the will, but does not consummate the formation of the subject's multiple orders.
[Emergent] Confessional causality is asymmetrical: the will bears defect and guilt, whereas providence preserves goods, orders events, and initiates liberation.
[Emergent] Confession turns memory and narrative into an engine of conversion, because it restores identity, redistributes causes, and forms the reader within the same movement.
[Terminal] Wisdom stably possessed remains unavailable within temporal life; therefore mercy, sacrifice, and intercession constitute an ultimate rather than a meritorious closure.
Restlessness changes from an index of ontological dependence into epistemic hunger, desire for rest, and an attractor of Wisdom not yet possessed.
Created good passes from an object wrongly usurped into an imitable appearance of good and then into a medium of healing; goodness persists, function changes through relation.
Mediation migrates from discipline and fellowship to rhetoric, teacher, Scripture, and ecclesial apparatuses, retaining the power to form reception.
Authority changes from socially captivating power into an object of examination, then into medicinal mediation that forms judgment rather than suspending it.
Delay is inverted according to order: delaying baptism opens license, suspending doctrine prepares correction, postponing conversion strengthens habit.
Memory passes from reconstruction of origins to moral judgment and finally to a performative operation by which fall, guilt, and providence are reclassified.
Truth changes from a sought object into a judgment of the knowing subject's impotence, a norm of formation, and an attractor to which stable adherence is still lacking.
Conversion changes from biographical closure into a principle of formation; baptism stabilizes it ecclesially, but does not end the need for further mercy and transformation.
Childhood, theft, mourning, teachers, astrology, exemplary conversions, and death remain local cases; they constitute the present level only as mutations of aversion, mediation, and return.

Anti-Manichaean and exegetical corrections transcend local polemic, because they constitute the transition from the externalization of evil to the distinction between knowledge of the end and the healing way.
School, fellowship, crowd, and singular example are amplified into a single theory of socially distributed reception, by which praise, shame, and imitation alter the subject's state.
Astrology as a local doctrine vanishes, but its function persists in every attempt to confuse causality and transfer guilt to external necessity.
Interior ascents do not remain episodic contemplations, but jointly distinguish knowledge of truth, incapacity for adherence, and a brief anticipation of eschatological possession.
Baptism, Monica's life, and her death amplify conversion beyond a singular act into regeneration, discipline of the affections, liturgical memory, and intercession.
No ontological exteriority is given in which creature, matter, or evil can subsist outside dependence on God.
Evil is neither created substance nor uncreated matter nor a principle coordinated with God.
No finite good is condemned in itself, but no mutable creature can provide a stable end of desire.
Desire, society, rhetoric, and delay cannot be neutral, because they already effect the recipient's state and the direction of the will.
Eloquence, knowledge, right doctrine, and metaphysical certainty do not by themselves effect either salvific truth or moral adherence.
The subject is neither an autonomous repairer nor the foundation of its own liberating consent.
Virtue, baptism, and praiseworthy life constitute neither absolute innocence nor meritorious closure.
It must be false that the mind can be the principle of its own truth and the ultimate norm of its own judgment.
It must be false that affections and social environments constitute neutral matter, because they recursively form knowledge and will.
It must be false that total transparency of origins, intentions, and providence is available before confession or faith.
It must be false that knowledge of the end carries with it the capacity to attain it, because right doctrine can leave the habit of desire untouched.
It must be false that delay is an empty medium; between the old and the new will no morally neutral future is given.
It must be false that grace is a mere subsequent response or a coercive substitution for the will; it itself provides the beginning to a will that nevertheless consents.
It must be false that a good effect proves the goodness of intention, otherwise providence and moral imputation would be confused.
The system is ordered around God's impossible absence: no creature locally escapes him or subsists outside the order of participation.
Between retained falsehood and refused conversion, no stable position or neutral will is granted.
Full conversion and stable possession of Wisdom remain unavailable within present temporality, whence closure receives force from a future not yet possessed.
Regeneration of the subject produced by itself is an inadmissible possibility; return is conceived only as participation in healing and grace.
Absolute innocence, closed merit, and transparency of providence are excluded; their absence makes confession, mercy, and intercession terminal.
The creature's ontological goodness and evil's lack of a substance of its own make temporal servitude real, yet allow the subject to be healed without destruction of nature.
Aversion does not reside in a singular act, but is distributed through institutions, images, authorities, and habits, which the diachronic subject both receives and reinforces.
Medicinal authority constitutes a circuit: faith heals the faculty of judging, but recognition of healing itself already requires trust in authority.
Correction of the known object transfers the impediment to the knowing capacity: demonstrated truth manifests impotence and demands conversion of the faculty.
Delay is active temporal causality: according to order it can mature correction, but for a will refusing conversion it amplifies habit and servitude.
Responsibility and grace cohere asymmetrically: the subject fashions bonds through its acts, but does not provide itself the principle by which it can consent integrally.
The event of conversion does not abolish process but compresses it: it integrates the will in one act, whose effects are unfolded temporally by sacrament, discipline, and communion.
Confession does not merely interpret providence, but enacts the order of causality by narrating and inserts the reader into thanksgiving, imitation, and intercession.
The autobiographical subject becomes a culpable agent, a patient of healing, and a history of relations, whose identity is constituted by memory and confession rather than immediate introspection.
De-substantialized evil does not become inefficacious, but draws strategic force from the conversion of goods into false ends and from the sedimentation of acts.
Time is reclassified as a moral medium in which objects pass away, habits increase, conversion takes on a catastrophic moment, and formation unfolds its effects.
Epistemology becomes soteriology: true knowledge proceeds through purification of the faculty and transformation of affect, not through the mere accumulation of propositions.
Social institution is a governance of affects and credibility, whose media can, according to the recipient, captivate, correct, or propagate conversion.
The Church emerges as a temporal apparatus that transfers truth into address, consent into sacrament, affect into song, and memory into intercession.
Death does not destroy relation but changes its form, while converting bodily possession into ordered mourning, hope of resurrection, and liturgical memory.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Unacknowledged hunger for the immutable good absolutizes a finite substitute; the substitute's insufficiency increases emptiness and generates a new flight toward externals.
Social praise generates authority, authority moves imitation, imitation stabilizes new praise; visible conversion applies the same inverted circuit to liberation.
Pride chooses a bodily image, the image sustains false doctrine, doctrine confirms aversion, and appetite refuses the truth of correction.
A perverse act begets habit, habit division, division an intermediate resolve, resolve delay, while delay further diminishes freedom.
Known truth discloses impotence, impotence dissolves excuses, dissolution opens supplication, while grace returns the will to truth already seen.
An event reconsidered in confession manifests providence, confession generates imitation, and the narrative of conversion turns the text into a present address for another reader.
Stable enjoyment of Wisdom is the common attractor of restlessness, knowledge, conversion, mediations, and mourning, because the sought presence remains true but not yet possessed.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Gift of being and goodness → dependence of the creature → constitutive desire for the immutable good.
Forgetfulness of the principle → finite good made absolute → dispersion of affect → poverty and restlessness.
Dispersion → social and imaginative mediation → false authority → capture of intellect and confirmation of aversion.
Discrepancy of experience and ontological refutation → dissolution of falsehood → rehabilitation of faith → medicinal authority.
Truth understood → detection of intact habit → divided will → servile delay → necessity of grace.
Prevenient grace → integrated consent → point-like conversion → baptism and ecclesial formation → discipline of the affections.
Confession of causality → thanksgiving → liturgical memory → intercession → eschatologically delayed possession of Wisdom.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Dependent created goodness → affective aversion → social amplification → doctrinal error → ontological refutation → responsibility of the will.
Ruin of false certainty → provisional faith → incorporeal truth → detection of impotence → integrating grace → conversion.
Point-like conversion → renunciation and baptism → ecclesial communion → unstable contemplation → death and mourning → mercy and intercession.
Evil is reclassified from adverse nature into a structure conjoined of ontological privation, voluntary aversion, and temporally acquired inertia.
The subject is reclassified from a soul transparent to itself into a culpable and healable history, formed through bodies, signs, societies, habits, and sacraments.
Freedom is transferred from autonomy and the capacity to choose to participation in right order and consent healed by grace.
Authority ceases to be the opposite of freedom and becomes an examinable mediation, whose validity depends on order, fruit, and the capacity to form judgment.
Time changes from a neutral receptacle into a moral machine that sediments habit, compresses the moment of conversion, and defers eternal possession.
Conversion expands from substitution of opinion into integration of the will and an intellectual, sacramental, affective, and social process.
Narrative is reclassified from an account of the past into an intervention that orders present memory, causality, imitation, and prayer.
The surface level contains childhood, institutions, theft, mourning, sect, migrations, interior ascents, conversion, baptism, Monica's death, and intercession.
The structural level composes participation in being, aversion, mediation, habit, temporality, grace, and providence into a single machine of formation.
The metastrategic level transfers the contest from choice among objects or doctrines to formation of the faculty able to love, believe, judge, and consent.
The ontological and temporal level establishes reality as participation in the immutable good, in which the subject is bound, healed, and directed toward eternity through succession.
The methodological and performative level accomplishes by confession what it asserts, because by narrative it distributes guilt to the will, good to God, and the reader to imitation and intercession.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: A culpable will and prevenient grace are simultaneously required, but the manner in which divine action effects consent without coercion remains formally indeterminate.
Providence orders wicked events toward good and leaves guilt to the agent, but the distinction of causalities is asserted more firmly than it is explained.
Faith receives medicinal authority in order that reason may be healed, but reason must judge healing authority; the medicinal circle lacks an entirely external criterion.
Created goods remain legitimate, but the same goods become bonds under cupidity; the boundary between ordered use and a covering for appetite is not always explicit.
Conversion as an integral act and a multilayered process cohere only through the distinction between integration of the will and further transformation of intellect and affect.
Evil changes sense from substantial adversary to privation, then to aversion of the will and finally to temporally efficacious habit.
Mediation changes from an instrument of capture into a condition of healing, then into an ecclesial network that stabilizes conversion temporally.
Truth changes from an object of doctrine into a norm that judges the knower, discloses impotence, and requires a new order of life.
Delay changes value from providential patience to a mechanism of servitude, where postponement no longer prepares but confirms old habit.
The closure of conversion changes into a principle of formation, and the closure of a praiseworthy life into liturgical memory, mercy, and hope of resurrection.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is a field of participation around an immutable source, in which defect wounds order but cannot produce a contrary nature.
The subject is a permeable diachronic nexus, which binds itself by repetition, is released by another principle, and is recollected by confessional memory.
Time is river, sediment, and threshold: it removes objects, forms habit, compresses decision, and defers future possession of Wisdom.
Mediation is a navigable network that distributes truth through voices, texts, bodies, examples, sacraments, and memory, while governing the path from externals to interiors.
Death is a threshold that breaks bodily communion without abolishing relation, and transfers it into mourning, prayer, and expectation of stable presence.
The extracted axioms suffice to reconstruct the movement from ontological dependence through affective aversion, doctrinal capture, and servitude of the will to ecclesially formed conversion.
The firmest structure joins the creature's goodness, privative evil, responsibility of the will, and redistribution of causality between guilt and grace.

The coherence of this level consists in spiral return: the same aversion changes through affect, intellect, and habit, while mediation is inverted from an instrument of capture into apparatuses of liberation.
The efficacy of grace without coercion, the ultimate criterion of true authority, and the concurrence of providence with particular guilt remain less determined.

Acts of confession, the density of affects, temporal address, and the singularity of mourning resist axiomatic reduction, because they are themselves the means by which the doctrine of conversion is effected.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo creatura sibi opaca, mutabilis et temporalis originem praetemporalem, veritatem sui atque directionem ad requiem recipiat.
Thesis globalis omnem cognitionem, formationem, actionem et quietem sub asymmetria donationis divinae constituit: creatura accipit quod ex se producere non potest.
Argumentatio confessionem apophaticam cum reconstructione metaphysica, hermeneutica et ecclesiali coniungit, ut dependentia ontologica in disciplina temporalis receptionis explicetur.
Motus ab origine non chronologica per signa, interioritatem et successionem procedit, deinde interioritatem ad Verbum, communitatem formatam et finem aeternum transcendit.
Progressio est spiralis: quaelibet illuminatio novam opacitatem aperit, et quaelibet formatio originem atque finem ex novo prospectu retrospecte reconstituit.
Dispersio et informitas sunt modi non identici carentiae unitatis propriae; caritas, intentio et Verbum eos in formationem sine abolitione pluralitatis convertunt.
Tempus fit simul medium vulneris et formationis: in eo attentio dispergitur, dona recipiuntur, opera exercentur et creatura ad propriam temporis transcensionem ordinatur.
Clausura praesens semper differtur, sed dilatio non est infinita: pax nondum possessa in sabbatum sine vespera terminaliter colligitur.
[Persistent] Deus immutabilis neque tempore continetur neque creatione perficitur, sed mensura veritatis et fons omnis formationis manet.
[Persistent] Creatura ex nihilo facta neque causam essendi neque principium cognitionis, ordinis aut perseverantiae in se possidet.
[Mutating] Mutabilitas transit a capacitate ontologica formae recipiendae ad successionem, distentionem subiecti et historiam formationis communis.
[Emergent] Creatura est capacitas receptiva cui unitas effecta datur; interioritas, materia informis et vita ecclesialis diversos huius receptivitatis gradus exhibent.
[Persistent] Veritas interior et Verbum increatum subiectum transcendunt, errores eius iudicant et capacitatem dispersam ad formam vocant.
[Mutating] Interioritas ex loco sui-examinationis in commissuram ontologiae et hermeneuticae mutatur, ubi opacitas creaturae cum iudicio veritatis concurrit.
[Emergent] Tempus est modus creatus receptionis et transitus: mutationibus oritur, operationibus animi mensuratur et historiam formationis sustinet.
[Attractor] Unitas in Deo per caritatem est attractor qui attentionem, amores, sensus et opera colligit sine diversitate creata delenda.
[Mutating] Memoria et Scriptura sunt mediationes temporales quibus absentia operativa fit: praeteritum per vestigium, Verbum aeternum per sermonem humilem adest.
[Persistent] Bona creata et multiplicitas sunt positiva, sed medium in finem mutatum dispersionem efficit, dum relatio ad fontem bonitatem totius constituit.
[Emergent] Confessio et interpretatio non referunt tantum veritatem iam possessam, sed affectum, intellectum et communitatem sub veritate performative reformant.
[Persistent] Gratia et causalitas divina actionem finitam non supprimunt, sed facultatem cognoscendi, volendi et operandi participative constituunt.
[Emergent] Principium creatorium Verbi et mediatio Christi unum axem constituunt quo creatura in esse vocatur, reformatur et per mortalitatem ad iustitiam dirigitur.
[Terminal] Pax nondum praesens et sabbatum sine vespera unam clausuram eschatologicam constituunt, in qua opera transeunt neque successio renovatur.
[Attractor] Unitas vera non est univocitas aut simplicitas vacua, sed ordo plurium sub uno fonte, una veritate et uno fine.
Creatio ex nihilo identitatem stabilem retinet, sed ex propositione cosmologica in legem epistemicae, moralis et ecclesialis dependentiae amplificatur.
Veritas immutabilis manet mensura, sed munus eius a iudicio interiori ad vocationem formativam Verbi creatoris extenditur.
Memoria ab archivo interiori in mediationem temporalem migrat, cui Scriptura respondet ut medium communitatis ad Verbum aeternum.
Dispersio et informitas eandem functionem non explent, sed recurrenter designant capacitatem quae unitatem ex se non habet et formatione indiget.
Attentio ex facultate mensurandi in directionem amoris mutatur, deinde in caritate normam hermeneuticam et pondus ontologicum acquirit.
Iudicium veritatis ex confessione motuum interiorum ad exegesim pluralium sensuum migrat, servata correctione affectus et intellectus.
Praesens ex instanti morali examinando in medium pedagogicum historiae mutatur, quo forma recipitur, exercetur et memoriae traditur.
Mediatio a reconciliatione peccatoris ad structuram universam originis, formationis et directionis temporalis amplificatur.
Multiplicitas vim invertit: sine fine uno dispersiva est, sub unitate fontis vero fecunditatem rerum et intellectuum efficit.
Dilatio pacis transformationem terminalem patitur, cum requies ex stabilitate participata in finem irreversibilem totius successionis transit.
Taxonomiae memoriae et quaestio materiae informis locales manent; sursum ascendit sola structura capacitatis quae vestigium aut formam recipit.
Triplex cupiditas et correspondentiae singulorum dierum sunt machinae inferiores; gradus praesens retinet legem distributionis attentionis et mediorum secundum capacitatem.
Creatio ex nihilo et prioritas originis sine intervallo amplificantur in principium universale causalitatis non autonomae.
Aporiae de praesentis longitudine et mutationis ordine localiter permanent, sed coniunctae demonstrant tempus non esse receptaculum neque plenam sui possessionem.
Iudicium interius et pluralitas hermeneutica gradus inferiores coniungunt, quia sensus recipiuntur multipliciter sed veritati supra interpretem subiciuntur.
Communitas confessionis et recapitulatio ecclesialis constituunt transitionem praesentis gradus, qua formatio interior in corpus interpretans et exercitum exteriorizatur.
Polemica anti-Donatistica et refutatio circuituum caelestium opere locali peracto recedunt, sed earum exclusio iudicii autonomi et mensurae creatae persistit.
Christus mediator et Verbum creatorium non manent conclusiones regionales, sed pontem maiorem inter donationem essendi et reformationem vitae efficiunt.
Dubia de affectione temporali et statu materiae informis limites inferiores servant; synthesis ea coordinat, sed in unam ontologiam exhaustivam non solvit.
Nulla creatura sui causa, mensura, illuminatrix aut consummatrix esse potest.
Nec materia nec tempus nec mens neque alia substantia potest Deo coaeterna aut ab eius causalitate independens constitui.
Deus neque memoria continetur neque temporaliter deliberat, mutatur aut per opera creata completur.
Interioritas nec transparantiam sui nec prospectum exhaustivum veritatis praebet.
Multiplicitas neque per se ordinem efficit neque simpliciter falsitati aequatur; univocitas et licentia indiscriminata pariter excluduntur.
Mediatio non est impedimentum quod ascensus autonomus superet, sed modus necessarius formationis intra mortalitatem, signa et gradus capacitatis.
Corpus, materia, tempus et bona sensibilia non sunt substantiae malae, sed neque fines ultimi aut principia sui iuris.
Nulla clausura intra statum mortalem neque perpetuatio operum temporalium consummationem creaturae constituit.
Causalitas divina et actio creata relatione competitiva explicari non possunt, quia dependentia doni ipsam operationem finitam constituit.
Immutabilitas divina inertiam significare non potest, quamvis actus aeternus effectus successivos sine mutatione sui producat.
Successio non potest causam divinam continere aut eius voluntatem narrare, sed tantum modum quo effectus creati recipiuntur.
Unitas non potest plenam identitatem partium exigere, quia systema cohaeret tantum si pluralitas vera sub fonte indiviso subsistit.
Veritas nec ab affectu interiori nec ab intentione conscia ministri humani producitur aut terminatur.
Introspectio, analysis temporis et mediatio signorum non possunt in ascensum immediatum ad immutabilitatem converti.
Homologia inter distentionem, informitatem et formationem non demonstrat per se necessitatem mediatoris aut translationem totius creationis in Ecclesiam.
Possibilitas radicaliter indisponibilis est creatura quae se totam simul possideat atque stabilitatem ex propria natura habeat.
Origo ante tempus nec ordine chronologico repraesentari nec per aliquod alterum Deo coaeternum explicari potest.
Finis sine vespera non potest tamquam ultimum momentum intra seriem concipi, quia pacem nondum possessam successione ipsa terminat.
Nullum extra causalitatem divinam datur ex quo subiectum esse, veritatem aut oppositionem substantialem accipiat.
Prospectus creatus qui animam, tempus, Scripturam et intentionem divinam simul exhauriat constitutive praecluditur.
Neutralitas attentionis et amoris indisponibilis est: omnis receptio aut ad fontem ordinatur aut medium in finem convertit.
Dependentia ex nihilo ontologiam excedit atque in cognitione, voluntate et interpretatione recurrit, quia nulla operatio creaturae principium suum sufficiens continet.
Informitas et distentio duas magnitudines carentiae unitatis propriae exhibent: prima capacitatem formationis, altera divisionem vitae iam formatae sed nondum collectae.
Tempus est simul effectus mutationis creatae et forma interior receptionis eius; ideo neque obiectivum receptaculum neque fictio privata est.
Memoria et Scriptura absentiam in praesentem efficaciam convertunt: una vestigia vitae, altera Verbum per verba temporalia operari facit.
Caritas est forma superior attentionis, quia simul obiecta desiderii, sensus textus et opera communitatis ad finem communem dirigit.
Confessio et exegesis sunt machinae correctionis recursivae: utrumque actum sub veritate ponit, falsam clausuram excludit et ampliorem receptionem aperit.
Gratia actionem creatam constituit, sed responsabilitas eiusdem actionis retinetur; dependentia et imputabilitas igitur cohaerent sine modo cooperationis plene formalizato.
Verbum creatorium et Christus mediator unam directionem efficiunt: donatio essendi in vocationem formativam, reconciliationem mortalem et reditum ad iustitiam continuatur.
Multiplicitas est bifurcationis locus: a fonte et fine separata dispergit, sub unitate veritatis ordinata fecunditatem rerum et intellectuum constituit.
Opera praesentia propriam obsolescentiam continent, quia sanationem incohant sed ad pacem et sabbatum quae successionem claudunt ordinantur.
Asymmetria creationis et gratiae unam legem participationis generat: sicut esse donatur, ita sui cognitio, formatio et perseverantia recipiuntur.
Subiectum est capacitas temporaliter distributa, cuius identitas ex appetitu, memoria, attentione, signis et orientatione amoris componitur.
Historia non est successio neutralis, sed apparatus quo voluntas reformatur, opera transeunt et creatura ad statum non temporalem praeparatur.
Ecclesia exteriorizat collectionem interiorem, quia communitas confessionis, interpretatio et distributio mediorum eandem formationem quam animus recipit corporaliter exercent.
Pluralitas ontologica et pluralitas hermeneutica homologae fiunt: utraque capacitatem determinatam ad plures formas veras recipiendas praesupponit.
Malum ex agro substantiarum removetur et in directionem boni creati transfertur, qua attentio medium usurpat aut caritas illud ad fontem refert.
Salus est reconfiguratio totius temporalitatis creatae, non fuga ab ea: mediatio successionem assumit, ordinat et ad requiem irreversibilem perducit.
Cognitio participata certitudinem principii cum provisionalitate applicationis coniungit; veritas stabilis manet, dum intellectus et communitas corrigibilia sunt.
Aporia fit disciplina theologica positiva, quia ignorantia virium, temporis et causalitatis a simulatione comprehensionis ad confessionem dependentiae transfertur.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Opacitas confessionem generat, confessio illuminationem petit, illuminatio ampliorem capacitatem aperit, et capacitas renovata novam confessionem requirit.
Donum facultatem operandi constituit, operatio vulnus et receptivitatem manifestat, atque haec manifestatio receptionem ulterioris gratiae amplificat.
Bonum creatum attentionem allicit; amor inordinatus illud in finem mutat; dispersio crescit; misericordia petita ordinem amoris instaurat.
Sonus ad iudicium interius remittitur, iudicium Verbum quaerit, Verbum plures sensus veros aperit, et hi rursus examen caritatis postulant.
Interior formatio communitatem gignit, communitas ordinem creationis recapitulat, et recapitulatio conditionem interiorem sub ampliori historia iterum interpretatur.
Pluralitas sensuum examen veritatis excitat; exclusio falsi concordiam caritatis format; concordia novam fecunditatem semanticam producit.
Exspectatio per attentionem in memoriam transit, transitus repetiti historiam formationis efficiunt, et historia desiderium suae consummationis auget.
Unitas divina est attractor recursivus intra tempus, sed requies sine vespera attractor terminalis est qui recursionem operum tandem claudit.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Deus sibi sufficiens + creatio ex nihilo → dependentia universalis → impossibilitas autonomiae ontologicae et epistemicae.
Capacitas nondum formata + vocatio Verbi → receptio formae → mutatio ordinata → tempus creatum.
Creatura temporalis + memoria + attentio + exspectatio → identitas distributa → distentio sive historia formationis.
Signum exterior vel Scriptura → iudicium interius → sensus veri multiplices → exclusio falsi → concordia caritatis.
Bonum creatum + attentio inordinata → captatio → dispersio → confessio limitis → petitio illuminationis.
Gratia + mediatio + causalitas participativa → actio creata → collectio interior et ecclesialis → renovata capacitas receptionis.
Opera temporalia + intentio ad unum → sanatio incohata → pax futura → sabbatum sine vespera.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Sufficientia divina → origo non chronologica → capacitas creata → vocatio formativa → mutationes ordinatae → tempus.
Signa et vestigia → iudicium interius → opacitas et distentio → confessio → illuminatio → caritas → formatio communis.
Multiplicitas ordinata → opera temporalia → collectio ad unum → mediatio Christi → pax futura → requies sine vespera.
Dependentia ontologica fit tabula communis essendi, cognoscendi, volendi, interpretandi et perseverandi.
Interioritas ex spatio autonomiae in locum receptionis mutatur, ubi ontologia creaturae et disciplina interpretationis intersecantur.
Tempus ex continente universali in effectum mutationis et distributionem praesentium operationum reclassificatur.
Multiplicitas desinit esse aut pura dispersio aut error, quia ordo finis eam in fecunditatem ontologicam et hermeneuticam convertit.
Auctoritas ex possessione sensus in ministerium corrigibile sub veritate et canone transfertur.
Malum ex proprietate rerum in modum directionis reclassificatur, quo bonum creatum a fonte avertitur et attentionem captivam facit.
Ecclesia fit extensio historica formationis interioris et locus ubi grammatica creationis per signa, ministeria et intellectus recapitulari potest.
Bonitas temporalium non ex perpetuitate eorum, sed ex transitu ordinato ad fruitionem et requiem aestimatur.
Gradus superficiei confessionem, memoriam, tentationem, creationem, verba Geneseos, Ecclesiam et sabbatum tamquam obiecta distincta proponit.
Gradus structuralis capacitatem, memoriam, attentionem, formam, mutationem, caritatem et gratiam in machinam receptionis atque collectionis componit.
Gradus metastrategicus certamen de autonomia vel sensu unico in disciplinam dependentiae, pluralitatis verae et auctoritatis corrigibilis transfert.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis Deum ut causam aeternam, creaturam ut receptionem mutabilem et historiam ut ordinem formationis constituit.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus reditu, variatione et negatione efficit quod affirmat: lectorem a dispersione ad intentionem et a clausura ad corrigibilitatem transfert.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Tempus oscillat inter affectionem animi, effectum mutationis et medium historiae salutis; relatio ontologica horum trium statuum non plene solvitur.
Actus aeternus successionem creatam producit, sed transitus ab origine non chronologica ad effectus ordinatos formalizationi resistit.
Gratia omnem facultatem bonam constituit, dum voluntas responsabilitatem retinet; nexus causalitatis participativae et imputabilitatis incompletus manet.
Veritas interior criterium certum praebet subiecto opaco, dum auctoritas ecclesialis participata et corrigibilis idem iudicium socialiter distribuit.
Pluralitas sensuum auctoritate, Spiritu et caritate limitatur, sed regula plena compatibilitatis inter sensus veros non exhibetur.
Analogia inter informitatem et distentionem fecunda est, sed conflationem capacitatis ontologicae cum culpa morali minatur.
Mediatio Christi cum Verbo creatorio structuram globalem claudit, quamquam necessitas huius coniunctionis ex phaenomenologia temporis sola non deducitur.
Creatura naturaliter mutabilis manet, sed requies terminalis reditum mutationis excludit; modus stabilizationis sine abolitione naturae fragilis est.
Informitas mutatur ex capacitate privativa in figuram aversionis, deinde cum distentione tamquam indigentia collectionis coniungitur.
Attentio mutatur ex mensura successionis in intentionem normativam, quae sub caritate etiam interpretationem et motum ontologicum regit.
Memoria mutatur ex operatione retinendi in exemplar mediationis, quod Scriptura et communitas ad praesentiam Verbi amplificant.
Tempus mutatur ex mensuratione transitus interioris in intervallum pedagogicum fidei, actionis et institutionis communis.
Requies mutatur ex directione stabilizante vitae praesentis in transformationem terminalem quae omnia opera temporalia claudit.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas est machina donationis et conversionis circa centrum immutabile, in qua dependentiae mutabiles formam, directionem et quietem recipiunt.
Subiectum est nodus receptivus et porosus, cuius unitas ex memoria, attentione, appetitu, signis et pondere amoris efficitur.
Tempus est simul fluvius transitus et officina formationis, inter originem sine successione et requiem sine vespera extensum.
Memoria et Scriptura sunt duae superficies prismaticae quibus absentia non removetur, sed in vestigium, sensum et praesentem operationem refringitur.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga a conditione creata, sed directio attentionis et amoris per confessionem, Verbum, gratiam et mediatorem.
Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad restituendam machinam quae creationem, interioritatem, tempus, interpretationem, Ecclesiam et requiem sub una lege participationis coordinat.
Structura firmissima est asymmetria inter Deum sibi sufficientem et creaturam cui esse, veritas, actio, unitas et quies donantur.
Nondum satis determinantur relatio temporis ad affectionem animi, status informitatis et causalitas qua actus aeternus successionem producit.
Regula plena discernendi sensus multiplices et traducendi ordinem creationis in Ecclesiam axiomaticae reductioni adhuc resistit.
Coordinatio gratiae, actionis et responsabilitatis cohaeret ut postulatum systemicum, sed nondum in formulam causalem completam redigitur.
Pons inter Verbum creatorium et mediationem Christi clausuram globalem sustinet, quamvis praemissis revelatis atque analogia plus quam deductione interna nitatur.
Restitutio motum verum servat si dependentiam, recursionem, pluralitatem ordinatam et terminalem requiem retinet, neque imagines memoriae, informitatis et sabbati in identitatem complanat.
The system asks how a creature opaque to itself, mutable and temporal, receives a pretemporal origin, the truth of itself, and a direction toward rest.
The global thesis places all knowledge, formation, action, and rest under the asymmetry of divine donation: the creature receives what it cannot produce from itself.
The argument joins apophatic confession with metaphysical, hermeneutical, and ecclesial reconstruction, so that ontological dependence may be explained in the discipline of temporal reception.
The movement proceeds from a non-chronological origin through signs, interiority, and succession, then transcends interiority toward the Word, the formed community, and the eternal end.
The progression is spiral: every illumination opens a new opacity, and every formation retrospectively reconstitutes origin and end from a new perspective.
Dispersion and formlessness are non-identical modes of lacking proper unity; charity, intention, and the Word convert them into formation without abolishing plurality.

Time becomes at once the medium of the wound and of formation: within it attention is dispersed, gifts are received, works are performed, and the creature is ordered toward its own transcendence of time.
Present closure is always deferred, but the delay is not infinite: peace not yet possessed is terminally gathered into the Sabbath without evening.
[Persistent] The immutable God is neither contained by time nor perfected by creation, but remains the measure of truth and the source of all formation.
[Persistent] The creature, made from nothing, possesses in itself neither the cause of being nor the principle of knowledge, order, or perseverance.
[Mutating] Mutability passes from the ontological capacity to receive form to succession, the distention of the subject, and the history of common formation.
[Emergent] The creature is a receptive capacity to which effected unity is given; interiority, formless matter, and ecclesial life exhibit diverse degrees of this receptivity.
[Persistent] Interior truth and the uncreated Word transcend the subject, judge its errors, and call dispersed capacity to form.
[Mutating] Interiority changes from a site of self-examination into the joint of ontology and hermeneutics, where the creature's opacity encounters the judgment of truth.
[Emergent] Time is a created mode of reception and passage: it arises from changes, is measured by the operations of the mind, and sustains the history of formation.
[Attractor] Unity in God through charity is the attractor that gathers attention, loves, meanings, and works without destroying created diversity.
[Mutating] Memory and Scripture are temporal mediations through which absence becomes operative: the past is present through trace, the eternal Word through humble speech.
[Persistent] Created goods and multiplicity are positive, but a means turned into an end produces dispersion, whereas relation to the source constitutes the goodness of the whole.
[Emergent] Confession and interpretation do not merely report truth already possessed, but performatively reform affection, understanding, and community under truth.
[Persistent] Grace and divine causality do not suppress finite action, but participatively constitute the capacity to know, will, and act.
[Emergent] The creative principle of the Word and the mediation of Christ constitute one axis through which the creature is called into being, reformed, and directed through mortality toward justice.
[Terminal] Peace not yet present and the Sabbath without evening constitute one eschatological closure, in which works pass away and succession is not renewed.
[Attractor] True unity is not univocity or empty simplicity, but the order of many under one source, one truth, and one end.
Creation from nothing retains a stable identity, but is amplified from a cosmological proposition into a law of epistemic, moral, and ecclesial dependence.
Immutable truth remains the measure, but its role extends from interior judgment to the formative calling of the creator Word.
Memory migrates from an interior archive into temporal mediation, to which Scripture responds as the community's medium toward the eternal Word.
Dispersion and formlessness do not fulfill the same function, but recurrently designate a capacity that does not possess unity from itself and needs formation.
Attention changes from the faculty of measuring into the direction of love, then in charity acquires a hermeneutical norm and ontological weight.
The judgment of truth migrates from confession of interior movements to exegesis of multiple meanings, while preserving the correction of affection and understanding.
The present changes from a moral instant to be examined into the pedagogical medium of history, through which form is received, exercised, and handed over to memory.
Mediation is amplified from the reconciliation of the sinner to the universal structure of origin, formation, and temporal direction.
Multiplicity reverses its force: without one end it is dispersive, but under unity of source it produces the fecundity of things and understandings.
The delay of peace undergoes terminal transformation, as rest passes from participated stability into the irreversible end of all succession.
Taxonomies of memory and the question of formless matter remain local; only the structure of capacity that receives trace or form ascends.
The threefold desire and correspondences of individual days are lower mechanisms; the present level retains the law of distributing attention and means according to capacity.
Creation from nothing and the priority of origin without interval are amplified into a universal principle of non-autonomous causality.
Aporias concerning the length of the present and the order of change remain locally, but together demonstrate that time is neither a receptacle nor full self-possession.
Interior judgment and hermeneutical plurality join the lower levels, because meanings are received multiply but subjected to truth above the interpreter.
The community of confession and ecclesial recapitulation constitute the transition of the present level, by which interior formation is externalized into an interpreting and exercising body.
Anti-Donatist polemic and the refutation of celestial cycles recede after performing their local work, but their exclusion of autonomous judgment and created measure persists.
Christ the mediator and the creative Word do not remain regional conclusions, but effect the greater bridge between the donation of being and the reformation of life.
Doubts concerning temporal affection and the state of formless matter preserve lower limits; the synthesis coordinates them but does not resolve them into one exhaustive ontology.
No creature can be its own cause, measure, illuminator, or consummator.
Neither matter nor time nor mind nor any other substance can be posited as coeternal with God or independent of his causality.
God is neither contained by memory nor deliberates, changes, or is completed through created works temporally.
Interiority provides neither self-transparency nor an exhaustive view of truth.
Multiplicity neither produces order of itself nor is simply equivalent to falsity; univocity and indiscriminate license are equally excluded.
Mediation is not an impediment to be overcome by autonomous ascent, but a necessary mode of formation within mortality, signs, and degrees of capacity.
Body, matter, time, and sensible goods are not evil substances, but neither are they ultimate ends or self-governing principles.
No closure within the mortal state, nor the perpetuation of temporal works, constitutes the creature's consummation.
Divine causality and created action cannot be explained by a competitive relation, because dependence on gift constitutes finite operation itself.
Divine immutability cannot signify inertia, although eternal act produces successive effects without change in itself.
Succession cannot contain the divine cause or narrate its will, but only the mode in which created effects are received.
Unity cannot require the complete identity of parts, because the system coheres only if true plurality subsists under an undivided source.
Truth is neither produced nor terminated by interior affection or the conscious intention of a human minister.
Introspection, analysis of time, and mediation of signs cannot be converted into immediate ascent to immutability.
The homology between distention, formlessness, and formation does not by itself demonstrate the necessity of a mediator or the translation of all creation into the Church.
Radically unavailable is the possibility of a creature that possesses itself wholly at once and has stability from its own nature.
Origin before time can neither be represented in chronological order nor explained through anything coeternal with God.
The end without evening cannot be conceived as a final moment within a series, because it terminates succession itself with peace not yet possessed.
There is no outside divine causality from which the subject might receive being, truth, or substantial opposition.
A created perspective that exhausts soul, time, Scripture, and divine intention simultaneously is constitutively precluded.
The neutrality of attention and love is unavailable: every reception is either ordered to the source or turns a means into an end.
Dependence from nothing exceeds ontology and recurs in knowledge, will, and interpretation, because no operation of the creature contains its sufficient principle.
Formlessness and distention exhibit two magnitudes of the lack of proper unity: the former, capacity for formation; the latter, the division of a life already formed but not yet gathered.
Time is at once the effect of created change and the interior form of its reception; therefore it is neither an objective receptacle nor a private fiction.
Memory and Scripture convert absence into present efficacy: the one makes traces of life operate, the other the Word through temporal words.
Charity is the higher form of attention, because it simultaneously directs the objects of desire, meanings of the text, and works of the community toward a common end.
Confession and exegesis are mechanisms of recursive correction: each places action under truth, excludes false closure, and opens broader reception.
Grace constitutes created action, but responsibility for the same action is retained; dependence and imputability therefore cohere without a fully formalized mode of cooperation.
The creative Word and Christ the mediator effect one direction: the donation of being continues into formative calling, mortal reconciliation, and return to justice.
Multiplicity is the locus of bifurcation: separated from source and end it disperses; ordered under unity of truth it constitutes the fecundity of things and understandings.
Present works contain their own obsolescence, because they begin healing but are ordered toward peace and Sabbath, which close succession.
The asymmetry of creation and grace generates one law of participation: as being is given, so self-knowledge, formation, and perseverance are received.
The subject is a temporally distributed capacity, whose identity is composed from appetite, memory, attention, signs, and the orientation of love.
History is not neutral succession, but the apparatus through which the will is reformed, works pass away, and the creature is prepared for a non-temporal state.
The Church externalizes interior gathering, because the community of confession, interpretation, and distribution of means corporeally exercises the same formation that the mind receives.
Ontological plurality and hermeneutical plurality become homologous: each presupposes a determinate capacity for receiving several true forms.
Evil is removed from the field of substances and transferred into the direction of created good, by which attention usurps a means or charity refers it to the source.
Salvation is the reconfiguration of all created temporality, not flight from it: mediation assumes succession, orders it, and leads it to irreversible rest.
Participated knowledge joins certainty of principle with provisionality of application; truth remains stable, while understanding and community are corrigible.
Aporia becomes a positive theological discipline, because ignorance of powers, time, and causality is transferred from the simulation of comprehension to confession of dependence.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Opacity generates confession, confession seeks illumination, illumination opens a broader capacity, and renewed capacity requires a new confession.
Gift constitutes the capacity to act, operation manifests wound and receptivity, and this manifestation amplifies reception of further grace.
Created good draws attention; disordered love turns it into an end; dispersion increases; mercy requested restores the order of love.
Sound is referred to interior judgment, judgment seeks the Word, the Word opens several true meanings, and these in turn demand examination by charity.
Interior formation generates community, community recapitulates the order of creation, and recapitulation again interprets interior condition under a broader history.
Plurality of meanings arouses examination of truth; exclusion of the false forms the concord of charity; concord produces new semantic fecundity.
Expectation passes through attention into memory, repeated transitions produce the history of formation, and history increases desire for its consummation.
Divine unity is a recursive attractor within time, but rest without evening is the terminal attractor that finally closes the recursion of works.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: God self-sufficient + creation from nothing → universal dependence → impossibility of ontological and epistemic autonomy.
Capacity not yet formed + calling of the Word → reception of form → ordered change → created time.
Temporal creature + memory + attention + expectation → distributed identity → distention or history of formation.
Exterior sign or Scripture → interior judgment → multiple true meanings → exclusion of the false → concord of charity.
Created good + disordered attention → capture → dispersion → confession of limit → petition for illumination.
Grace + mediation + participatory causality → created action → interior and ecclesial gathering → renewed capacity for reception.
Temporal works + intention toward one → healing begun → future peace → Sabbath without evening.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Divine sufficiency → non-chronological origin → created capacity → formative calling → ordered changes → time.
Signs and traces → interior judgment → opacity and distention → confession → illumination → charity → common formation.
Ordered multiplicity → temporal works → gathering toward one → mediation of Christ → future peace → rest without evening.
Ontological dependence becomes the common map of being, knowing, willing, interpreting, and persevering.
Interiority changes from a space of autonomy into a place of reception, where the ontology of the creature and the discipline of interpretation intersect.
Time is reclassified from a universal container into the effect of change and the distribution of present operations.
Multiplicity ceases to be either pure dispersion or error, because the order of the end converts it into ontological and hermeneutical fecundity.
Authority is transferred from possession of meaning into corrigible ministry under truth and canon.
Evil is reclassified from a property of things into a mode of direction, by which created good is turned away from the source and makes attention captive.
The Church becomes the historical extension of interior formation and the place where the grammar of creation can be recapitulated through signs, ministries, and understandings.
The goodness of temporal things is assessed not from their perpetuity, but from their ordered passage to fruition and rest.
The surface level presents confession, memory, temptation, creation, the words of Genesis, the Church, and Sabbath as distinct objects.
The structural level composes capacity, memory, attention, form, change, charity, and grace into a mechanism of reception and gathering.
The metastrategic level transfers the contest over autonomy or a single meaning into a discipline of dependence, true plurality, and corrigible authority.
The ontological and temporal level establishes God as eternal cause, the creature as mutable reception, and history as the order of formation.
The methodological and performative level accomplishes by return, variation, and negation what it affirms: it transfers the reader from dispersion to intention and from closure to corrigibility.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Time oscillates between affection of the mind, effect of change, and medium of the history of salvation; the ontological relation of these three states is not fully resolved.
Eternal act produces created succession, but the passage from non-chronological origin to ordered effects resists formalization.
Grace constitutes every good capacity, while the will retains responsibility; the nexus of participatory causality and imputability remains incomplete.
Interior truth provides a certain criterion to an opaque subject, while participated and corrigible ecclesial authority distributes the same judgment socially.
Plurality of meanings is limited by authority, Spirit, and charity, but no full rule of compatibility among true meanings is exhibited.
The analogy between formlessness and distention is fruitful, but threatens conflation of ontological capacity with moral fault.
The mediation of Christ with the creative Word closes the global structure, although the necessity of this conjunction is not deduced from the phenomenology of time alone.
The creature remains naturally mutable, but terminal rest excludes the return of change; the mode of stabilization without abolition of nature is fragile.
Formlessness changes from privative capacity into a figure of aversion, then is joined with distention as a need for gathering.
Attention changes from the measure of succession into normative intention, which under charity also governs interpretation and ontological movement.
Memory changes from the operation of retaining into a model of mediation, which Scripture and community amplify toward the presence of the Word.
Time changes from the measurement of interior passage into a pedagogical interval of faith, action, and common institution.
Rest changes from the stabilizing direction of present life into a terminal transformation that closes all temporal works.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is a mechanism of donation and conversion around an immutable center, in which mutable dependencies receive form, direction, and rest.
The subject is a receptive and porous node, whose unity is effected from memory, attention, appetite, signs, and the weight of love.
Time is at once a river of passage and a workshop of formation, extended between origin without succession and rest without evening.
Memory and Scripture are two prismatic surfaces through which absence is not removed, but refracted into trace, meaning, and present operation.
Navigation is possible not as flight from the created condition, but as the direction of attention and love through confession, the Word, grace, and the mediator.
The present axioms suffice to restore the mechanism that coordinates creation, interiority, time, interpretation, the Church, and rest under one law of participation.
The firmest structure is the asymmetry between God self-sufficient and the creature to which being, truth, action, unity, and rest are given.
The relation of time to affection of the mind, the status of formlessness, and the causality by which eternal act produces succession are not yet sufficiently determined.
The full rule for discerning multiple meanings and translating the order of creation into the Church still resists axiomatic reduction.
The coordination of grace, action, and responsibility coheres as a systemic postulate, but is not yet reduced to a complete causal formula.
The bridge between the creative Word and the mediation of Christ sustains the global closure, although it relies on revealed premises and analogy more than on internal deduction.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement if it retains dependence, recursion, ordered plurality, and terminal rest, and does not flatten the images of memory, formlessness, and Sabbath into identity.
