The geography of nature is not compelled to admit any opening to a punitive kingdom after death.
The therapeutic machine follows this order: external abundance without a healthy receptacle → insatiability and corruption → desire and fear → definition of limits → tranquility.
The diagnostic machine follows this order: terrible phenomenon → ignorance of cause → divine attribution → religious fear → material inquiry → removal of divine governance.
The explanatory machine follows this order: sensible effect → signs and analogies → limits of powers → possible mechanisms → selection of a cause or constrained plurality.
The interaction machine follows this order: body with void → emanation of bodies → selective passages → pressure, penetration, conjunction, or repulsion → manifest effect.
The plague machine follows this order: disease-bearing seeds → corruption of air or food → entry into bodies → contagion → dilemmas of care → dissolution of remedy, rite, and social order.
The closure of the system follows this order: knowledge of causes → knowledge of limits → diminution of wonder → removal of divine fear → peace of mind and a more correct conception of the gods.

Therapeutic discovery → diagnosis of the defective mind → necessity of the account of nature → mortality of the world → explanation of celestial things → explanation of terrestrial things → particular interactions → plague → social dissolution.
In individual treatments the movement recurs: wonder or terror → observed effect → one or multiple material mechanisms → refutation of divine cause → reduction of fear.
Security is transferred from possession of external things to the capacity of the mind to receive them.
Terrifying religion is reclassified from knowledge of the gods into an effect of ignorance of causes.
The opposition between piety and naturalism collapses, because the peace of the gods is preserved through the exclusion of divine intervention.
A plurality of causes is transformed from a defect of reasoning into a form of causally constrained discipline.
Heaven, earth, body, and disease are reduced to one continuum of material mechanisms.
Miracle is transferred from a separate class of things into an effect of magnitude, rarity, and ignorance.
The living body is reclassified from a closed unity into a permeable and environmentally dependent structure.
Calamity is reordered from moral judgment into a material process with biological, social, and ritual effects.
Knowledge of nature is distinguished from the promise of remedy, protection, or practical control.
At the surface level, celestial, terrestrial, magnetic, diseased, and pestilential events that provoke wonder or fear are explained.
At the structural level, events are generated from bodies, void, effluvia, textures, passages, motions, and local compositions.
At the metastrategic level, the contest is transferred from propitiating divine powers to correcting opinions and defining the limits of causal powers.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality consists of mortal bodies, composition, dissolution, contingent encounters, and an infinite totality.
The body of axioms suffices to reconstruct the movement from anxiety of mind through natural causality to the consequences of plague.
The matter of the highest good and the full doctrine of desire and fear are presupposed rather than determinately explained in this book.
The actual mechanism of many events remains indeterminate, because the text often demonstrates natural possibility without selecting a single cause.
The system coheres internally, because it combines a plurality of mechanisms with unity of ontology and limits of powers; no direct contradiction emerges.
The firmest joint is the connection among ignorance of causes, divine attribution, fear, and the discipline of natural limits.
The principal fragility consists in analogies, which establish the possibility of a mechanism but do not always prove its actuality.
The affirmation of the truest account generates tension with the frequent plurality of causes between therapeutic certainty and epistemic modesty.
The promise of purification of mind is constrained by the closure on plague, because natural knowledge guarantees neither a common remedy nor social stability.
The gods are preserved as peaceful beings, but their ontological status and relation to divine images are not fully derived within this machine.
Gaps in the source leave certain local connections, but the reconstruction preserves the principal movement from therapy of the mind to the physics of causes and thence to mortal vulnerability.
Systema quaerit quibus principiis materia, motus, compositio et vita constent, ut cognitio eorum terrorem religiosum et metum mortis dissolvat.
Thesis globalis naturam constituit ut campum corporum primorum in inani motorum, ex quorum coniunctionibus res, qualitates, mundi et personae temporariae emergunt.
Terror non ut responsio ad potestatem transcendentem, sed ut effectus ignorantiae causalitatis, falsa bonorum aestimatio et anticipatio subiecti post mortem denuo constituitur.
Argumentatio diagnostica, reconstructiva, polemica et therapeutica fit, quia errorem affectivum detegit, structuram invisibilem restituit, exemplaria aemula excludit atque vitam praesentem reordinat.
Motus manifestus ab effectibus sensibilibus ad principia occulta, ab his ad compositiones emergentes, deinde ad mortalitatem mundi et personae procedit.
Motus verus est recursivus et cumulativus: sensus indicia praebet, ratio causas invisibiles construit, consequentiae ad apparentias redeunt, probationes autem multiplicatae statum affectivum mutant.
Directio systematis a concursibus sine consilio ad ordinem materialem, ab ordine ad vitam sensibilem, a vita finita ad therapiam sine providentia fertur.
Clausura est causaliter naturalis et therapeutice terminalis: exterior divinus excluditur, sed series naturalis non omnino fatalis manet; dissolutio personae aufert ipsum subiectum mali posthumi.
[Attractor] Ratio naturae terrorem dissolvit non consolatione extrinseca, sed translatione affectus in quaestionem causalitatis.
[Persistent] Omnis processus naturalis in corporibus primis, inani et motibus eorum fundatur.
[Persistent] Materia nec ex nihilo producitur nec ad nihilum reducitur, sed inter formas successive distribuitur.
[Persistent] Primordia solida, immutabilia et perpetuo mobilia permanent, dum concilia eorum nascuntur et dissolvuntur.
[Mutating] Configuratio principiorum primum diversitatem rerum, deinde qualitates emergentes, postremo identitatem personae constituit.
[Emergent] Infinitas materiae promiscuitatem non infert, quia semina certa et compatibilitates selectivae fines generationis servant.
[Mutating] Infinitas summae mundum a centro removet, pluralitatem mundorum generat et quemque mundum in concilium locale atque mortale mutat.
[Emergent] Clinamen seriem causarum fataliter clausam interrumpit sine causa supernaturali introducenda.
[Mutating] Sensus est simul fundamentum cognitionis et effectus emergens communis ordinationis corporis, animi atque animae.
[Persistent] Dei causaliter semoti neque naturam administrant neque ordinem mundanum ad usum humanum dirigunt.
[Emergent] Persona est ordinatio temporaria corporis, animi, animae et motuum sensiferorum, non substantia simplex transmigrans.
[Terminal] Mors dissolvit concilium personae; quia idem subiectum sentiens non superest, mors ei malum fieri non potest.
[Attractor] Divitiae, gloria, potentia et violentia sunt circuitus compensatorii quibus metus mortis frustra tegitur.
[Terminal] Vita est usus finitus materiae, cui sufficientia non ex duratione indefinita sed ex terminatione cupiditatis provenit.
Distinctio corporis et inanis identitatem ontologicam retinet atque fundamentum tam cosmologiae quam physicae animi manet.
Concilium redit functione amplificata: primo rem genitam, deinde proprietatem relationalem, tandem personam temporalem significat.
Qualitas a dependentia corporum ad emergentiam dispositionis migrat; quod initio eventum non substantialem designat, postea differentiam inter principia insensilia et effectus sensibiles ordinat.
Sensus a norma epistemica in effectum corporeum mutatur, deinde in condicionem continuitatis personalis absorbetur.
Infinitas ab amplitudine summae ad pluralitatem mundorum amplificatur atque postremo omnem exceptionem cosmicam vel individualem excludit.
Mors invertitur: ex momento destructionis fit redistributio materiae, ex vicissitudine compositionis fit absentia subiecti patientis.
Mythologia a causalitate naturali removetur, sed non simpliciter evanescit: nomina divina et inferna in figuras generationis, affectuum et conscientiae transferuntur.
Invocatio divina literalitatem amittit, dum vis poetica eius in instrumentum dispositionis et transmissionis rationis absorbetur.
Clausura causalis functionem mutat: exclusio interventionis divinae persistit, sed necessitas absoluta per clinamen limitatur.
Probationes particulares inanis et minimorum inferiores manent; hoc gradu valent ut condiciones iam constitutae motus, compositionis et dissolutionis.
Mechanica clinaminis et figurarum atomicarum localiter motum explicat, sed sursum amplificatur in theoriam differentiae emergentis et agentiae non fatalis.
Distributio anatomica animi et animae mechanismus localis manet; eius effectus praesentis gradus est definitio personae ut organizationis materialis.
Ontologia corporis et inanis omnes unitates coniungit, quia eadem fundamenta a rebus externis ad animam et identitatem transferuntur.
Mortalitas mundi et mortalitas animi efficiunt transitionem maiorem qua lex compositorum a cosmologia ad anthropologiam descendit.
Appellationes mythicae locales aliter codificantur: causalitatem amittunt, sed in schemata generationis naturalis vel perturbationis praesentis servantur.
Refutationes elementorum sensibilium, medii cosmici et dispositionis Democriteae munere polemico perfecto non fiunt axiomata globalia, quamquam fines exemplarium admissibilium muniunt.
Generatio et interitus neque creatio absoluta neque annihilatio absoluta sunt.
Nulla tertia natura incorporea intra ordinem causalitatis admittitur, ideo anima separabilis causaliter agens excluditur.
Ordo mundanus neque consilium principiorum neque creationem ad hominis utilitatem neque administrationem divinam requirit.
Medium universale, mundus unicus et exceptio individualis sunt formae eiusdem privilegii cosmici repudiati.
Principia ultima non gerunt qualitates sensibiles aut formas mortales compositorum quae efficiunt.
Lux sensibilis, opes, honores et mutatio loci causam perturbationis non attingunt.
Anima extra corpus integra non persistit, inferi posthumi non subsistunt, mors autem non est malum a mortuo experiendum.
Ut systema constet, ignorantia causae non potest vim probativam pro numine habere.
Apparentia sensibilis non potest esse inventarium completum realitatis neque qualitates conspicuae essentiam principiorum immediate manifestare.
Stabilitas ordinis non potest intentionem praesupponere, sed neque omnis motus potest serie antecedentium perfecte necessaria claudi.
Identitas non potest in materia uniformi aut mera eiusdem materiae restitutione consistere; ordinatio selectiva et continuitas sensus requiruntur.
Subiectum propriae non-exsistentiae testis esse non potest; sine eo neque malum neque poena posthuma locum habet.
Securitas non potest per accumulationem rerum exteriorum aut per fugam spatialem acquiri, quia utraque causam perturbationis intactam relinquit.
Systema circa absentiam omnis exterioris ordinatur: nullus creator, terminator, receptaculum aut supplementum extra summam rerum poni potest.
Nulla potestas transcendens personam dissolutam reservat neque prospectum personalem trans mortis terminum continuat.
Initium absolutum, interitus absolutus et status finalis universalis sunt possibilitates inadmissibiles; permanent tantum redistributiones sine clausura ultima.
Nullus locus, mundus, homo aut destinatarius privilegiatus potest ordinem infinitum ad se referre.
Possibilitas maxime exclusa est mors ut experientia personae: mors ipsum campum experientiae aufert.
Eadem lex compositionis et dissolutionis res particulares, mundos et personas regit; differentia inter eos est magnitudinis et ordinationis, non generis ontologici.
Qualitas, sensus et identitas personalis sunt proprietates relationum materialium quae in primordiis separatim inesse non debent.
Clausura naturalis excludit arbitrium divinum, non autem omnem contingentiam; clinamen facit ut immanentia materialis a fatalismo distinguatur.
Mundus localis et persona localis sunt stabilizationes temporariae intra campum materialem maiorem, unde neuter singularitatem aut immunitatem a dissolutione possidet.
Religio timida, appetitus bonorum exteriorum et ambitio politica sunt varia remedia falsa eiusdem ignorantiae de natura et mortalitate.
Methodus quae ex effectibus sensibilibus causas invisibiles infert eodem actu corpora prima, motus sub limine sensus et corporeitatem animi restituit.
Sublata providentia mundana et subiecto posthumo, ordo moralis ad effectus praesentes actionum, affectuum et conscientiae reponitur.
Realitas exhibet ordines inclusos stabilizationis: concilia rerum intra mundos locales et personae intra concilia organica, omnibus dissolutioni obnoxiis.
Tempus stratificatur in motum aeternum principiorum, durationes finitas mundorum et vitae, atque absentiam cuiuslibet temporis experti post dissolutionem personae.
Agentia naturalis neque libertas a natura neque mera necessitas est, sed apertura localis intra leges materiales et compatibilitates determinatas.
Veritas physica criterium therapeuticum accipit: tabula causalitatis probatur etiam per facultatem suam terrores fictos et fugas exteriores dissolvendi.
Ambitio et violentia politica non sunt principia autonoma, sed amplificationes sociales metus mortis intra cosmologiam sine privilegio humano.
Bonum vitae finitae non pendet a perpetuitate personae, sed a limitatione cupiditatis et usu temporario materiae communis.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Ignorantia causarum → terror indefinitus → religio et metus mortis → conatus compensatorii → maior perturbatio → renovata necessitas rationis naturalis.
Effectus sensibilis → causa invisibilis restituta → apparentia reclassificata → novum indicium sensibile constituit circuitum epistemicum systematis.
Compositio → proprietas emergens → dissolutio → redistributio materiae → nova compositio est circuitus conservationis qui generationem sine initio absoluto sustinet.
Concursus innumeri → dispositiones stabiles → mundi locales → incrementum et senectus → dissolutio → novi concursus efficiunt spiralem cosmologicam.
Metus mortis → ambitio et violentia → productio mortis → metus amplificatus est via catastrophica qua fuga a morte obiectum suum multiplicat.
Attractor occultus est configuratio: diversitas rerum, proprietates compositorum et persona ad modos ordinationis potius quam ad substantias separatas convergunt.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Ignorantia causalitatis → terror religiosus et mortis → perturbatio affectiva → quaestio de natura.
Corpora prima + inane → campus ontologicus sufficiens sine tertia natura aut interventu externo.
Motus perpetuus + pondus + plagae + clinamen → concursus non providentiales neque fataliter exhausti.
Figurae et ordines varii + compatibilitas selectiva → genera stabilia sine exemplaribus transcendentibus.
Principia qualitatibus carentia + ordinatio relationum → qualitates, vita et sensus emergentes.
Stabilizatio localis → res composita / mundus / persona → incrementum, alteratio et mortalitas.
Dissolutio conciliorum → materia conservata → successio formarum sine annihilatione aut identitate personali restituta.
Reclassificatio causalitatis → remotio providentiae et subiecti posthumi → imminutio cupiditatis compensatoriae → tranquillitas vitae finitae.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Effectus sensibilis → causa corporea invisibilis → corpus et inane → motus principiorum → compositio selectiva → proprietates emergentes → mundus et persona mortales → redistributio materiae.
Ignorantia → terror → religio, cupiditas et ambitio → investigatio naturae → mortalitas animi demonstrata → nullum subiectum post mortem → sufficientia vitae finitae.
Oppositio inter visibile et reale corruit: invisibilitas non removet rem e cognitione, sed methodum inferentialem requirit.
Qualitas et sensus ex proprietatibus simplicibus substantiarum in effectus relationum et motuum communium reclassificantur.
Mundus et mens ex entibus privilegiatis in organizationes locales, multiplicabiles et mortales transferuntur.
Ager causalitatis non iam inter providentiam et fatum dividitur; immanentia materialis contingentiam limitatam continere potest.
Mors et vitia politica in eadem tabula disponuntur: absentia subiecti posthumi verum mortis statum constituit, dum imaginatio contraria cupiditatem et violentiam parit.
Oppositio inter doctrinam et therapiam solvitur: forma poetica rationem transmittit, ratio autem campum affectivum et practicum reordinat.
Gradus superficiei principia rerum, metus humanos, qualitates conspicuas, naturam animi et quaestionem mortis coniungit.
Gradus structuralis corpora prima, inane, motus, compositiones, leges conexionis et organizationem sensiferam continet.
Gradus metastrategicus apparentias in vestigia causarum convertit atque certamen contra deos, fatum et mortem in correctionem tabulae causalitatis mutat.
Gradus ontologicus et temporalis materiam aeternam, concilia mortalia, mundos plurales, identitatem continuam et mortem sine experientia distinguit.
Gradus methodologicus et performativus obscuritatem doctrinae per carmen, analogiam et probationem cumulativam tractat, ita ut forma expositionis transitum ab affectu ad rationem efficiat.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Sensus fundamentum probationis manet, quamquam ratio inventarium apparentiae corrigere debet; regula huius correctionis non plene formalizatur.
Leges certas compositionis et compatibilitatis clinamen loco temporeque incertum interrumpit, sine clara mensura relationis inter necessitatem et contingentiam.
Sensus ex principiis insensilibus emergere debet, sed transitus a figura et motu ad qualitatem sentiendi mechanice incompletus manet.
Immortalitas deorum cum lege dissolutionis compositorum nondum componitur, quia dei remoti potius postulantur quam materialiter restituti.
Invocatio Veneris vim agendi poeticam retinet, quamquam interventio divina physice negatur; distinctio figurae et causalitatis hanc commissuram sustinet.
Unitas animi et animae cum hierarchia inter animum regentem, animam consentientem et quartam vim sensiferam imperfecte cohaeret.
Qualitas mutatur ex accidente dependenti in proprietatem relationalem emergentem quae gradus ontologicos distinguit.
Clinamen causalitatem clausam mutat in immanentiam apertam, sed nexus inter declinationem atomicam et voluntatem conscientem fragilis manet.
Mors ab eventu dissolutionis ad mutationem logicam transit qua, subiecto sublato, ipsa relatio nocendi impossibilis fit.
Identitas a similitudine materiae ad continuitatem organizationis, sensus et memoriae transfertur.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est campus infinitus corporum mobilium qui sine centro concilia localia, mundos et ruinas eorum generat.
Subiectum est nodus corporeus temporarius in quo animus, anima, organa et motus sensiferi identitatem finitam efficiunt.
Tempus est distributio ordinum heterochronorum: principia manent, concilia durant et intereunt, persona autem propriam absentiam numquam experitur.
Navigatio possibilis non est fuga e natura aut e se ipso, sed cognitio causarum intra naturam non fataliter clausam.
Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad restituendam catenam a materia conservata et motu ad emergentiam, mundos mortales, personam dissolubilem et therapiam metus.
Structura firmissima est coniunctio conservationis materiae, explicationis configurationalis et probationis cumulativae mortalitatis organicae.
Minus determinati manent nexus a clinamine ad voluntatem et a motibus primordiorum insensilium ad sensum.
Systema hoc gradu cohaeret quia motum ab effectu affectivo ad physicam, ab ontologia ad cosmologiam, deinde ad conversionem vitae servat.
Commissurae fragiliores analogiis qualitatum, principio mutationis substantialis et correctione rationali apparentiarum nituntur.
Reductioni axiomaticae resistit transitus performativus quo doctrina obscura per formam poeticam et cognitionem causalitatis in acceptationem affectivam vitae finitae convertitur.
The system asks by what principles matter, motion, composition, and life consist, so that knowledge of them may dissolve religious terror and fear of death.
The global thesis establishes nature as a field of first bodies moving in void, from whose conjunctions things, qualities, worlds, and temporary persons emerge.
Terror is reconstituted not as a response to transcendent power, but as an effect of ignorance of causality, false valuation of goods, and anticipation of the subject after death.
The argument becomes diagnostic, reconstructive, polemical, and therapeutic, because it detects affective error, restores invisible structure, excludes rival models, and reorders present life.
The manifest movement proceeds from sensible effects to hidden principles, from these to emergent compositions, and then to the mortality of the world and the person.
The true movement is recursive and cumulative: sense supplies indications, reason constructs invisible causes, consequences return to appearances, while multiplied proofs alter the affective state.
The direction of the system leads from chance encounters without design to material order, from order to sentient life, from finite life to therapy without providence.

The closure is causally natural and therapeutically terminal: a divine exterior is excluded, yet the natural series does not remain wholly fatal; the dissolution of the person removes the very subject of subsequent evil.
[Attractor] The account of nature dissolves terror not by extrinsic consolation, but by translating affect into a question of causality.
[Persistent] Every natural process is founded in first bodies, void, and their motions.
[Persistent] Matter is neither produced from nothing nor reduced to nothing, but is successively distributed among forms.
[Persistent] The first principles remain solid, immutable, and perpetually mobile, while their compounds arise and dissolve.
[Mutating] The configuration of principles first constitutes the diversity of things, then emergent qualities, and finally personal identity.
[Emergent] Infinity does not entail the indiscriminate mixture of matter, because determinate seeds and selective compatibilities preserve the limits of generation.
[Mutating] The infinity of the whole removes the world from the center, generates a plurality of worlds, and transforms each world into a local and mortal compound.
[Emergent] Clinamen interrupts a fatally closed sequence of causes without introducing a supernatural cause.
[Mutating] Sense is at once the foundation of knowledge and an emergent effect of the common ordering of body, animus, and anima.
[Persistent] Causally removed gods neither govern nature nor direct worldly order to human use.
[Emergent] The person is a temporary ordering of body, animus, anima, and sentient motions, not a simple transmigrating substance.
[Terminal] Death dissolves the compound of the person; because the same sentient subject does not survive, death cannot become an evil for it.
[Attractor] Wealth, glory, power, and violence are compensatory circuits by which fear of death is vainly covered over.
[Terminal] Life is a finite use of matter, whose sufficiency proceeds not from indefinite duration but from the termination of desire.
The distinction between body and void retains its ontological identity and remains the foundation of both cosmology and the physics of the animus.
Compound recurs with an expanded function: first it signifies the generated thing, then relational property, finally the temporal person.

Quality migrates from dependence on bodies to the emergence of disposition; what initially designates a non-substantial event later orders the difference between insentient principles and sensible effects.
Sense changes from an epistemic norm into a bodily effect, then is absorbed into the condition of personal continuity.
Infinity is amplified from the magnitude of the whole to the plurality of worlds and finally excludes every cosmic or individual exception.
Death is inverted: from a moment of destruction it becomes redistribution of matter, from a change of composition it becomes the absence of a suffering subject.
Mythology is removed from natural causality, but does not simply vanish: divine and infernal names are transferred into figures of generation, affects, and consciousness.
Divine invocation loses literalness, while its poetic force is absorbed into an instrument of disposition and transmission of reason.
Causal closure changes function: the exclusion of divine intervention persists, but absolute necessity is limited through clinamen.
The particular proofs of void and minima remain lower-level; at this level they are valid as already established conditions of motion, composition, and dissolution.
The mechanics of clinamen and atomic shapes explains motion locally, but is amplified upward into a theory of emergent difference and non-fatal agency.
The anatomical distribution of animus and anima remains a local mechanism; its present-level effect is the definition of the person as material organization.
The ontology of body and void unites all units, because the same foundations are carried from external things to the anima and identity.
The mortality of the world and the mortality of the animus effect the major transition by which the law of composites descends from cosmology to anthropology.
Local mythical appellations are encoded differently: they lose causality, but are retained in schemas of natural generation or present disturbance.

Having fulfilled their polemical function, refutations of sensible elements, the cosmic medium, and Democritean arrangement do not become global axioms, although they secure the boundaries of admissible models.
Generation and destruction are neither absolute creation nor absolute annihilation.
No third incorporeal nature is admitted within the order of causality; therefore a separable causally acting anima is excluded.
Worldly order requires neither a design of principles, nor creation for human benefit, nor divine administration.
A universal medium, a unique world, and individual exception are forms of the same rejected cosmic privilege.
Ultimate principles do not bear sensible qualities or the mortal forms of the composites they produce.
Sensible light, wealth, honors, and change of place do not reach the cause of disturbance.
The anima does not persist whole outside the body, posthumous infernal regions do not subsist, and death is not an evil to be experienced by the dead.
For the system to stand, ignorance of a cause cannot have probative force for divinity.
Sensible appearance cannot be a complete inventory of reality, nor can conspicuous qualities immediately reveal the essence of principles.
The stability of order cannot presuppose intention, but neither can every motion be enclosed by a perfectly necessary series of antecedents.
Identity cannot consist in uniform matter or in the mere restoration of the same matter; selective ordering and continuity of sense are required.
A subject cannot be witness to its own non-existence; without it, neither evil nor subsequent punishment has a place.
Security cannot be acquired through accumulation of external things or through spatial flight, because each leaves the cause of disturbance untouched.
The system is ordered around the absence of every exterior: no creator, terminator, receptacle, or supplement can be posited outside the sum of things.
No transcendent power preserves the dissolved person or continues a personal perspective beyond the boundary of death.
An absolute beginning, absolute destruction, and a universal final state are inadmissible possibilities; only redistributions without ultimate closure remain.
No privileged place, world, human being, or recipient can refer the infinite order to itself.
The possibility most excluded is death as the experience of a person: death removes the very field of experience.
The same law of composition and dissolution governs particular things, worlds, and persons; the difference among them is one of magnitude and ordering, not ontological kind.
Quality, sense, and personal identity are properties of material relations that need not inhere separately in the first principles.
Natural closure excludes divine arbitrariness, but not every contingency; clinamen ensures that material immanence is distinguished from fatalism.
The local world and the local person are temporary stabilizations within a greater material field, whence neither possesses singularity or immunity from dissolution.
Fearful religion, desire for external goods, and political ambition are various false remedies for the same ignorance concerning nature and mortality.
The method that infers invisible causes from sensible effects restores in the same act first bodies, motions beneath the threshold of sense, and the corporeality of the animus.
With worldly providence and the subsequent subject removed, moral order is relocated to the present effects of actions, affects, and consciousness.
Reality exhibits nested orders of stabilization: compounds of things within local worlds and persons within organic compounds, all subject to dissolution.
Time is stratified into the eternal motion of principles, the finite durations of worlds and lives, and the absence of any experienced time after the dissolution of the person.
Natural agency is neither freedom from nature nor mere necessity, but local openness within material laws and determinate compatibilities.
Physical truth acquires a therapeutic criterion: the causal map is proved also by its capacity to dissolve fictitious terrors and external flights.
Political ambition and violence are not autonomous principles, but social amplifications of fear of death within a cosmology without human privilege.
The good of finite life does not depend on the perpetuity of the person, but on the limitation of desire and the temporary use of common matter.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Ignorance of causes → indefinite terror → religion and fear of death → compensatory efforts → greater disturbance → renewed need for natural reason.
Sensible effect → restored invisible cause → reclassified appearance → new sensible indication constitutes the epistemic circuit of the system.
Composition → emergent property → dissolution → redistribution of matter → new composition is the circuit of conservation that sustains generation without an absolute beginning.
Innumerable encounters → stable dispositions → local worlds → growth and old age → dissolution → new encounters produce a cosmological spiral.
Fear of death → ambition and violence → production of death → amplified fear is the catastrophic path by which flight from death multiplies its object.
The hidden attractor is configuration: the diversity of things, the properties of composites, and the person converge upon modes of ordering rather than upon separate substances.

sections.original_name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Ignorance of causality → religious terror and death → affective disturbance → inquiry into nature.
First bodies + void → an ontological field sufficient without a third nature or external intervention.
Perpetual motion + weight + blows + clinamen → encounters neither providential nor fatally exhausted.
Various shapes and orders + selective compatibility → stable kinds without transcendent models.
Principles lacking qualities + ordering of relations → emergent qualities, life, and sense.
Local stabilization → composite thing / world / person → growth, alteration, and mortality.
Dissolution of compounds → conserved matter → succession of forms without annihilation or restored personal identity.
Reclassification of causality → removal of providence and the subsequent subject → diminution of compensatory desire → tranquillity of finite life.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Sensible effect → invisible bodily cause → body and void → motion of principles → selective composition → emergent properties → mortal world and person → redistribution of matter.
Ignorance → terror → religion, desire, and ambition → investigation of nature → mortality of the animus demonstrated → no subject after death → sufficiency of finite life.
The opposition between visible and real collapses: invisibility does not remove a thing from knowledge, but requires an inferential method.
Quality and sense are reclassified from simple properties of substances into effects of relations and common motions.
World and mind are transferred from privileged entities into local, multipliable, and mortal organizations.
The field of causality is no longer divided between providence and fate; material immanence can contain limited contingency.
Death and political vices are arranged on the same map: the absence of a subsequent subject constitutes the true state of death, while contrary imagination produces desire and violence.
The opposition between doctrine and therapy is dissolved: poetic form transmits reason, while reason reorders the affective and practical field.
The surface level joins the principles of things, human fears, conspicuous qualities, the nature of the animus, and the question of death.
The structural level contains first bodies, void, motion, compositions, laws of connection, and sentient organization.
The metastrategic level converts appearances into traces of causes and transforms the struggle against gods, fate, and death into correction of the causal map.
The ontological and temporal level distinguishes eternal matter, mortal compounds, plural worlds, continuous identity, and death without experience.
The methodological and performative level treats the obscurity of doctrine through poetry, analogy, and cumulative proof, so that the form of exposition effects the transition from affect to reason.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Sense remains the foundation of proof, although reason must correct the inventory of appearance; the rule of this correction is not fully formalized.
Clinamen, uncertain in place and time, interrupts determinate laws of composition and compatibility, without a clear measure of the relation between necessity and contingency.
Sense must emerge from insentient principles, but the transition from shape and motion to the quality of sensing remains mechanically incomplete.
The immortality of the gods is not yet reconciled with the law of dissolution of composites, because the remote gods are postulated rather than materially reconstructed.
The invocation of Venus retains poetic agency, although divine intervention is physically denied; the distinction between figure and causality sustains this joint.
The unity of animus and anima coheres imperfectly with the hierarchy between the governing animus, the consenting anima, and the fourth sentient force.
Quality changes from a dependent accident into an emergent relational property that distinguishes ontological levels.
Clinamen transforms closed causality into open immanence, but the link between atomic deviation and conscious will remains fragile.
Death passes from an event of dissolution to a logical change whereby, once the subject is removed, the very relation of harming becomes impossible.
Identity is transferred from likeness of matter to continuity of organization, sense, and memory.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly an infinite field of moving bodies that, without a center, generates local compounds, worlds, and their ruins.
The subject is a temporary bodily node in which animus, anima, organs, and sentient motions produce finite identity.
Time is the distribution of heterochronous orders: principles remain, compounds endure and perish, but the person never experiences its own absence.
Possible navigation is not flight from nature or from oneself, but knowledge of causes within nature not fatally closed.
The present axioms suffice to reconstruct the chain from conserved matter and motion to emergence, mortal worlds, the dissoluble person, and therapy of fear.
The firmest structure is the conjunction of conservation of matter, configurational explanation, and cumulative proof of organic mortality.
The links from clinamen to will and from the insentient motions of first principles to sense remain less determinate.
The system coheres at this level because it preserves the movement from affective effect to physics, from ontology to cosmology, and then to the transformation of life.
The more fragile joints rest on analogies of qualities, the principle of substantial change, and the rational correction of appearances.
The axiomatic reduction resists the performative transition whereby obscure doctrine is converted, through poetic form and knowledge of causality, into affective acceptance of finite life.

items.text: Systema quaerit quomodo perceptio, affectus, mundus, vita, historia et calamitas ex principiis corporeis explicentur, providentia et animorum immortalitate exclusis, ut metus religiosus tollatur.

Thesis globalis est unam causalitatem materialem, per fluxum, concursum, congruentiam et dissolutionem variatam, operationes sensibiles, ordines cosmicos, formas viventes et eventus morbidos sine ruptura supernaturali generare.
Argumentatio coniungit restitutionem materialem, polemicam adversus providentiam, genealogiam ordinum emergentium et therapiam opinionum timorem producentium.
Motus progreditur a transmissionibus minimis et perceptione ad cosmogoniam atque historiam, deinde ad calamitatem biologicam quae ordinem socialem dissolvere potest.
Cognitio a sensibus incipit, causas occultas ex effectibus manifestis infert, atque incertitudinem causae singularis per pluralitatem possibilitatum materialiter finitarum administrat.
Motus verus est recursivus et amplificativus: ignorantia causae attributionem divinam et timorem gignit, inquisitio materialis autem circuitum rescindit et ad tranquillitatem redit.
Ordo non est exemplar antecedens sed stabilitas temporaria inter concursus, cuius regularitas intentionem ordinatricem non probat.
Clausura fit catastrophica potius quam triumphalis: pestilentia confirmat causalitatem materialem, sed simul ostendit intelligibilitatem neque remedium certum neque dominationem practicam praestare.
Clausura ultima est apophatico-therapeutica: pax animi ex cognitione finium et remotione gubernationis divinae petitur, nulla tamen immunitate ontologica hominibus promissa.
[Persistent] Omnis res operans, animus inclusus, est compositio corporea cuius facultates ex motibus et interactionibus primordiorum oriuntur.
[Persistent] Potestas cuiusque naturae finita est, atque effectus possibilis terminis texturae, motus et compositionis continetur.
[Mutating] Effectus neque in agente neque in recipiente solitario residet, sed ex congruentia selectiva corporum, viarum et texturarum emergit.
[Emergent] Ordo est stabilizatio temporaria configurationum inter concursus innumeros, non forma finalis antecedenter imposita.
[Persistent] Omne compositum est permeabile, mutabile et mortale; eadem conditio corpus, mundum et ordines ex corporibus constitutos attingit.
[Mutating] Affectio sensibilis verum eventum relationis corporeae refert, falsitas autem nascitur cum opinio causam, identitatem vel finem affectioni addit.
[Emergent] Causae occultae ex effectibus sensibilibus inferuntur, sed unitas ontologiae cum pluralitate mechanismorum particularium compatitur.
[Persistent] Ignorantia causalis imagines, admirationem et eventus naturales in signa potestatis divinae convertit, inde timorem religiosum generans.
[Persistent] Finalitas providentialis excluditur: usus, aptitudo et regularitas sunt effectus structurarum et stabilitatum, non causae originis earum.
[Emergent] Subiectum est nexus materialis permeabilis, non principium separatum: imaginibus, ambiente, anima corporea et institutis mediantibus agit.
[Mutating] Facultates, usus, vocabula et instituta post structuram per consuetudinem, utilitatem et experientiam emergunt.
[Attractor] Therapia affectuum opiniones retractat, attentionem convertit et cupidinis timorisque fines definit, potius quam sensus vel corpora repudiat.
[Terminal] Intelligibilitas naturalis a dominio practico separatur: causa materialis cognosci potest etiam ubi remedium, tutela vel imperium deest.
[Attractor] Tranquillitas ex conspectu naturae et cognitione finium causalium emergit, non ex favore divino aut accumulatione bonorum externorum.
[Terminal] Calamitas sine destinatario morali corpora, officia, ritus et ordines sociales materialiter dissolvere potest.
Effluxus corporeus identitatem causalitatis servat, sed a productione simulacrorum ad circulationem ambientalem et morbidam amplificatur.
Congruentia a qualitate sensibili ad generationem, conservationem biologicam et susceptibilitatem regionalem migrat; functio eius ex perceptione in viabilitatem extenditur.
Imago a nuntio sensibili in instrumentum captationis affectivae et attributionis religiosae mutatur.
Opinio addita affectioni, primo fons erroris perceptivi, in scala sociali fit machina qua ignorantia eventus naturales ad deos refert.
Pluralitas causarum ex cautela astronomica in disciplinam epistemicam generalem amplificatur, qua naturalitas sine falsa certitudine singulari defenditur.
Utilitas, postquam ex causa originis organorum in effectum posterioris usus conversa est, in genealogiam institutionum transit et tandem per progressum bellicum invertitur.
Mortalitas a dissolutione personae ad dissolutionem mundi et ordinum curae atque ritus amplificatur.
Divinitas inversionem patitur: a causa providentiali removetur, deinde vel nomen honorificum sapientiae vel exemplar pacis non intervenientis fit.
Continuitas ex successione imaginum pereuntium ad historiam statuum irreversibilium transfertur; tempus apparens fit tempus generationis et amissionis facultatum.
Circuitus amoris, ubi imago attentionem et cupiditatem alit, in circuitu religionis absorbetur, ubi ignorantia, timor et attributio divina se mutuo confirmant.
Repercussiones speculorum, divisiones vocis et singulae transmissiones sensuum machinae locales manent; hoc gradu tantum exemplar commune medii, itineris et ictus sustinent.
Causae particulares motuum caelestium localiter indeterminatae manent neque in propositionem globalem de causa singulari convertuntur.
Physiologia Venerea localis est, sed circuitus imaginis, opinionis et attentionis ad theoriam generalem captationis affectivae amplificatur.
Semina morbida et contagio sunt mechanismi locales; permeabilitas subiecti et dissolubilitas ordinis socialis sunt consequentiae huius gradus.
Hoc gradu visio, cosmogonia et pestilentia non ut argumenta separata aggregantur, sed ut variationes unius ontologiae materialis per diversas magnitudines coniunguntur.
Centauri, monstra et alia exemplaria fabulosa opere exclusorio peracto evanescunt; persistit regula incompatibilitatis materialis, non catalogus fabularum.
Status ontologicus deorum et simulacrorum divinorum minus determinatus manet; synthesis praesentis gradus tantum eorum gubernationem causaliter excludit.
Facultates biologicae, stabilitates cosmicae et nexus subiecti in structuram superiorem absorbentur, cuius termini sunt emergentia, permeabilitas et dissolutio.
Systema negat animam personalem incorpoream dissolutionem corporis integram superare.
Providentia et finalitas excluduntur tamquam causae sensuum, membrorum, mundi et historiae.
Scepticismus universalis et tribunal cognitionis sensibus extrinsecum simul reiciuntur.
Imago composita, raritas aut magnitudo eventus correspondentem naturam supernaturalem non requirit.
Distributio calamitatum meritum, innocentiam et sanctitatem causaliter non sequitur.
Homo neque finis processus cosmici neque mensura magnitudinis et aptitudinis naturae est.
Stabilitas foederum, specierum et institutionum aeternitatem vel immutabilitatem non implicat.
Divitiae, honores et progressus technicus incrementum necessarium felicitatis non constituunt.
Cognitio naturalis promissionem remedii, tutelae aut imperii universalis non continet.
Falsum esse oportet omnem regularitatem intentionem ordinatricem vel propositum humanum implicare.
Falsum esse oportet continuitatem apparentem vel stabilitatem localem substantiam permanentem et aeternam requirere.
Falsum esse oportet ignorantiam causae testimonium positivum gubernatoris divini praebere.
Falsum esse oportet mentem vel corpus terminum clausum extra circulationem naturalem constituere.
Falsum esse oportet futuram utilitatem formam organi vel institutionis originarie causare.
Falsum esse oportet naturalem explicationem certitudine unius causae actualis in omni casu niti.
Falsum esse oportet causam naturalem effectum benignum, coercibilem aut remedio communi tractabilem reddere.
Falsum esse oportet ordinem physicum ordinem moralem exprimere vel calamitatem destinatario merenti assignare.
Indisponibilis est locus cognitionis extra sensus, corpus et naturam ex quo totum systema sine mediatione iudicetur.
Indisponibilis est custodia providentialis quae mundum regat aut hominibus immunitatem ontologicam concedat.
Indisponibilis est possessio plena quae cupiditatem semel satiat, quia relatio semper imaginibus, corporibus et opinionibus mediatur.
Indisponibilis est finis cosmicus vel historicus qui mundos, civitates et artes ad perfectionem necessariam conducat.
Calamitas circum absentiam iudicis moralis ordinatur: effectus habet causas et victimas, sed nullum destinatarium metaphysicum.
Clausura epistemica totalis et dominium practicum naturae vetantur, etiamsi fines potestatum ac genera causarum cognosci possunt.
Circulatio quae imagines ad sensus defert eadem structura amplificata corpora ambientalia et semina morbida diffundit; realitas igitur systemice ut commercium permeabile constituitur.
Veritas affectionis et indeterminatio mechanismi actualis simul efficiunt realismum asymmetricalem: eventus relationis certior esse potest quam causa singularis eius.
Cum structura usum antecedat et ordo ex concursibus stabilitur, functio fit effectus retrospectivus conservationis, non consilium originarium.
Captatio erotica et religio eandem formam recursive variant: repraesentatio repetita attentionem figit, affectum auget et fontem commotionis falso obiecto attribuit.
Quia persona, mundus et instituta sunt composita, dissolutio socialis pestilentiae non est casus ontologiae extrinsecus, sed amplificatio mortalitatis communis.
Recta pietas per negationem constituitur: pax deorum servatur tantum si administratio providentialis et ira causaliter operans removentur.
Congruentia est operator transversalis qui qualitatem sensibilem, generationem, conservationem specierum et differentiam morborum ex relationibus, non essentiis absolutis, producit.
Ars et divitiae facultates augent, sed tranquillitatem aut immunitatem non augent necessario; mediatio technica potest etiam desiderium, bellum et vulnerabilitatem amplificare.
Actio et institutio originem sovereignam non habent: utraque per imagines, motus corporeos, vulnerabilitatem mutuam et consuetudinem distributim constituitur.
Efficacia cognitionis est imprimis modalis et affectiva: causas divinas excludit et timorem minuit, sed eventum naturalem neque necessario sanat neque coercet.
Causalitas materialis invarians magnitudine est: eadem syntaxis differentiarum, fluxuum, viarum et congruentiarum a perceptione ad cosmologiam et pestilentiam operatur.
Ontologia huius gregis est ontologia compositorum apertorum, in quibus identitas temporaria ex permutatione materiae et finibus interactionum persistit.
Tempus componit successionem celerrimam, emergentiam irreversibilem et dissolutionem mortalem; permanentia est effectus localis intra has tres operationes.
Epistemologia resultans est realismus finitus: affectiones, signa et limites potestatum cognitionem sustinent, dum causa actualis interdum indeterminata manet.
Libertas practica non est exemptio a causalitate, sed facultas circuitus attentionis, opinionis et timoris per cognitionem atque redirectionem materialem interrumpendi.
Ordo politicus est compositum contingens ex vulnerabilitate et utilitate ortum, ideo eadem dissolutione materiali ac corpora constituentia affici potest.
Religio terrifica est compressio causalis quae ignorantiam in intentionem divinam vertit; pietas naturalis hanc compressionem solvit sine deis ipsis necessario tollendis.
Pestilentia promissionem liberationis non negat, sed eius ambitum terminaliter restringit: mens a falso terrore liberari potest, corpus et societas a calamitate non immunia fiunt.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Effluxus → receptio selectiva → affectio → nova dispositio recipientis constituit circuitum basalium interactionum, ex quo sensationes, actiones et contagiones variantur.
Imago amati → cupiditas → opinio idealizans → attentio fixa → maior copia imaginum efficit escalationem affectivam quae se ipsa pascit.
Ignorantia → timor → attributio divina → observatio anxia → renovata ignorantia constituit attractorem religiosum, ad quem admiratio sine causa cognita relabitur.
Concursus innumeri → configuratio stabilis → ordo localis → conflictus partium → dissolutio → materia novis concursibus reddita constituit circuitum cosmicum.
Ars → opes → distinctio → ambitio → arma → periculum collectivum est via amplificationis qua progressus commodorum in augmentum conflictus invertitur.
Cura aegroti → propinquitas → contagio, sed fuga → desertio → interitus aegroti constituit duplicem clausuram tragicam officii.
Effectus sensibilis → analogiae → fines potestatum → causae naturales restrictae → remotio gubernationis divinae constituit circuitum inquisitivum qui timorem minuit.
Attractor communis est cognitio potentiarum finitarum: ad eum perceptionis correctio, cosmogonia naturalis et explicatio calamitatum diversis viis convergunt.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Differentiae primordiorum + inane → composita corporea varia et permeabilia.
Compositum permeabile → effluxus continuus + motus per medium → commercium cum aliis compositis.
Commercium → selectio per vias et texturas → congruentia, repulsio vel penetratio → affectio determinata.
Concursus repetiti → configurationes stabiles → usus, species, ordines cosmici et instituta → dissolutio ubi congruentia deficit.
Affectio → opinio addita → falsa identitas, finalitas vel intentio → captatio affectiva et religio terrifica.
Structura nata → usus repetitus → consuetudo et utilitas → facultas vel institutum emergens sine auctore originario.
Effectus manifestus → inferentia causae materialis intra fines potestatum → exclusio causae divinae → correctio opinionis et imminutio timoris.
Calamitas materialis → vulnerabilitas corporis → defectus remedii communis → dissolutio ordinis → distinctio terminalis inter intelligibilitatem et dominium.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Differentia primordiorum → effluxus → receptio congruens → sensus → opinio addita → error corrigibilis.
Concursus sine consilio → stabilitas cosmica → vita viabilis → instituta emergentia → progressus ambivalens → mortalitas ordinum.
Admiratio → ignorantia causae → attributio divina → timor → causalitas naturalis restricta → pietas sine gubernatione divina.
Permeabilitas ambientalium corporum → contagio → dilemma curae → ruptura ritus et ordinis → clausura sine remedio aut iudicio morali.
Cognitio naturae → imminutio timoris → tranquillitas possibilis → persistentia mortalitatis → recusatio immunitatis et dominii totalis.
Oppositio apparentiae et veritatis reordinatur in distinctionem inter affectionem materialiter veram et opinionem causaliter corrigibilem.
Ordo a consilio antecedente separatur et ut effectus stabilitatis post concursus reclassificatur.
Subiectum ex unitate clausa in nodum permeabilem circulationis corporum, imaginum et affectuum mutatur.
Oppositio pietatis et naturalismi corruit, quia tranquillitas divina per exclusionem interventus servatur.
Incertitudo causae singularis ex defectu explicationis in disciplinam pluralitatis materialiter restrictae convertitur.
Lingua, lex et potestas ex fundamentis originariis in eventus genealogicos utilitatis, conflictus et consuetudinis transferuntur.
Progressus technicus ex incremento necessario boni in amplificatorem simultaneum commodorum, desideriorum et belli mutatur.
Cognitio naturae ab imperio practico separatur; eius effectus proprius est reordinatio timoris et interpretationis, non tutela universalis.
In gradu superficiei apparent imagines, errores sensuum, mundus et sidera, origines vitae, eventus terrestres, morbi et pestilentia tamquam obiecta explicanda.
In gradu structurali emissiones, concursus, viae, texturas, congruentiae, utilitates et conflictus operationes diversas in unam causalitatem materialem distribuunt.
In gradu metastrategico certamen a repudiatione sensuum et placatione deorum ad correctionem opinionum, definitionem finium et interruptionem timoris transfertur.
In gradu ontologico et temporali realitas est nexus compositorum finitorum, subiectum est nodus corporeus, et tempus coniungit successionem, emergentiam irreversibilem atque dissolutionem.

In gradu methodologico et performativo textus per reditum eiusdem grammaticae in campos maiores id quod affirmat efficit: asperam doctrinam causaliter reconstructivam in experientiam repetitionis cum variatione convertit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Ratio sensibus innititur, quamvis primordia et simulacra singula sensum excedant; transitus ab effectu visibili ad causam invisibilem analogia potius quam inspectione directa firmatur.
Certitudo therapeutica rationis cum indeterminatione mechanismorum actualium tensionem servat, quia exclusio divini firmior est quam electio unius causae naturalis.
Promissio purificationis animi a clausura pestilentiali comprimitur: cognitio timorem corrigit, sed remedium commune vel conservationem societatis non praestat.
Dei causaliter remoti servantur, sed eorum status ontologicus et relatio ad simulacra divina non plene ex machina materiali derivantur.
Concursus fortuiti cum foederibus stabilibus componendi sunt; casus eventum eligit, sed limites naturae infringere non debet.
Veritas affectionis sensus cum distortionibus apparentibus cohaeret tantum si veritas ad eventum recipientis, non ad omne iudicium de obiecto, restringitur.
Simulacrum mutatur a nuntio qui formam originis servat in operatorem recursivum cupiditatis, memoriae et attentionis.
Congruentia mutatur a principio differentiae sensibilium in regulam generationis, viabilitatis et susceptibilitatis morbidae.
Ordo mutatur a consecutione recurrente in configurationem temporaliter stabilem, cui dissolutio iam intrinseca est.
Pietas mutatur ab obsequio rituali in contemplationem naturae et conservationem pacis divinae per non-interventionem.
Mortalitas mutatur a fine personae in principium cosmologicum et tandem in potestatem dissolvendi instituta socialia.
Therapia mutatur a fiducia in cognitionem causarum ad formam sobriam liberationis quae timorem tollit sine promissione dominii.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Realitas implicite est machina porosa compositorum, per quam corpora fluunt, formae substituuntur, configurationes stabilizantur et partes tandem discedunt.
Subiectum intra hanc machinam est receptor selectivus et nodus motuum distributorum, non centrum immateriale neque unitas clausa.
Tempus est simul velocitas substitutionis formarum et successio irreversibilis statuum in quibus facultates oriuntur atque pereunt.
Certamen principale fit inter circuitus captationis, qui imaginem vel ignorantiam se ipsam alere cogunt, et cognitionem quae attentionem atque attributionem causaliter convertit.
Navigatio possibilis est inferentia finita intra naturam: mechanismi restringuntur sine clausura absoluta, timor minuitur sine immunitate, et actio exercetur sine dominio totali.
Axiomata praesentia sufficiunt ad machinam principalem a perceptione corporea per emergentiam cosmologicam et historicam ad vulnerabilitatem pestilentialem restituendam.
Structura firmissima est communis grammatica causalitatis materialis coniuncta cum finibus potestatum, mortalitate compositorum et correctione attributionis divinae.
Minus determinata manent origo quarundam imaginum, causa actualis plurium phaenomenorum et exacti mechanismi quorum possibilitas analogiis tantum demonstratur.
Cohaerentia huius gradus pendet ex distinctione foederum stabiliter finitorum a configurationibus temporalibus, contingentibus et dissolubilibus.
Restitutio verum motum servat: a fluxu corporeo ad cognitionem, a concursu ad ordinem emergentem, ab ignorantia ad timorem, atque ab explicatione ad limites imperii.
Tensionem terminalem eliminare non licet, quia discrimen inter liberationem animi et persistentem vulnerabilitatem corporis structuram, non defectum accidentalem, constituit.
Reductioni axiomaticae partim resistit vis performativa formae poeticae, quae doctrinae asperitatem tractabilem reddit et repetitionem causalitatis in actum persuasionis convertit.

The system asks how perception, affect, world, life, history, and calamity may be explained from bodily principles, with providence and the immortality of souls excluded, so that religious fear may be removed.

The global thesis is that a single material causality, through varied flux, encounter, congruence, and dissolution, generates sensible operations, cosmic orders, living forms, and morbid events without supernatural rupture.
The argumentation joins material reconstruction, polemic against providence, a genealogy of emergent orders, and a therapy of opinions producing fear.
The movement proceeds from minimal transmissions and perception to cosmogony and history, then to biological calamity capable of dissolving social order.
Knowledge begins from the senses, infers hidden causes from manifest effects, and manages uncertainty concerning a singular cause through a plurality of materially bounded possibilities.
The true movement is recursive and amplifying: ignorance of the cause generates divine attribution and fear, whereas material inquiry breaks the circuit and returns to tranquillity.
Order is not a prior model but temporary stability among encounters, whose regularity does not prove an ordering intention.
The closure is catastrophic rather than triumphant: plague confirms material causality, but also shows that intelligibility provides neither certain remedy nor practical mastery.
The final closure is apophatic-therapeutic: peace of mind is sought from knowledge of limits and the removal of divine governance, though no ontological immunity is promised to human beings.
[Persistent] Every acting thing, including the mind, is a bodily composite whose capacities arise from the movements and interactions of primordial elements.
[Persistent] The power of each nature is finite, and every possible effect is contained by the limits of texture, motion, and composition.
[Mutating] An effect resides neither in the agent nor in the recipient taken alone, but emerges from the selective congruence of bodies, pathways, and textures.
[Emergent] Order is the temporary stabilization of configurations among innumerable encounters, not a final form imposed in advance.
[Persistent] Every composite is permeable, mutable, and mortal; the same condition affects body, world, and orders constituted from bodies.
[Mutating] Sensible affection reports a true event of bodily relation, whereas falsity arises when opinion adds cause, identity, or end to the affection.
[Emergent] Hidden causes are inferred from sensible effects, but ontological unity is compatible with a plurality of particular mechanisms.
[Persistent] Causal ignorance transforms images, wonder, and natural events into signs of divine power, thereby generating religious fear.
[Persistent] Providential finality is excluded: use, fitness, and regularity are effects of structures and stabilities, not causes of their origin.
[Emergent] The subject is a permeable material nexus, not a separate principle: it acts through images, environment, bodily soul, and institutions.
[Mutating] Capacities, uses, terms, and institutions emerge after structure through custom, utility, and experience.
[Attractor] The therapy of affects revises opinions, redirects attention, and defines the limits of desire and fear, rather than repudiating senses or bodies.
[Terminal] Natural intelligibility is separated from practical mastery: a material cause may be known even where remedy, protection, or control is absent.
[Attractor] Tranquillity emerges from contemplation of nature and knowledge of causal limits, not from divine favor or the accumulation of external goods.
[Terminal] Calamity without a moral addressee can materially dissolve bodies, duties, rites, and social orders.
Bodily efflux preserves the identity of causality, but is amplified from the production of simulacra to environmental and morbid circulation.
Congruence migrates from sensible quality to generation, biological preservation, and regional susceptibility; its function extends from perception to viability.
The image changes from a sensible message into an instrument of affective capture and religious attribution.
Opinion added to affection, initially a source of perceptual error, becomes on the social scale the machine by which ignorance refers natural events to the gods.
The plurality of causes is amplified from astronomical caution into a general epistemic discipline, by which naturalness is defended without false singular certainty.
Utility, after being converted from the cause of the origin of organs into an effect of later use, passes into the genealogy of institutions and is finally inverted through military progress.
Mortality is amplified from the dissolution of the person to the dissolution of the world and of orders of care and rite.
Divinity undergoes an inversion: it is removed from providential causation, then becomes either an honorific name for wisdom or a model of non-intervening peace.
Continuity is transferred from the succession of perishing images to the history of irreversible states; apparent time becomes the time of the generation and loss of capacities.
The circuit of love, in which the image feeds attention and desire, is absorbed into the circuit of religion, in which ignorance, fear, and divine attribution mutually confirm one another.
Mirror reflections, divisions of sound, and individual sensory transmissions remain local mechanisms; at this level they sustain only the common pattern of medium, path, and impact.
Particular causes of celestial motions remain locally indeterminate and are not converted into a global proposition concerning a singular cause.
Venereal physiology is local, but the circuit of image, opinion, and attention is amplified into a general theory of affective capture.
Morbid seeds and contagion are local mechanisms; the permeability of the subject and the dissolubility of social order are consequences at this level.
At this level, vision, cosmogony, and plague are not aggregated as separate arguments, but are joined as variations of one material ontology across diverse magnitudes.
Centaurs, monsters, and other fabulous exemplars vanish once their exclusionary work is done; what persists is the rule of material incompatibility, not a catalogue of fables.
The ontological status of gods and divine simulacra remains less determinate; the synthesis at the present level excludes only their governance causally.
Biological capacities, cosmic stabilities, and nexuses of the subject are absorbed into a higher structure, whose terms are emergence, permeability, and dissolution.
The system denies that an incorporeal personal soul survives the dissolution of the body intact.
Providence and finality are excluded as causes of the senses, limbs, world, and history.
Universal skepticism and a tribunal of knowledge extrinsic to the senses are rejected together.
A composite image, rarity, or the magnitude of an event does not require a corresponding supernatural nature.
The distribution of calamities does not causally follow merit, innocence, or sanctity.
The human being is neither the end of the cosmic process nor the measure of nature's magnitude and fitness.
The stability of compacts, species, and institutions does not imply eternity or immutability.
Wealth, honors, and technical progress do not constitute a necessary increase in happiness.
Natural knowledge contains no promise of universal remedy, protection, or control.
It must be false that every regularity implies an ordering intention or human purpose.
It must be false that apparent continuity or local stability requires a permanent and eternal substance.
It must be false that ignorance of a cause supplies positive testimony of a divine governor.
It must be false that mind or body constitutes a closed boundary outside natural circulation.
It must be false that future utility originally causes the form of an organ or institution.
It must be false that natural explanation depends in every case upon certainty of one actual cause.
It must be false that a natural cause renders an effect benign, controllable, or manageable by a common remedy.
It must be false that physical order expresses moral order or assigns calamity to a deserving addressee.
Unavailable is a site of knowledge outside the senses, body, and nature from which the whole system may be judged without mediation.
Unavailable is a providential guardianship that governs the world or grants human beings ontological immunity.
Unavailable is a complete possession that satisfies desire once and for all, because relation is always mediated by images, bodies, and opinions.
Unavailable is a cosmic or historical end that leads worlds, cities, and arts toward necessary perfection.
Calamity is ordered around the absence of a moral judge: it has causes and victims, but no metaphysical addressee.
Total epistemic closure and practical mastery of nature are prohibited, even if the limits of powers and kinds of causes may be known.

The circulation that conveys images to the senses, in the same structure amplified, diffuses environmental bodies and morbid seeds; reality is therefore constituted systemically as permeable exchange.
The truth of affection and the indeterminacy of the actual mechanism together produce an asymmetrical realism: the event of relation may be more certain than its singular cause.
When structure precedes use and order is stabilized from encounters, function becomes a retrospective effect of preservation, not an original design.
Erotic capture and religion recursively vary the same form: repeated representation fixes attention, increases affect, and falsely attributes the source of disturbance to an object.
Because person, world, and institutions are composites, the social dissolution of plague is not extrinsic to ontology, but an amplification of common mortality.
Right piety is constituted through negation: the peace of the gods is preserved only if providential administration and causally operating anger are removed.
Congruence is a transversal operator that produces sensible quality, generation, preservation of species, and difference in diseases from relations, not absolute essences.
Art and wealth increase capacities, but do not necessarily increase tranquillity or immunity; technical mediation can also amplify desire, war, and vulnerability.
Action and institution have no sovereign origin: each is constituted distributively through images, bodily motions, mutual vulnerability, and custom.
The efficacy of knowledge is primarily modal and affective: it excludes divine causes and diminishes fear, but neither necessarily heals nor controls a natural event.
Material causality is invariant across magnitude: the same syntax of differences, fluxes, pathways, and congruences operates from perception to cosmology and plague.
The ontology of this whole is an ontology of open composites, in which temporary identity persists through the exchange of matter and the limits of interactions.
Time composes most rapid succession, irreversible emergence, and mortal dissolution; permanence is a local effect within these three operations.
The resulting epistemology is a finite realism: affections, signs, and the limits of powers sustain knowledge, while the actual cause sometimes remains indeterminate.
Practical freedom is not exemption from causality, but the capacity to interrupt circuits of attention, opinion, and fear through knowledge and material redirection.
Political order is a contingent composite arising from vulnerability and utility, and may therefore be affected by the same material dissolution as its constituent bodies.
Terrifying religion is a causal compression that turns ignorance into divine intention; natural piety dissolves this compression without necessarily abolishing the gods themselves.
Plague does not negate the promise of liberation, but terminally restricts its scope: the mind can be freed from false terror, but body and society do not become immune to calamity.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Efflux → selective reception → affection → new disposition of the recipient constitutes the circuit of basic interactions, from which sensations, actions, and contagions vary.
Image of the beloved → desire → idealizing opinion → fixed attention → a greater abundance of images produces a self-feeding affective escalation.
Ignorance → fear → divine attribution → anxious observation → renewed ignorance constitutes a religious attractor, to which wonder without a known cause relapses.
Innumerable encounters → stable configuration → local order → conflict of parts → dissolution → matter returned to new encounters constitutes a cosmic circuit.
Art → wealth → distinction → ambition → weapons → collective danger is a path of amplification by which progress in advantages is inverted into an increase of conflict.
Care for the sick → proximity → contagion, but flight → abandonment → death of the sick constitutes the double tragic closure of duty.
Sensible effect → analogies → limits of powers → restricted natural causes → removal of divine governance constitutes an inquiring circuit that diminishes fear.
The common attractor is knowledge of finite powers: correction of perception, natural cosmogony, and explanation of calamities converge upon it by different routes.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Differences of primordial elements + void → varied and permeable bodily composites.
Permeable composite → continuous efflux + motion through a medium → exchange with other composites.
Exchange → selection through pathways and textures → congruence, repulsion, or penetration → determinate affection.
Repeated encounters → stable configurations → uses, species, cosmic orders, and institutions → dissolution where congruence fails.
Affection → added opinion → false identity, finality, or intention → affective capture and terrifying religion.
Structure arisen → repeated use → custom and utility → capacity or institution emerging without an original author.
Manifest effect → inference of material cause within the limits of powers → exclusion of divine cause → correction of opinion and diminution of fear.
Material calamity → bodily vulnerability → lack of common remedy → dissolution of order → terminal distinction between intelligibility and mastery.

sections.original_name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Difference of primordial elements → efflux → congruent reception → sensation → added opinion → corrigible error.
Encounter without design → cosmic stability → viable life → emergent institutions → ambivalent progress → mortality of orders.
Wonder → ignorance of cause → divine attribution → fear → restricted natural causality → piety without divine governance.
Permeability of environmental bodies → contagion → dilemma of care → rupture of rite and order → closure without remedy or moral judgment.
Knowledge of nature → diminution of fear → possible tranquillity → persistence of mortality → refusal of immunity and total mastery.
The opposition of appearance and truth is reordered into the distinction between materially true affection and causally corrigible opinion.
Order is separated from antecedent design and reclassified as an effect of stability after encounters.
The subject changes from a closed unity into a permeable node of the circulation of bodies, images, and affects.
The opposition of piety and naturalism collapses, because divine tranquillity is preserved through the exclusion of intervention.
Uncertainty concerning a singular cause is converted from a deficiency of explanation into a discipline of materially restricted plurality.
Language, law, and power are transferred from original foundations into genealogical events of utility, conflict, and custom.
Technical progress changes from a necessary increase of good into a simultaneous amplifier of advantages, desires, and war.
Knowledge of nature is separated from practical control; its proper effect is the reordering of fear and interpretation, not universal protection.
At the level of the surface appear images, errors of the senses, the world and stars, origins of life, terrestrial events, diseases, and plague as objects to be explained.
At the structural level, emissions, encounters, pathways, textures, congruences, utilities, and conflicts distribute diverse operations into one material causality.
At the metastrategic level, the struggle shifts from repudiation of the senses and propitiation of the gods to correction of opinions, definition of limits, and interruption of fear.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality is a nexus of finite composites, the subject is a bodily node, and time joins succession, irreversible emergence, and dissolution.

At the methodological and performative level, the text accomplishes what it affirms through the return of the same grammar in larger fields: it turns a harsh causally reconstructive doctrine into an experience of repetition with variation.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reason relies upon the senses, although primordial elements and individual simulacra exceed sensation; the transition from visible effect to invisible cause is secured by analogy rather than direct inspection.
The therapeutic certainty of reason sustains a tension with the indeterminacy of actual mechanisms, because exclusion of the divine is firmer than selection of one natural cause.
The promise of purification of the mind is compressed by the pestilential closure: knowledge corrects fear, but does not provide a common remedy or preservation of society.
The gods are causally removed yet preserved, but their ontological status and relation to divine simulacra are not fully derived from the material mechanism.
Fortuitous encounters must be reconciled with stable compacts; chance selects the event, but must not violate the limits of nature.
The truth of sensible affection coheres with apparent distortions only if truth is restricted to the event in the recipient, not to every judgment concerning the object.
The simulacrum changes from a message preserving the form of its origin into a recursive operator of desire, memory, and attention.
Congruence changes from a principle of the difference of sensible things into a rule of generation, viability, and morbid susceptibility.
Order changes from recurrent succession into a temporally stable configuration, to which dissolution is already intrinsic.
Piety changes from ritual obedience into contemplation of nature and preservation of divine peace through non-intervention.
Mortality changes from the end of the person into a cosmological principle and finally into a power to dissolve social institutions.
Therapy changes from confidence in knowledge of causes into a sober form of liberation that removes fear without promising mastery.

sections.original_name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reality is implicitly a porous machine of composites, through which bodies flow, forms are replaced, configurations stabilize, and parts finally depart.
Within this machine, the subject is a selective receiver and node of distributed motions, not an immaterial center or closed unity.
Time is at once the speed of the substitution of forms and the irreversible succession of states in which capacities arise and perish.
The principal struggle occurs between circuits of capture, which compel image or ignorance to feed itself, and knowledge, which causally redirects attention and attribution.
Navigation is possible as finite inference within nature: mechanisms are restricted without absolute closure, fear is diminished without immunity, and action is exercised without total mastery.
The present axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal mechanism from bodily perception through cosmological and historical emergence to pestilential vulnerability.
The firmest structure is the common grammar of material causality conjoined with the limits of powers, mortality of composites, and correction of divine attribution.
Less determinate remain the origin of certain images, the actual cause of many phenomena, and exact mechanisms whose possibility is demonstrated only through analogies.
The coherence of this level depends on the distinction between stably finite compacts and temporal, contingent, and dissoluble configurations.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement: from bodily flux to knowledge, from encounter to emergent order, from ignorance to fear, and from explanation to the limits of mastery.
The terminal tension must not be eliminated, because the distinction between liberation of the mind and persistent bodily vulnerability constitutes a structure, not an accidental defect.
The performative force of poetic form partly resists axiomatic reduction; it renders the harshness of doctrine manageable and turns the repetition of causality into an act of persuasion.
